body:
Refs #71

## 內容

issue #71 的實作：admission/報名網站認定的隊伍（`registrant_roster.team`）跟座位命名（`container` 字首，`red-01` / `blue-a-01` / `blue-b-01`）推斷出的隊伍不一致時記一筆，供人工排查——**不取代**既有以 IP/destination 為準的判斷邏輯（issue #62 PR #64），純供稽核參考。

- `store.py`：新表 `team_mismatches`，`sync_team_mismatches()` upsert（保留 `detected_at`，清掉這輪已經不再不一致的舊紀錄）；`clear_all()` 六張表 → 七張表。
- `roster_receiver.py`：`infer_team_from_container()`（跟 `seat_log_receiver.get_team_from_filename()` 同字首規則，命名網域不同故意分開寫，不共用）＋ `compute_team_mismatches()` 純函式；`_poll_once()` 每輪跟 roster 一起同步。
- `server.py`：`GET /team-mismatches`，一律要求 `INGEST_TOKEN`——過程中發現一個差點寫出來的設計問題：一開始比照 `/analysis` 想用 `caller=public/purple` 切換，但 `require_purple_clearance` 只在 `caller="purple"` 時才驗 token，`public` 預設會直接放行，等於公開洩漏診斷資訊，改成不提供 public 分支。
- `admin.html`：新增一張卡片查詢不一致清單，用跟清場功能同一組 token。
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`／`README.md` 同步更新。

## 阻塞狀態

`se-218/Metis#161`（報名網站 API 接入）已於 2026-08-26 定案並關閉，`team` 欄位在 `registrant_roster` 表裡本來就有（issue #74 起），這張票的阻塞條件已解除。

211 個測試全過（`test_roster_receiver.py`／`test_server.py` 各數筆，涵蓋 `infer_team_from_container()`、`compute_team_mismatches()`、`_poll_once()` 同步行為、`/team-mismatches` 的 token 驗證）。

author: jeanibarz
body:
## Summary

Starting an agent could hang past the configured launch ceiling on two paths that already have a task: **pending promotion** (a queued task becoming a running session) and a **Ralph relaunch** (the iterative loop starting the next session on the same in-progress task). If the caller had already given up, a late success from the agent adapter could still attach a live session to that task, or leave a **dtach master** (the persistent terminal process that owns the agent) with no owner.

Those paths now share the same ceiling as a brand-new task. When the timeout fires, adapters abort session creation and prompt delivery. Any session already created is linked then killed. A late registry attach of that session id is refused. Promotion still cancels the task on failure. A Ralph relaunch still leaves the existing in-progress task in place. Crash-recovery was not named in the issue, but it was the last start path that raced the clock without aborting the adapter, so it now uses the same abort signal.

## Changes

- `launchFreshTaskSession` races `adapter.launch` against `launchTimeoutSeconds` and aborts a shared `AbortSignal`.
- Pending promotion and crash-recovery pass the same signal.
- Claude, Codex, and Grok adapters honor the signal around `createSession` and prompt delivery.
- `SessionRegistry.addSession` refuses a duplicate or already-aborted session id, so a late ack cannot attach onto a still-non-terminal Ralph task.
- Bookkeeping errors after attach no longer tear down a live worker, matching the promotion isolation from #1588.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm test` — 15957 passed, 3 expected fail, 59 skipped (pre-push)
- [x] `pnpm build:server` clean
- [x] `pnpm check:e2e` clean
- [x] Promotion timeout: pending task cancelled, created session aborted and stopped
- [x] Fresh-session timeout: existing task stays `inProgress`, late `addSession` refused
- [x] Session created before timeout is reaped
- [x] Late completion after timeout does not leave a live owned session
- [x] Post-attach registration failure does not reap a live fresh-session

## Verification

Before this change, `launchFreshTaskSession` awaited `adapter.launch` with no timeout. A never-settling mock now rejects with `LaunchTimeoutError` within the configured `getLaunchTimeoutMs` (20ms in tests). A session reported via `onSessionCreated` before that timeout is `adapter.stop`ped and recorded `aborted`. After timeout, `addSession` of the same id throws `Cannot attach aborted session`.

Happy path: a relaunch that `addSession`s within the timeout still returns the session id and registers the agent; `adapter.stop` is not called.

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] Unit tests pass (`pnpm test`)
- [ ] ~~E2E tests pass (`pnpm exec playwright test`)~~ — server-side launch/lifecycle only; no UI surface
- [ ] ~~Canary test pass locally (`CANARY=1 npx playwright test e2e/canary.spec.ts`)~~ — no mock event fixtures or hook-event shapes changed
- [ ] ~~Reviewed the CI coverage summary on this PR (Checks → `test` job → Summary)~~ — operator CI is billing-blocked; local `pnpm test` is the merge gate
- [x] <!-- kookr:check:tests --> Added or updated tests for the changed behavior, or explained why this change is docs/config-only
- [x] <!-- kookr:check:mbse --> System design documents are up to date with codebase changes (ADRs, `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/features.md`, skills — verify no drift) — `launchTimeoutSeconds` JSDoc in `src/core/settings-store.ts` updated; architecture/features already describe the timeout race without claiming promotion/fresh-session were unbounded
- [x] <!-- kookr:check:prose --> Summary is cold-reader clear: plain-language intent first, jargon glossed, symbols only in technical details (`clear-technical-writing` skill). Strike with a one-line reason only for pure typo / formatting / mechanical renames.

Closes #2766

author: kyzcreig
body:
## The incident

A user DM was fetched by the poller, offset-confirmed to Telegram (`pending_update_count` back to 0), and then **never reached any handler**. The gateway was healthy the whole time — no restart, no 409 conflict, no polling recovery — and the loss produced **zero** log evidence.

The bug worth fixing is that undetectability: an inbound message can vanish between PTB's update queue and the adapter with nothing to show for it, and the next occurrence would be just as unattributable.

## The fix

An observation-only sentinel at the ingest boundary, registered as a **group `-1` `TypeHandler`** so it sees every update before any filter, authorization prefilter, or text batching can discard one.

1. **Attribution** — one INFO line per update (`update_id`, chat, kind). A missing message is now classifiable: no line = transport/Bot-API loss; line present with no handler work = in-process drop after ingest.
2. **Gap detection** — Telegram `update_id`s are sequential per bot, and PTB advances its offset to `updates[-1].update_id + 1` only *after* queueing. So a forward jump between consecutively observed updates proves an update was fetched and offset-confirmed but never dispatched. Logged at WARNING with the exact missing range.

```
WARNING [Telegram] Telegram intake gap: 3 update(s) consumed but never dispatched
        (update_id 1002..1004 missing; last seen 1001, now 1005).
        These were offset-confirmed to Telegram and are unrecoverable.
```

### Why blocking, not `block=False`

A separate handler group already guarantees the sentinel cannot consume an update — PTB runs at most one handler *per group* but runs *every* group. `block=False` would defer the callback to `Application.create_task`, which allows out-of-order observation; for a sequential-id gap detector that **manufactures false alarms**.

This was caught by driving the **real PTB dispatcher** rather than trusting unit fakes: with `block=False` the sentinel never fired at all (the deferred task no-ops when the app isn't running), even though the unit tests were green.

### Reset on reconnect

The high-water mark clears on each new polling generation. A session legitimately starts at an arbitrary offset (cold boot uses `drop_pending_updates=True`; a reconnect replays a backlog), so carrying it across would emit a false gap on the first update after a reconnect.

## Single registration site

Handler registration was duplicated verbatim between initial connect and the rebuild-on-retry path, so every new handler had to be remembered in **two** places or silently exist on only one. The sentinel would have been a fresh instance of that bug. Both paths now call `_register_handlers`, and a structural test asserts they share the one site and that the sentinel keeps its ordering guarantees.

## Verification

- **Tests proven RED first** — `AttributeError` on the absent sentinel against unfixed code, then green.
- **8 new tests**: attribution, gap detection with exact missing range, no false positive on a contiguous stream, no gap on a session's first update, duplicate/reordered redelivery tolerance, malformed-update tolerance, generation reset, and the structural single-site guard.
- **Live dispatch proof** through a real `telegram.ext.Application`: sentinel logged every update, fired the WARNING naming `1002..1004`, and the functional handlers still received all three updates (`[1000, 1001, 1005]`) — proving it observes without consuming.
- `633 passed, 1 skipped` across the gateway Telegram suite; `ruff` clean.

Six failures in `tests/test_telegram_polling_progress_ptb.py` appear only in a combined run and reproduce identically on clean `main` with this branch stashed and the new test file removed — pre-existing mock pollution (the `telegram` MagicMock other gateway tests install leaks into the real-PTB tests), untouched by this change.

author: volodymyrkhrystynych
body:
## Context

Production runs as the `systemd --user` unit `lunaschal.service` (`ops/run-prod.sh`, `Type=exec`), so all app output goes to the user journal. Until now the only way to read it was an SSH session and `journalctl --user -u lunaschal` — from the phone or the Pocket 2, no visibility at all.

The recent newspapers confusion is the motivating example: a sync that looked like it was "failing" was actually just frontpages.com serving a day-old edition, and `already-saved 2026-08-25` was sitting right there in the journal the whole time.

## What this adds

A **Logs** tab in Settings (next to General / Tags / Shortcuts) that reads four fixed `systemd --user` journals over the existing authenticated API:

- Unit picker: **App server / llama.cpp / Deploy watcher / Backup job**
- Time window (15 min … 3 days), line count (200–2000)
- Client-side severity filter, text search, **"Hide requests"** toggle (on by default — the raw journal is mostly werkzeug access-log spam)
- **Auto-refresh** toggle (polls every 5s, off by default), manual Refresh, Copy
- Priority colouring; tail-follow scroll unless you scroll up

Degrades to `available: false` with a muted note under a bare shell with no user bus — same pattern as the Backup panel.

## Files

| Path | Role |
|---|---|
| `backend/ops/journal_logs.py` | Pure parser + `journalctl` argv builder. Unit from a fixed allowlist, `lines`/`priority` coerced to int, `since` from a preset map — **request input never reaches the command line**. Handles journald's byte-array `MESSAGE` form; strips ANSI/control chars. |
| `backend/routes/logs.py` | `GET /api/logs` + `GET /api/logs/units`; subprocess + graceful-degrade helper copied from `routes/backup.py`. |
| `backend/app.py` | Blueprint registration. |
| `src/lib/serverLogs.ts` | Severity/search/hide-requests filtering, priority metadata, timestamp formatting. |
| `src/components/Settings/LogsPanel.tsx` | The tab. |
| `src/components/Settings/index.tsx`, `src/hooks/api.ts` | Wiring. |

## Security

Endpoints sit behind the existing `check_auth` — in network mode a logged-in session is required, same as every `/api/*` route. Logs can contain client IPs / request paths; acceptable for a single-user app the owner is already authenticated into. No shell injection surface: unit via a dict lookup, numbers coerced, `since` via a preset-key lookup.

## Tests

- `backend/tests/test_ops_journal_logs.py` (13) — string + byte-array messages, ANSI stripping, timestamp/priority parsing, malformed-line skipping, argv clamping, `since`/`priority` gating, access-log detection.
- `backend/tests/test_routes_logs.py` (7) — parse-in-order, unknown unit → 400, unavailable → `available: false`, `lines` clamp reaches the argv, `/units` shape.
- `src/lib/serverLogs.test.ts` (13) — filter combinations, access-log regex, tz-independent timestamp formatting, priority-metadata completeness.

Full frontend suite (1439) green; production build clean. Verified against the live production journal.

## 가장 큰 것

**`audit.sh`가 무슨 일이 있어도 exit 0이었다.** ❌를 찍기만 하고 세지 않았고 파일 끝에 `exit`이 없었다. `js/prompts.js`에 문법 오류를 넣어도 `npm run audit`은 성공으로 끝났다. 셈해서 그걸로 끝낸다.

| 검사 | 무엇이 통과했나 |
|---|---|
| 폐지 목록 | 한글 이름만 막고 있었다 — `landmine` / `undisclosed` / `read the room` / `sense the air`로 되살리면 통과 |
| 점수 축 차단 | 대문자만 잡았다 — `"the love score is climbing"`은 통과 |
| 한글 검사 | 안 짓는 가지가 넷 (주문 없음 · 마지막 구간 · 앞대화 있음) + 스키마를 아예 안 봤다 |
| R 격리 | `reactSystem`에 애초에 그 인자가 없어 부정 단언이 항상 참이었다 |

| A는 타겟 안 봄 | `system`만 보고 user 절반을 안 봤다 |
| 노출 라벨 둘 | `label`과 `en`이 **같아도** 통과 |

스키마도 프롬프트다 — 구조화 출력이 막히면 `js/llm.js`의 `withSchemaInstruction`이 스키마를 시스템 프롬프트에 통째로 붙인다. 한글 검사가 스키마도 훑도록 넓혔고, `PROP_SCHEMA`의 한글 예시(`폭탄 / 후광`)를 영어로 옮겼다.

body:
The classify road stands on one claim: an assignment nothing can query is not a
classification, which is why every filing on the task side is looked for through
`dim:<axis>=<value>` rather than read off a field. The decision half was written
before decisions could be queried that way, so it read its filing off the
decision's own page — the one place the claim was not being made.

It now asks the same question in the same grammar: found under the value it was
filed under, absent from the other, and after the filing is taken off, absent
from the value and standing in `=none` — which is what says the decision is
unfiled rather than gone.

author: tylerecouture
body:
### What?

Campaigns only trade places with the campaigns they stand beside, so a map whose intro campaign leads into parallel paths stops drawing those paths on top of each other.

Closes #2627

### Why?

`orderCampaignColumns()` in `maps.js` (added for #1977) permutes campaigns among the x positions dagre gave them, sorted by `(map_order, smallest quest id)`. It treats those positions as interchangeable slots. They are not.

dagre widens a slot for whatever competes with it **at the same ranks**. Two campaigns standing side by side get slots spaced to fit them both; a campaign in a vertical band of its own gets its x for free, with room on either side that nothing else needs. Handing that solitary slot to one of a side-by-side pair puts it closer to its neighbour than a node is wide, and the two are drawn over each other for their whole height.

Measured on a map shaped like the reported one, an intro campaign of four quests feeding two campaigns of eleven. Campaign boxes are 222 px wide:

| | Side Scroller | Top Down | overlap |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| with the reorder | x[148, 369] | x[286, 507] | **83 x 550 px** |
| with the reorder removed | x[9, 231] | x[286, 507] | none |

It happens at the **default** `map_order` too. Ties fall back to the smallest quest id, the intro campaign holds the smallest of all, so it sorts into the leftmost slot and displaces a path into the middle slot, which only existed because the intro campaign sat above the others.

**The #1787 duplicate intra-campaign edges are not involved.** Rendering with those removed, with `orderCampaignColumns` removed, and with both removed gives identical geometry; only removing the reorder clears the overlap. So this is not a case for reverting both recent changes.

### How?

Campaigns are grouped into rows whose quests share vertical space, by sweeping their extents, and only campaigns within a row trade places. Every swap then stays inside a set of slots dagre did size to fit those campaigns, and `map_order` keeps working between the campaigns that actually stand beside each other, which is what #1977 asked for.

Grouping reads the **quests'** own extent rather than the campaign box's: the box adds padding that dips into the band below, which would merge two rows of slots into one and reintroduce the bug.

Everything else is unchanged. The set of x positions, each campaign's internal shape, every node's vertical position (the #1787 stacking) and the re-centring of campaign-less connector nodes all behave as before.

### Testing

Full suite green (2898 tests), plus `ruff check src`, `manage.py check` and `makemigrations --check --dry-run`.

Three new tests in `djcytoscape/tests/test_map_order_render.py`, which drives the real vendored cytoscape/dagre and the real `maps.js` in headless Chromium. They render an intro campaign feeding two paths and assert no two campaign boxes intersect, at the default `map_order` and at four different orderings, plus one asserting the two paths still swap by `map_order` between themselves.

Measured against the code with only the row grouping removed, so they fail for the reason they name:

```
FAIL: test_campaign_columns__do_not_overlap_at_the_default_map_order
AssertionError: Lists differ: ['Path A and Path B overlap by 84x150 px'] != []
FAIL: test_campaign_columns__do_not_overlap_when_map_order_reorders_them (orders=(1, 2, 3))
AssertionError: Lists differ: ['Path A and Path B overlap by 84x150 px'] != []
```

The five existing `map_order` render tests still pass, and they really run here rather than skipping (`Ran 8 tests ... OK`), so the #1977 behaviour is intact.

### Screenshots (if front end is affected)

Rendered through the real `maps.js` and the vendored cytoscape/dagre, on a map shaped like the reported one.

**Before:** the two paths are drawn over each other, each column's quest names clipped by the other column's boxes, and "2D Top Down Path" rotated and buried between the columns.

![Quest map with the 2D Side Scroller and 2D Top Down columns overlapping, quest names clipped mid-word](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bytedeck/bytedeck/pr-assets/2627/before.png)

**After:** the two paths sit in their own columns, every quest name readable and each campaign name legible down its left edge.

![The same map with the two paths cleanly separated side by side](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bytedeck/bytedeck/pr-assets/2627/after.png)

`maps.js`'s cache-buster in `quest_map.html` goes to `?v=1.2`, so people who have the old file cached get this.

### Anything Else?

**Visible in both screenshots, not fixed here.** A campaign box's padding dips about 34 px into the vertical band below it, so a campaign sitting above another clips the top of it slightly (the "Game Analysis and Design" label crossing the first path node). It is independent of this bug, present with the reorder removed as well, and comes from `rankSep: 15` being smaller than the compound node's padding. Raising `rankSep` would fix it and would also re-space every map vertically, so it wants its own change and its own look. Happy to open an issue if you want it tracked.

### Review request
@tylerecouture

- Claude Code (`bytedeck - single session`)

author: vburenin
body: Honor Panel option **Reverse files only** (`panel_opts.reverse_files_only`, default **true**) during panel sort. ## Behavior When directories-first is on (`dirs_first == true`, i.e. Mix all files is off) and the panel sort direction is reverse: - **true** (default): directories stay sorted **ascending** by name; only the file group is reversed. - **false**: both the directory group and the file group reverse. When Mix all files is on (`dirs_first == false`), reverse applies to the whole mixed list either way (the flag does not split groups). `..` stays first. ## Files - `crates/rmc-core/src/panel.rs` — `apply_sort_with(reverse_files_only)`; `apply_sort()` remains a default-true wrapper. `set_entries` / `set_panelized_entries` thread the flag the same way. - `crates/rmc-core/src/app.rs` — `reload_panels`, `change_dir`, `handle_action(Sort(_))`, and `panelize_paths` pass `app.panel_opts.reverse_files_only`. Comment on `PanelOptions.reverse_files_only` updated (no longer store-only). Did not touch `render.rs`, `terminal.rs`, or PR #13. ## Tests `reverse_files_only_dirs_first` in `panel.rs`: dirs-first + reverse + flag true → `..`, `a`, `b`, `z`, `y`; flag false → `..`, `b`, `a`, `z`, `y`.

author: blackest21
body:
두 가지 변경을 함께 담는다.

---

## 1. 가짜 '연계전공' 요건 행 40개 제거 (`scripts/remove_spurious_interdisciplinary_backfill.py`)

### 무엇을

`graduation_requirements`에서 `program_type='interdisciplinary'`(연계전공)로 잘못 만들어진 요건 행 **40개**를 삭제했다 (gr#335~374). 삭제 스크립트를 커밋한다. Supabase에는 `--apply`로 이미 반영 완료.

**학과·전공(`departments`/`majors`)은 하나도 안 건드렸다.** 사회학과·경영학과 등의 진짜 `primary`/`minor`/`dual` 요건 행도 전부 그대로다 — 그 위에 중복으로 얹혀 있던 `interdisciplinary` 행만 제거.

### 왜

`backfill_sw_convergence_rules.py`가 `program_courses`를 `(department_id, major_id, curriculum_year)`로 묶어서 그룹이 하나라도 있으면 무조건 `program_type='interdisciplinary'` 요건 행을 만들었다. 실제 SW연계전공 5개(빅데이터/산업수학SW/에너지IoT/임베디드SW/산업AI, `required_total_credits=48`로 정상 시딩)에는 맞지만, **부전공(minor) 시딩이 이미 있던 일반 학과 40곳**(사회학과·심리학과·경영학과·국어국문학과·정보컴퓨터공학부 3개 전공 등)에도 똑같이 적용돼, 그 학과의 부전공 `program_courses`를 그대로 재사용한 가짜 "연계전공" 요건 행이 생겼다.

### 오류라는 근거 (3단계)

1. **학사규정 원문**(`raw_data/manual_staging/05_minor_dual_programs/_source_학사규정_2026-08-10.md`)의 "연계전공" 절은 정확히 **10개 지정 프로그램**만 나열한다. 사회학과·경영학과·컴퓨터공학전공 등은 이 목록에 없다 — 일반 학과 전체가 연계전공 대상이 되는 제도가 아니다.
2. **경영학과로 직접 대조**: 진짜 부전공 요건은 `{"groups":[{"n":3,"type":"min_courses","label":"택3/9"}],"total_credits":21}`, 문제의 백필 행은 `{"groups":[{"type":"all","label":"택3/9"}]}`(규칙 타입도 틀리고 `total_credits`도 없음). 참조하는 8개 과목은 완전히 동일(전부 경영학과 자체 개설분). 사람이 조사한 부전공 데이터를 프로그램 타입만 바꿔 기계 복제한 것.
3. `program_type='interdisciplinary'`인 `UserAcademicProgram`은 회원가입 폼이 아니라 `/me/tracks/enroll`(AI융합트랙 전용)로만 생성되고, 그 행들은 AI융합트랙 14개(`required_total_credits=21`)를 가리켜 이 40개 backfill 행과 키가 안 겹친다. 40개 행에 걸린 실제 `UserAcademicProgram`도 전부 0건 — 지워도 영향받는 실사용자 없음.

### 어떻게

스크립트는 세 조건을 **모두** 만족하는 행만 대상으로 한다:
- `program_type = 'interdisciplinary'`
- `required_total_credits IS NULL` (진짜 SW연계전공 5개는 48로 채워져 있어 제외됨)
- `special_rules.notes == 'SW융합 라벨 자동 파싱 (backfill)'`

삭제 직전 해당 `(department_id, major_id, program_type='interdisciplinary')`로 등록된 실사용자를 한 번 더 조회해서 1건이라도 있으면 SKIP하는 안전장치 포함. 기본은 dry-run, `--apply`로만 실제 삭제.

### 검증

- dry-run/apply 모두 정확히 40개 대상, SKIP(실사용자 있음) 0건.
- `pytest -q` → 738 passed, 101 subtests passed.
- `tests/run_golden_tests.py` → TC01~TC11 전부 PASS.
- 삭제 후 확인: `required_total_credits IS NULL`인 backfill-note `interdisciplinary` 행 **0개**. 남은 `interdisciplinary` 행은 전부 정상(SW융합트랙 인증 14개 `=21`, 진짜 SW연계전공 5개 `=48`, 핀테크융합전공 1개 `=42`).
- 독립 리뷰(격리 worktree, 정적 분석) → **APPROVE WITH NITS**. nit 2건(docstring 표현 정확도, `run()` 반환 카운트) 후속 커밋으로 반영. 필터/안전장치 자체는 결함 없음, 정당한 행이 잡히거나 orphan이 생기는 경로 없음 확인.

### 이 변경이 다루지 않는 것

학사규정 연계전공 10개 중 우리 DB에 아예 없는 5개(의생명과학전공·통합사회전공·통합과학전공·차량용AI반도체·탄소중립바이오기술)와, `graduation_requirements`가 비어 있는 융합전공 여러 개(반도체융합전공·DX융합전공·그린바이오융합전공·미래도시건축환경융합전공 등)는 별도 데이터 수집 과제로 남긴다.

---

## 2. AI 활용 문서 정확도 개선 (`docs/ai-usage.md`)

- 근거를 robust하게 대기 어려운 수치 주장 제거: "gpt-4o-mini 대비 정답률 +24%p, 지연시간 -30%" 비교 표 → "골든 평가의 도구 호출 성공률·시나리오 충족·지연시간을 함께 검토해 기본값 설정", "LLM 응답은 확률적이므로 단일 실행/단일 지표로 우열을 단정하지 않는다"로 교체.
- 골든 시나리오 개수 표기 `TC01~TC09` → `TC01~TC11` (현재 실제 개수와 일치).
- 주간 골든 평가는 품질 추이 관찰용이며 자동 병합 차단 기준이 아님을 명시(실제 CI 설정과 일치).
- Figma/Notion MCP 서술을 "필요 시 선택적으로 조회, 적용 전 화면·코드·최신 결정과 재대조"로 톤 조정.
- 규모 자랑성 문구("수백 건의 PR…") 제거, 사람이 담당한 범위(문제 정의·규칙 설계·데이터 출처 확인·최종 승인) 명시.

## Q&A

**Q. 뭐가 문제였나?**
A. (1) `backfill_sw_convergence_rules.py`가 `program_courses` 그룹만 보고 기계적으로 연계전공 요건 행을 찍어내는 바람에, 부전공 시딩이 있던 일반 학과 40곳에 실제로 존재하지 않는 "연계전공" 이수요건이 생겼다. (2) `docs/ai-usage.md`에 재현·검증이 어려운 성능 수치와 골든 개수 오표기가 있었다.

**Q. 바꾸면 뭐가 달라지나?**
A. 존재하지 않는 프로그램의 잘못된 이수요건 40개가 DB에서 사라진다(실사용자 0명이라 사용자 노출 동작 변화 없음, 향후 연계전공 판정/추천이 가짜 행에 걸릴 위험만 제거). 진짜 SW연계전공 5개·핀테크융합전공·SW융합트랙 인증 행은 유지. 문서는 실측으로 뒷받침되는 서술만 남긴다.

author: mikalstill
body:
Every code finding from the `PLAN-idle-cpu-and-latency` push audit that
was agreed for fixing. The audit's *harness* findings are #325; the plan
and the decision record are #326.

## The structural one, and the bug it found

62 event sends across the seven channel handlers were each hand-followed
by `repaint_notify.notify_one()`, with nothing coupling them. A channel
event added without the notify would silently stop the UI updating for
that event — no error, no test failure, just a UI that quietly stops
refreshing on one message type.

`EventSink` now owns the sender and the `Notify` together and emits both.
Each channel struct loses its `event_tx`/`repaint_notify` pair for one
sink. The whole renderer now contains **exactly one `notify_one()` call**
— the one inside `EventSink::emit`.

**This found a bug the audit missed.** Three separate judgment agents
enumerated these call sites and all three reported the pairing complete.
The counts on `develop`:

```
send_event calls in main_channel.rs:  15
notify_one calls in main_channel.rs:  11
```

`main_channel.rs:1126` and `:1133` emit `AgentConnected(true)` and
`AgentConnected(false)` with no notification at all. The UI did not
repaint when the guest agent connected or disconnected until the 1 Hz
fallback next fired. Bounded to a second of staleness, so low severity —
but real, and exactly the failure mode this change makes unwriteable.
Three independent enumerations agreeing did not make the claim true.

## Filing a bug report no longer freezes the window

`BugReport::new()` sleeps 2 s to sample per-thread CPU. On the interactive
path that ran on the egui UI thread — which is also the only consumer of
the bounded 1024-event channel, so a full channel then back-pressured
every SPICE read loop. The sample now runs on a named thread with the UI
polling for it.

Two corrections worth recording:

- **The audit's suggested fix would have panicked.** It recommended
  `tokio::task::spawn_blocking`, copying the two call sites that already
  use it. But `eframe::run_native` is called outside any tokio runtime,
  and every runtime in the GUI build is created inside a
  `std::thread::spawn` — there is none on the UI thread to spawn onto.
  `PLAN-bugreport-trigger-snapshot-phase-02-snapshot.md:422` already
  spelled out the right pattern for this side: *"use
  `std::thread::Builder`, not `tokio::spawn_blocking`"*.
- **Two things the finding did not mention.** Nothing prevented a second
  bug report starting while the first was sampling — all three submit
  paths clear the dialog state immediately, so F12 was live again at once.
  And deferring the report by 2 s would have cropped
  `screenshot-region.png` from a frame two seconds *after* the user drew
  the region. Both handled.

The false comment justifying the blocking sample as "gated on a file
dialog" is deleted — `generate_bug_report` resolves `--bug-report-dir`,
`<capture>/bug-reports/`, or `current_dir()`. There is no dialog.

## The status bar no longer overclaims

It said `Latency:` for the interval between server PINGs — a number the
server alone chooses. A compromised server could make it read flat while
the link stalled. It now says **PING interval**, matching what
`docs/diagnostics.md` already said. The `ChannelEvent` variant, the
`sample_ms` field and the bug-report JSON key are unchanged.

The sample is now emitted *after* `Ping::read()` validates the payload and
*after* the PONG is written, so a truncated PING produces no sample and a
stalled UI cannot sit in front of a keepalive reply.

## Linux metrics gets the guards its macOS twin already had

The macOS path clamps its sample window, sorts with a total order, and has
a zero-window regression test. The Linux path it was modelled on had none
of them: an unguarded `window_secs` divisor yields NaN, and
`partial_cmp().unwrap_or(Equal)` over NaN is a non-total order that Rust's
sort can panic on. Fixed with `total_cmp` plus an ascending-`tid`
tie-break, which also makes the JSON independent of `readdir` order.

The delta arithmetic is extracted as a pure `diff_snapshots()` so it can be
tested without sleeping, and the PING interval likewise as
`ping_interval_ms()`. Seven new tests, none of which sleep.

## Smaller items

- The `SAFETY` comment on the `sysconf` call justified it with
  async-signal-safety — which concerns reentrancy from signal handlers and
  says nothing about Rust's `unsafe` obligations. Rewritten to state the
  real invariant.
- `libc` was a **dead** dependency in `ryll` (zero `libc::` references
  remain) and an ungated one in the renderer, where it is used on Linux
  *and* macOS. Deleted from the former, gated `cfg(any(linux, macos))` in
  the latter. The audit's original `cfg(target_os = "linux")` suggestion
  would have broken the macOS build.

## Verification

794 tests pass, up from 787. `pre-commit run --all-files` clean,
`make lint` clean.

Declined findings and their reasons are recorded in the master plan in
#326.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: alexzihaoxu
body:
`PROTECTED_TOP` omitted three names anvil itself reserves, so a manifest item could target them.

## The hole

`PROTECTED_TOP` was `{.anvil, .anvilignore, saves}` and did not include `anvil.toml` (`MANIFEST_FILENAME`), `anvil.lock` (`LOCK_FILENAME`) or `.anvilexclude` (`EXCLUDE_FILE`). An item declaring `path = "./anvil.toml"` passed `declaredPlacementTarget` and reached `journaledSwap` as an ordinary link target — **a build could overwrite the instance's own manifest, lock, or exclude rules with package content.**

## Why the tests could not catch it

`test/security/local-placement-traversal.test.ts` tested placement refusal for exactly the three names in `PROTECTED_TOP`. **The test set and the constant were written from the same list**, so the omission was invisible: a check that cannot fail for the case it exists to catch.

This is demonstrated, not asserted. Emptying the constant with the new tests kept fails 4 of 23 — **and the pre-existing "REFUSES a protected top-level target" test still passes.**

## Widening the existing constant would have been a regression

Every call site was checked rather than assumed, and two of them cannot take the wider set:

- `safeJoin` (`internal/fs.ts`) **also runs on VC checkout** — `materializeSnapshot` joins every tracked and carried path through it.
- `WorktreeExclusion.excludes` governs what VC records and materializes.

Measured with a probe: `WorktreeExclusion.excludes(".anvilexclude") === false` — it is an **ordinary tracked file today**. In `PROTECTED_TOP` it would stop being recorded in commits, stop being materialized on switch, and make `safeJoin` throw on every checkout of a commit that tracks one. (`anvil.toml` and `anvil.lock` were already excluded via `SNAPSHOT_SLOTS`; only `.anvilexclude` actually breaks — which is enough.)

So this adds `ANVIL_RESERVED_TOP` and `isPlacementRefusedTop` (the union), applied **only** to placement-declaring surfaces — `place.ts`, `anvilignore.ts`, `mrpack.ts`, `pack-common.ts`, `mrpack-base.ts`. `safeJoin` and `WorktreeExclusion` keep the narrow set.

## The test enumerates independently of the constant

Cases are spelled from `MANIFEST_FILENAME`, `LOCK_FILENAME` and `EXCLUDE_FILE`, imported from where those filenames are actually decided, plus literals for the three with no defining constant. **Nothing iterates either constant.** `internal/fs.ts` sits below those layers and cannot import them without a cycle, so the constant holds literals — and a drift test asserts it equals exactly the set built from the three sources. Rename `anvil.toml` upstream and this goes red instead of the reserved set silently narrowing.

## LB-721, folded in

**Unreachable snapshot object.** The dirty check `put` a comparison snapshot nothing would ever reference. Control: reverting it reads `expected 6 to be 5` — exactly one leaked object per refused switch.

**Windows reserved device names.** `CON`, `NUL`, `PRN`, `AUX`, `COM1`–`COM9`, `LPT1`–`LPT9` now refuse at decode time. Matching is case-insensitive and extension-bearing (`con.txt` reserved, `CONSOLE` not), tested on both sides of that boundary.

⚠️ **Scope decision, flagged deliberately: it also refuses at build time.** Decode-only is a trap — `getSnapshot` decodes local objects through the same path a remote's arrive on, so a Linux user could commit `mods/con.txt` and then be unable to read back their own history. This mirrors `trackedPathCollision`, already refused in both places for the same reason. The cost is that a Linux user with a legitimately-named `aux.json` can no longer commit it; that is the intended trade, and the one anvil already makes for case-colliding paths.

## Verification

`tsc --noEmit` and `biome` clean. Full suite **95 files / 715 tests** (was 94 / 704). Three negative controls, each reported with its failure count and message.

## Out of scope, named not fixed

`carried` paths get no device-name check — only `tracked` is screened, and `declaredPlacementTarget` keeps a declared path verbatim, so a pack shipping `config/con.toml` could still fail mid-materialize on Windows. Refusing it would reject packs that work today, so it needs its own decision. Also: `buildSnapshot` still `put`s three slot blobs during a dirty check, and `prism.ts:232`'s `isProtectedTop(dir)` is dead code.

Closes LB-734, LB-721

body:
## Result

Block 208 proves bounded **typed compiler support** on the fixed H1 fixture.

The reproduced local Clifford cell is a strict CPTP/unital qubit Choi operator
in both conjugate realifications and, at `c=5/13`, also one effect of a strict
binary POVM.  As a channel it is reciprocal; as a typed two-leg effect its
ordered contrast is exactly `-(65/313) sin(Delta)`.

A normalized, proper-cubic-covariant 36-outcome endpoint CP instrument recovers
the complete relative central phase from labeled outcome rates, without a
`p/q` argument to the law.  It conditionally reconstructs the complete fixed
H1 forward and literal actual-reverse sources at grouped rank `18/18`, atom
rank `136/136`, and zero exact residual in both realifications, while separating
the same-`q`, different-`p` collision at rank/nonzeros `12/56`.

A normalized 12-outcome displaced CP relay with componentwise scores closes
the four missing temporal groups.  An independent construction of the target
as full raw source minus all 14 spatial columns gives forward and actual-
reverse designs of shape `128 x 4`, rank/augmented rank `4/4`, residual zero,
and the registered `1/8` witness.

## Boundary and TOE effect

This is not complete H1 physical ownership.  The 36 prepared one-qubit output
states are distinct but full-rank and every pair overlaps, so they are not 36
perfectly distinguishable Records.  The action-to-`M2` state solder, physical
typing of the cell legs, sharpness/output/radial selection, readable outcome
register or quotient, and attachment of displaced branches to blank-to-locked
permanent framework Records remain open.  The host still supplies the time
coordinate, branch routing and incoming/outgoing carrier.

Sharp and `u=1/2` unsharp laws give different same-input distributions but the
same calibrated H1 statistic, while equivariance and right-inverse constraints
leave a two-parameter radial-section family.  Neither law is physically
complete, so the axiom-update threshold is not met.  H2, formation/history,
retained status, formal obligation retirement and TOE percentage movement
remain open/zero; lane scores do not move.

## Review surfaces

- [Bounded theorem note](https://github.com/jonathonreilly/qubit-lattice-axiom-framework/blob/physics-loop/toe-axiom-closure-block208-two-time-clifford-schur-m2-compiler-20260826/docs/ADMISSIBILITY_D4_H1_TWO_TIME_CLIFFORD_CELL_M2_RECORD_COMPILER_BOUNDARY_BOUNDED_THEOREM_NOTE_2026-08-26.md)

- [Assumptions/imports](https://github.com/jonathonreilly/qubit-lattice-axiom-framework/blob/physics-loop/toe-axiom-closure-block208-two-time-clifford-schur-m2-compiler-20260826/.claude/science/physics-loops/toe-axiom-closure-block208-two-time-clifford-schur-m2-compiler-20260826/ASSUMPTIONS_AND_IMPORTS.md)
- [Adversarial relay/type check](https://github.com/jonathonreilly/qubit-lattice-axiom-framework/blob/physics-loop/toe-axiom-closure-block208-two-time-clifford-schur-m2-compiler-20260826/.claude/science/physics-loops/toe-axiom-closure-block208-two-time-clifford-schur-m2-compiler-20260826/ADVERSARIAL_RELAY_TYPE_CHECK.md)
- [Panel and cluster cap](https://github.com/jonathonreilly/qubit-lattice-axiom-framework/blob/physics-loop/toe-axiom-closure-block208-two-time-clifford-schur-m2-compiler-20260826/.claude/science/physics-loops/toe-axiom-closure-block208-two-time-clifford-schur-m2-compiler-20260826/PANEL_RETURN.md)

The user explicitly disabled `review-loop`; it was not used.  No audit verdict,
minimal-axiom edit, registry edit, ledger edit or governance edit is authored.
N1--N8 is complete in the source note.  The independent cluster-cap evaluator
returned `OPEN, narrowly` only for this bounded labeled-CP/readout-obstruction
claim.

## Verification

- Primary exact runner: `10/10`; all `38/38` mutations rejected.
- Structurally independent checker: `10/10`; all `31/31` nonidentical
  mutations rejected; no primary import.
- Both caches are fresh, content/input-pinned, and declare `120`/`180` second
  timeouts; both cached stdout streams carry exact N5 scope lines.
- Frozen-byte adversarial relay/type check: `PASS with qualifications`; final
  source-note delivery delta: `PASS`, no claim widening.
- Post-result five-role panel: `5/5` typed compiler support, `0/5` complete
  physical ownership.
- Changed-file vocabulary, strict audit lint, repository invariants, enforced
  local links, compilation and diff checks pass.  Strict lint reports only the
  inherited repository warnings/notices.
- Citation topology is `+1` node / `+0` edges relative to the checked-in
  manifest.  The campaign does not author audit/governance metadata; that
  manifest refresh remains audit-lane work.
- The full pipeline passes through effective-status computation and stops at
  stage 7 on the parent stack's inherited dependency-policy epoch mismatch.
  Block 208 changes none of the governed epoch/fingerprint/build/restore files;
  the run was isolated and no generated audit delta is retained.
- Fresh PR check: parent #7746, comparison #7745, and new diagnostic #7747 are
  clean.  #7747 reinforces that a context-independent four-label shortcut is
  unsafe but does not supply the missing physical dilation or Record readout.

## Next campaign

Solve the complete local action-native, proper-cubic-covariant Record-forming
dilation/intertwiner, including state solder, cell-leg typing, selected
instrument/preparation, readable register/quotient and permanent formation.
Compute the image of its complete solution set in readable probability laws,
modulo physical gauge and unreadable relabeling:

- nonempty singleton: complete H1 ownership; open H2;
- two distinct complete same-input laws: axiom-update decision witness;
- empty: falsify this proposed action/dilation family.

author: dustinvtran
body:
Closes #254. #257 did the axios half; this is the rest of the ACCEPTED map. Bootstrap goes 3.3.1 to 3.4.1, bootstrap-table 1.12.1 to 1.21.2, jQuery 1.11.1 to 1.12.2. Every one of the five urls has its `integrity` recomputed from the bytes cdnjs actually serves — a wrong hash blocks the file silently, and these five draw the whole page, so all five were checked in a browser rather than trusted.

| package | was | now | advisories |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `bootstrap-table` | 1.12.1 | 1.21.2 | 2 → **0** |
| `bootstrap` | 3.3.1 | 3.4.1 | 7 → 2 |
| `jquery` | 1.11.1 | 1.12.2 | 3 → 3 |

**bootstrap-table's ceiling is jQuery, not Bootstrap.** The old note said it was pinned to match Bootstrap 3 and so could not move ahead of it. That turns out to be wrong in a way worth writing down: Bootstrap 3 theming survives the entire 1.x line — `getBootstrapVersion` still reads `$.fn.dropdown.Constructor.VERSION` and the `3:` branch of the constants table is still there in 1.27.3, the current release. What actually stops is the jQuery peer range. 1.21.2 is the last release declaring `jquery: "1.9.1 - 3"`; 1.21.3 narrows it to `"3"`. So this pin tracks the jQuery pin above it and can only move again when that one does, which is the opposite of the dependency the old comment described. 1.21.2 also happens to clear both of its own advisories — the moderate is fixed in 1.20.2, the low in 1.19.1 — so its entry is the only one that leaves ACCEPTED.

**That bump changes `customSearch`, which is why `utils/tables.js` is in this diff.** 1.12 read the option as the *name of a global*, called `window[name]` with the table as `this` and the search text as its one argument, and took the surviving rows back off `this.data`. 1.21 takes the function itself, calls it with `(data, searchText, filterColumns)` and `this` bound to the *options* object, and assigns `this.data` from the return value. All three of those moved at once, so the old shape does not degrade into a worse search — it binds `searchText` to an array of rows and then blanks the table by returning `undefined`. The global goes away with the name that was the only reason for it, which is what the now-stale comment in `tables.test.js` was explaining.

One subtlety worth a reviewer's eye: `this.columns` on the options object is the nested `[[column, ...]]` that `initColumns` rewrites the option into, one inner array per header row, and not the flat list of the same objects the table itself keeps — so `freeTextFields` gets `this.columns.flat()`. The column objects are shared between the two shapes, so `visible` is still live and a column the reader unhides through the dropdown becomes searchable the moment it appears. That is the behaviour #228 and the `nolan` bug were about, and it is the specific thing I went looking for in the browser.

**jQuery buys less than the issue assumed, and this is the one decision here worth arguing with.** 1.12.2 is genuinely special: it is the only release on the whole 1.x line where CVE-2015-9251 is fixed, because the fix regressed in 1.12.3 and was not made again until 3.0. The advisory range says so out loud — `<1.12.2 || >=1.12.3 <3.0.0` — which also means 1.12.4, the end of the 1.x line, is strictly worse than what we are replacing. But 1.12.0 is where CVE-2020-11022 *begins*, so this trades one moderate XSS for another and the reported count stays at three. The entry stays in ACCEPTED with that written down. If you would rather not take a lateral move on a page this dependent on jQuery, dropping that one hunk changes nothing else in the branch — bootstrap-table 1.21.2 supports jQuery 1.11 just as happily.

What it does buy, beyond the trade, is that jQuery's own documented workaround for both 11022 and 11023 — reassigning `jQuery.htmlPrefilter` to the identity — cannot be applied at all before 1.12. **I did not attempt the 3.x jump and I think it deserves its own issue.** After this branch, 3.5.0 is the only thing that moves jQuery's number at all, so the choice is between that migration and the `htmlPrefilter` one-liner as an interim; the latter is cheap but needs checking against Bootstrap's and bootstrap-table's own use of self-closing tags, which is more than a version bump.

Bootstrap keeps its entry too, and not for lack of trying: 3.4.1 clears six of the seven, but CVE-2024-6485 (`data-loading-text` in the button plugin) and CVE-2025-1647 (popover and tooltip, reported against 3.4.1 exactly) have **no patched release anywhere on the 3.x line**. They are the floor for as long as the site is on Bootstrap 3, and both need markup this site writes itself to carry an attacker-controlled `data-*`. So this is not a case of 3.4 being behind 3.4.1; there is nothing on 3.x left to move to.

## What I actually looked at

`npx netlify dev` needs a login and points at production Atlas, so I built the site with Eleventy and served `dist/` from a throwaway stub that answers `/.netlify/functions/*` with fixtures. The page is the real `base.njk` and the real bundle pulling the real CDN files; only the data is fake, and nothing touched the database. Checked in a browser, logged out and then as the owner:

- **A logged-out list page** (`/films/nil`) — both sublists draw, sorted by score descending, with the summary-stats line under each. Confirmed in-page that jQuery is `1.12.2`, Bootstrap `3.4.1`, bootstrap-table `1.21.2`, and that all three stylesheets are in `document.styleSheets` with their rules readable, which is what proves the new `integrity` hashes let the files through rather than silently blocking them.
- **The search box** — `director:nolan` filters to the two Nolan films and the sibling table re-searches with it, the query lands in the url as `?q=`, and clearing it restores every row and strips the param. `formatNoMatches` still renders "No matching records found" rather than the abandoned-search message. The migration-critical case: `pacino` matches nothing while the Actors column is hidden, and after unhiding Actors from the Columns dropdown the same text immediately matches Heat — which is the flattened `this.columns` and the live `visible` flag both doing their job.
- **The sublist collapse** — clicking the "Completed" heading hides the table, the comments hint and the summary stats together and marks all three `is-collapsed`; clicking again brings them back with the rows intact. That is jQuery's `.toggle(200)`, so it is really a jQuery 1.12.2 check.
- **The expanded comment panel** — the caret opens a detail row, `expand-row.bs.table` still fires with the detail cell as its fourth argument, `includeReviewIn` reads the `data-review-type` / `data-review-ref` back off the panel, and the note renders through marked and DOMPurify with its headings and emphasis intact.
- **A profile page with its charts** (`/profile/nil`) — the four recent-update tables draw with headers hidden and the page-size cap applied, and the four per-category ApexCharts histograms render at full container width with all eleven buckets. The fifth chart, Global stats, is zero-width because its tab is hidden until clicked, which is also true on `main`.
- **The entry form's date fields** — the edit modal opens populated, and clicking the completed-date field opens litepicker on the right month with the stored date selected.

One honest note, since a reviewer may hit it. On the very first cold-cache load of the profile page I saw all five charts render at `width="0"`, and could not reproduce it on any subsequent load. It is not caused by these bumps: I bisected it by serving `main`'s bundle with each new pin applied alone and then all three together, and the charts render correctly in every combination. The cause is that `ProfileStatsOfType` calls `new ApexCharts(...).render()` synchronously in its initializer, so whatever the container measures at that instant is baked into the SVG — a pre-existing race, not something introduced here. author: bwsalmon
body:
## The bug

`branch_name` is a pure function of the issue number (`grain/issue-{n}`), so a **second run of the same task** — a human re-applying `trigger_label` for another round, or `_restart_commented_completions` doing it for them — pushes to the very branch the first run already opened a PR from. GitHub allows one open PR per head branch and answers the second `create_pull_request` with a `422`.

That 422 propagated straight out of `run_once`, which left the task in the worst state available:

- `in_progress_label` never came off — it is removed *after* the PR step, deliberately, so the issue doesn't look finished with nothing to show
- no `completed_label` went on
- no open-PR record was written, so `_close_finished_prs` never tracked it
- `_requeue` never ran either

So the issue sat marked in-progress indefinitely, with its work sitting in a PR nobody had been told about. This is routine, not an edge case — asking for another round on a task is normal use.

## The fix

It isn't a failure. **A PR tracks its branch**, so the commits this run just pushed are already in the existing PR. On a 422, look the PR up and carry on through the same finish path, recording it exactly as if this run had opened it. The audit line reads `pushed to the branch of existing PR o/r#42` rather than claiming it opened one.

**Only when an open PR for that head actually exists.** 422 is also GitHub's answer to *"No commits between `main` and `grain/issue-5`"* — a real problem whose message is worth keeping — so anything the lookup cannot explain is re-raised untouched.

Adds `GitHubClient.find_open_pull_request_for_branch`, with the `head` filter qualified `owner:branch` and percent-encoded. GitHub silently ignores an unqualified head filter and would otherwise answer with *every* open PR in the repo, whose first entry is some unrelated PR — a test pins the exact query string for that reason.

## Relationship to #124

These compound. #124 stopped `_suggest_fix`'s own comment from restarting a completed task; each spurious restart then re-ran the task and hit this 422. Fixing the restart loop reduces how often this fires, but any legitimate second round would still have hit it.

## Verification

Both reuse tests were confirmed to **fail with the handling removed** (with exactly the reported symptom: `GitHubError: GitHub API error 422`), and the "no existing PR still raises" control to pass either way — so the gate is not over-broad.

Branch merged up to current `main` before pushing. Full suite: 1212 passed, 41 skipped.

author: swiggityswerve
body:
#1385 said the next work was to settle how a co-op encounter becomes a `ServerMatchHost` match, because #1384 had assumed a route it never verified. Traced it — and the honest answer is that **no such route exists today**.

- `launchCoopMission` composes the encounter and hands it to `launchCampaignEncounter`, which has **no multiplayer references at all** — it creates an encounter and a game session, never a match.
- The launch page routes to `campaignEncounterHref(...)` → `/gameplay/encounters/<id>?campaignId=…&missionId=…`, with **no match id**.
- The destination carries no binding to recover one: `encounters/[id].tsx` and every page under `[id]/` (`pre-battle`, `select-force`, `sim`) contain no reference to `matchId`, `multiplayer`, or `coop`.
- The only multiplayer match in the co-op flow is the one `CampaignCoopEntryPanel` POSTs at session start — the **campaign-sync vessel** carrying `coopCampaign`, not a combat engine.

So the co-op unit-ownership question has no host to be asked of. That is almost certainly why `ownsCoopUnit` was never called and why `coopSeats` never needed to leave `composeCoopEncounter`: there is no shared combat host to wire them to. Two co-op players who launch a mission each land on their own local encounter page.

### Stated carefully

This is a negative claim from reading, not execution.

**Established:** the launch path passes no match id; `launchCampaignEncounter` has no multiplayer surface; the destination page tree has no match binding.

**Not established:** that no path whatsoever could produce a shared co-op combat host. I found none, and I searched the launch call chain and the destination tree — but a negative is only as good as the search behind it. Re-run it before treating co-op combat as *unbuilt* rather than merely *unwired*.

Docs only. The two shipped guards stand: cross-side commands are refused for versus matches (#1384), and the co-op exemption (#1385) is correct whether or not anything currently sends those intents.

author: tolkmislk
body:
## Release changes / 发布变更

- promote the backend from `0.4.0-SNAPSHOT` to `0.4.0`
- move all completed v0.4 entries into the dated `2026-08-27` changelog
- preserve an empty `Unreleased` section for continued maintenance
- document the Flyway V2 upgrade boundary
- keep configuration keys and the default Compose workflow unchanged

## Release notes / 发布说明

## Webhook Delivery Platform v0.4.0

v0.4.0 strengthens operator control without weakening accepted-delivery guarantees. Queued work can be canceled safely, state notifications reflect committed data, and Endpoint configuration can evolve while every accepted delivery keeps its original target and signing-secret snapshots.

v0.4.0 在不削弱已接收任务保证的前提下增强运维控制：排队任务可安全取消，状态通知只反映已提交数据；Endpoint 配置可以演进，同时每个已接收任务继续使用原有目标地址与签名密钥快照。

### Delivery lifecycle / 投递生命周期

- Race-safe, idempotent cancellation for `PENDING` and `RETRY_SCHEDULED` work with a stable state-conflict response.
- Bilingual cancellation controls and bounded Prometheus coverage for `CANCELED`.
- SSE state notifications and operator action logs are emitted only after transaction commit.
- Scheduled worker shutdown is coordinated with PostgreSQL integration-test teardown.

- 对 `PENDING` 与 `RETRY_SCHEDULED` 任务提供并发安全、幂等的取消能力，并返回稳定的状态冲突响应。
- 增加中英双语取消控制，以及对 `CANCELED` 的有界 Prometheus 指标覆盖。
- SSE 状态通知与人工操作日志只在事务提交后产生。
- 定时 Worker 会在 PostgreSQL 集成测试清理前有序关闭。

### Immutable configuration snapshots / 不可变配置快照

- Every accepted delivery stores its normalized target URL and encrypted signing-secret snapshot.
- Retries and manual replay keep the accepted snapshot instead of reading mutable Endpoint configuration.
- Endpoint signing-secret rotation uses optimistic versions, returns no secret material, and records metadata-only after-commit audit logs.
- Endpoint name and target-URL updates re-run the complete URL safety policy, reject stale writes, and treat normalized no-ops without version churn.
- Bilingual inline controls explain the old/new delivery boundary before saving or rotating.

- 每个已接收任务都会固化规范化目标 URL 与加密签名密钥快照。
- 重试与人工重投继续使用接收时快照，不读取可变的 Endpoint 实时配置。
- Endpoint 签名密钥轮换使用乐观版本校验，不返回密钥内容，并只在提交后记录元数据审计日志。
- Endpoint 名称与目标 URL 更新会重新执行完整安全策略，拒绝陈旧写入，规范化后的空操作不会增加版本。
- 中英双语内联控制会在保存或轮换前明确说明新旧任务边界。

### Verification / 验证

- 26 backend unit and architecture tests.
- 8 PostgreSQL integration scenarios covering cancellation, transaction-consistent events, immutable targets, and old/new secret or URL behavior.
- Frontend lint, 9 tests, strict TypeScript, and production build.
- OpenAPI lint, Google Java Format, and production dependency audit.
- All feature PRs and the latest post-merge `main` CI passed.

### Security and upgrade / 安全与升级

Flyway migration `V2__snapshot_delivery_target.sql` adds target URL and encrypted signing-secret snapshots to `delivery_job`, backfills existing rows from their Endpoint, and then enforces `NOT NULL`. Back up PostgreSQL before upgrading and allow Flyway to complete before serving traffic. Existing secrets remain encrypted and are never returned or logged.

Flyway 迁移 `V2__snapshot_delivery_target.sql` 会为 `delivery_job` 增加目标 URL 与加密签名密钥快照，从对应 Endpoint 回填已有数据，再施加 `NOT NULL` 约束。升级前请备份 PostgreSQL，并在对外提供服务前等待 Flyway 完成。已有密钥保持加密，且不会被返回或记录。

No configuration key or default Compose workflow changes are required.

无需修改配置键，默认 Compose 使用方式保持不变。

## Verification checklist / 验证清单

- [x] Release diff is one commit, two files, and not behind `main`
- [x] Local frontend lint, 9 tests, TypeScript, production build, OpenAPI lint, and dependency audit
- [x] Release-branch CI ([run #33033750610](https://github.com/TolkmisLK/webhook-delivery-platform/actions/runs/33033750610))
- [x] Post-merge `main` CI ([run #33033881636](https://github.com/TolkmisLK/webhook-delivery-platform/actions/runs/33033881636))
- [x] Tag and [published Release](https://github.com/TolkmisLK/webhook-delivery-platform/releases/tag/v0.4.0) verification

author: simsimhugh
body:
#616 4단계(분석 활용). 3단계(#697)가 쌓아 둔 runbook 지식을 분석이 실제로 쓰게 한다.

## 흐름

```
분석 턴 (원인 확정 — runbook 은 아직 안 보임)
   ↓
[신규] runbook 턴 — 항목이 하나라도 있고 env 가 켜져 있을 때만
   프롬프트: 원인 문장 목록 + 항목별 조치 파일 경로
   모델: 같은 상황이면 그 파일만 Read → 조치 비교 → fix_hint 확정
   서버: 보호 필드 대조 → 통과하면 텍스트 채택 + report.runbook 채움
   ↓
윤문 턴 (기존 그대로 — 이제 runbook 필드는 못 만짐)
```

사람 개입은 없다. 모델이 스스로 훑고, 자기 조치(A)보다 runbook 조치(B)가 정확하면 B 를,
아니면 A 를, 둘 다 필요하면 A+B 를 쓴다.

## 원인 목록만 인라인하고 조치는 파일로 깐다

조치까지 전부 실으면 항목 상한 60 × 조치 상한 4000자 = **24만 자**가 프롬프트를 채워
정작 이번 분석이 뒤로 밀린다. 원인 문장만이면 같은 상한에서 1.2만 자다.

조치는 모델이 **같은 상황이라고 판단한 항목만** `Read` 로 연다. 엔진에 이미 열려 있는
도구라 새 배관이 없고, 윤문 턴이 룰북 파일을 cwd 밖 절대경로로 Read 하는 것과 같은 수법이다.

부수 효과가 하나 붙는데 작지 않다: **무엇을 열어 봤는지가 evidence 타임라인에 남는다**
(목록은 인라인이라 흔적이 없으므로, Read 한 줄이 곧 "같은 상황이라고 봤다"는 신호다).

조치 파일 디렉터리는 분석 워크스페이스 **밖**이다 — 안에 두면 모델이 에러 문자열을 grep 할 때
우리가 깔아 둔 파일이 걸려, 과거 케이스의 문장이 이번 로그의 증거로 둔갑한다.

## 원인은 잠근다 (이 PR 의 핵심 게이트)

이 턴이 바꿀 수 있는 것은 `fix_hint` 와 `runbook` 둘뿐이다. 보호 목록
`_RUNBOOK_PROTECTED_KEYS` (= 공통 뼈대 + `root_cause` + `reasoning_summary`)가 하나라도
달라지면 윤문 턴과 같은 fail-open 으로 **턴 결과를 통째로 버리고** 직전 턴 리포트를 쓴다.

`root_cause` 를 잠그는 것이 존재 이유다 — 열어 두면 runbook 이 지식이 아니라 원인 판단
편향 주입기가 된다. `reasoning_summary` 도 함께 잠근다(근거 서술만 열면 거기에 원인
재해석을 적는 우회로가 생긴다).

부분 채택은 하지 않는다. 필드끼리 맞물려 있어 원인만 되돌리면 A 원인에 B 조치가 붙은
짜깁기가 남는다.

## 관측

`report.runbook = {entry_id, use}` — 서버가 저장소 실존을 검증해 채우고, 모델이 지어낸
id 는 필드 통째로 null 이다(초안 라우트와 같은 규칙).

이력 표에 `runbook 참조` 열을 하나 붙였다. 옆 `runbook` 열과 축이 다르다 — 그쪽은 사람이
적었나, 이쪽은 모델이 참조했나.

| 값 | 뜻 | LLM 호출 |
|---|---|---|
| `runbook` / `own` / `merged` | 모델이 고른 값 **그대로** | 있음 |
| `해당없음` | 돌았는데 같은 상황이 없었음 | 있음 |
| `미실행` | 항목 0개 · inconclusive | 없음 |
| `미채택(사유)` | 게이트가 턴을 버림 | 있음 |
| `꺼짐` | env | 없음 |

성사 값 세 개가 리포트 필드와 **같은 글자**인 것은 계약이다 — 화면용 한국어 어휘를 따로
두면 두 벌이 갈라져, 표에서 거른 값과 리포트가 말하는 값이 서로 다른 것을 가리킨다
(`등록됨`·`미등록` 과 같은 규약). 테스트가 대조한다.

`own` 이 곧 "그 항목이 낡았다"는 신호다 — 그것만 걸러 훑는 것이 이 열의 존재 이유다.

## 구현 중 잡힌 고장

보호 목록을 `(*_POLISH_PROTECTED_KEYS, ...)` 로 파생시켰더니, 윤문용으로 잠근 `runbook`
키를 runbook 턴이 물려받아 **자기 필드를 못 바꿔 매번 통째로 기각**됐다. 공통 뼈대
(`_TURN_PROTECTED_KEYS`)에서 각 턴이 자기 필드만 빼고 더하는 구조로 고쳤고,
`test_each_turn_leaves_its_own_field_open` 이 재발을 막는다.

## 함께 정리한 것

초안 라우트(3단계)와 runbook 턴이 각자 `60` 을 들고 "같은 값"이라는 주석만 달고 있었다.
상한을 저장소(`runbook.MAX_PROMPT_KEYS`) 한 곳으로 모았다.

## env

`MACRO_LOGBOT_RUNBOOK_TURN` — 기본 켜짐, `0/false/no/off` 로만 끈다(윤문 턴 규약 복제).
항목이 0개면 애초에 안 돈다.

## 검증

- 전체 스위트 2956 통과 · ruff check/format · mypy strict · 누출 게이트 · 셸 테스트
- 신규 테스트 24개 (`tests/test_agent_runbook_turn.py`)
- **실측은 아직이다.** 프롬프트가 모델을 원하는 대로 움직이는지는 테스트가 답하지 못한다 —
  배포 뒤 `runbook 참조` 열로 `미채택(보호 필드 변경)` 빈도와 `해당없음` 비율을 본다.
- 선행 조건: `.macro-logbot-runbook` 마운트가 실제로 붙어 있어야 한다. 안 붙어 있으면
  항목이 0개라 이 턴은 조용히 `미실행` 만 찍는다.

author: ex4cto
body:
## Qué

Al terminar un flujo del bot (p.ej. eliminar un freelancer y confirmar), los botones inline del mensaje anterior quedaban colgados y presionables, y el usuario creía que aún funcionaban. Este PR agrega el cierre limpio de flujos y lo aplica al grupo **Administración** (freelancers).

Es el **PR-1** de 2. PR-2 llevará el mismo patrón a **Tours** y **Gestión de ventas** (reusando el helper ya construido aquí).

## Causa raíz

En python-telegram-bot los botones inline no desaparecen solos: hay que editar el mensaje para quitarles el `reply_markup`. Los flujos de freelancers/tours/gestión respondían con `reply_text` (mensaje nuevo) sin editar el viejo, dejando los botones. (Los flujos de venta y egreso ya lo hacían bien vía `_enviar_salida`/`_reply`.)

## Cambios

**Foundation (reutilizable):**
- `menu.py`: `render_submenu(grupo, tier)` — submenú del grupo como comandos clicables (excluye `/cancelar`) + hint de `/start`. No usa botones inline (evita reintroducir el problema).
- `handlers.py`: `finalizar_flujo(update, context, mensaje_final, grupo)` — limpia el teclado del mensaje tapeado, envía el mensaje final, muestra el submenú del grupo + `/start`, y retorna `END`.

**Grupo Administración (freelancers):**
- `nuevo_freelancer`, `eliminar_freelancer` (el reportado), `editar_freelancer` — terminales (éxito y cancelación) ahora usan `finalizar_flujo`.
- `catalogo.py`: nueva clave `freelancer.edicion_finalizada`.

## Estándares

- **TDD**: `test_menu.py` (render_submenu) + `test_finalizar_flujo.py` (11 tests nuevos), RED→GREEN.
- Suite **2483 passed**, `mypy --strict` limpio, ruff limpio. Commits atómicos por work-unit.

## Verificación en vivo (post-merge)

Eliminar un freelancer y confirmar → los botones de la lista deben desaparecer, sale el mensaje de confirmación + submenú de Administración + `/start`.

author: exactmike
body:
Closes #698

## What changed

- Ask for `MESSAGES` in the per-folder `STATUS` that already runs, and use it as
  the deletion detector CONDSTORE would otherwise provide.
- Resolve each mailbox's enumeration plan once, before the label map is built:
  skip mailboxes whose `UIDVALIDITY`, `UIDNEXT` and message count all match the
  stored baseline; enumerate from `prior.UIDNext` when `UIDNEXT` advanced and
  the merged UID set still matches the count; fall back to full enumeration
  otherwise. Both the label map and the message listing consume that one plan,
  so they cannot disagree about what changed.
- Publish an explicit no-op delta for a skipped mailbox instead of omitting it.
  `applyIMAPMailboxDeltas` derives the current topology from the delta list
  alone, and `retireAbsentIMAPMailboxes` deletes the memberships of — and
  tombstones the messages in — any mailbox missing from it.
- Suppress the authoritative snapshot when the delta set does not cover every
  mailbox, so a partial topology can never reach the store.
- Force full enumeration for any client that reconciles labels immediately, as a
  limited run already did. Folder shortcuts leave the session's label map
  covering only what changed, which is sound only because the post-sync
  mailbox-delta transaction is what reconciles labels.

## Why

Servers that cannot negotiate QRESYNC take the full-enumeration fallback on
every run, and that fallback also disabled the unchanged-mailbox skip and the
`UIDNEXT` high water mark. A Microsoft 365 account with 41 folders and ~96,000
messages spent 1h21m–2h10m per scheduled sync to archive 0–8 messages: roughly
1,920 sequential `Message-ID` header fetches, a second full `UID SEARCH` pass,
and a ~22-minute transaction rewriting all ~96,000 membership rows because every
delta carried `Reset: true`.

`UIDNEXT` is raised by every `APPEND`, so an unchanged `UIDNEXT` proves nothing
arrived, and an unchanged message count then proves nothing was expunged. That
is enough to make the fallback incremental without pretending to have
change-tracking the server does not offer. Every uncertainty resolves toward
more enumeration, never less: membership rows are only ever written from UIDs
the client observed, so a stored baseline can lag the server but cannot exceed
it, and a lagging baseline fails the count check and triggers a full rebuild.

The expected count is the size of the *merged* UID set rather than
`len(prior) + len(new)`, because RFC 3501 §6.4.8 makes `UID SEARCH UID n:*`
return the last message in the mailbox even when `n` is past it — summing reads
that re-reported UID as a deletion and re-enumerates every run.

## Usage

No usage or configuration change. Accounts on servers that negotiate QRESYNC are
unaffected; accounts that fall back now skip mailboxes they can prove unchanged
and fetch only what arrived. Read and unread state in a skipped mailbox is
refreshed the next time that mailbox changes — without CONDSTORE there is no
cheap way to observe a flag change on its own, which is the same trade the
pre-existing unchanged-mailbox skip made.

## Assertions this changes

Three tests asserted the behaviour being replaced and were rewritten rather than
adjusted around:

- `TestListMessages_FallsBackWhenSavedStatesLackModSeq` →
  `TestListMessages_SkipsUnchangedFoldersWithoutModSeq`. It asserted that a

author: redswimmer
body:
Phase 1 of the trace-inversion reproduction: build `D₂ = {(x', y', b', t')}`, the inverter's training set. Generation for the 7B arm is running as this opens — the branch will keep moving.

## Readiness review (`docs/12`)

Phase 0 deferred the training-stage measurements, so every VRAM number in the plan was arithmetic and the student choice rested on an unverified "full fine-tuning fits ~15 GB". Measured it on the 4090, each figure re-run and reproduced to ±0.01 GiB:

| Model | Role | Mode | @8192 | @16384 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-2B | student | FFT + 8-bit Adam | 12.64 GiB ✅ | **15.79 GiB ✅** |
| Qwen3.5-4B | inverter | FFT | 27.81 GiB ❌ | OOM ❌ |
| Qwen3.5-4B | inverter | **LoRA, bf16 base** | **15.11 GiB ✅** | 21.47 GiB ⚠️ |

- Student full fine-tunes at the paper's own `cutoff_len` 16384 — no method deviation.
- The inverter needs LoRA but **not** QLoRA, so `bitsandbytes` and NF4 drop out entirely.
- DeltaNet forward+backward verified on Ada/SM89 — the largest unverified architectural risk.
- `chunked_nll` confirmed load-bearing: naive fp32 logits at 248k vocab are 30.31 GiB at 16k.

Four plan errors fixed along the way: the two OpenThoughts schemas were swapped in the docs, the 8192 cap's truncation rate was read off a mean rather than a tail, the inverter's `max_length` was ~1,524 tokens short of what a capped trace needs, and Phase 1's budget was ~4× understated.

## Phase 1

Splits A/B drawn disjoint from one seeded permutation (16,000 / 9,000). Surrogate system prompt and compression prompt `π` are both verbatim from source with sha256 assertions — `π`'s text was found transcribed in `docs/01` §6.4 after an initial reconstruction from a paraphrase contradicted it.

Harnesses: `phase1_generate.py` (resumable), `phase1_compress.py`, `phase1_stats.py` (five gates, exits non-zero), `test_phase1_gates.py` (each gate fires on exactly one flipped input, plus the two cases that must *not* fire).

## Findings

- **Cap-hit is ~35%, and it is substantially stochastic.** Two independent draws of the same prompts at temperature 0.7 disagree on capped-vs-kept for 15% of rows, so every cap-hit figure carries ~±4 pts of resampling noise on top of binomial CI.
- **The drop is not neutral.** ~20% of dropped rows are surrogate-specific rather than genuinely hard prompts (`docs/09` 7.10/7.11) — a train/serve shift the paper never measured.
- **Swept throughput does not predict realized throughput** (~2.4×): `llama-batched-bench` batches at identical depth, `llama-server` batches ragged. A sweep ranks slot counts; it never builds a time budget.

## Scope decisions recorded

Table 2 fidelity metrics rejected — across the paper's own six rows, TF1 correlates 0.92 with trace length, and the paper labels them auxiliary. An R1-surrogate arm rejected — the bundled traces differ in provenance as well as surrogate strength, confounding the variable it would measure. `docs/10` carries a four-question checklist for proposing experiments, derived from how that one survived four rounds of review.

author: cyberlife-coder
body:
## Description

Closes #2106 items 6 and 7. They asked **"fix or retire"**. Retire — 1590 lines removed: the module, its 553-line test file, and the BDD characterization test written to document its defects.

The reasons are checkable rather than aesthetic:

| finding | evidence |
|---|---|
| **It duplicates a shipping feature** | The live path is `crate::fusion::FusionStrategy` driven by VelesQL's `FusionClause` (`collection/search/text_fusion.rs`, exercised by `examples/python/fusion_strategies.py`). `score_fusion` shares **no code** with it. |
| **It says so itself** | `mod.rs`: *"named `ScoreFusionMethod` to distinguish from the public `crate::fusion::FusionStrategy`"* |
| **It was never shipped** | Marked `EPIC-049 US-004`; has never appeared in `CHANGELOG.md` under any release. |
| **The code admits it is test-only** | `mod.rs` carried `#[allow(unused_imports)] // Re-exported for test access` |
| **Its only Rust consumer asserted it is broken** | `tests/bdd/fusion_weighted_bug.rs` locked in `Weighted == Average` and called it *"a DEAD-PATH defect"* |

Alongside that: the pseudo-RRF `1/(60+(1−s)·100)` divides by zero at `s = 1.6` and goes negative beyond (item 6), and `BoostCombination::Max` folds from an identity of `1.0`, so an all-penalty boost set is ignored (item 7).

**Fixing three bugs in an unshipped duplicate would have added a maintained surface with no consumer.** Git history keeps it for anyone reviving the epic — including the per-hop decay fix landed for item 8, which went in before its home turned out to be dead.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🔧 Refactoring (no functional changes)
- [x] 💥 Breaking change — `score_fusion` was `pub mod`, so its types leave the public API

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Unit tests
- [x] Integration tests

**Full suite green after the removal**, which is the real assertion here: nothing depended on any of it.

### Three greps that look like consumers, and are not

This is where an earlier, narrower search was imprecise — worth recording so the next reader does not repeat it. A repo-wide grep returns four files beyond the module itself. Three are **name collisions**:

| hit | what it actually is |
|---|---|
| `metrics/query.rs` — `ScoreFusion` | a variant of `QueryPhase`, a tracing-span label |
| `text_fusion.rs` — `score_fusion_strategy` | a **private local function** building the live `FusionStrategy` |
| `fusion_strategies.py` — `example_relative_score_fusion` | a Python example of VelesQL **RSF**, the live feature |

Only `tests/bdd/fusion_weighted_bug.rs` genuinely imported the module — and it is the test that documents the defects, so it goes with them.

What the module *would* have cost to keep was also checked. `ScoreExplanation` / `ComponentExplanation` looked like they might touch VelesDB's headline explainability promise; they do not. Nothing outside the module references either type, and the `agent/` subsystem where `why()` lives does not touch `score_fusion` at all.

**Test Configuration:**
- OS: Linux x86_64
- Rust: 1.90

`cargo fmt --check` clean; `cargo clippy -p velesdb-core -p velesdb-server --all-targets --features persistence,gpu,update-check -- -D warnings -D clippy::pedantic` clean (the CI's own flags); all three repo guards pass, file budgets included.

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the style guidelines of this project
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my code
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [x] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

## Additional Notes

### `MatchMetrics` is deliberately **not** deleted here

Its module header asserted these metrics were *"consumed by velesdb-server"*. **That was false** — nothing consumes them, and nothing records into them either: `MatchMetrics` is never constructed outside its own tests, so `to_prometheus` would export a permanently-zero family. That false assurance is exactly what let the surface sit unexamined, the same way it did for the graph metrics in #2091.

The comment is corrected rather than the module removed, because unlike `score_fusion` the underlying question is real: **MATCH is a shipped query path**, and its latency, error rate and traversal-depth distribution are worth having.

It is also **not the #2091 case**, and lumping them would be the wrong call. There, `GraphMetrics` was already being updated on every edge write and traversal — wiring the exporter recovered signal that existed and was being thrown away. Here the write path does not exist at all, so wiring the exporter alone would publish zeros. Adding the recording first is real work and belongs in its own change; it is tracked separately rather than smuggled into a deletion PR.

author: eldastito
body:
## Contexto

O `computeCampaignSocialSignals` (PR 15) roda para **uma** campanha por call. Este PR fecha o gap para **N campanhas** num único call — pré-requisito para o scheduler autônomo (PR futuro) e para um endpoint admin de "roda tudo agora".

## O que muda

### Novo módulo — `socialSignalsBatchRunner.ts`

- **`runSignalsForCampaigns(supabase, {campaignIds, options?})` → `BatchSignalsSummary`**
  - Roda em série (evita hammer no Supabase; ok pra <10 campanhas)
  - Propaga `options` (`focusTopics`, `persist`, `broadcast`, `now`, etc.) idênticas pra cada iteração
- **`discoverActiveCampaigns(supabase, {limit?})` → `string[]`**
  - Helper opcional que lista campaigns do `campaign_configs`
  - Caller pode ignorar e passar sua própria lista (queries variam por deploy)

### Isolamento de erro por-campanha

Erro em C1 **NÃO derruba** C2/C3. O erro fica em `perCampaign[C1].error` com `{message, kind}`. Log defensivo pra não sumir se o caller não inspecionar. Isso permite que o scheduler fique up mesmo com uma campanha problemática.

### Isolamento por-tenant (§35)

Cada iteração é escopada por `campaignId` **DENTRO** do runner de campanha (que já filtra tudo pelo tenant via `queryStoredPosts`/`queryStoredComments`). O batch runner NUNCA cruza dados entre campanhas.

### Dedup + validação

- IDs duplicados na entrada são deduplicados (`new Set`)
- IDs vazios são filtrados

## Determinismo (§39)

Pura orquestração — delega decisão pro runner puro. Não introduz lógica de scheduling (`setInterval`, cron) — isso fica pra próximo PR.

## Backward-compatibility

Módulo NOVO — nenhum consumer usa ainda. Nenhum arquivo existente foi modificado.

## Tests

**`tests/socialSignalsBatchRunner.test.ts`** — 11 suites cobrindo:

**`runSignalsForCampaigns`:**
- Lista vazia → summary vazio, `ok=0`
- N campanhas OK → `totalSignals` agregado, `perCampaign[i].result` presente
- IDs duplicados são deduplicados
- IDs vazios são filtrados
- `options` (`focusTopics`) propagados pra cada run
- Uma campanha falha (via mock que rejeita CAMP_B) → `ok=2`, `failed=1`, error registrado, resultado das outras intacto

**`discoverActiveCampaigns`:**
- Rows normais → array de campaignIds
- Rows sem `campaignId` (null/undefined) são filtradas
- `limit` propagado pra query

## Gates

- `npx tsc --noEmit` (CI) → **exit=0**
- `npm test` → **523/523 pass** (9 novas suites, 0 regressão)
- `npx vite build` → **exit=0**

## Fora de escopo (próximos PRs)

- **Scheduler autônomo** (`setInterval` / integração com routinesWorker) chamando este batch runner periodicamente
- **Concurrency controlado** (atualmente série; ok pra <10 campanhas; parallelismo com limite fica pra follow-up se necessário)
- **Endpoint admin** `POST /admin/social/run-batch` chamando este
- **Pulso Digital §53-§59 UI**
- Meta OAuth unificado; YouTube OAuth + Analytics; TikTok Login Kit
- Publisher core §68

## Roadmap Social Intelligence

| PR | Tema | Status |
|---|---|---|
| F0 | AS-IS + GAP-MATRIX | merged |
| 1-8 | Contracts, adapters, credential service, ingestion, 7 providers | merged |
| 9-11 | Intelligence engine (topic, sentiment, trend, anomaly, correlator) | merged |
| 12-15 | Signals bus + pipeline + aggregators + runner | merged |
| 16 | Persistência (social_signals table + store) | merged |
| 17 | HTTP endpoints /signals + /signals/compute | merged |
| 18 | Realtime broadcast | merged |
| **19** | **Batch runner multi-campanha (este PR)** | **this** |
| 20+ | Scheduler autônomo, notificações PUSH, Pulso Digital UI | pending |

author: blurbery
body:
## What I changed

I added an Android-mobile fallback for multichannel E-AC-3 on Bluetooth outputs that advertise no E-AC-3 passthrough. Direct play remains the first choice. If Android rejects that route, the next HLS plan copies the original video bitstream and converts only E-AC-3 audio to AAC. Full video transcoding remains available only if the direct-stream route also fails.

## Why

I reproduced this with the exact same media file on Android and iPhone. The iPhone direct-played H.264 High Level 4.0 with E-AC-3/Atmos and reached first frame. The Android phone advertised ample H.264 hardware support, but returned `ERROR_CODE_DECODING_FAILED` for both original HTTP and a codec-copy HLS remux. The old final fallback then re-encoded H.264 to H.264 as well as converting the audio.

That video encode did not address the observed failure and added unnecessary quality loss and compute. The deployed correction now reaches first frame as `server_remux_hls` with one transformation, `audio_to_aac`; the H.264 video is copied byte-for-byte. In media-server terms this is Direct Stream/Remux, not video transcoding.

The rule is capability-scoped rather than model-scoped: Android platform, mobile form factor, Bluetooth sink, empty passthrough set, E-AC-3, and at least six channels. It therefore covers Android mobile models reporting the same route facts. The live validation device was one Pixel 7; the test fixture uses a non-Pixel Android model to verify that planning does not depend on manufacturer or model.

## Validation

Passed against current upstream `main`:

```text
go test ./internal/playback -run 'Test(AndroidMobileBluetoothEAC3Fallback|AFTKRTEAC3HLSCorrection|DeviceQuirkProtocol)' -count=1
ok github.com/Silo-Server/silo-server/internal/playback 1.436s
```

The production fork passed its complete Go, Web, and docs GitHub Actions gates. After deployment, the live plan selected `server_remux_hls`, copied H.264, converted only audio to AAC, reached first frame, and stopped cycling.

## Scope and risk

A working direct route is never displaced. Android TV, speaker output, stereo E-AC-3, Apple clients, passthrough-capable routes, and other codecs keep existing planning. No API, schema, migration, configuration, or Jellyfin compatibility changes are included.

Source implementation and production validation: [blurbery/silo-server#51](https://github.com/blurbery/silo-server/pull/51).

Related issue: N/A — narrow fix reproduced on a live deployment.

## AI Disclosure

- Tool(s): OpenAI Codex desktop
- Model(s): gpt-5.6-sol
- Involvement: AI-assisted; I designed the capability boundary, reviewed the implementation, compared both clients on the same source, and validated the deployed route
- Adversarial review: Checked that direct play remains first, the fallback copies video, and the correction cannot activate for TV, speaker, stereo, passthrough-capable, Apple, or non-E-AC-3 routes. Focused positive and negative tests passed against current upstream main.

  * Improved playback for E-AC-3 audio on Android mobile devices connected via Bluetooth.
  * Automatically falls back to HLS with AAC audio conversion while preserving video when required.
