author: karlkfi
body:
## What

A grooming pass over `docs/queue/`, in two commits.

**Premises re-checked, two rewritten.** [Q48](docs/queue/Q48.md) said "on `main` today there is no prefilter at all, so the field is read by nobody and the defect is latent." The prefilter landed with the pipeline and took the `gates()` direction, so a credential rule carrying `keywords: [""]` loads clean and buys a full-corpus regex pass on every file. Live rather than latent, and the row no longer argues from two branch SHAs. [Q23](docs/queue/Q23.md)'s deferred trigger was "the docs grow past the design set", which a groom cannot answer; it is now a count with the command that takes it.

**One row filed.** [Q70](docs/queue/Q70.md): the vendored `queue.py` is pinned at `c0a239b` and predates `metrics --labels`, so this store can read the `open-question` stock and not the flow.

**The release path ranked to the head** — Q50, Q62, Q15, Q9, Q10. `queue.py next` picks Q50.

**Q54 loses `open-question`**, with the reasoning written into the row in the same edit.

## Why

`docs/releases/README.md` records the theme in its own words: there is no release, and the first ships when there is a binary and a hook that fires. The rank did not reflect it. Q50 is the only row in the store that unblocks any other, and Q9 and Q10 sat at 17 and 18 behind it while Q50 itself sat at 14 — so the two rows that make the tool installable and verifiable were ranked below refinement of components no user can reach.

What the re-rank displaces is the loader trio, and that is affordable for a measured reason rather than an assumed one. Against `rules/spill-guard.json`'s 14 rules, all 10 credential rules carry keywords and all 4 pii rules carry none, so Q46, Q48 and Q49 are latent for the shipped set. They bite an author writing project overrides, and there is no release yet to write overrides against.

Q54 asked for a backlog row in `claude-bouncer`, not an issue. A row is published only when a pull request the maintainer has read is merged, so the review is the confirmation and a second one before the file is written buys nothing. Q16 keeps the label: a third-party GitHub issue is public the moment it is filed.

```release-note
NONE
```

## Verification

`make queue`, `make queue MERGED=true` and `make docs` all exit 0 over the final tree. `queue.py claims` reports the one added id holds a claim on origin.

Those are weak on their own — a backlog edit adds no assertion, and a gate that has never failed here is not evidence. What carries this PR is that each claim it rests on had a way to come back the other way, and one did:

- **Q48's rot was found against the tree, not the row.** `internal/scan/prefilter.go` and the `gates(rule.Keywords)` call site in `scan.go` both exist and were read; the row's sentence could have been confirmed and was not.
- **Q43's premise was re-driven rather than trusted.** `cd tools && go build github.com/rhysd/actionlint/cmd/actionlint` still fails with the same five errors, `parse.go:1567:26: undefined: yaml.ParserError` among them. A green build would have made that row stale, and it did not come back green.
- **Q49 and Q46 were checked at their cited code.** `entropyCeiling` is still `log2(min(n, 256))` in `internal/rules/capture.go`; the pii-keywords clause is still absent from `load.go` beside the two that are there.
- **Q23's counts disagreed with my hand-count and the command won.** I wrote "11 at filing"; `git ls-files` against the 2026-08-22 tree said 12, and the row was corrected before commit. The command is in the row so the next reader re-runs it rather than trusting the number.
- **Q70's size rests on a diff that was taken, not recalled** — four hunks, purely additive, nothing before line 709 moving, so `CITATION_WINDOW` does not shift and `lint` is untouched. The row says to re-derive it at the revision actually taken, because the measurement was against a working checkout nobody else can resolve.

Two limits worth a reviewer's attention. I read 22 of the 40 rows in full — the head of the queue, both blocked rows, both deferred rows and the bash-3.2 cluster — and checked the rest by title and labels for duplicates only. And [Q39](docs/queue/Q39.md) stays at position 33 though it is a live break: `.githooks/pre-commit` dies on stock macOS bash 3.2, so `git commit` fails outright for a contributor who follows the setup instructions. The repair is one line and known; only the gate shape is Q35's call. It is the row to pull up if the release ordering is not what you want at the top.

author: longwarriors
body:
## Purpose

PR-8A "frontend truthfulness and test foundation": the UI stops claiming things the server does not do, every request states its physics explicitly, and the frontend gains the test harness and full coverage gate the repo's own config had deferred to "PR-8".

## Changes

1. **Capability matrix** (`web/src/api/capability.ts`) — a single `(state kind × representation)` table transcribed from `routes.py`, distinguishing `available` / `unsupported` (physics or server bound, with the reason) / `not_implemented` (superposition × point cloud). `planSceneRequest` can only produce a request from an `available` cell, by construction. ControlPanel button state, slider presence/ranges, and the canvas dispatch all derive from this one table — pinned by an `it.each` over every cell plus a flip-one-cell sabotage test. This also fixes four live mismatches: the streamlines button ignored the server's `n ≤ 6`/`l ≤ 5` bounds; the Seeds slider exceeded the superposition route's `≤ 128`; the superposition Grid/Mass sliders were placebos (resolution hardcoded 65); the Grid minimum used an eigenstate-only rule in superposition mode.
2. **Superposition requests are explicit** — new store fields `superpositionBasis` (default `'complex'`, decoupled from the eigenstate toggle so today's rendered physics is unchanged), `superpositionZ`, `superpositionAMu` (no slider by decision; shown read-only). The isosurface call now sends terms, time, resolution, basis, z, a_mu, probability_mass; nothing falls to server defaults.
3. **Superposition current-field wired end to end** — `fetchSuperpositionCurrentField` + `useSceneAsset` dispatch + `CurrentStreamlines` accepting the shared `StreamlineGeometry` shape + Inspector fields. Superposition × point cloud now surfaces "not implemented" honestly instead of silently rendering an isosurface; the statusbar shows `showing t=… · computing t=…` while a playback frame is in flight.
4. **`useSceneAsset` hook** — the fetch orchestration (coordinator, AbortController, latest-wins playback, error recovery) extracted from OrbitalCanvas into a store-free, prop-fed hook with race/abort/starvation/clock behavior each pinned by its own red-first test. OrbitalCanvas becomes a declarative shell over a discriminated `SceneAsset` union (the old four-nullable-slot design could draw two objects at once during a scene change).
5. **QVPC body validation, both ends** — the decoder now rejects non-finite values, intensity outside `[0,1]`, and phase outside `[-fround(π), +fround(π)]` (float32(π) > π in double — a `Math.PI` bound would reject legitimate payloads; both directions sabotage-tested). The Python encoder contract test pins the same invariants over the encoded buffer.
6. **Inspector truthfulness** — one `formatFinite` used by every numeric cell (NaN/Infinity render an em-dash, never "NaN"); the six populated-but-never-rendered continuity/finite-box fields now display next to the ratio they explain; z / a_mu / reduced_mass_ratio shown for superpositions.
7. **Harness + coverage expansion** — `jsdom@30.0.1` + `@react-three/test-renderer@9.1.1` (exact-pinned; per-file `@vitest-environment` docblocks, zero vitest plugin changes); scene components tested against real THREE objects incl. geometry dispose on unmount; the coverage gate expands from 4 modules to **all 24 production modules** at per-file 90/85/90/90 (triple latch updated: vitest include globs, guards.test.ts — including a red-first fix of the extension-leak root derivation that would otherwise have gone silently vacuous — and the regenerated coverage-scope.json). The stale "no DOM harness" and QVPC-deferral comments and the documented re-export escape hatch are deleted.

## Verification

- Full gate `pwsh -NoProfile -File scripts/check.ps1` exit 0, run twice (before and after status bookkeeping) with matching numbers.
- Frontend: **25 spec files / 504 tests**, 0 skipped/todo (was 8/264); coverage-scope: **24 modules**, all per-file thresholds met; aggregate 100% statements/functions/lines, 99.83% branches.
- Python: 903 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped, coverage 92.36% (+1: encoder body-invariant pin).
- Build: 1,219.07 kB (gzip 333.41 kB), +11.5 kB over baseline for the new capability/hook/validation code.
- Every task red-first with quoted failures and sabotage negative controls (all reverted); measured superposition endpoint latencies recorded in `status.md`.

## Out of scope (per the adopted roadmap)

Slice representation (PR-8B), visual/screenshot CI (PR-8C) — OrbitalCanvas's spec states it proves composition, not rendering — bundle splitting/perf (PR-9), and a server-side superposition point-cloud sampler (this PR makes its absence visible, not filled).

author: williecubed
body:
# TL;DR

The bundle report now measures startup transfer and complete JavaScript closure as separate delivery contracts. The production embed reports a 280,476-byte gzip JavaScript closure and passes its 300,000-byte launch gate. The report now identifies the editor and viewer closure debt without counting HTML, CSS, or fonts as JavaScript.

# Overview of Changes

The existing report already built eager, lazy, and complete transfer graphs from the Vite manifest. The first-load budgets correctly used the eager graph. The implementation plan defines a different launch gate over every JavaScript module that an entry can reach. The previous report did not expose that graph, so reviews compared the JavaScript limit with the complete transfer graph, which also contains HTML, CSS, fonts, and other assets.

Each entry now includes a `javascriptClosure` graph derived from its complete manifest closure. The bundle report evaluates the eager transfer graph against the existing startup budgets and evaluates the JavaScript closure against the launch limits from the Views plan. It stores those violations separately so one metric cannot be presented as the other.

Frozen schema-version-three reports remain readable. The validator derives the JavaScript closure from their complete file roster when the older report does not contain the new field. Bundle comparisons include the derived graph, so existing N-1 evidence does not need regeneration.

The production web build passes. The complete JavaScript closure is 280,476 gzip bytes for the embed, 393,471 for the viewer, and 571,275 for the editor. The repository check passed all 49 tasks. The web suite passed 304 files and 2,852 tests.

# Follow-ups

The viewer exceeds its 300,000-byte launch gate by 93,471 bytes. The editor exceeds its 450,000-byte launch gate by 121,275 bytes. This pull request reports those failures. It does not weaken their limits or start another runtime optimization pass.

The JavaScript closure violations remain launch diagnostics while the existing startup-transfer and individual-chunk violations remain blocking build checks. A later reduction can make the closure diagnostics blocking after the editor and viewer meet their declared limits.

body:
Maintenance-only pass for YAO-350: dependency/security, runtime warnings, and reproducible health checks. No product features, no UI changes, no destructive ops.

## P0 — dependency / security

**frontend: production audit 0 vulnerabilities** (was 4 high)
- `npm audit fix` bumped `next` to 15.5.24, clearing `nanoid` and `sharp`.
- `next` hard-pins `postcss@8.4.31`, so the high-severity postcss chain survived. Fixed with an `overrides: {"postcss": "$postcss"}` entry plus a direct-dep bump to `^8.5.26` — npm requires the override to align with the direct dependency. Avoids the `next@16` semver-major that `npm audit fix --force` wanted.

**mobile: 28 → 17 findings, criticals 0** (was 2 critical / 17 high / 8 moderate / 1 low)
- `npm audit fix` (no `--force`, so no Expo major) cleared both criticals — `tar`, `shell-quote` — plus `axios`, `undici`, `form-data`, `brace-expansion`, `js-yaml`, `fast-uri`, `nanoid`.
- `ws@7.5.10` was still flagged high; a scoped `"ws@7.0.0 - 7.5.10": "^7.5.11"` override lifts only the vulnerable copy to 7.5.13.

**Remaining 17 (0 critical, 9 high, 8 moderate) — requires-major-upgrade.** All are transitive under `expo@54`'s *build-time* toolchain (`@expo/cli`, `@expo/metro`, `metro*`, `image-size`, `postcss`, `uuid`→`xcode`, `@expo/config*`). npm reports the only fix as `expo@57.0.17`, a semver-major. Per the issue's Out-of-scope rule I did not force it. Worth a follow-up issue for a planned Expo 54→57 upgrade.

## P1 — warnings

Backend warnings **304 → 5**:
- Renamed deprecated `HTTP_422_UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY` / `HTTP_413_REQUEST_ENTITY_TOO_LARGE` to the `_CONTENT` successors — verified identical numeric values, so no behavior change.
- **Flagging this one:** `default_model` was `claude-sonnet-4-20250514`, whose end-of-life was **June 15, 2026** — already past. This was a latent runtime bug, not just log noise. Moved to `claude-sonnet-4-6` (verified non-deprecated in the installed SDK's `DEPRECATED_MODELS` table). `.env.example` already used a 4.6-series model, so deployments setting `DEFAULT_MODEL` were unaffected; only the built-in default was stale.
- Tests now set a ≥32-byte `JWT_SECRET`. I deliberately left the short production placeholder alone so PyJWT's `InsecureKeyLengthWarning` still fires for a deployment that forgets to set it.

Frontend warnings **2 → 0**:
- `ResizeObserver` mock now invokes its callback with a non-zero `contentRect`, silencing recharts' 0-size chart warning.
- `vitest.config.ts` → `.mts` so Vite loads it as ESM instead of the deprecated CJS API. Added `**/*.mts` to `tsconfig.json` `include`, which globs `**/*.ts` and would otherwise have silently dropped the file from typechecking.

**5 backend warnings remain, intentionally:** `DeprecationWarning: builtin type SwigPyObject/SwigPyPacked/swigvarlink has no __module__ attribute` — a SWIG-generated C extension under Python 3.14. Third-party, not fixable in this repo.

## P2

- No setup/build commands or default env vars changed, so `README.md` / `docs/deployment.md` / `mobile/README.md` / `mobile/AGENTS.md` needed no edits.
- Default backend URL unchanged: `mobile/app.json:83` and `mobile/src/lib/api.ts:18` both still `https://lumingchuan.vip/api`.

## Verification

Full run from a clean checkout — `node_modules` deleted and reinstalled via `npm ci`:

```
backend  uv run --frozen pytest -q        → 234 passed, 5 warnings
frontend npm run typecheck --pretty false → exit 0
frontend npm test -- --run                → 89 passed (18 files), 0 warnings
mobile   npm run typecheck --pretty false → exit 0
frontend npm audit --omit=dev             → found 0 vulnerabilities
mobile   npm audit --omit=dev             → 17 (0 critical, 9 high, 8 moderate)
```

## Note for the reviewer

`uv sync` silently rewrote every `backend/uv.lock` registry URL to a Microsoft-internal package proxy configured in my local `~/.config/uv/uv.toml`. Package versions and hashes were identical, but the URLs would have been wrong for everyone else. I reverted the file and used `uv run --frozen` for all subsequent runs; `uv.lock` is unchanged in this PR. I also checked both `package-lock.json` files for the same contamination — clean, `registry.npmjs.org` only. Worth confirming CI doesn't hit this.

author: mmalfertheiner
body:
## Problem

`PageParameter` clamps the page to 0 and the size to `MAX_PAGE_SIZE`, but a size below 1 passes through unchanged. `toPageRequest()` then calls `PageRequest.of`, which throws `IllegalArgumentException` for a size below one. In consuming applications a request with `size=0` or a negative size ends in an unhandled exception (HTTP 500) instead of a corrected page request.

## Fix

The size is now clamped to a minimum of 1, with a warn log in the same style as the existing maximum clamp. This matches how the page is already clamped to 0.

## Tests

New `PageParameterTest` covers the defaults for null values, the page clamp, both size clamps (minimum and maximum), and that `toPageRequest()` succeeds for a zero size.

author: usetheodev
body:
Corrige o #175.

## O que estava partido

O pacote existe para "server field errors landing on the right input", e isso funcionava por HTTP e falhava para uma action local — o caminho que o `appplugins` usa no browser.

`extractFieldsFromError` procurava `err.fields` no topo. Por HTTP o transporte desembrulha a resposta antes de o adapter a ver, portanto chegava `{ code, message, fields }` achatado. Uma action local resolve com o envelope que o próprio tipo declarado promete — `Promise<{ data, error }>` — e o `fields` fica **dentro** de `error`. A procura devolvia `undefined`, o `routeActionError` caía no `throw err`, e o submit rejeitava com uma unhandled promise: sem banner, sem mensagem inline, sem `aria-invalid`. O utilizador não via nada.

## A correção

Lê as duas formas. Não uma em vez da outra: a achatada é o que o caminho HTTP sempre produziu e não pode ser largada; o envelope é o que o tipo da action diz que ela devolve. Um duck-type que só conhece uma delas é um duck-type que conhece o **transporte** — exatamente o que este helper existe para evitar.

O ramo `throw err` fica intacto e coberto: uma falha arbitrária não é um erro de validação, e engoli-la trocaria um defeito visível por um silencioso.

## Verificado por mutação

Revertendo a segunda leitura:

```
× reads the envelope a local action resolves with
× routes the envelope onto the form instead of re-throwing
  3 passed   (os casos pré-existentes continuam verdes)
```

Suíte completa: **70 testes**, acima dos 65 anteriores.

Closes #175

body:
## What

Label di kartu kloter pada layar Daftar Kloter:

| Keadaan | Sebelum | Sesudah |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Belum berangkat | Estimasi jam berangkat | **Prediksi Berangkat** |
| Sudah berangkat | Jam berangkat | **Jam Berangkat di Lapangan** |

Plus `tests/kloter_departure_label.test.mjs`.

## Why

Pasal 10.6: *"An estimate is never a record... a screen showing both must say which is which."*

Keduanya jam yang terlihat sama — "07:05" — dan sama sekali bukan hal yang sama. Yang satu dihitung sistem untuk merencanakan pagi; yang satu diketik petugas dari jam dinding dan menjadi dasar penalti **seluruh regu di kloter itu**.

Label lamanya tidak menyebut bedanya: "Jam berangkat" polos terbaca seperti jadwal, dan petugas yang membaca kartu ini untuk memutuskan apakah sebuah kloter sudah jalan tidak punya cara membedakan keduanya selain mengingat kloter mana yang sudah ia ceklis.

## Notes

**Kertas TIDAK ikut berubah, dan ada tes yang menjaganya.** Blangko difotokopi dan masternya bisa sudah beredar (pasal 8.1). Lagi pula keduanya sudah benar apa adanya: kertas peserta memang selalu memuat perkiraan — ia dicetak sebelum ada yang berangkat — dan kertas staging menyediakan garis kosong "Jam sebenarnya: ______" untuk ditulis tangan.

**Satu hal, tiga nama — dan sekarang masih dua.** Sebelum PR ini layar menyebutnya "Estimasi", kertas menyebutnya "Perkiraan", dan chip Keberangkatan menandainya "~". PR ini menyatukan layar ke "Prediksi" sesuai permintaan pemilik acara, tetapi kertas masih "Perkiraan". Menyamakannya bisa dikerjakan kapan saja setelah lomba — bukan dua hari sebelumnya, saat masternya mungkin sudah di mesin fotokopi.

Diukur di browser dengan database dev berisi 10 kloter, 7 di antaranya sudah berangkat:

...

Kloter 9  Prediksi Berangkat: 07:24
Kloter 10 Prediksi Berangkat: 07:27

body:
## Zusammenfassung

Ein Schüler konnte seine Diagnostikdaten trotz wiederholter Versuche nicht an die Lehrkraft senden (`regelradar-lehrkraft.html` / RegelRadar-Selbsttest).

**Ursache gefunden:** Das Backend (`reso-backend/api.py`, Endpunkt `POST /ergebnis`) lehnt jede Einsendung mit `404 "Klassencode nicht gefunden"` ab, wenn der eingegebene Klassencode nicht in der Datenbank existiert (z. B. Tippfehler oder veralteter/falscher Code). Alle fünf RegelRadar-Sendeformulare zeigten dabei aber immer nur die generische Meldung **„Senden fehlgeschlagen – nochmal versuchen"** an – unabhängig davon, ob der Code falsch war oder ein echtes Verbindungsproblem vorlag. Ein falscher Klassencode führt bei jedem erneuten Versuch zwangsläufig wieder zum selben Fehler, ohne dass der/die Schüler*in je erfährt, dass der **Code** das Problem ist – daher die wiederholten erfolglosen Versuche.

## Änderungen

In allen fünf Sendefunktionen wird jetzt der HTTP-Status der Antwort ausgewertet und eine passende, umsetzbare Fehlermeldung angezeigt:

- **404 (Klassencode unbekannt):** „Klassencode falsch/unbekannt – bitte bei der Lehrkraft nachfragen"
- **alle anderen Fehler (z. B. Netzwerk/Server):** „Senden fehlgeschlagen – Internetverbindung prüfen und nochmal versuchen"

Betroffene Dateien:
- `regelradar-selbsttest.html`
- `regelradar-selbsttest2.html`
- `regelradar-diktat.html`
- `regelradar-quatsch.html`
- `regelradar-strategieabfrage.html`

Keine Backend-Änderung nötig – das Verhalten (404 bei unbekanntem Code) ist korrekt, es fehlte nur die Weitergabe an die Nutzer*innen. Die Testdaten bleiben nach einem fehlgeschlagenen Versuch erhalten, sodass erneut gesendet werden kann, sobald der richtige Code vorliegt.

## Test plan

- [x] `node --check` auf den extrahierten `<script>`-Inhalten aller 5 geänderten Dateien (keine Syntaxfehler)
- [ ] Manuell im Browser: Selbsttest mit ungültigem Klassencode abschließen und senden → neue Meldung „Klassencode falsch/unbekannt …" erscheint
- [ ] Manuell: Selbsttest mit gültigem Klassencode senden → weiterhin erfolgreich (unverändertes Verhalten)

author: toiroakr-release-bot[bot]
body:
This PR was opened by the [Changesets release](https://github.com/changesets/action) GitHub action. When you're ready to do a release, you can merge this and the packages will be published to npm automatically. If you're not ready to do a release yet, that's fine, whenever you add more changesets to main, this PR will be updated.


# Releases
## vinfer@0.2.0

### Minor Changes

- 3699f73: Add `--inline-external-types` (config `inlineExternalTypes`) to replace an `import("...")` reference to a plain type reached through an explicit `v.GenericSchema<T>` annotation with that type's own structure, recursively across as many files as needed, instead of leaving the generated output pointing back at them. Off by default; existing generated output is unchanged unless the flag is set.

  - A reference that would recurse into itself, directly or through another file, is left as a resolvable `import(...)` at the point it would repeat. A same-file type that isn't exported has no importable name to fall back to, so a cycle through one is left as a bare (unresolved) identifier instead - the same known limitation already documented for a local explicit annotation.
  - A reference reached through a recursed-into file's own imports - printed by TypeScript as a bare name valid only in that file's own scope - is re-anchored to the same explicit, resolvable form before being embedded in the output.
  - A qualified name (e.g. an enum member, `Kind.A`) or a generic instantiation (`Box<string>`) is never expanded, only referenced - expanding just the base name would strand the rest against whatever replaced it.
  - A `typeof` operand and a method signature's own name are never expanded either, only referenced - substituting either would produce invalid syntax.
  - An enum whose member value ts-morph cannot statically resolve (e.g. initialized from a function call) is left unexpanded entirely, rather than silently printing a literal union narrower than the enum itself - this also fixes the same silent-narrowing bug in the existing (flag-independent) same-file enum expansion `resolveType()` already performed.

  Ported from [toiroakr/zinfer#446](https://github.com/toiroakr/zinfer/pull/446), [#447](https://github.com/toiroakr/zinfer/pull/447), and their review-fix follow-ups.

### Patch Changes

- bf9a76e: Fix a recursive getter field wrapped in `v.nullable()` losing its `| null` and being wrongly printed as an optional key (`?`) rather than a required one with a nullable value. `v.nullable()` and `v.undefinedable()` widen a field's value type without making the object key itself optional - unlike `v.optional()`, `v.exactOptional()`, and `v.nullish()`, which do. The getter resolver previously collapsed all of these into a single "is this wrapped in something" flag, so a `v.nullable()`-only recursive field ended up both missing `| null` in its printed type and incorrectly marked optional; a `v.undefinedable()`-only one was missing `| undefined` while also incorrectly marked optional. Both are now derived independently from the AST, matching Valibot's own `OptionalEntrySchema` semantics.
- 4845e93: Port several bug fixes from `toiroakr/zinfer`, plus two related fixes found while porting them:

  - Fix an enum-to-literal-union expansion bug: when a native `enum` referenced through `v.enum()` had a member whose value couldn't be statically resolved (e.g. initialized from a function call), the generated type silently dropped that member instead of the whole union, printing a type narrower than the enum itself and rejecting values TypeScript accepts. It now leaves the enum unexpanded in that case.
  - Fix three occurrences of a naive string-literal boundary check (`prevChar !== "\\"`) that misjudged a string ending in an even number of backslashes (e.g. `"a\\\\"`) as still escaped. Replaced with the correct backslash-parity check already used elsewhere in the codebase, shared through a new `string-scan.ts` module.
  - Fix `__Normalize` silently stripping the brand's symbol key - and with it the brand itself - from a schema branded as a whole object (`v.pipe(v.object({...}), v.brand("Tag"))`), instead of only from a branded field inside an object. (The same gap for a directly-branded tuple is deliberately left open; see the comment on `NORMALIZE_TYPE_DEFINITION` in `normalizer.ts` for why.)
  - Use Windows-compatible directory junctions instead of symlinks in the CLI runner tests, matching zinfer.

author: psaab
body:
`opus-review-001.md` existed only at `/home/ps/git/opus-review-001.md` — **outside the repository** — while two OPEN issues cite it as their evidence base:

- **#6751** — live High-severity interface-SNAT forwarding work, currently in progress
- **#6813** — the audit cohort, whose annotation points readers at a repo path that does not exist

So the evidence behind an open High was reachable only from the machine that produced it.

`md5 d3de78f1fdaace39adc9fcfcfeca9c8d`, 2.4 MB, 20k+ lines, reviewed at base `ad959117` on 2026-08-02.

## On the size, since it is a real cost

A 2.4 MB markdown file in a repository is not free, and it is justified here only because live issues depend on it and **a review document that cannot be read is not evidence**. It joins `claude-opus-XC-show.md`, already in this directory for the same reason.

## A caveat that belongs with it

The review is anchored at `ad959117` and master is thousands of commits ahead, so **every file:line in it should be treated as a coordinate that has probably rotted**. The finding usually survives; the cite usually does not.

That failure mode is worth naming because it does not announce itself: a stale cite reads as *false reassurance*. Someone re-checking a finding at its recorded line sees unrelated code, concludes the finding is gone, and closes it. #6739 has a worked example — a finding whose two cites now point at a blank line and a boot-listener comment, where half had genuinely shipped 140 lines away in a different file and half was still open.

No code changes; docs only.

La cause des pannes d'accès au site. GitHub Pages publie un site d'**1 Go maximum** ; l'arbre suivi en faisait **1,8**, dont 1,7 pour le seul détail des matchs — 5 704 fichiers repartis à chaque commit.

Ils sont sur R2 depuis ce matin, versés et vérifiés à **0 écart** (5 704 objets, 1 737 Mo, 7 min 21 s). Ils quittent le dépôt ici.

## Ce retrait se serait défait tout seul

C'est le vrai sujet. Trois scripts écrivent dans `data/match/` et leurs workflows commitent ce qu'ils produisent : supprimer le dossier sans toucher à la chaîne l'aurait vu revenir à la collecte de nuit.

Le dépôt a déjà payé ce motif avec les secondes divisions — supprimées une fois, ramenées par un robot, et il a fallu couper leur *collecte* pour que ça tienne.

**La chaîne, dans les deux sens :**

| Sens | Où | Règle |
|---|---|---|
| Écriture | `update-data.yml`, `fetch-season.yml` | versent sur R2 **avant** de commiter le reste |
| Lecture | `compute-models.yml`, `derive-xg-round.yml` | rapatrient **avant** de calculer |

L'ordre compte des deux côtés. Si le versement échoue, l'étape rougit et rien n'est publié — plutôt qu'un calendrier à jour et des matchs nulle part. Et sans rapatriement, `compute_team_stats.py` ne trouve aucun fichier et rend un résultat vide **sans échouer** : un workflow vert qui ne calcule rien.

## Rapatrier plutôt que réécrire les lecteurs

Faire lire R2 à `compute_team_stats` demanderait de toucher à son parcours de fichiers pour un gain nul : il balaie `*/*/*.json` et a besoin du bucket entier de toute façon. Une commande dans le workflow vaut mieux qu'une couche réseau dans un script de calcul qui n'en avait pas.

`derive_xg_round` passe quatre fois par jour : il ne rapatrie que la saison retenue, ligue par ligue — la saison est au second niveau de la clé, hors de portée d'un préfixe unique. La liste des ligues vient de `paths.py` plutôt que d'être recopiée : le périmètre a déjà changé deux fois cet été.

## Le Studio

Seul consommateur hors workflow, donc seul à avoir besoin d'une adresse publique. La carte « onze type » va chercher les fichiers directement sur R2, **sans essayer le dépôt d'abord** : le fichier local n'existe plus, et 380 tentatives inutiles doubleraient son temps d'affichage. L'adresse est en un seul endroit, pour que le passage à un domaine propre ne change qu'une constante.

⚠️ **Elle sera bloquée par CORS tant qu'une politique n'est pas posée sur le bucket.** C'est mesuré, pas supposé : la réponse ne porte aucun `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`, là où deux services témoins interrogés par le même proxy en renvoient un. À ajouter dans R2 → le bucket → Settings → CORS Policy.

## Les garde-fous

`tests/test_depot_r2.py` tient cinq invariants : `.gitignore` couvre le dossier, aucun workflow ne le commite, tout workflow qui collecte verse, tout workflow qui calcule rapatrie **avant**, et les étapes R2 reçoivent leurs trois secrets.

Deux de ses assertions étaient fausses au premier jet et méritent d'être dites : `data/match` attrapait aussi `data/matches.json` — le calendrier, qui reste — et la recherche dans le Studio échouait sur le commentaire qui explique la bascule.

## Un test qui se serait mis à se sauter en silence

`test_sync_r2_parcours` prenait son échantillon dans `data/match/5/2026-2027` derrière un `skipUnless`. Le dossier disparaissant, ses 18 tests se seraient sautés sur le serveur sans que rien ne le dise — exactement le motif des seize classes du Studio de la mi-août. Il recopie désormais de vraies fiches post-match, qui restent dans le dépôt, sous une arborescence temporaire.

## Vérifications

Suite lancée **en masquant `data/match/`**, pour reproduire la CI : **318 tests, 0 échec, aucun saut supplémentaire.** `ruff` propre, les onze fichiers du Studio passent `node --check`, 104 tests JavaScript verts.

## What

- honor BrowserArena’s existing recording option when creating Browser Use sessions
- use the Browser Use V4 browser resource to create, stop, and retrieve `recordingUrl`
- add three mocked HTTP regression tests for create, recording download, and stop

## Why

BrowserArena’s record command already calls `provider.create({ recording: true })`, but `BrowserUseProvider` ignored that flag. It also polled the V3 agent-session resource, which is not the browser record that owns `recordingUrl`. The result was a Browser Use run without an available proof video.

This patch sends `enableRecording` to V4 and reads the V4 browser record after the run stops.

author: kvark
body:
The Pages crash after #11 was not the HTML `return`.

`Rasterizer::new` always builds a depth-only shadow pipeline. Blade only attaches the dummy `raster_shadow_fs` under `cfg(gles)`, but WASM uses the GLES/WebGL2 backend via `target_arch = "wasm32"` without that cfg. WebGL then tries to link a vertex-only program:

`Link: Must have a compiled fragment shader attached: Missing shader.`

`.cargo/config.toml` now sets `--cfg gles` for `wasm32-unknown-unknown`, and `main.rs` `compile_error!`s if a wasm build is missing it.

Verified locally: `cargo rustc --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -- --print cfg` includes `gles`; a release WASM build served to headless Firefox created a canvas and cleared the boot overlay with no link panic.

author: clayshentrup
body:
#1080 pinned three things a page does that no program had ever asked it to do. Two of them were wrong, and this fixes them.

## The mechanism

The wasm backend emits every builtin as a `RT_BUILTIN` call — `src/wasm_backend.rs:947` handles `args`, `stdin` and `now` identically — and `src/wasm_rt.rs:809` lands that on `call_builtin`. `call_builtin` had an arm for `now` and none for the other two, so those fell through to `unknown builtin` at `src/eval.rs:2800`.

Native and `--interp` never go through that door. They reach all three through `eval_ident`, which has had the arms since the builtins were written.

So `now` working on wasm was a coincidence of coverage. Worth stating plainly, because the first reading of this was "every zero-argument builtin is broken on wasm" and `now` disproved it — the real rule is narrower and duller.

## The fix

One match arm covering all three, returning the descriptors `eval_ident` already returns.

```
args    error[runtime]: unknown builtin `args`   ->  args holds 0 of them
stdin   error[runtime]: unknown builtin `stdin`  ->  the playground has no stdin
now     the clock is past the epoch: false       ->  unchanged
```

`args` is fully closed: a page and native agree byte for byte, and the entry leaves `tests/golden/wasm_gaps.txt` entirely.

`stdin` stays a gap, because a page genuinely has no stdin — but it is now the honest capability refusal that `src/wasm.rs` and `src/wasm_rt.rs` have each carried since they were written and that nothing had ever been able to reach. It sits in the same family as "the playground has no filesystem" rather than reporting a missing builtin.

## Watched red first

That is what #1080 was for. With the arms in and the old entries still in place:

```
args_are_empty_without_any.kso is a known gap answering
`error[runtime]: unknown builtin `args``, and it now answers
`args holds 0 of them` — close it or restate it in tests/golden/wasm_gaps.txt
```

The ledger doing its job. The `now` entry's comment is corrected in the same commit, since it asserted that `now` "unlike those two REACHES the executor" and that is no longer the distinction.

## Verification

```
PASS  328 agree, 9 known gaps, 0 disagree   (browser differential, headless chrome; was 327/10)
7 passed                                    (tests/wasm_engine.rs)
cargo test --release                        0 failed
cargo fmt --check / cargo clippy            clean
welfare 84.12, floor 84.12                  unmoved
```

The compile veins are host-divergent and are left to CI to measure.

author: badjoke-lab
body:
## Purpose

Harden Stage 3 transformed-video temporal coherence without changing the completed Stage 1 + Stage 2 contracts or claiming Stage 3/Public Alpha complete.

## Problem found in audit

Raster sampling itself is deterministic and anchored to source-space coordinates, so Point/Particle positions are not randomly reassigned every video frame. However, the Glyph `symbols` preset derived glyph identity from active-sample array index. When a moving contour caused an earlier sample to enter/leave the active set, later samples could all shift index and change glyph identity even though their own source-space positions were unchanged.

## Scope

- derive Symbols glyph identity from deterministic source-space position hashing rather than active array rank
- keep Binary/Density glyph presets luminance-driven
- add regression coverage proving inserting an earlier sample does not change glyph IDs at unchanged positions
- add core coverage proving shared source UVs keep identical canonical point positions across adjacent synthetic video frames
- preserve existing Stage 3 video import/playback/seek/current-frame export baseline
- retain real-video Glyph/Symbols evidence at the start and 80% seek positions

## Verification

PR CI #108 is green across typecheck, unit tests, build, Chromium browser smoke, focused WebKit check, evidence upload and browser-candidate upload.

The retained real-video evidence was inspected: the Symbols-rendered moving square is visible at the left-hand start position and at the right-hand 80% seek position without blank/corrupt output. Existing Point video evidence still moves left -> middle -> right, and the 390x844 Japanese first-run evidence remains intact.

The application candidate from run #107 and the final run #108 candidate are byte-identical at `index.html`, JS and CSS SHA-256. The only final change between those runs was the added browser evidence/test coverage.

## Not claimed complete

- full optical-flow/object tracking
- temporal denoising across arbitrary footage
- original + transformed composition
- texture/mask/analysis-input composition
- Stage 3/Public Alpha completion

author: kilo-loco
body:
## Problem

`create ssh-key` imports `get_ssh_key` and then never calls it — it passes `args.ssh_key` straight to the API:

```python
from vastai.cli.util import get_ssh_key, generate_ssh_key   # imported, unused

ssh_key_content = args.ssh_key
...
result = keys_api.create_ssh_key(client, ssh_key=ssh_key_content)
```

So the form the hello-world guide and this command's own epilog prescribe:

```
vastai create ssh-key ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub
```

stores the literal string `/home/you/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub` as the account's public key:

```
$ vastai show ssh-keys
[{'id': 1276050, ..., 'public_key': '/Users/me/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub', ...}]
```

The command prints success. The key is silently useless. The first symptom is `Permission denied (publickey)` on an instance that is already created and already billing.

## Cause

`update ssh-key` and `attach ssh` both call `get_ssh_key`; only `create` misses it — so the one broken path is the account-level one new users are walked through first. The unused import is the tell: the call was dropped, most likely when the commands moved into `vastai/cli/commands/`. This restores the behavior originally requested in #133.

## Fix

One line, routing through the existing helper:

```python
ssh_key_content = get_ssh_key(ssh_key_content)
```

That also picks up `get_ssh_key`'s two guards: a private key or a non-key string now raises before anything is sent, rather than being stored verbatim.

Routing `create` through the helper newly exposed one crash: `get_ssh_key`'s `open()` raises bare `OSError` subclasses, which `main()` doesn't handle (it catches `HTTPError` and `ValueError` only), so `vastai create ssh-key ~/.ssh` printed a raw traceback. Those are now converted to `ValueError` with a message in the same shape as the function's two existing ones. `update ssh-key` and `attach ssh` get the same treatment for free.

## Test plan

The existing test asserted only that the parameter was present:

```python
assert "ssh_key" in call_args[1]["json_data"]
```

true for any value, including a file path — which is why the regression went unnoticed. It now asserts the exact string sent, alongside four new cases: a `.pub` path is read, a private key is rejected, a non-key string is rejected, an unreadable path raises cleanly.

- [x] `pytest tests/cli/test_keys_commands.py` — 4 failed / 6 passed before, **10 passed** after
- [x] `pytest tests/cli tests/sdk` (covers `update`/`attach`, which share `get_ssh_key`) — **532 passed**
- [x] Full `pytest tests/` — 12 failed / 12 errors, identical on clean `master` (tar-utils and credential-requiring suites), unrelated to this change

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

- `vast.py` carries the identical bug at `create__ssh_key` (its own `get_ssh_key` sits unused at line 1310). Left alone deliberately: it's marked `DEPRECATED`, isn't in the wheel, and recent behavior fixes have been package-only — the last one mirrored there was the #471 credential fix. Happy to mirror it if you'd rather.
- `get_ssh_key` uses `os.path.exists` without `expanduser`, so a *quoted* `"~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub"` still falls through as a literal. Unquoted paths are shell-expanded and unaffected.

Re-fixes #133.

author: jose-sequeira
body:
## Problem

An engineer looking at a slow `processPersonsStep` or `lazyLoader.loadViaCache` span in APM cannot tell which team or distinct id caused it, or whether a cache lookup went to Postgres.

- Ingestion step spans carry no attributes, so `apm-attribute-breakdown` by `team_id` returns only the empty value.
- `lazyLoader.loadViaCache` uses one span name for every loader and never records the loader name.
- A `loadViaCache` call that waits on another caller's in-flight load has no child span, so it looks like a slow cache lookup.
- In `processPersonsStep`, waiting on a shared fetch promise in the persons batch store is invisible in the trace.

## Changes

- Every per-event step span now carries `team_id`, `distinct_id` and `event`, so slow spans can be broken down by tenant and action.
- Attributes are built only when the parent batch span is sampled, so the unsampled majority pays nothing.
- `lazyLoader.loadViaCache` spans now carry `lazyloader.name`, `lazyloader.keys`, `lazyloader.misses` and `lazyloader.outcome` (`all_cached`, `loaded`, `waited_pending`).
- The persons batch store emits a `personsStore.awaitPendingFetch` span while a caller waits on another caller's fetch, tagged with `persons.pending_fetch`.
- Chunk step spans carry `chunk_size`.
- Mechanical: `instrumentFn` accepts an `attributes` option that reaches the span only, never the Prometheus labels.

Nothing user-visible changes. Span volume is unchanged except for the new wait span in the persons store.

## How did you test this code?

- `span-attributes.test.ts` covers attribute extraction from each step input shape and rejects wrong-typed fields.
- `lazy-loader.test.ts` gains a case that checks the three `lazyloader.outcome` values for a concurrent pair of gets followed by a cached get.
- Existing step-pipeline, chunk-pipeline and persons batch store suites pass unchanged.
- Not checked: a real trace export against a collector. Attribute presence in production spans should be confirmed after deploy via `apm-attribute-breakdown` on `ingestion-analytics-main`.

## Automatic notifications

- [ ] Publish to changelog?

## Docs update

None.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

Claude Code (Fable 5). Skills invoked: `/writing-pr-descriptions`. The APM MCP tools (`apm-spans-aggregate`, `apm-spans-tree`, `apm-attribute-breakdown`) were used to confirm the gaps before the change. Two related findings were left out on purpose for a separate PR: orphan root spans from lost async context in the lazy loader buffer, and the per-message `kafka_produce_callback` span volume.

author: michi71
body:
Michael's ear on A20 Marimba SW: *"dieses marimba hatte bei uns eine art trommel im hintergrund (so ein tack,tack,tack). im video hört man das nicht."* It is a real tone of the patch — it just is not supposed to sound at that velocity.

## What was wrong

Each tone carries a velocity window at `+03/+04`. The window is real, but it only gates while **bit 7 of the patch common byte** (`+12`, the patch velocity switch) is set. Missing that condition makes the bytes look wrong in *both* directions, and this engine has had it wrong both ways:

- **Gating unconditionally** silenced six bank-A basses below velocity 61 — St Fretless, House Bass, Thumpin Bass, Pick Bass, Wonder Bass, Yowza Bass, all carrying `+03 = 61` on every tone with the switch **clear**, so the machine ignores the window and plays them. 70 of 1600 cells sounded on the reference and were silent here. That is why the gate came out.
- **Not gating at all** sounds tones the machine keeps silent. A20 Marimba SW windows its third tone — wave 78 "Anklungs" — to `126..127` with the switch **set**. Played at every velocity it lays a rattle under the marimba: ~12 Hz, 26 % of the modulation energy in the 8–16 Hz band against 1.3 % for the reference, and 50–60 dB of excess above 1 kHz.

## Why the switch is the answer

Measured on the reference at note 60:

| A20 Marimba SW | RMS | high/low | 8–16 Hz |
|---|---|---|---|
| reference, velocity 100 | 0.00923 | −35.2 dB | 1.3 % |
| **ours, before** | 0.00759 | +18.9 dB | 25.8 % |
| **ours, after** | 0.00653 | −33.8 dB | 1.5 % |
| reference, velocity 127 | 0.02260 | +25.9 dB | 33.3 % |
| ours, after, velocity 127 | 0.01014 | +18.5 dB | 25.8 % |

The switched layer arrives exactly where `+03` says it should, on both sides.

And bank A splits without a single exception: of the 27 patches carrying a window at all, the **10 whose window must be ignored have the switch clear**, and the **17 whose window must bite have it set** — precisely the velocity-layered material (the Rhodes family, SwitchOnMute, Velo Harmnix, Slap Bass, Marimba SW).

## Regression

At note 60 and velocities 20/40/100/127 across banks A and B, **no patch sounds on the reference and is silent here**. (One case at velocity 20, B50 Log Drum at −78 dBFS, is pre-existing: its switch is clear and its window is `0..127`, so the new test is skipped entirely for it.)

Of the 21 patches whose window can bite, **none moved away** from the reference:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| SwitchOnMute | 0.325 | **0.785** |
| Marimba SW | −0.008 | **0.444** |
| Slap Bass | 0.619 | 0.726 |
| SA Rhodes | 0.749 | 0.839 |
| Pop Strat | 0.608 | 0.696 |

Bank-wide median similarity is unchanged (0.910 → 0.911) — only 21 of 128 patches have a window that can bite at all.

## A caveat, and one thing the video could not decide

The owner's manual describes bit 7 as *disabling* velocity response, which is the opposite of what bank A shows. The reading here is the measured one.

The demo video cannot adjudicate this patch: its A20 segment is correctly aligned (it matches patch 20 better than any neighbour) but **the reference emulator itself only reaches 0.313 there**, against 0.92–0.98 on the surrounding patches — the demo plays A20 as a phrase, not our single note, and a marimba roll at ~10 strokes/second lands in the same 8–16 Hz band. The evidence for this change is the ROM bytes and the reference, not the recording.

author: rquitales
body:
fix(sandbox): kill the whole process group on timeout/cancel

fix(sandbox): kill the whole process group on timeout/cancel

exec.CommandContext's default cancellation kills only the shell, so a
pipelined streaming command (kubectl logs -f | grep error) kept its
grandchildren running — and since stdout is a pipe feeding a capture
buffer, cmd.Wait() blocked until all writers closed it: forever. The
7s streaming timeout silently never fired for the most natural form of
streaming command, and orphaned kubectl -w processes leaked.

The local executor now runs commands in their own process group and
kills the group (SIGKILL -pgid, falling back to the shell alone), with
a 3s WaitDelay as a safety net if a grandchild still holds the pipes.

author: antonioventilii
body:
# Motivation

[`impls.rs`](https://github.com/dfinity/oisy-wallet/blob/main/src/shared/src/impls.rs#L861) carries this comment on `ContactAddressData`:

> Note: We don't need to validate `TokenAccountId` since it has its own validation

That is not true. There is no `Validate` impl for `TokenAccountId`, `Icrcv2AccountId`, `SolPrincipal`, `BtcAddress` or `EthAddress`, and none of them appear in the `validate_on_deserialize!` list. `SolPrincipal` is a bare `pub struct SolPrincipal(pub String)`. Contact addresses are completely unbounded.

Only the address *count* is capped (`CONTACT_MAX_ADDRESSES` = 40) and the contact count (500). With an unbounded string in each slot, a principal's stored blob can grow far past anything the image cap bounds, and every contact operation decodes that blob in full.

# Changes

- Add `impl Validate for TokenAccountId`, bounding the string-bearing arms at 128 characters. `Icrcv2` carries a `Principal` and a `[u8; 32]`, both already bounded by their own types, so it returns early.
- Call it from `UpdateContactRequest::validate`, the only path that writes addresses into storage.
- Replace the incorrect comment with one that says where the bound actually lives and why.

Two deliberate choices worth reviewing:

**128 characters, not a per-chain exact length.** The longest address any supported chain produces is 62 characters (bech32 P2WSH and bech32m P2TR); Ethereum is 42, Solana base58 is 44. A generous single bound achieves the memory goal without any chance of rejecting something a real wallet hands us. Tightening to exact per-variant lengths is a separate question, and a riskier one.

**Enforced on the write path, not via `validate_on_deserialize!`.** This is the important one. `ContactAddressData` is already wired into `validate_on_deserialize!` and is deserialized both from inbound requests *and* from stored state. A bound applied there would also run against addresses already in stable memory, and anything stored before the bound existed that failed it would trap on read and take the entire contact list with it, including the delete call needed to recover. Validating `UpdateContactRequest` reaches every address that can enter storage without re-judging what is already there. There is a comment in the code saying so, because the "cleaner" refactor is an outage.

# Tests

Unit tests in `shared`:

- Real addresses from all five arms (P2PKH, P2TR, Ethereum, Solana, Icrcv2) are accepted, so the bound cannot silently break a supported chain.
- An address one character over the bound is rejected, and one exactly at the bound is accepted.
- `UpdateContactRequest::validate` rejects an over-long address and accepts a normal one.

Integration test `test_update_contact_rejects_an_over_long_address` asserts a normal address round-trips, an over-long one is rejected at the boundary (the call is rejected outright rather than returning a typed `ContactError`, since validation runs during deserialization), and the stored contact is left untouched by the rejected write.

Gates run locally: `scripts/format.sh`, `scripts/lint.rust.sh`, `cargo test -p shared`, contacts integration suite (29 passed). No candid impact: this adds trait impls and a private constant, and changes no type definition.

author: amindell11
body:
## Summary

Unity CLI adoption arc ([#429](https://github.com/amindell11/astronomical-home/issues/429)) **slice 5 build**. The slice-5 probe measured a ~20× iteration win from routing test runs into a resident `com.unity.pipeline` editor instead of booting a batch Unity per run, and the user ruled the fork: **dev-loop runs route warm; the merge gate stays cold-process single-boot**, with the wrapper living as a routed mode inside `unity_test_agent.ps1` (one entry point, one artifact contract, through the `unity_access` coordinator seam).

This PR builds exactly that: a `-Routed` switch on the existing runner, plus the guard that keeps the merge gate cold.

## What changed

**`scripts/unity_test_agent.ps1`** — new `-Routed` switch (and `-UnityCliPath`, defaulting to `unity`):

- **Attach-only.** It never boots an editor and never takes a lease. It asks `unity_access.ps1 -Action Status` whether a tracked **editor**-mode owner serves this project; if not, it fails with the `StartEditor` recipe. Editor lifetime, the ≥10 GB RAM floor, and the boot lane stay with the work stream that owns the editor — the runner adds no new owner semantics.
- **Selection is resolved, then verified.** The pipeline's `run_tests` takes a *single include-only* filter — no `!` exclusion, no `;` lists (verified against the package source, `Editor/Testing/PipelineTestRunner.cs`). So the wrapper resolves the expected set from `list_tests` ground truth and **refuses anything it cannot reproduce exactly**, rather than silently running a different set than the flags say:
  - one selector axis per run (filter OR categories OR assemblies);
  - no selection whose matched tests carry an excluded category — which structurally refuses an unfiltered PlayMode/Both Workspace run under the default `-ExcludeCategory RequiresGraphics`;
  - a zero-test selection is an error, never a green run.
  After the run it diffs the executed set against the expected set and reports `infra_error` on any drift.
- **Always async.** Both platforms use `run_tests --async_tests true` + `test_status` polling. Sync PlayMode `run_tests` is a silent no-op (returns success having run nothing — a gate trusting it goes green on zero tests), and a long sync call risks CLI client timeouts. The sync path is simply not reachable from the wrapper.
- **Autotick re-armed around every domain reload.** An unticked idle background editor starves command servicing into 30 s timeouts that read as a wedged server.
- **Same artifact contract.** Identical summary-JSON shape, `STATUS=` line, and exit codes (0/1/2), plus `"transport": "routed"` and `editorPid` at the summary root. `xmlPath`/`logPath` are empty — results come from the pipeline, not NUnit XML.
- Refuses `-WithGraphics`, `-Windowed`, `-CaptureScenario`, `-OrderedTestListFile`, `-RerunFailedFrom`, `-ValidateScope`, `-SkipUnityAccess`.

**`scripts/agent_worktree_pool.sh`** — both full-coverage parsers (Python and PowerShell) refuse a `transport: routed` summary as merge proof, ahead of every other check and fail-closed. This is the "gate stays cold" ruling made structural rather than documentary: a routed run cannot arm merge proof even if it were otherwise full-shaped.

**`scripts/tests/test_pool_merge_gate.sh`** — regression case for that guard: a full-shaped routed summary never arms proof, the gate re-runs cold (no `-Routed`), and the cold run arms proof.

**Docs** — `TESTING.md` § Routed runs (full contract), a bullet in `doc/agents/testing.md`, and a rung-3 pointer in the `unity-access` skill.

## Test proof

**Live legs against a real resident editor** (agent-2, coordinated GUI editor pid 11100, run inside a user-authorized ~10-minute window beside the live RL fleet):

| Leg | Result |
|---|---|
| Routed EditMode, `-ScopeType Smoke` | 4/4 passed, **18.5 s** wall (cold floor is ~80 s, boot-dominated) |
| Routed `-Mode Both -ScopeType Workspace` | **refused** — named exactly the 9 `RequiresGraphics` tests, matching the probe's 828-vs-819 delta |
| Routed PlayMode `-TestCategory Smoke` (async path) | 4/4 passed, 18.1 s |
| Failure mapping, across a forced `recompile`/domain reload | exit 1, 1 passed / 1 failed, failure entry carries name, fullName, message, topStack, stackTrace |
| Real pool parser vs. real routed summary | `partial\|transport=routed …` — the transport refusal wins over every other reason |

Plus: `test_pool_merge_gate.sh` passes end-to-end including the new routed case; both scripts parse clean; the attach-only and flag-combo refusals were exercised against the real coordinator; every command and parameter used was read from `unity command --format json` rather than guessed.

**One real bug was caught by the live legs and fixed** (`ea542449`): a single-platform routed run returned a one-element array that PowerShell unrolls on return, serializing `runs` as an object instead of an array while the cold path emits a list. The artifact-contract claim was false until fixed; it is now verified true on a real artifact.

**No full-suite proof is recorded on this PR.** Opening via `create-pr` rather than `submit` deliberately: free RAM is ~8.7 GB against the ≥10 GB boot floor, with agent-4's ~10 h RL retrain live. The merge gate will run the single full cold suite on the exact landing tree — which doubles as the cold-path regression check, since the gate runs through this very script.

## Quality pass

A combined quality sub-agent reviewed the diff (simplification/reuse, comment hygiene on touched hunks, PS 5.1 + StrictMode hazards, bash `set -euo pipefail` hazards, doc/code consistency) and made three changes, all folded into `ea542449`: dropped a duplicate failure counter; filtered null entries out of the completed-results array so a missing result surfaces through the parity check instead of as a phantom failure; corrected a TESTING.md claim that implied only PlayMode ran async. It verified the StrictMode-sensitive paths empirically and found no further issues. Its one incidental observation — pre-existing "No such file" noise from `agent_worktree_pool.sh` around the merge-runs `.jsonl` read — is unrelated to this diff and left alone.

## Scope-conservation check

Scope was: a routed mode inside `unity_test_agent.ps1`, async-only PlayMode, `test_status` polling, `!RequiresGraphics` parity, autotick re-arm, `editor_status` readiness gating, plus the ruled forks (attach-only, `-Routed` switch, gate guard in the same PR). The diff is that and nothing else. Two things a scope-reader might not have predicted, both flagged deliberately:

1. **Parity is enforced by refusal, not replication.** The scope said "replicate the gate's `!RequiresGraphics` filter". The pipeline's filter cannot express exclusion, so exact replication is impossible; the wrapper refuses those selections instead of approximating them. This is stricter than asked, and it is what makes the "same selection as cold" claim true rather than aspirational.
2. **`-TestFilter` is split on `|`.** Scope-resolved filters are fixture-name alternations that cold Unity reads as regex; the pipeline matches literal substrings, so each alternative becomes its own call. Other regex syntax is not supported and is documented as such.

Not included, by design: the unity_access global editor cap (slice 6 / [#437](https://github.com/amindell11/astronomical-home/issues/437)), warm-capture dispatch ([#414](https://github.com/amindell11/astronomical-home/issues/414)), and routed support for ordered-list/rerun runs.

## Deferral candidate

Routed mode cannot serve `-CaptureScenario`: the scenario name is read from boot-time `GetCommandLineArgs`, so a routed `run_tests` can never select one. That is the known `capture.record` `[CliCommand]` need already recorded in the warm-capture arc — no new issue filed here.

Vocab: none

author: adammarquette
body:
## What this is

`AGENT-MEMORY.md` is the one document `AGENTS.md` mandates reading **before every task**. It had only half a
lifecycle — *"append, don't overwrite"* with nothing that ever took an entry out — and its own header called
the read cheap. On the base this now sits on, **`6b6a9d9`**, it measures **37,895 bytes / 9,474 tokens =
9.5K** — it was 9.2K at `fecc463` where this branch started, and #284 has grown it since.

This is not a drift card. The `~tok` row was already correct and gated. The defect was that a truthful 9.5K
was charged to every agent on every task, and nothing ever removed anything.

## The retirement rule

It lives in the file's own header, so the agent who promotes a note is the one who reads it. **An entry earns
its place by being the only copy of a practice, and it leaves when it stops being one.** The test is never its
age — four exits over five clauses, one condition on staying, and one sweep to run **before** any
removal:

| Exit | When |
|---|---|
| **Enforced — caught** | A gate, a test or a workflow now **fails** on the mistake *and names the remedy in its own output*. If it does not name the remedy, fix the gate rather than keep the entry. |
| **Enforced — prevented** | A setting or a stanza (`.editorconfig`, `cancel-in-progress: false`) makes the mistake **impossible**, so nothing fails and there is no output. **A comment beside it is not output.** Retires the *cause*; any *recovery* it does not carry stays. |
| **Contracted** | `AGENTS.md`, a role or subtree contract, an ADR or `CONTRIBUTING.md` states it where the work happens. |
| **Superseded** | A later entry corrects it. Not *old*: **contradicted**. The correction stays; the corrected text goes. |
| **Tracker state** | Open-PR counts, which sibling is fixed. That is a card's job; this file has no expiry. |

**Age is deliberately not a criterion.** gh#262's entry went stale *inside its own pull request* — the commit
that added it and the commit that falsified it were in the same merge. What was wrong there was a **mutable
reference**, not an old one. So the rule requires worked evidence to be pinned to a sha rather than a branch,
a date or "the current tree", and it says out loud that **nothing leaves for being long, narrow or
unglamorous** — the entry gh#254's own comments asked me to protect stays untouched, and so does the whole
gh#187 rebase entry it sits inside. Where only half of an entry found a home, only that half goes.

**And before any removal, sweep what points *at* the entry** — added in round 4, because its absence produced
a defect inside this very pull request. The exits all ask where the lesson went; none asks what referred to
the entry, and orphaning a reference breaks nothing a gate can see. The clause names the two things that make
the sweep hard: **prove the grep on a known positive before trusting an empty result** (case and line-wrapping
each hide a hit), and **re-run it after a rebase**, since an inbound reference can arrive from a branch that
merged after the removal was reviewed.

## Applied — ten retired whole, each against a home I read rather than assumed

| Retired entry | Where the lesson already lives | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| the venue seam is the safety boundary | `AGENTS.md` non-negotiable #1 (auto-loads, near-verbatim), ADR-0002, Coding contract's two-runs rule | contracted |
| never `git merge develop` (29 lines) | `CONTRIBUTING.md` §*Falling behind* — both symptom strings, the rebase, the *Update branch* default, the Dependabot disownment, the promotion exception; `branch-policy.yml:116-141` prints the remedy; `platform.md` the rationale | caught + contracted |
| absent dependencies degrade, not crash | ADR-0007 decision log *Update (2026-08-22)*, `architecture.md:319` — the entry announced its own promotion in 2026-08 and never left | contracted |
| `dotnet ef` fights the style rules | `.editorconfig:118-134` — the exemption, the reasoning and the BOM note; with the exemption in place nobody meets the problem, so there is no recovery to keep | prevented |
| App Control blocks `dotnet test` (2026-08-22) | `docker-compose.dev.yml`'s header (both commands + the SAC rationale); and the 2026-08-23 entry already corrected its compose form | superseded + caught |
| the integration tier does not run locally | false since 2026-08-23, and that entry names *this* one as what nearly shipped a migration nothing had applied | superseded |
| full `decimal` vs `numeric(18,8)` | ADR-0006 states the general form verbatim, "worth carrying to the next `numeric(18,8)` column" | contracted |
| test the composition root | `CompositionRootTests.cs` XML remarks — the captive dependency, why no other test could catch it, why it only reproduces configured | caught |
| register the MCP tool types | `CompositionRootTests.cs`'s theory over all five tool types, whose comment carries the per-call activation mechanism | caught |
| published is not released | ADR-0003 — *"tag versus feed"*, and the entry already pointed there | contracted |

**Five trimmed to the half that had no home:** the MCP filter entry keeps the SDK call and the test seam
(`architecture.md:111` states the rule); the indicator entry keeps how to *choose* the series (the Coding
contract states the rest); the ProjectX entry keeps the next-bump practice; the `.worktrees` entry drops three
cross-repo PR states this repository cannot keep true; and **the `gh pr checks` entry keeps its two commands**
— see the round-2 section below.

**Four prose repairs the removals required** — docs in lockstep: the 2026-08-23 Docker entry said *"the
entries below"*, and `platform.md:666` said the `AGENT-MEMORY.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md` entries are both the
floor; both now name what survives. The third is `CONTRIBUTING.md`'s, below. **The fourth arrived with the
round-3 rebase**, because #284's new entry pointed at an entry this PR retires — see the round-3 section.

## Round 2 — the blocking finding, and why I took the *first* of the two offered fixes

The review was right: the `gh pr checks` entry was classified **Enforced** against `cancel-in-progress: false`,
and a preventive setting neither fails nor emits output, so it met neither clause of the rule this PR itself
introduces. Its two actionable commands left the tree with it. **Re-measured rather than taken on trust:**
`gh run rerun` has 1 hit at `fecc463` and **0** at `9654a5e`; `statusCheckRollup` survives at `9654a5e` only at
`platform.md:485-486` and `:722`, cited in both places for the opposite point.

Two fixes were offered and the reviewer preferred the second — move the commands into the two concurrency
comments. **I took the first, on the reviewer's own test.** The stated objection to the current state was that
the comment *"is reachable only by someone already reading the file that prevents the problem — never by
someone holding the symptom"*. Moving the commands **into that same comment does not change who reaches it**:
an agent whose merge is blocked while `gh pr checks` shows green has no route to `ci.yml`. And a YAML comment
is not *output* — the Enforced clause asks the mechanism to name the remedy **when it fires**, and a setting
that prevents the mistake never fires — so option 2 would not have made that clause true either.

So the recovery stays in the one document every agent reads before every task, cut to the half with no home.
**A trim in content, not in bytes, and the measurement says so: 446 bytes at `fecc463`, 503 here.** What went
is the gh#25 narrative and the *"should not recur"* reassurance, both of which the concurrency comments carry
better. What arrived is the sentence that justifies the entry's own survival — a prevention emits no output,
and a required check cancelled *any other way* still lands you here. The reviewer's own narrowing is what
makes that the load-bearing half: all nine required contexts come from guarded workflows, so the gh#25
**mechanism** is genuinely closed; it is the **recovery** that was los

author: 2002bishwajeet
body:
Closes #1349.

## Step 1 — reproduced first, and the issue's hypothesis was wrong

Reproduced on a Redmi Note 5 Pro (Android 11) with a real owner-console revoke of the debug build's registration. The issue suspected a crash loop. **There is no crash** — the app is worse than that: it is permanently and silently stuck in a false "logged in" state.

```
E WebSocket: WS[2] connect loop caught exception:
  Handshake exception, expected status code 101 but was 401
io.ktor.client.plugins.websocket.WebSocketException: ...but was 401
    at io.ktor.client.plugins.websocket.WebSockets$Plugin$install$2.invokeSuspend(WebSockets.kt:233)
W WebSocket: WS[2] disconnected, retrying in 5000ms

I AuthLifecycle: AuthCC: SNAPSHOT[onConnectError] authState=Authenticated
  isConnecting=false isConnected=false dsmRunning=true
  driveStatuses={...all 9 drives: Completed}
```

64 handshake 401s and 40+ `UnauthorizedException`s in one window, zero new crash tombstones, same PID throughout, and a clean cold start straight back into the same state.

| Issue's claim | Reality |
|---|---|
| "only 2 scopes carry a `CoroutineExceptionHandler`; an unwrapped throw is fatal" | Inaccurate. `supervisedScope()` (`CoroutineExceptionHandlers.kt:52-56`) bakes one into 11 more scopes. The sync engine, outbox, and own-identity WS are all protected — which is exactly why it churns instead of crashing. |
| "crashes in an endless loop" | No crash. `Process.killProcess` is never reached. |
| WS reconnect-loops forever | Confirmed — steady 5s cadence, indefinitely. |
| No 401→logout path | Confirmed. `UnauthorizedException` has two references in the whole tree: its declaration and its throw site (`OdinApiProviderBase.kt:543`). |

## The fix

Count **consecutive** WS upgrade-401s in `AuthConnectionCoordinator.onConnectError` and log out at three via `youAuthFlowManager.logout(force = true)`.

`force = true` matters: the non-forced path calls `POST /auth/logout` first, which would itself 401 — a dead token would fail its own logout.

### Corroboration is repetition, not a second endpoint

The issue suggested verifying with `YouAuthProvider.hasValidToken()`. **That function is a booby trap and must not be used as-is**: it calls `httpClient.get(".../verifytoken")` with no `bearerAuth`, and `HttpClientProvider` installs no `Auth` plugin — so it returns `false` unconditionally and would log out every user on the first call. It has zero callers, which is the only reason nobody has been bitten.

Three consecutive upgrade-401s are already three separate server responses that each specifically rejected this token — same evidentiary strength, no new network code. Any success or non-401 failure resets the count:

| Scenario | What the WS throws | Counter |
|---|---|---|
| Offline / airplane mode | `UnknownHostException` | reset to 0 |
| Server down | `ConnectException` / timeout | reset to 0 |
| 502/503 (deploy, proxy restart) | `WebSocketException("…but was 502")` or raw `ProtocolException` | reset to 0 |
| TLS failure, captive portal | `SSLHandshakeException` | reset to 0 |
| **Token revoked** | `WebSocketException("…but was 401")` ×3 | fires |

An offline device can never trip it, and the logout itself needs no network.

### Two supporting fixes, both required to reach a genuinely quiet logged-out state

**Clear `lastAuthenticatedDrives` on `Unauthenticated`.** It gates `applyWsHold`'s `authResolved` check and was never cleared, so a foreground transition after logout rebuilt a WS with no credentials — and `connectOnce()` *returns false* rather than throwing, so the loop backed off and retried `"No active credentials"` forever at the 5s ceiling. Pre-existing; manual logout hits it too.

**Run the logout on `Dispatchers.Main.immediate`.** `logout()` flips `authState`, which makes this class close the Koin identity scope; `AppNavHost`'s body resolves five identity-scoped ViewModels *outside* its `isAuthenticated` gate. Off the main dispatcher a recomposition lands between the flip and the close and dies:

```
FATAL EXCEPTION: main
java.lang.IllegalStateException: Can't get Koin scope. Scope '['identity:…']' is closed
	at org.koin.compose.KoinApplicationKt.currentKoinScope(KoinApplication.kt:113)
	at id.homebase.core.ui.navigation.AppNavHostKt.AppNavHost(AppNavHost.kt:…)
```

Both existing callers already log out from `viewModelScope` (`Main.immediate`), so this matches an invariant the codebase already relies on — it is not a delay or a swallowed exception. The underlying gap (ungated resolutions in `AppNavHost`) is filed as #1373.

## Ktor coupling, and why it fails loudly

`WebSocketException` carries no status — the 401 survives only inside the message. OkHttp and Darwin both special-case 401 (KTOR-7363) so it arrives as that exception rather than a raw engine error the way 403/500 do; CIO produces it for any non-101. `DeadTokenLogoutTest` pins the exact wording captured on-device, so a Ktor upgrade that reworded it fails the build instead of silently disabling the logout.

## Verification

Unit — 8 tests in `DeadTokenLogoutTest`, covering the real Ktor message, non-matching of the `101`/`403`/`502` variants, wrapped and cyclic cause chains, and the threshold behaviour (including a 10-round transient-churn loop that must never log out). `WebSocketHoldPolicyTest:59` already covered the hold-policy half.

Builds — `homebase-api` + `homebase-common` JVM suites green; compiles on JVM, Android, iosSimulatorArm64, wasmJs.

Device, on a real revoke:
- Logout fires after 3 consecutive 401s → `onAuthStateChanged(Unauthenticated)` → `disconnect() end (wsClient nulled)` → `SessionEnded` → login screen.
- Process survives (same PID before/after), 0 `FATAL EXCEPTION`, 0 Koin ISE, no new tombstone.
- WS goes quiet after logout — no rebuilt client, 0 `"cannot connect"` lines.
- 60s in airplane mode: 5 × `UnknownHostException`, 0 logouts. Reconnects cleanly on restore.
- Re-login on the same process works, confirming the latch reset.

## Not included

- `OutboxFailureClassifier` has no 401 case, so a 401 burns the ~48h retry budget. Irrelevant here — `logout()` calls `clearStorage()` → `wipeAndRecreate()`, which destroys the outbox table, so those rows never survive to retry.
- 403 handling untouched: a revoked drive ACL still unmounts that one drive for the session.

author: hellohidi
body:
Refs #32

## Material change
- Replace hard industry/region filtering with an explainable weighted score and deterministic descending ranking.
- Recognize parent-province matches and retain explicit women-only and inferred tenure mismatches as hard exclusions.
- Produce up to 35 authoring recommendations with 20 business, 10 voucher, and up to 5 IP candidates; exclude certification and fill unused IP capacity from business/voucher.
- Preserve fixed A4 row ceilings by auto-placing only the highest-ranked fitting candidates.
- Show rank, score, scoring reasons, and placement availability in the authoring UI.

## Pre-merge checks
- `npm test` — passed (108 tests)
- `npm run build` — passed
- `npm run test:sites` — passed (17 tests)
- `git diff --check` — passed
- Browser QA — passed with a mocked 35-record catalog; recommendation count, scores, reasons, and filled-row states rendered correctly.

## Deployment considerations
- No database migration or binding change.
- Private Sites deployment must use the exact squash-merged `origin/master` SHA.
- Public/shared deployment is out of scope.

## Sourcery 摘要

支持在 Android 物理设备上运行游戏自动化，同时新增部署所需的设备配置、输入、显示管理、文档以及可选的 Web 控制台功能。

新功能：
- 支持 NKAS 在 Android 物理设备上运行游戏自动化，包括可配置的设备检测、分辨率处理、ADB 截图以及多种输入控制方式。
- 添加用于选择 ADB 设备和管理物理设备显示分辨率的 Web 界面。
- 添加可选启用且限制主机访问的 Web 控制台，用于运行本地 Shell 命令并实时显示输出。
- 提供物理设备使用文档和公告，并更新受支持平台的说明及问题反馈选项。

错误修复：
- 通过选定的控制方式处理基于坐标的点击、长按和拖动操作，使现有自动化任务能够在受支持的设备类型上正常运行。
- 在实例停止或退出时恢复物理设备的显示设置，并在 UI 中提供手动分辨率控制功能。

改进：
- 扩展模拟器配置，支持 ADB 截图、uiautomator2、ADB 和 MaaTouch 控制选项，同时减少重复的截图日志记录。

构建：
- 刷新已提交的 Web UI 资源，并在前端构建期间移除过时的生成文件包。

部署：
- 添加用于启用 Web 控制台并限制其允许访问主机的部署设置。

文档：
- 更新中文、英文和日文文档，说明对 PC、ARM 模拟器和 Android 物理设备的支持。
- 添加物理设备设置指南以及相关的 DroidCast/OCR 文档。

杂项：
- 删除已废弃的导出 Kimi 会话文档。

author: lajay06
body:
## The question this answers

*Does the publish backstop resolve an ambiguous derived address?*

**It did not.** `togglePublish` wrote `websiteEnabled` and swept guest tokens. Nothing touched the slug. The three-layer claim design's publish backstop lived on the claim path, and #594 repointed that path at derivation — so the backstop stopped being reached without anyone removing it.

## Why "it converges on the next load" was not good enough

Convergence that requires a visit is not convergence for a couple who does not visit. The harmful case is precisely a couple who publishes, sends invitations, and never returns — their address stays contested while the links are already out.

**Guests only exist after publish.** So publish is where the window closes: the address a guest is ever given has already been settled, and the tie-break has already decided who moves.

`await`ed, and before enabling only. The point is certainty at the moment the site becomes shareable.

## Prior art

The publish-time guest token sweep directly above it — same handler, same reasoning: publishing is the moment the site becomes something a guest can arrive at, so that is where the safety net belongs.

## Two defects from #594, both mine

**An empty `useEffect`.** Removing `setSlugInput` by regex left `useEffect(() => {}, [details?.slug])` behind — dead code that lint does not flag. This is the mechanical-substitution rule again: the replacement was correct and what it left behind was not.

**Copy pointing at a control that no longer exists.** The status line read *"Set a URL below before publishing"* — and after #594 there is nothing below to set. Documentation is a surface, and so is product chrome. It now says *"Add your names in Event details to get your address"*, which is both true and actionable.

## The guard

A fifth case in `test:slug-claim` — **publish-settles** — asserting `togglePublish` awaits `syncWeddingAddress` before the site is enabled, not merely that it calls it somewhere.

## Checks

`build` exit 0 · `test:ci` **1283/1283** · `test:slug-claim` 24/24 · `test:couple-names` · `test:marketing-routes` 14/14 · `lint` clean.

body:
## מה קרה

אחרי משיכת הגרסה `7f4f4e8` ה-API קורס בלולאה מיד אחרי המיגרציות:

```
Error: Cannot find module 'express'
Require stack: /app/dist/main.js
```

וכל המערכת מחזירה 502.

## למה

קוד קליטת המייל מייבא את `express` ישירות — `import { json } from "express"` ב-`main.ts` (מפרק ה-40MB לנתיב הוובהוק הנכנס) — אבל `express` לא הוצהר בתלויות של ה-API; הוא הגיע בעקיפין דרך `@nestjs/platform-express`.

בפיתוח וב-CI זה עובד: pnpm מתקין את כל העץ ו-node מוצא את החבילה בטיפוס למעלה. **בתמונת הפרודקשן** — `pnpm deploy --prod` ב-Dockerfile — מותקנות רק תלויות מוצהרות, ושם הייבוא נופל. לכן כל השערים היו ירוקים והשרת נפל: אין שער שבודק את העץ הפרוס.

## התיקון

שורה אחת: `"express": "^5.2.1"` (הגרסה שכבר בנעילה דרך NestJS) + עדכון lockfile.

## איך אומת

בדיוק באותה דרך שהתמונה נבנית: `pnpm deploy --prod --legacy` מקומי, ואז סריקה שכל ייבוא חבילה בקוד ה-API (16 מזהים) נפתר בתוך העץ הפרוס. `typecheck` והבדיקות ירוקים.

## אחרי המיזוג

CI בונה תמונות מתוקנות (~8 דקות), ואז בשרת: `docker compose pull api web workers` + `up -d --no-deps --force-recreate api web workers`, או הכפתור ב-`/platform`.
