author: febbryandika
body:
Follow-up to #7.

## Why

The README cited `SPEC 1.3`, `7`, `8`, `11` and `15` in six places — but `SPEC.md` is a private planning doc and is gitignored, so every one of those references was a dead end for the only audience the README has. `.gitignore` already reserved `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` as a tracked deliverable; this fills it in and links the six citations to real anchors.

## What

`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` is the public version of the reasoning, not a copy of SPEC:

- **The shape**, and why the API is a separate process — the honest version, including that a single Next app is a legitimate choice and what specifically ruled it out
- **What MediaMTX owns vs what the app owns** — auth, timeline arithmetic, honesty about gaps
- **The media pipeline** — two paths per camera, 10-minute segments, and the `yard_sub` dev-source finding from #7 (MediaMTX splits path names on `_`, so no `MTX_PATHS_*` var can address it)
- **The trust boundary** — loopback publishing, the RTSP-path-is-a-password-hash problem, WHEP session ownership — plus the `Location` failure written up in one place
- **Timeline, gaps, and coverage** — the four ways the naive model breaks, the 2-second tolerance, the epoch-ms rule
- **Testing**, and **what this deliberately does not do** with reasons

Sections describing unbuilt work say so, and a status note at the top marks the line between shipped and designed, so the doc does not imply the timeline exists yet.

## Scope

**Code comments still cite SPEC.** That convention is ~100 references deep across four phases and is aimed at whoever is editing the file, not at a reader of the repo. Churning it here would touch a lot of files this branch has no business in — happy to do it separately if you want.

## Test plan

- All 8 internal anchors validated programmatically against the headings actually present in `ARCHITECTURE.md` — 0 dead links (5 from the README, 3 within the doc).
- `grep 'SPEC' README.md` → no matches remaining.
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` confirmed tracked, not caught by the `docs/*` ignore rule.

Docs-only — no code, config, or test changes.

author: tomaz-cvetko
body:
# Brief

Fix the issue where renderer FB displayed garbled points when sample type changed (float32 <-> float64) during operation.

# Description

Renderer used to assume the latest descriptor described all data points being drawn. This is false when descriptors change. Especially for the case where the width of the single sample value changed, the result was a garbled graph (random lines due to incorrect casting).

To fix that, use descriptor of each packet to draw the line by casting to the provided per-packet type.

Similar fix was applied for the domain. Although with domain it is expected to be significantly fewer occurences of this phenomenon (changing width of the domain sample affects the duration from origin that can be covered by the ticks). Additionally, this issue may have arisen only for explicit data rules, otherwise the ticks were computed from a rule in a correct manner.

author: weiwutichai
body:
Root-caused the "every page loads slowly / laggy" report (read-only sweep → **19 causes**, 8 high) and fixed them all. Review doc kept local.

## Mobile
- **Stale-while-revalidate** — ~16 screens showed a full-screen spinner on open/re-entry; now render chrome + last-known value (`.valueOrNull`) + a light skeleton (`pg_skeleton`). No more blanking.
- **Parallelize** — `guard_jobs` fires `/bookings` + `/bookings/open` concurrently; profile/avatar controllers no longer chain `/auth/me` → next call serially.
- **Kill duplicate `/auth/me`** — avatar/profile/documents controllers read the id from the session instead of a round-trip.
- **Images** — new `PgNetworkImage` (`cached_network_image`): disk cache + downsize to display px + a stable cache key that strips the presigned query (re-mint = cache hit). Replaced 13 raw `Image.network` sites.
- **Cold start** — `runApp` immediately after `ensureInitialized`; Firebase + local-notif init moved post-first-frame.
- **Discovery** — fire `/available-guards` immediately (server order) instead of blocking up to 10s on a GPS fix, then re-sort nearest when it arrives; poll 25s→12s + an "updating…" affordance.
- **Auth interceptor** caches the decoded token in memory (no Keychain read per request); interactive GETs get a shorter receive timeout.

## Backend (`/available-guards` was the dominant cost)
- **rating** — new `POST /internal/guards/rating-summaries` (one grouped query): booking's per-guard rating **N+1** (N HTTP + N JWT mints) collapses to **1** call.
- **booking** — the 3 upstream reads (profile catalog / busy DB / presence) now run **concurrently** (`tokio::join!`) instead of 3 serial awaits; fail-open/closed preserved.
- **identity** — `/auth/me` runs its 2 DB reads + the profile pending-roles HTTP concurrently.
- **profile** — composite index `(approval_status, created_at DESC, user_id DESC)` → index scan, no sort (mig 0014).

<!--
# nf-core/metatdenovo pull request

Many thanks for contributing to nf-core/metatdenovo!

Please fill in the appropriate checklist below (delete whatever is not relevant).
These are the most common things requested on pull requests (PRs).

Remember that PRs should be made against the dev branch, unless you're preparing a pipeline release.

Learn more about contributing: [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/nf-core/metatdenovo/tree/master/docs/CONTRIBUTING.md)
-->

## PR checklist

- [x] This comment contains a description of changes (with reason).
- [x] If you've fixed a bug or added code that should be tested, add tests!
- [ ] If you've added a new tool - have you followed the pipeline conventions in the [contribution docs](https://github.com/nf-core/metatdenovo/tree/master/docs/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [ ] If necessary, also make a PR on the nf-core/metatdenovo _branch_ on the [nf-core/test-datasets](https://github.com/nf-core/test-datasets) repository.
- [x] Make sure your code lints (`nf-core pipelines lint`).
- [x] Ensure the test suite passes (`nextflow run . -profile test,docker --outdir <OUTDIR>`).
- [ ] Check for unexpected warnings in debug mode (`nextflow run . -profile debug,test,docker --outdir <OUTDIR>`).
- [ ] Usage Documentation in `docs/usage.md` is updated.
- [ ] Output Documentation in `docs/output.md` is updated.
- [x] `CHANGELOG.md` is updated.
- [ ] `README.md` is updated (including new tool citations and authors/contributors).

## Description

Closes #477.

`TRANSDECODER_PREDICT` could never resume, and its re-execution always failed. Full analysis and reproduction in #477 and the upstream report, [nf-core/modules#12799](https://github.com/nf-core/modules/issues/12799).

Short version: `TransDecoder.Predict` writes its checkpoint directory into the LongOrfs directory it receives as a staged input, which belongs to a different task's (`TRANSDECODER_LONGORF`'s) work directory. So the task mutates its own input and stops being cacheable, and when Nextflow re-executes it the task directory is wiped while the checkpoints -- living in the LongOrfs task's directory -- are not. `TransDecoder.Predict` then skips every step, including the ones that write the outputs, and exits 0 with nothing produced.

This PR pulls in the fix, merged upstream in [nf-core/modules#12829](https://github.com/nf-core/modules/pull/12829): `nf-core modules update transdecoder/predict --no-preview`. The module now gives Predict a private, writable directory of symlinks to the same files, instead of writing through the staged symlink into another task's directory.

### Testing

- `tests/metaeuk_transdecoder.nf.test` passes unmodified against the existing committed snapshot -- output content is unchanged.
- Reproduced the bug and verified the fix directly against this pipeline, not just the module in isolation: ran `-profile test,docker --outdir <dir> --orf_caller transdecoder`, then the same command with `-resume`.
  - **Before this fix:** `TRANSDECODER_PREDICT` fails on resume with `Missing output file(s) '*.transdecoder.pep'`, exit status 0 -- exactly as described in #477.
  - **After this fix:** the trace report shows `TRANSDECODER:TRANSDECODER_PREDICT` as `CACHED`, and the whole pipeline resumes cleanly.
- `nf-core pipelines lint` and `prek run -a`: clean (one pre-existing, unrelated bioconda-version warning on the module itself, 5.7.1 -> 6.0.0 available, left untouched -- out of scope for this fix).

Isolated from #479 (the in-review protein-consolidation PR) -- branched off `dev` rather than `issue-460-protein-consolidation`, and touches only the vendored `transdecoder/predict` module, `modules.json`, and the changelog, so it should merge independently without conflict.

author: victormico
body:
## Per què

El paperam que un arxiu et fa presentar —una **instància** per una llei de procediment, i la **contestació** que diu què han trobat i què no— no tenia cap `tipus` on anar. Els dos que semblen a mà no hi encaixen:

- **`transcripcio`** diu que s'està transcrivint una cosa històrica. Ací el document és d'enguany, produït o rebut per nosaltres, no llegit d'un llibre.
- **`recerca`** diu que algú va deduir alguna cosa. Ací el que es guarda és **què es va demanar, quin dia, amb quina referència, i què va tornar**.

Presentar-ne una és sovint l'única via per arribar a un registre, o siga que la petició i la resposta valen la pena **tant si troben res com si no**: un «no en tenim d'aquells anys» és un resultat, i la fitxa és el que evita tornar-ho a demanar.

## D'on ve

Del cas de l'expòsit d'Albacete ([victormico/genealogia#44](https://github.com/victormico/genealogia/pull/44)), on la instància a la Diputació i la seva contestació sortien a `tools.lint --frontmatter` com a tipus inventat:

```
Fonts/…/Contestacion_SEFYCU_6131258.md	tipus 'tramit' no és dels declarats
Fonts/…/Instancia_2358005_Consulta_1909.md	tipus 'tramit' no és dels declarats
```

## Comprovat

Amb **instal·lació no editable**, que és la que corre a la CI, sobre l'arbre de `genealogia` amb la #44 fusionada:

| | Avisos de `--frontmatter` |
|---|---|
| `main` | 78 |
| amb la #44 | **78** |

O siga que amb això aquella PR **no n'afegeix cap de nou**.

La prova nova fixa les dues bandes —que «tramit» s'accepta i que «instancia», que no és del vocabulari, es continua rebutjant— perquè això sigui una entrada al vocabulari i no un forat. 13/13 mòduls de proves i 7/7 `tools.lint` verds.

author: aanm
body:
The tunnel id carries the source security identity to the peer node and
is only 24 bits wide, since overloadable_skb.h and overloadable_xdp.h
write get_tunnel_id(seclabel) into the VXLAN or Geneve VNI. A node-local
identity does not fit there, so its scope byte is silently truncated and
the peer decodes an unrelated identity.

The from-host encap path forwards whatever the ipcache holds for the
source address, which for external traffic can be a CIDR or a toFQDNs
identity. The first local identity a node allocates is 0x01000001, which
arrives as HOST_ID and cil_from_overlay drops it as
DROP_INVALID_IDENTITY. That is how CI found this, as four INGRESS
"Invalid identity" drops in the egress gateway L7 test. Truncation also
aliases onto REMOTE_NODE_ID, WORLD_ID and INGRESS_ID, and onto real
endpoint identities once a node holds more than 256 local ones, so the
peer can just as well enforce the wrong ingress policy with no drop.

Collapse local identities in get_tunnel_id(), the only place a tunnel id
is derived from a security identity. Remote node scope becomes
REMOTE_NODE_ID, which the receiver refines from its own ipcache anyway,
and the rest becomes WORLD_ID, which is what identity_is_world() already
classifies a CIDR identity as and what the egress gateway reply redirect
puts on the wire itself. That loses precision for the CIDR scope, but
the peer never had a usable identity there to begin with.

```release-note
Fix dropped and misclassified tunneled traffic whose source address holds a node-local CIDR or FQDN identity
```

author: juresavron
body:
Six pools, photographed the same way by the same supplier, and every gallery opened on a different kind of picture: a top-down view on one model, a close-up of a jet on the next. Somebody comparing two of them had to learn each gallery instead of comparing like with like. Nobody had told the software what the categories were.

So the model that already looks at every photograph to write its description is asked a second question **in the same call** — what is this a picture *of*, from a fixed list — and the panel renumbers the set by the answer.

## The order

`src/admin/shots.ts` holds the vocabulary and, more to the point, the **order**. That order is editorial rather than technical and is meant to be argued with. It runs from what the thing *is* to what it is *like*:

`top` → `side` → `lit` → `cover` → `interior` → `seat` → `jets` → `other`

The whole object from above and from the side first, because that is what somebody choosing between models needs; then lit and covered; then inside; then the details that only matter to someone already interested. Moving one entry in that array reorders every gallery in the shop at the next arrange, and nothing else changes.

Keys are English, labels Slovenian. A key goes into a database constraint and a prompt, and an identifier that changes when somebody improves a translation is a migration nobody asked for.

## The guards

- **Idempotent.** Ties keep the order they already had, so two interior shots do not swap on every press, and an already-sorted gallery costs no database writes at all. That is what makes the button safe to press twice.
- **Unclassified sorts last**, in the order it had — not knowing what a photograph is must never promote it. `NULL` stays distinct from `other`, which is an answer rather than the absence of one.
- **Batches of six.** Three subrequests per photograph against a Worker's budget means a model with thirty would blow it and fail having done nothing. Instead it places a few, keeps the progress, reorders what it knows, and says how many are left.
- **Looks at the 800px rung, not the 2K one.** "Whole tub or close-up of a seat" is not a question detail answers; reading thirty 2K files through a Worker to ask it is bandwidth, CPU and tokens spent on pixels that change no answer.

## The response schema is an improvement, not a requirement

Constrained decoding is what makes the category reliable, but it is newer than some models in the fallback list, and an unsupporting one answers 400 rather than ignoring the field. Were that the only attempt, the day a model was retired would be the day every upload lost its **description** as well as its category — trading the alt text, which works today and is worth more, for the sorting, which is new.

So it tries every model *with* the schema, then every model *without*, and a bare sentence is still read as a description with no category.

251 tests pass, `tsc --noEmit` clean, both audits at 0 errors, 8 browser upload cases green.

body:
# What this changes

The commands a learner actually types now reach the host: `journal.Collector`
reads the in-sandbox `journal.tsv`, `game.JournalSink` appends each record to the
`events` table and publishes one `CommandExecuted` per record, and
`pty.CommandEvent` gains `UsedTab`. That is what the efficiency bonus and four
achievements need, which have been reading zeroes.

Neither the collector nor the sink is wired into the orchestrator. This ticket
builds them as independently testable units, exactly as issue #123 scopes it; the
wiring is a later Day 4 task, the same way the bus package landed.

## Review round: what changed since the reviewed commit

`reviewed_sha` is `5d8e69c729a47a5a9974c23dc38edd1a4ba71859`.
`merged_sha` is `05160750f184a1d970ab21f8e5bc9bc04d548f75`.

Seven review findings, addressed in one follow-up commit. Nothing else changed
between the two SHAs.

1. **BLOCKING, fixed:** `Collector.Since` kept a stale `c.offset` after
   `journal.tsv` shrank under it. Once the file grew back past that value, the
   next read started mid-record and `ReadTSV` was handed whatever four tab
   separated fields happened to land there, silently dropping every command
   written since the shrink or admitting a garbled row. `Since` now resets the
   offset to 0 on that branch and re-syncs from byte 0 of the new content.
   `Collector` gained an explicit lifetime rule in its doc comment: one per
   attempt, never carried across a level reset.
   `TestSinceResyncsFromTheStartWhenTheJournalRegrowsAfterAShrink` is new and
   collects zero of four commands with the one-line reset removed.
2. **BLOCKING, disclosed rather than coded around:** `Duration` is always zero on
   this path, so acceptance criterion 1's "durations" clause is unmet on its
   literal wording. It is now a fourth named contract decision below, in
   `PROGRESS.md`, and at the call site, with
   `TestDrainPublishesAZeroDurationForEveryTSVRecord` pinning the zero.
3. **Question, doc tightened:** `maxRecordsPerSince` bounds parsing, not the
   `PullFile` read. Its doc comment now says so in its first sentence, and the
   whole-file read stays a `TODO(v0.2)` because a ranged read is a
   `runtime.Session` interface change.
4. **Suggestion, applied:** `NewCollector` now returns `(*Collector, error)` and
   refuses a `stateDir` that is empty, relative, carries a `..` segment, or sits
   outside `platform.LearnerHomePrefix`, through the same
   `platform.UnsafeLevelRoot` that `internal/content/setup` puts the same value
   through. `internal/platform` is L0, so the import points downward and
   `archtest` needed no table edit.
5. **Question, test added:**
   `TestDrainLosesTheRestOfTheBatchWhenAnAppendFailsPartWayThrough` fails the
   second of three appends and asserts a later `Drain` never sees the lost two
   again. It pins the documented trade-off; it does not change the behaviour.
6. **Nit, applied:** `Drain`'s doc comment no longer says "simply".
7. **Suggestion, applied:** both `TestDrainDegradesToZeroCommands...` tests now
   count `PullFile` calls and require exactly one. A `Drain` that did nothing at
   all used to pass them; it now fails both.

## Type

- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] New level or content change
- [x] Engine feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Build, CI, or tooling

Documentation is unticked as a primary type, but `PROGRESS.md` and
`docs/04-how-it-works.md` are updated in the same branch.

## Checklist

- [x] `gofmt -s -w .` applied
- [x] `go vet ./...` clean
- [x] `go test ./...` and `go test -race ./...` pass
- [x] `./scripts/check-punctuation.sh` passes (no em dash, no en dash, no smart quotes)
- [x] Layer test still passes (`go test ./internal/archtest/...`)
- [x] No new dependency, or I asked first and the answer was yes
- [ ] Any new user-facing error has a remediation and a doc anchor that exists
- [ ] Any new subprocess call uses argv form and validates interpolated identifiers

The last two are unticked because neither applies: this change adds no
user-facing error at all (a missing or unreadable `journal.tsv` degrades
silently to zero commands and must never reach the learner, so nothing here
reaches `ux.Fail` and no new `DocAnchor` exists), and it spawns no subprocess
(the collector's only sandbox call is `runtime.Session.PullFile`).
`NewCollector`'s new refusal is a construction-time error returned to whoever
wires the sink up, not a message a learner can reach.

## If this touches the level format

Not applicable: no level schema change and no new check type, so
`docs/LEVEL-FORMAT.md` is deliberately untouched.

- [ ] `docs/LEVEL-FORMAT.md` updated in this same commit
- [ ] If a check type was added: registered, tested, and documented in the catalogue

## If this adds or changes a level

Not applicable: no level is added or changed.

- [ ] `shellforge author validate` passes
- [ ] `shellforge author test` passes: checks fail before the solution, pass after, teardown leaves nothing
- [ ] Every check has a specific, actionable `on_fail`
- [ ] Setup is deterministic and makes no network calls
- [ ] At least two hints, escalating
- [ ] I tried to pass it the wrong way and it rejected me
- [ ] I did not loosen a check to make the solution pass

## Platforms exercised

- [x] Linux
- [ ] Windows
- [ ] macOS (community supported)

Windows and macOS are unticked because this environment has neither. Nothing
here is platform specific: no syscall, no console mode, and the one path
construction uses `path.Join` rather than `filepath.Join` precisely so a Windows
host builds the same Linux path inside the sandbox. `platform.UnsafeLevelRoot`,
new to this path in the review round, uses `path` for the same reason and says
so in its own doc comment. CI's Windows leg is the witness.

## What was built

- `internal/journal/collector.go`: `Collector`,
  `NewCollector(runtime.Session, stateDir) (*Collector, error)`,
  `Since(ctx, levelID)`. One `PullFile` of
  `path.Join(stateDir, "journal.tsv")`, parsed by the existing `ReadTSV`. No
  second channel, and no OSC event correlated with a TSV row by index.
- `internal/game/journalsink.go`: `JournalSink`, `NewJournalSink`,
  `Drain(ctx, levelID, attemptID)`.
- `internal/pty/mux.go`: `CommandEvent.UsedTab` plus the `tabTap` reader that
  feeds it, wrapping host stdin inside `Run`'s existing `io.Copy`. It flags byte
  `0x09` as it passes and forwards every byte unchanged; `onOSCEvent`'s
  `PreExec` case reads and clears the flag with one `atomic.Bool` swap, because
  the stdin copy goroutine writes it and the OSC goroutine reads it.

Layers: `internal/journal` (L2) importing `internal/runtime` (L1) is downward,
and `internal/runtime` is the interface package, never an implementation.
`internal/journal` importing `internal/platform` (L0) is downward.
`internal/game` (L4) importing `internal/journal` (L2) is downward.
`internal/archtest` needed no table edit and none was made.

## Contract decisions taken in this run

**`Append` did not need a batch form, and did not get one.** `Drain` appends one
row at a time so that a publish follows exactly the appends that succeeded. A
batch insert that half succeeded would either publish `CommandExecuted` for rows
that were never written or lose the ones that were, and "exactly one
`CommandExecuted` per appended entry" is an acceptance criterion. The write
volume is a handful of rows per check against a WAL database, so a transaction
per row costs nothing worth that risk. What it does cost is the rest of a batch
when one `Append` fails part way through, which
`TestDrainLosesTheRestOfTheBatchWhenAnAppendFailsPartWayThrough` now pins.

**`UsedTab` on every entry flowing through `JournalSink.Drain` is always false
today, and that is acceptable for this ticket's scope.** `instrument.bash`
writes four fields (`EPOCHREALTIME`, exit code, `PWD`, command line) and none of
them is a tab tap, so `ReadTSV` cannot know it and `Since` does not invent it. A

author: erschoenfeld2-tech
body:
## Summary

Addresses a Supabase Security Advisor finding about the `nutzer_public` view being a "Security Definer View" by adding schema qualification to the base table reference and documenting the deliberate security design decision.

## Changes

- **Recreate `nutzer_public` view** with explicit `public.nutzer` schema qualification in the SELECT clause (prevents theoretical `search_path` manipulation attacks)
- **Add comprehensive DB comment** to `nutzer_public` explaining why `security_invoker = false` is intentional and necessary:
  - The base `nutzer` table has no SELECT policy for anon/authenticated users (to protect `nfc_uid` from exposure via the public anon key)
  - The view must run with owner privileges to selectively expose only `id`, `name`, and `ist_admin`
  - Setting `security_invoker = true` would break login lookup and the nutzerMap in `index.html` (view would return 0 rows)
  - Reverting to a permissive policy on `nutzer` would re-expose `nfc_uid`
- **Cross-reference both migrations** in the comment to make the security rationale discoverable during future Advisor scans

## Implementation Details

This is a **hardening without behavior change**: the view's functionality remains identical, but the schema-qualified reference closes a theoretical attack surface and the comment marks this as a reviewed exception rather than an oversight. The design preserves the security boundary established in `20260821120000_harden_nutzer_exposure.sql` while satisfying the Advisor's recommendation for defense-in-depth.

author: dshah1333
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #6671.

`test_duplex_admission_and_expiry_reaper` times out on both CUDA and NPU:

```text
FAILED tests/e2e/online_serving/test_minicpmo_4_5_duplex_expansion.py::test_duplex_admission_and_expiry_reaper[three-stage-single-gpu] - TimeoutError
```

My read is the server is fine here and the test just carries a stale number.

The test hardcodes `verify_admission_limit = 2`, so the probe opens 2 sessions and waits for the 3rd to be rejected. #6619 repointed this test from `minicpmo_4_5_duplex.yaml`, which sets `duplex_session.max_sessions` to 2, to the shipping `minicpmo_4_5.yaml`, which sets it to 4. With room for 4 the 3rd session is admitted, no error event ever arrives, and `_receive_until` blocks until the timeout.

The capacity flows deploy yaml -> `omni_config.py:1424` -> `serving.py:916` -> `duplex_session.py:404`, and that last one only rejects once `len(_sessions) >= max_sessions`.

So this reads the limit from the deploy config the test starts the server with instead of hardcoding it. The number then lives in one place and a later capacity change can't turn into an unrelated probe timeout.

## Test Plan

**vLLM Version:** 0.27.0

**vLLM-Omni Commit:** a57246e4 (see the note under Test Result)

Served MiniCPM-o 4.5 on 1x H100 80GB from the unmodified shipping yaml, then ran the test's own `run_lifecycle_probes` admission probe at both limits:

```bash
vllm-omni serve openbmb/MiniCPM-o-4_5 --omni \
  --deploy-config vllm_omni/deploy/minicpmo_4_5.yaml \
  --trust-remote-code --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8099
```

```python
import asyncio, sys
sys.argv = ["drv", "--url", "ws://127.0.0.1:8099/v1/realtime?duplex=1",
            "--model", "openbmb/MiniCPM-o-4_5",
            "--input-wav", "tests/assets/minicpmo_4_5/response_required_16k.wav",
            "--ref-audio", "<ref_audio>.wav",
            "--verify-admission-limit", "2",   # then again with 4
            "--timeout-s", "40", "--output-dir", "/tmp/probe"]
from tests.e2e.online_serving.run_minicpmo_realtime_duplex_multi_session import (
    parse_args, run_lifecycle_probes)
print(asyncio.run(run_lifecycle_probes(parse_args())))
```

## Test Result

| probe limit | what it means | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2 | what the test hardcodes today | `TimeoutError`, same as #6671 |
| 4 | what the deploy yaml configures | `ok=True`, `overflow_error_code=resource_exhausted` |

Server log at the configured capacity:

```text
open_duplex_session rejected: duplex_session_capacity_exhausted: limit=4
error: {'code': 'resource_exhausted', 'message': 'duplex_session_capacity_exhausted: limit=4', 'retryable': True}
```

`ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass on the 3 changed files.

Two notes on how I validated this:

- I ran it on a57246e4 with vLLM 0.27.0 rather than current main, because main needs vLLM 0.28.0 and my box wasn't on it yet. The capacity check in `duplex_session.py` is identical between that commit and main, and the shipping yaml has `max_sessions: 4` in both, so I think the result carries over. Happy to rerun on main if you'd rather see that.
- The limit-4 arm needs a freshly started server. A probe that ends in a timeout leaves one accepted session alive until the reaper runs, which eats capacity and skews the next arm. That caught me the first time round.

author: jubacch
body:
Completes the UI half of the update orchestrator (#17).

## Problem

System → Update showed a single "Updating..." state, then went silent while the
backend restarted. An operator could not tell a slow build from a stuck one, and
a failed update gave no indication of *what* failed.

## What it does

Polls `GET /api/update/status` every 2 s and renders the orchestrator's step
list — which step is running, what each finished step reported, where it
stopped.

- **Failure banner** names the failing step *and* the database backup taken
  beforehand. That backup is the operator's escape hatch, so it must be visible
  exactly when things went wrong.
- **Restart gap**: the backend disappears mid-run, so a failed poll during the
  `restart` step is expected. It renders as "Backend restarting…" rather than an
  error, and polling continues until the new backend answers.
- **Resume**: a run started in another tab or before a reload is picked up on
  mount, so progress does not vanish when someone navigates away.

## Tests

The rendering rules live in `lib/updateSteps.ts` — framework-free, so they are
tested directly rather than through the DOM. 15 vitest tests cover the terminal
shapes (running, success, failure-with-backup), the restart gap, and label
fallbacks.

vitest is new to this frontend; it now runs in CI alongside typecheck and build.

author: venkat-uk
body:
## The bug

`api/plugin/v1` panics at package init on `main`, so every importer crashes on startup:

```
panic: runtime error: slice bounds out of range [-4:]
google.golang.org/protobuf/internal/filedesc.(*File).unmarshalSeed
github.com/mindfulcto-labs/apiloom-ce/api/plugin/v1.file_api_plugin_v1_plugin_proto_init()
```

That is the `controlplane-1 | panic` in compose-smoke and the failure of all of `examples/plugins`.

## Cause

The module rename in 4207d7d string-replaced the module path across the tree, including inside the serialised `file_api_plugin_v1_plugin_proto_rawDesc` in the generated `plugin.pb.go`.

A raw descriptor is a length-prefixed FileDescriptorProto. The `go_package` option carried:

```
B;   field 8 (options), 59 bytes
Z9   field 11 (go_package), 57 bytes
```

`github.com/flexgateway/flexgateway/api/plugin/v1;pluginv1` is exactly 57 bytes, so the file was correct when generated. The first rename made it 55, the second made it 60, and neither touched the prefixes. protobuf read 57 bytes as the string, then parsed the leftover 3 plus `b\x06proto3` as the next field, got a negative length, and panicked.

## Fix

The `.proto` was the root cause: its `go_package` still said `github.com/flexgateway/flexgateway/...`, so a plain regenerate would not have produced the right path either. That is presumably why both renames edited the generated file by hand.

Point the option at the current module and regenerate with protoc. The prefixes come out as `B>Z<`, 62 and 60, which match the new string.

## Testing plan

```
$ go test ./api/plugin/v1/ ./examples/plugins/... -count=1
ok  	.../api/plugin/v1                          0.351s
ok  	.../examples/plugins/custom-auth           0.361s
ok  	.../examples/plugins/response-transform    0.688s
ok  	.../examples/plugins/webhook               1.053s
```

All four panicked before this change.

`go build ./...`, `go vet ./api/... ./examples/...` and the full `go test ./...` are green: 35 packages ok, none failing.

## Not in this PR

CI has other failures that are unrelated to this crash and want separate changes:

- `lint`: a long list of errcheck, staticcheck `QF1012` and `unused` findings.
- `dependency-review`: fails because Dependency graph is not enabled in repository settings, which is a settings change rather than a code one.
- `secrets-scan`, `sast-gosec`, `web`: not yet diagnosed.

author: cyrilknops
body:
Follow-up to #6, which shipped the button as **Reset all** running
`docker compose down && up -d`.

That recreates every container in the project — a heavier operation than the
name suggests, and heavier than what the button was wanted for: bouncing a
stack that has wedged itself.

## What it does now

`docker compose restart` — the same thing the per-container **Restart** button
does, for a whole compose project. Containers keep their image, their volumes
and their identity; nothing is pulled, removed or recreated.

The trade-off is stated in the confirmation dialog and the README rather than
left to be discovered: a compose file edited since these containers were
created is **not** picked up by a restart. **Update** and **Save & apply** are
the buttons that reconcile a container with its file.

## Renamed throughout

| before | after |
|---|---|
| `POST /api/compose/reset` | `POST /api/compose/restart` |
| `compose.reset()` | `compose.restart()` |
| `resetSelfDetached()` | `restartSelfDetached()` |
| `SELF_RESET_SH` | `SELF_RESTART_SH` |
| `ConfirmReset.jsx` | `ConfirmRestart.jsx` |

## The self case gets simpler

A restart of the project containing kissd still has to be handed to the host —
restarting the project restarts kissd, which kills the request that asked for
it — but the detached script is now a plain `docker compose restart`.

The `down && up -d` version needed `up -d --force-recreate` there instead,
specifically so a detached run that died mid-teardown could not leave the whole
project stopped. With a restart there is no teardown to be caught halfway
through, so that special case and its explanation are gone from both the code
and the README.

## UI

The button loses its `danger` styling to match the per-container Restart — red
is Stop's colour on the container cards. It keeps its confirmation: one click
still bounces a whole stack, unlike the per-card button which only ever affects
the card it sits on.

Alert muting is unchanged and still applies: a restart takes containers down,
so the project is muted for the length of the run plus the settle grace.

## Verification

- `vite build` clean; every touched server module passes `node --check`.
- Against a running server: `/api/compose/reset` now returns 404,
  `/api/compose/restart` returns 200 and registers the project mute (the alert
  log note reads "A restart is running").
- Grepped the tree for surviving `reset` references — none outside an unrelated
  pre-existing comment in `auth.js`.

body:
## 何を変えたか

PR #454（マージ済み）で追加した GPM の MCP ツールに、マージ直前の敵対的レビューで見つかった3件を修正した。**#454 は私がレビュー指摘の修正を push する前にマージされてしまったため、指摘は main に未反映のまま残っていた。** 本PRでそれを埋める。

- **[P1・セキュリティ] `list_gpm_box_files` に GLS-B 確認を追加**。内部で使う `listProjectFolder` は案件（GLS-A）の BOX ファイル一覧とプロジェクト（GLS-B）のそれを共用しており `gls_category` を確認しない。このツールは読み取り専用のため権限ゲートが無く（`docs/mcp-server.md` に明記の既知の設計）、`id` に案件の id を渡すと**その案件の BOX フォルダの中身（取引先の書類）が読めてしまう**状態だった。`assertGpmProjectId` で確認するよう修正
- **[P2] `get_gpm_estimate` のエラー握りつぶしを修正**。`.catch(() => null)` が DB接続断のような無関係な失敗まで「見積が見つかりません」に変換し、`isError` も付かないため呼び出し側が失敗に気づけなかった。素の `throw` を `runTool` にそのまま処理させる形に変更
- **[P3] `PATCH /gpm/projects/:id/members/reorder`（HTTP）に形の確認を追加**。`id` が文字列でない・`sort_order` が数でない行を捨ててから渡すようにした（MCP 側の zod と同じ確認を HTTP 側にも）

## なぜ変えたか

PR #454 のマージ後、同PRに対して実施していたマルチエージェントの敵対的レビューが完了し、上記3件（うち1件はP1セキュリティ）が見つかった。修正コミットを push した直後に #454 がマージされており、main には未反映のまま取り残されていたため、本PRで追いかけて塞ぐ。

author: dwaynebailey
body:
## The raw Python 3 + GTK3 port (pioneer era)

First of two PRs (split from #3342, which GitHub's rebase-merge button
couldn't compute cleanly at 144 commits - confirmed a false positive:
a forced local `git rebase` replays all 144 commits with zero
conflicts, byte-identical result, but the button itself stayed red).
Splitting at the branch's own natural seam instead.

This PR is the real, original mechanical port - `pygi-convert.sh`-driven
PyGTK→PyGObject conversion, GTK2→GTK3 widget porting, and the Python
2→3 syntax/API migration - carrying its own original authorship, email,
and date throughout. This isn't just credited in prose; the git history
itself is theirs:

- **licamla** did the original `pygi-convert.sh`/PyGTK→PyGObject pass (13 commits)
- **Friedel Wolff** did the bulk of the real review and correctness work fixing it up (63 commits - bytes/str handling, colour/RGBA plumbing, popup positioning, a segfault fix in `cellrendererwidget.py`, and much more)
- **Stuart Prescott** did the Python 3 syntax pass and stood up the original CI for it (12 commits)
- **Rafael Fontenelle** reviewed/merged a piece of it (1 commit)

Verified all 89 commits shared with `translate/virtaal`'s old `py3`
branch carry byte-identical author name, email, and original date -
only the committer changed (exactly what a clean history reconstruction
does).

### Known incomplete on its own - by design

This PR predates two things it needs to actually run cleanly against
current `main`: PR-0's file renames/removals (`test_selectdialog.py`
etc. → `demo_*.py`, three dead TM plugins), and translate-toolkit's own
API drift since 2020 (`translate.lang.data.tr_lang`/`forceunicode`
removed upstream, `six` no longer vendored). Neither is fixed here -
fixing them means editing code these commits didn't touch, which would
break the "this is really their work, unmodified" property this PR
exists to preserve. **#3342 (retargeted to build on this PR) is what
makes the combined result actually work end to end** - treat this PR
as the historical record, not a standalone deliverable.

Depends on #3341 (merged).

author: akr0n
body:
## Cosa cambia

Nessun cambiamento di comportamento del servizio. Un difetto reale nel banco di prova, una
specifica corretta e un piano eseguibile.

### 1. La specifica poggiava su una premessa falsa

Il documento trattava una named pipe come un canale che non esce dalla macchina, e da li'
derivava la regola "arriva dalla pipe, quindi salta il token". Una named pipe e' raggiungibile
via SMB sulla porta 445: quella riga aprirebbe la telemetria alla rete credendo di chiuderla.

La decisione presa resta valida — parlava di **identita'**, non di localita'. Cambia la regola
che la traduce in codice: *il trasporto instrada, l'identita' concede, l'identita' non
determinabile rifiuta*. Il discriminante che funziona davvero e' `GetNamedPipeClientComputerName`,
con la tabella misurata delle tre vie: `"."` e' locale, l'indirizzo di rete no, e nemmeno
`localhost`.

### 2. Il banco di prova sporcava il processo

`ServizioInMemoria` impostava tre variabili d'ambiente e non le rimuoveva mai. Innocuo oggi,
velenoso appena il canale locale costruira' host Kestrel veri nello stesso assembly. Corretto
con un test visto fallire prima, e le classi che toccano stato globale ora stanno in una
collezione xunit comune.

### 3. Piano 1, eseguibile

Sei task in TDD. Si apre dichiarando cio' che NON fa: alla sua fine il token resta obbligatorio
ovunque, canale locale compreso. Il cambio di autorizzazione e' il piano 2.

## Verifica

- `dotnet build -c Release`: **0 avvisi, 0 errori**
- `dotnet test --no-build -c Release`: **201 test verdi** (53 Core, 45 App, 103 Service)

## Cosa resta scoperto

Dichiarato nei documenti, non nascosto: la combinazione LocalSystem + GUI dell'utente non e' mai
stata eseguita (nessuna sessione di misura era amministratore), la DACL non e' stata provata da
una seconda macchina, e il banco verifica la `PipeSecurity` come dato e non come effetto.

author: cutekorea
body:
## What

Adds four widgets to `/mackerel` (39 → 42) built on two source documents that the mackerel report cited but never archived. Both are now stored with originals and upgraded from grade C to A in the source ledger.

- **MOF distribution survey, 2024 edition** (2023 base year, 396pp) — the primary source behind the report's value-chain section
- **Self-sufficiency notice 2026-53** — the formula behind every self-sufficiency figure

## Why it mattered

The report had been computing its own self-sufficiency rate (145.6%) from customs tonnage. **The government already publishes the figure**, on a different basis: a conversion yield is applied to processed products, carry-in and carry-over come from the cold-storage survey, and consumption is an estimate. The published series for 2018–2023 is 151.1 / 85.7 / 76.6 / 112.2 / 117.4 / 144.1%.

The notice's formula turned out to be a **GIF image rather than text** in the statute database, so reading the articles alone silently drops two terms from the denominator. It is `[production / consumption(production + imports + carry-in − carry-over − exports)] × 100`.

## Widgets

| id | finding |
|---|---|
| `s1_official_self_sufficiency` | 2023 exports of 111,431t were **1.34× domestic consumption** of 83,350t. The ratio is driven by exports and inventory, not domestic supply capacity. |
| `s1_self_sufficiency_species_gap` | The numerator excludes blue mackerel; the export term cannot, since HS 0303540000 covers three *Scomber* species in one line. 2018 was **34.3% blue mackerel**, so 151.1% becomes 128.5% once counted. |
| `s4_value_chain_domestic_vs_import` | The imported chain was missing entirely. The Korean fisherman takes **40.9%** of retail against the Norwegian CFR's **35.2%**; retail margins are nearly identical. The gap sits in the wholesale layer (22.6% vs 13.3%). |
| `s1_norway_catch_value` | Norwegian catch fell 37.6% in 2025 while ex-vessel price rose to 38.39 kr/kg, so catch value still rose. |

## Also

- **`CHART_TYPES` allowlist in the build.** The renderer's switch falls through to an empty fragment for unrecognized values, so a `chartType` typo shipped a blank card with no error. The build now refuses to write a widget the renderer cannot draw. All 42 pass.
- **A footnote trap recorded in the `commodity-report` skill.** This survey puts ten species in one chapter and repeats footnote wording, so a document-wide grep attributes the wrong species' note — the "mid-November" survey date belongs to live squid, while mackerel is December. Table numbers also shift between editions (4-13 in 2020, 4-11 in 2024), so cite by table title.

## Verification

Every figure was cross-checked mechanically against the source PDF: the supply-structure table (42 cells), the production table's species split (12), the value-chain table (24 lines), the import chain, and the ten-species comparison — **zero mismatches**.

- provenance 42/42
- `mackerel:test` 4/4
- tsc clean
- Vitest 157 files, 1,209 passed / 2 skipped
- 4-axis 90.0 (A 37 / B 5)

author: bluedragon-ctrl
body:
## Summary
- **Shield charge stacks**: `chargeShield()` now adds banked duration instead of capping at the longer crate, and the HUD prints the banked seconds (`SHIELD CHARGED 7.0s`) instead of just "SHIELD CHARGED", so a stacked charge is actually visible.
- **Shop status readouts**: every consumable row (hull repair, shield, each ammo type) now shows the player's current status alongside what a purchase gives — e.g. `142/200 HULL`, `32/120 RDS` — so buying is an informed decision instead of a guess.
- **New SIPHON RIG car system** (3 tiers, 100 CR each): raises siphon yield 100% → 120% → 140% → 160%, with reach (300→390px) and drain time (4s→1s) riding along on the same tier rather than getting rows of their own.
- **Car-editor updated**: the new shop stat surfaces automatically (data-driven), plus a new "Siphon rig" group under World exposes the real reach/drain/yield numbers per tier.

## Why yield, not reach or drain
Measured with `tools/econsim.js` before building anything: reach and drain-time both **saturate** past roughly one tier — a hunter-style driver is already taking essentially every node it passes, so a further tier of either alone would be a shelf row selling nothing. Yield has no ceiling, so it's the one number the shelf promises. Verified on the shipped code: hunter-style income goes 28.6 → 74.0 cr/min across the four levels, rising at every tier.

## Honesty invariant
`hints()` (the floating price shown over a node before you take it) and `collect()` (what actually lands) read the yield multiplier from the exact same table, so the HUD can never quote a number the wallet doesn't pay. There's a dedicated test for this.

## Test plan
- [x] `node --test test/*.test.js` — 588/588 pass, including new coverage for shield stacking and the siphon rig's reach/drain/yield-honesty invariants
- [x] Verified in the running dev server and the running car-editor (fetched `/api/state`, clicked through both the SIPHON RIG shop-stat form and the new "Siphon rig" World-tab group, confirmed values match the shipped constants)
- [x] Round-tripped `patchConstant`/`patchArrayConstantElement` against the real `wallet.js` text in-memory to confirm the editor's write path works on the new flat-array constants

## Notes for reviewers
- `Wallet.collect()`'s signature gained a `player` parameter (before the `push`/`busy` defaults) — only one call site in the repo, already updated.
- `wallet.js`'s `SIPHON_TIERS` (array of objects) was refactored into three flat single-line arrays (`SIPHON_RANGES`/`SIPHON_FAR_TIMES`/`SIPHON_YIELDS`) specifically so `tools/car-editor`'s existing array-index patcher (the same one `TIER_PRICES` uses) can reach them — not a style change.
- The shop-stat "step" field (Shop → Car systems → SIPHON RIG) only controls what the shelf *displays*; the real reach/drain/yield live in the new World → Siphon rig constants and have to be kept in step by hand. Documented in both places' descriptions since there's no code-level guard against drift.

body:
Fixes #9.

The demo dumped the parse result as raw JSON, so it was not clear whether a field was read from the WebM file or computed by the library — and there was no way at all to tell which of the three scanning methods produced the duration.

## Changes

**Library**
- Add `DurationSource` (`"header" | "cues" | "tail"`) and an optional `durationSource` field on `WebmMeta`, reporting which method produced `durationMilliSeconds` (`undefined` when none did). Additive, so no breaking change for existing callers; the CLI picks it up for free.
- Extract the duration pipeline into a pure `resolveDuration` function (no `let`, per AGENTS.md) and build `mimeType` through a small helper. Resolution behavior is unchanged: Header → Cues → Tail, stopping at the first value.

**Demo**
- New "How to read the results" section explaining that `info` and `tracks` are reported as stored in the file, that `fileSize` (source size) and `mimeType` (assembled from codec IDs) are produced by the library, and that `durationMilliSeconds` is the only resolved value.
- Each result now shows the method that resolved the duration above the JSON, colored by accuracy: Header is exact, Cues and Tail are estimates (they point at the last indexed cluster / last block timecode, not the end of the last frame).

**README**
- `durationSource` added to the output example, plus a table of where each field comes from and a table of the three resolution methods with their accuracy.

## Testing

- `npm run type-check`, `npm test` (20 passed), `npm run build`, `npm run build:demo` — all pass.
- `durationSource` assertions added to the synthetic integration tests (all three methods covered) and to the ffmpeg asset tests.
- Demo verified in Chromium against `test_assets/standard.webm` (reports Header/exact) and `test_assets/live_no_duration.webm` (reports Tail scan/estimated), with no console errors.

author: udhay-adithya
body:
Two client-level behaviours present in both official clients were missing.

**No `User-Agent`.** Requests were anonymous, which makes attribution and debugging harder for anyone running a shared Ollama instance behind a proxy. `ollama-python` identifies itself as `ollama-python/<version> (<machine> <system>) Python/<version>`.

**Redirects were not configurable.** `ollama-python` exposes `follow_redirects` (default `True`); Ktor's behaviour varies by engine with no way to override it here.

### What changed

`ollama-kotlin/<version> (<os> <arch>) Kotlin/<version>` on every request, including the hosted web calls. Overridable through `headers`, case-insensitively — a caller-supplied `User-Agent` or `user-agent` wins.

The version comes from a generated `BuildInfo.VERSION`. `build.gradle.kts` now holds `libraryVersion` as the single source of truth, feeding both `coordinates(...)` and a `generateBuildInfo` task wired into the main source set — so the User-Agent cannot drift from what was actually published, which hand-writing the constant would eventually allow.

`OllamaClientConfig.followRedirects` (default `true`).

### One wrinkle worth flagging

Redirect handling is **not** per-request in Ktor — `HttpClientConfig.followRedirects` is resolved when the client is built, and there is no per-request escape hatch in 3.2.3 (I checked `HttpRedirect` for a skip attribute; it has none). So unlike every other config field, it cannot vary across a `configProvider`'s return values.

Rather than pretend otherwise, it is read from the config passed at construction, and the primary `configProvider` constructor takes it as a third parameter. The KDoc and README both say so explicitly, since a silently-ignored field would be worse than an awkward one.

### Verification

`UserAgentAndRedirectTest`:

- the default User-Agent starts with `ollama-kotlin/` and names the Kotlin version
- the embedded version matches a semver pattern, confirming it came from the generated constant rather than a placeholder
- a caller-supplied `User-Agent` wins, and so does a lowercase `user-agent`
- the hosted web calls carry it too
- a 307 is followed by default, asserted via the engine seeing two requests
- `followRedirects = false` stops at one request

Closes #13

author: naftalis-elementor
body:
## Overview

Extends `WidgetConfig.localServers` so embed hosts can load a subset of the iframe's **built-in** MCP servers instead of the full default set. Previously the only control was `localServers.skipLoading`, which is all-or-nothing.

The SDK exposes configuration only — the fields are forwarded to the embedded application through the existing `sdk-widget-config` postMessage. No new transport or runtime logic in the SDK.

## Changes

### `localServers` configuration (`WidgetConfig`)

- `include?: string[]` — allowlist. When present, only the listed built-in servers load; `exclude` is ignored.
- `exclude?: string[]` — blocklist. Applied only when `include` is absent: all built-ins except the listed ones load.
- `skipLoading?: boolean` — now marked `@deprecated`, equivalent to `include: []`. Still works.
- Precedence: `include` wins if present, otherwise `exclude` applies, and omitting both preserves today's behavior (full default set). Unknown names are ignored with a warning.
- `LocalServersConfig` is kept internal to `WidgetConfig` and is not re-exported from the package entry point — hosts configure it via `WidgetConfig`.

### Docs

- Documented in `widget-config.md` under a new "Built-in local MCP servers" section, including the precedence rules and the deprecation of `skipLoading`.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run build` produces dist types with `include` / `exclude` on `localServers`

Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)
<!--start_gitstream_placeholder-->
### ✨ PR Description
## 1. Problem & Context

Extends `LocalServersConfig` with granular control over built-in MCP server loading via `include`/`exclude` allowlists, deprecating the coarse `skipLoading` boolean in favor of explicit filtering.

## 2. What Changed (Where)

- `src/angie-mcp-sdk.ts`: Added `include` and `exclude` fields to `LocalServersConfig` type; marked `skipLoading` deprecated.
- `src/load-sidebar-v2/widget-config.md`: Documented new fields, precedence rules, and deprecation path; clarified scope (built-in servers only).

## 3. How It Works

`include` takes absolute precedence (whitelist mode); `exclude` applies only when `include` absent (blacklist mode); both omitted loads defaults. Unknown server names logged as warnings but don't fail. `skipLoading: true` equivalent to `include: []`.

## 4. Risks

Backward compatibility preserved—`skipLoading` remains functional. Minor risk: users mixing `include` + `exclude` may expect AND behavior instead of include-wins semantics; docs mitigate this clearly.

author: gplanchat
body:
## Rupture

`WorkflowCommandBufferInterface::scheduleNexusOperation()` prend un **septième paramètre**,
`NexusOperationHeaders`. Toute implémentation tierce doit s'adapter, comme pour DUR031.

Il est **requis, pas optionnel**. Un défaut aurait laissé une implémentation l'oublier sans que rien
ne le dise — exactement la panne muette que l'objet-valeur qu'il transporte existe pour empêcher.

## Pourquoi §3.1 et §3.2 ensemble

Élargir le port sans que le pont n'écrive rien aurait livré un paramètre **accepté puis ignoré**.
Et PHP accepte silencieusement un argument de trop pour une fonction utilisateur : rien n'aurait
signalé qu'un appelant posait un en-tête qui n'allait nulle part.

Le test rouge l'a montré littéralement — deux cas sur trois échouaient, le troisième passait
**parce qu'il n'attendait aucun en-tête**. Livrer §3.1 seule aurait rendu ce test vert à 100 % sur
un pont qui ne portait rien.

## Deux décisions

**Le champ n'est écrit que s'il y a quelque chose à porter.** Une map vide n'est pas une map absente
pour qui relit un historique.

**La coercition de casse reste dans l'objet-valeur, pas dans le pont.** Un pont qui minusculerait
laisserait le domaine tenir une valeur que le serveur n'a jamais vue — et le test d'aller-retour de
§4.1 comparerait alors l'intention de l'appelant au souvenir d'autre chose.

## Ce que la rupture a touché

Quatre fichiers de test appelaient le port à six arguments. Ils sont mis à jour ; c'est la surface
réelle de la rupture à l'intérieur du dépôt.

phpstan a aussi refusé mon premier passage par une `MapField` — ses stubs ne disent pas le type de
clé. `setNexusHeader()` accepte un tableau aussi bien qu'une MapField, ce qui est plus simple et
plus sûr.

## Vérification

cs-fixer, unitaires, phpstan, psalm **et l'intégration contre `:7233`** : tous à zéro, vérifiés par
code de sortie.

Ce que ces tests ne peuvent pas dire : si le serveur accepte l'en-tête tel qu'écrit. C'est **§4.1**,
et la sonde du bloc 1 a déjà établi qu'il l'accepte — reste à le prouver à travers le pont.

author: srivardhanjalan
body:
Turns the step 11–17 proofs — originally one-off agent runs whose only artifact was a PR comment — into **re-runnable tests** you can point at any deployed kivan stack. Two layers, both under `tools/e2e/` (the harness branch, stacked on `step-17-polish`; it never edits the app PR's tree):

- **`tools/e2e/` — backend-flow pytest** (B1): each step's proof list as parameterized tests over the real API, minting real Clerk users, reading DynamoDB/CloudWatch for evidence. Skips cleanly when `E2E_API_URL` is unset.
- **`tools/e2e/maestro/` — Maestro UI flows** (B2): six flows that drive the app in an iOS simulator and assert its **visual components**, plus `scripts/mint_ui_user.py` (pre-arm) and `run.sh`.

## Why the Maestro flows live in `tools/e2e/maestro/` (not `17-polish/frontend/.maestro/`)
This is the harness branch. Putting flows under the app's folder would edit the code PR's tree. They sit beside the pytest suite and run against **any** Expo Go simulator serving the 17-polish app — importing no app code, only asserting what it renders.

## B1 evidence — smoke run vs a live stack (s17h), then torn to zero
- **42 tests collected, 40 passed** (1 skip, 1 xpass) against the isolated `s17h` App Runner stack.
- Stack **torn down to zero**: 71 resources created = 71 destroyed; App-Runner log groups swept; tag query = 0.
- Session JWTs via the Clerk **Backend API** (create user → open session → mint token), *not* a Frontend-API sign-in: FAPI's low per-instance rate limit trips on a single ~100-user run; BAPI keeps the suite re-runnable. The token is still a real RS256 session JWT the backend verifies via JWKS.

## B2 evidence — all six Maestro flows green end-to-end on the live s17v stack
Run via `run.sh` (pre-arm Vera → `00` with `--env`, then `01`–`05`); each `takeScreenshot` into `artifacts-gitignored/` (gitignored). Fresh single-use ticket, exit 0, **all flows passed**.

| Flow | Visual components asserted |
|------|----------------------------|
| `00-signin` | cover-band Home header (display name + gear) + **All-Wishes rail** |
| `01-wishlist-create` | pinned CTA carries the life-event **emoji** (`🎂  Start Adding Wishes`); lands **inside** the new wishlist (cover band + life-event name). Self-deletes after asserting. |
| `02-wish-add` | wish **masonry card** + **glass price pill** (`₹1,299`, asserted on the wish detail) |
| `03-notifications` | unread **badge** (`2`), feed **card rows** (+ per-type icon), grouped **Notification Settings** cards |
| `04-admin` | Settings **Admin dashboard** row (admin-gated) + admin **catalog** dashboard rows |
| `05-event` | event-detail **cover band** + **segmented toggle** (`Wishlists`/`Guests`) |

Auth is not Maestro's job: `scripts/mint_ui_user.py` pre-arms the seeded Vera fixture — mints a single-use Clerk **sign-in ticket** the SignInScreen exchanges (a server-authorized bypass of the dev instance's MFA), and `--admin` grants the admin role — **reusing** conftest's Backend-API client and `17-polish/infra/scripts/grant_admin.py` rather than duplicating either.

## Deviations (documented in `tools/e2e/maestro/README.md`)
- **BAPI over FAPI** — dev-instance FAPI rate limits force Backend-API session minting (above).
- **Regional S3 presign** — the suite reads presigned image URLs; the stack presigns the **regional** virtual host (`s3.{region}.amazonaws.com`), so evidence runs work outside us-east-1 (307s otherwise).
- **Sign-in ticket, not password** — the deployed frontend's SignInScreen accepts a ticket in the password field (harness-run accommodation for the instance's required-MFA state); not shipped behavior.
- **No testIDs** — the app uses `accessibilityLabel` only, matched as text; controls with a label are single a11y elements, so the **tab badge** is asserted via the NotificationsScreen pill, the **price pill** value via the wish detail, and the admin row via its label `Storefronts and products`.
- **`04-admin`** asserts the admin catalog **menu** (glyph rows), not an image grid — the image-forward tiles live on the user-facing Wish Store.
- **`02` omits the photo** and **`05` may leave the date `TBD`** — the native iOS image picker / inline calendar are OS controls not reliably scriptable by Maestro; the required visual assertions don't depend on them.

## Latent app defect surfaced (flagged, not fixed here)
A wishlist with a **cover preset** stores `preset:<id>`. The detail screen and Home rail resolve it to a gradient, but the **My Stuff wishlist grid** passes it straight to `<Image>` → `No suitable URL request handler found for preset:sunset-bliss` (dev red-box / broken image in prod). Belongs on the app PR; this branch must not edit 17-polish. (`01-wishlist-create` self-cleans partly to avoid piling up broken tiles.)

Stacked on `step-17-polish`; **not for merge** ahead of the app PR.

author: 0xmhha
body:
The code is cut by pipeline stage, not by concern, so the same idea appears
under several names. This adds the plan for cutting it by concern instead,
measured rather than asserted.

Documentation plus one measurement tool. No product code, no test changes.

## What the measurement says

Measured on `a63b500` with `go run ./scripts/inventory/code-graph -symbols .`
(75 packages, 268 edges, 2,860 declarations):

| Measured | Count | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Types meaning "one node" | **10** | driver · upgrade · chainsetup x3 · collector · node · topology · process · deploy |
| Entry points that launch a node | **8** | chainsetup x4 · driver x2 · upgrade · supervisor |
| Places that compute paths | **4** | netmap.Layout · session x5 · chainsetup.Workspace · deploy.RemotePaths |

One package carries most of it: `chainsetup` is 6,593 lines across 27 files,
22% of internal code.

## The plan

`docs/dev/architecture/module-plan.md` names three departments for what they
own — **resource decides, node records, process runs** — with the genesis,
nodeconfig, and dsl builders above them, then the surfaces (cmd, mcp), then
the orchestrators (chainsetup, testengine). P1 through P8, each with a gate
that can be checked by re-measuring, and a symbol-level move map for P1.

Naming rule: a module is named for the object it owns, the way a finance team
owns finance. That rules out metaphors (`netmap`), abbreviations (`netreg`,
`portplan`), output names (`place`, `layout`, `slot`), and verbs (`assign`).
`alloc` is unusable here — it already means genesis account allocation, and
the same word is used for node placement in `NetAllocate` (13 occurrences,
two meanings).

## Two defects the naming work surfaced

**`serverset.Placement` is a wrapper that should not exist.** Its three extra
fields are all copies of values already in the same returned struct: `Source`
duplicates `Pool.Source` (both set from one string at `placement.go:62`),
`DataRoot` duplicates `Target.DataRoot`, and `Remote` stores what
`machine.Spec.IsRemote()` derives — the very thing that method's comment says
must never be stored. So the fix is to delete the type, not rename it.

**`Config.Fleet` and `Config.Pool` do the same job, and one of them rounds
capacity down.** Both build one pool from every server in the set. `Pool` has
no production caller (three tests). `Fleet` computes `slots / len(hosts)` with
integer division, so a set declaring 2+1+1 slots silently allocates 3. The
decision recorded here is to keep each server's declared slots: P1.2 drops the
rounding and refuses a non-uniform set out loud, P1.3 gives `Host` its own
`Slots` and teaches `Assign` to skip an exhausted host.

The word `fleet` also contradicts the product term. "server set" was settled,
but `--fleet` is still a user-facing flag, `"fleet"` an MCP argument, and the
metaphor runs through comments and test fixtures. P1.2 removes it in one
atomic rename; its gate is zero occurrences of the string.

## Tooling

`scripts/inventory/code-graph` gains `-symbols`: a per-declaration inventory
(pkg, file, line, kind, name, receiver, signature, doc, size). Package edges
answer "what depends on what"; a refactor also asks "who owns this concern"
and "how many places compute the same thing", which needs symbols. Every
number in the plan comes from it.

Its layer map had gone stale — it named five packages that no longer exist
(`engine`, `netcompose`, `keygen`, `keymat`, `serverset`) and did not know
five that do, so those fell into "other". Every package now lands in a named
bucket, and a stale entry is documented as a signal the map is behind.

`code-graph.md` sections 2-3 are re-measured (zero layering violations; the
three edges that leave their layer are each accounted for) and gain a
netmap-family subgraph. The launchopt sections stay as the 2026-08 record.

## Verification

- `gofmt -l cmd internal tests scripts` clean, `go vet ./...`, `go build ./...`
- `go test ./...` passes (61 packages)
- `internal/arch` layering tests pass
- every local Markdown link resolves
- `git diff --check` clean

author: yashi
body:
Show collaborators to each other: named, colored remote cursors and selections in the editor, and a connected-user indicator in the topbar. All of it is ephemeral Yjs Awareness state, which already travels over the Phase 3 WebSocket; it never becomes part of the AsciiDoc document, never reaches SQLite, and the server drops a client's state the moment its socket closes, so departed users disappear immediately.

Each browser keeps one identity in localStorage: a generated adjective-animal display name and a palette color, editable through a topbar input, so a person keeps their identity across documents and visits. The identity is published as the awareness user field in exactly the shape y-codemirror.next reads to draw remote carets and selections, enabled by passing the provider's awareness to yCollab.  The connected-user list is derived from the raw awareness states by a pure function, local user first.

Unit tests cover identity generation and persistence, palette validation, and presence-list derivation. Browser tests with two real clients verify the indicator updates when users join, rename, and leave, that remote carets carry the collaborator's name, that remote selections are highlighted, and that presence data never leaks into the persisted document source.

author: abhishek-03113
body:
## Summary

This PR implements two major features: (1) daemon-to-daemon peer networking with automatic reconnection to trusted paired devices, and (2) a real OS tray icon and window for the Flutter UI with proper lifecycle management.

## Key Changes

### Daemon Peer Networking
- **Peer channel listener** (`spawn_peer_channel_listener`): Binds an ephemeral TCP port on `0.0.0.0` to accept incoming daemon-to-daemon connections, distinct from the local IPC port
- **Discovery service** (`spawn_discovery`): Implements UDP-based peer discovery that both announces this daemon's presence and listens for other daemons, with automatic redial to trusted paired devices
- **Bidirectional pipeline** (`run_paired_connection`): Runs input streaming over a single authenticated connection using `tokio::select!` to interleave both send (when local) and receive-inject (when remote) directions
- **Connection deduplication** (`try_claim_peer`): Prevents redundant connections when both inbound and outbound paths race to the same peer using an atomic check-and-insert pattern
- **Service extensions**: Added `accept_incoming_peer_channel`, `dial_if_trusted`, and `set_link_state` methods to `DaemonService` to handle peer authentication and link state updates

### Flutter UI Real OS Integration
- **Tray icon and window** (`_RealApp`): Docks a real native tray icon with context menu (Open/Quit) and a real window that hides on close rather than quitting
- **Onboarding flow**: Persists onboarding completion to local preferences (`shared_preferences`) and shows `OnboardingFlow` on first launch, `AppWindowShell` afterward
- **Window lifecycle**: Implements `WindowListener` and `TrayListener` to handle window close (hide instead), tray click (toggle visibility), and right-click (show context menu)
- **Platform detection**: Detects actual OS at runtime (`currentHostOs()`) rather than using dev harness's simulated platform selector
- **Build-time modes**: Adds `FLOW_UI_MODE` environment variable to switch between real app and dev harness, with dev harness remaining accessible for manual QA

### Configuration Changes
- Default daemon backend changed from `mock` to `ipc` (expects real `flow-daemon` at `127.0.0.1:47823`)
- Default UI mode is now the real app (not dev harness); harness accessible via `--dart-define=FLOW_UI_MODE=harness`
- Added dependencies: `window_manager`, `tray_manager`, `shared_preferences`

## Notable Implementation Details

- Graceful degradation: Both peer networking and tray/window setup swallow failures rather than crashing, matching the daemon's hotkey runner pattern
- Connection state tracking: `ConnectedPeers` (a `HashSet<DeviceId>` wrapped in `Arc<Mutex>`) prevents duplicate connections from racing outbound and inbound paths
- Shared channel direction: `run_paired_connection` uses a single `Box<dyn Channel>` with `tokio::select!` rather than splitting into separate read/write tasks, avoiding unsafe channel splitting
- Link state updates: `set_link_state` now reflects real peer connection status instead of static `Connected` value, enabling proper IPC contract state transitions
- Onboarding persistence: Stored separately from daemon state (user can complete onboarding without pairing, re-pairing doesn't resurface welcome flow)

author: marc0olo
body:
`icp.net` is the current default gateway domain for new frontend canisters, replacing `icp0.io`. All three official domains (`ic0.app`, `icp0.io`, `icp.net`) stay live and Internet Identity canonicalizes across them, so **nothing here was broken** — but the repo advertised the old default 37 times against 5 uses of the new one, including one pair of twin examples that disagreed with each other (`rust/daily_planner` already said `icp.net`; `motoko/daily_planner` said `icp0.io`).

### Swept

- **`native-apps/unity_ii_deeplink`** README (×6) + `unity_project/README.md` — the Android App Links / iOS Universal Links walkthrough. Safe as a single sweep because `assetlinks.json` and the AASA file **carry no domain of their own** (verified — they hold only app IDs and fingerprints) and are served by the same canister at every gateway domain. So `kAndroidHost`, `kDomain`, the callback URL, and the `curl` verification step all move together and stay matched. Every one is a `<your-canister-id>` placeholder, so no real URL changes.
- **`motoko/daily_planner`** — the HTTPS-outcall cost-calculator link, now matching its Rust twin.
- **`UnityHttp.cs`** — the base URI used when a relative URL reaches the adapter (`ic0.app`, the last one).
- **13 `_headers`** — `connect-src` now lists `https://icp.net https://*.icp.net` instead of the `icp0.io` pair. These apps talk to their own origin (covered by `'self'`) or to `icp-api.io` (unchanged), so this entry is belt-and-braces either way.

`grep` for `icp0.io` / `ic0.app` outside `node_modules` and `.claude/` now returns nothing.

### One thing that is *not* a domain rename

`hosting/oisy-signer-demo` built its anonymous agent with `host: 'https://icp0.io'`. `host` is the **API endpoint** calls go to, not the gateway the app is served from — so the correct value is `https://icp-api.io` (or omitting it and letting `@icp-sdk/core` resolve). Renaming it to `icp.net` would have been the same mistake in newer clothes. Fixed to `icp-api.io`, with a comment saying why.

### Note for reviewers

`UnityHttp.cs` is CRLF. The diff is the one intended line — I clobbered the line endings on a first pass and redid the edit byte-wise, so please shout if anything looks off there.

author: sephirothx
body:
First tranche of the wire-protocol work in #424, ordered by reliability and by packet volume rather than by issue number.

## Stroke path: 35.2 → 14.9 B per frame on the wire (−58%)

Measured for one drawer in a 16-player room. A frame's cost is mostly its Socket.IO envelope — 43 B around ~21 B of points — and the server rebroadcasts every frame to everyone else, so each byte counts N−1 times.

| | baseline | after delta | after base64 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| points payload, 5-point frame | 21 B | 13 B (−38%) | — |
| bytes per frame | 64 B | 56 B | **33 B** |
| 120-point stroke | 1,431 B | 1,231 B | **704 B** |
| **server egress, 16-player room** | **24,000 B/s** | 21,000 B/s | **12,375 B/s** |
| canvas resync, client holding 4 of 6 actions | 119 B | — | 47 B (−61%) |

**These are uncompressed figures.** The deployment already negotiates permessage-deflate
with context takeover (verified on a live handshake), so the real wire cost is lower and
the *attribution* differs. Measured through one deflate context, 600 frames of 5 points:

| points | transport | B/frame on the wire | vs original |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| absolute | binary attachment | 35.2 | — |
| absolute | base64 text | 33.4 | −5% |
| delta | binary attachment | 21.3 | −40% |
| **delta** | **base64 text (shipped)** | **14.9** | **−58%** |

Sustained model, 16-player room: **12,375 B/s of input → 3,405 B/s on the wire.**

Uncompressed I credited base64 with −41% and delta with −12.5%. Compressed it is the other
way round: deflate already squashes the repeated placeholder envelope, so base64 alone is
worth 5%. What base64 actually buys is putting the payload in the *same compression
context* as the framing — which is why the pair beats delta alone by much more than base64
alone suggests. The benchmark now reports both columns so this cannot be misread again.

A 5-point frame carries ~10 B of irreducible delta information and costs 9.1 B compressed,
so the encoding is at its floor. The remaining residue is ~5 B per message of deflate
flush overhead, which only *fewer messages* removes — i.e. the flush interval, already
rejected on perceptual grounds.

## What landed

- **`33861d0` Honest benchmark baseline.** The existing model omitted the `[generation, sequence]` argument every action-opening frame carries, understating the current protocol. Correcting it *raises* the baseline — two rows go negative — which is the honest number and the reason it lands before any change. Adds a sustained-drawing model reported as room egress, since per-frame bytes hide the fan-out.
- **`f0d5db6` Protocol version at the handshake (#416).** A stale build's frames are refused inside a handler with no acknowledgement, so it is never told: it draws into a canvas the server stopped recording, then loops on syncs it cannot decode. Now settled at the handshake, where there is somewhere to put the answer. Accepted-then-told, never refused; the client reloads at most once per server version.
- **`c6ab884` + `4b2de2c` Delta-coded path points (#414, live half).** Points travel as signed-byte offsets from the point before them, first point absolute so each frame decodes independently. Then made **adaptive**: see below.
- **`24b2256` Incremental resync (#415).** `request_sync_strokes` may claim `[generation, actionCount, historyHash]`, checked O(1) against the prefix-hash array the server already keeps, answered with only the tail.
- **`35255bc` Base64 wire shape for small frames.** Frames ≤85 B ride inside an ordinary text event instead of as a binary attachment, skipping the placeholder envelope and the second WebSocket frame. Crossover measured at ~85 B, so the sender picks per frame; the server takes either shape and rebroadcasts verbatim. Bumps `PROTOCOL_VERSION` to 2 — the first real use of `f0d5db6`.

## Two course corrections worth reading

**The flush interval was reverted.** Raising it 40→80 ms cut egress 34% on paper. It looked visibly steppy, and so did 56 ms and 50 ms. The byte curve was climbing steeply through the entire range the eye rejected — the measurement was of the wrong axis. 40 ms stands; filed as #446, since the right value is deployment-specific and only findable by looking.

**Delta coding was a bet on the user's hardware until it wasn't.** The escape threshold is a distance between consecutive samples, so it scales with sample rate — and the client takes one point per `pointermove`, i.e. display refresh, not the 120 Hz the first benchmark assumed. At 60 Hz the crossover is ~1905 px/s and at 30 Hz ~952, both reachable while drawing normally, and past them escapes made frames **22% larger** than before. The encoder now predicts both encodings and sends the smaller, tagged. Every regression became a fallback:

| payload vs original | 1500 px/s | 2500 px/s | 4000 px/s |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 60 Hz — before → after | −44% → −44% | **+22% → 0%** | **+22% → 0%** |
| 30 Hz — before → after | **+22% → 0%** | **+22% → 0%** | **+22% → 0%** |

Absolute frames keep tag 1 and their `(len−1) % 4` length check, so only genuinely-delta frames give that up.

## Verification

890 backend · 256 frontend · 54 E2E · ruff + eslint + tsc clean.

The codec got coverage proportional to being the only variable-length structure on the wire: 34 seeded property tests (round-trip on the quarter-pixel grid, never-larger-than-absolute, stability under re-encoding, both branches exercised, truncation refused, out-of-range deltas refused), plus cross-runtime checks — **252 generated strokes with zero byte mismatches between the Python and TypeScript encoders, 12,528 points decoded by the TS decoder from Python-encoded frames with zero coordinate mismatches, and the same 252 strokes re-checked across both wire shapes (180 base64, 72 binary) with zero mismatches and zero divergence between the shapes**. Hostile base64 is covered too: bad padding, non-base64, empty, over-length, and valid base64 carrying an unknown frame version. `test_wire_contract.py` is name-level and would not have caught a divergence here.

Every resync refusal path is tested to fall back to the full dump: wrong hash, stale generation, count past the history, client ahead after an undo, and a count landing inside an open path.

## Not in this PR

#417 `room_state` deltas, #418 folding `canvas_commit`, #419/#422 turn payloads, #420 lobby ETag, #421 guess dedupe, #423 fill integers. Also worth noting for #419: `hint_revealed` has the same per-socket fan-out as `turn_started` and fires more often, which was not in the original issue.

Refs #413 #414 #415 #416 #424

author: albidev
body:
## Problem

The 3D graph freezes on mobile (iPhone) with a loop of:
`THREE.WebGLRenderer: Context Lost.` → `Context Restored.`

Root cause: the FE has **no listener** for `webglcontextlost`/`webglcontextrestored`. When the browser/GPU loses the context (mobile memory pressure, tab sleep, GPU process reset), three.js logs the loop but the scene stays black. Desktop (M4) survives; iPhone doesn't.

Secondary cause: the heavy **bloom + SMAA post-processing composer** is installed unconditionally, even on constrained devices — it's the #1 WebGL context-loss trigger on mobile GPUs.

## Fix

- `graph-init.js`: install `webglcontextlost` (with `preventDefault()`) and `webglcontextrestored` listeners on the renderer canvas; on restore, re-sync visual state, redraw and mark the graph active so the animation loop resumes.
- `graph-core.js`: `installBloomPass()` now skips post-processing when `isConstrainedDevice()` — direct rendering on mobile/low-memory devices.
- `index.html`: cache-buster v78 → v79.

## Verification

- `node --check` on both JS files: OK
- Live server serves v79 with `installWebGLContextRecovery` present; `/api/graph` returns 200
- Desktop unchanged (bloom still active on non-constrained devices)

## Summary

Adds `launchpad/docs/corpus/architecture/flows/event-ingestion.md`, the single canonical corpus node documenting how a signed Nostr event submitted over WebSocket or HTTP becomes a durably stored, fanned-out event on a Buzz relay -- the shared `ingest_event` pipeline in `crates/buzz-relay/src/handlers/ingest.rs`.

Closes #676

## What's covered

- Trigger, preconditions, and the five terminal outcomes (accepted/duplicate/rejected/auth-failed/internal-error)
- The 16-step ordered pipeline: write fence, categorical rejects, signature verification, timestamp/size bounds, pubkey/scope checks, channel resolution, membership, kind-specific validation, storage (with its transactional dedupe + thread-counter update), post-storage side effects, and post-commit dispatch (audit, Redis pub/sub, local fan-out, workflow triggering)
- Authentication/authorization/trust-boundary crossings: transport auth, tenant/community binding, claimed-vs-resolved community, scope, channel membership/visibility (checked independently at both ingest and delivery time), and moderation state
- Failure/abort/rollback behavior: what leaves no trace, the single transactional storage step, duplicate-as-no-op semantics, kind:9007's explicit compensation on insert failure, and what does *not* roll back once storage succeeds (fan-out/audit/workflow failures)
- Scope and omissions, naming what this node deliberately does not enumerate (the ~30 per-kind envelope validators) and what it explicitly does not cover (ephemeral-kind handling, side-effect catalog internals, workflow-engine internals, the read/subscription path, Redis replication internals)
