body:
Response to the first piece of live user feedback (Reddit): "Tried the grid, feels lackluster. Not many players available… Arvydas Macijauskas, Mindaugas Kuzminskas and Rokas Giedraitis weren't in the game." He was right, twice over.

**1. The missing middle generation (30 new players).** The database held current rosters plus canonised legends and almost nobody in between — the well-travelled 2005–2024 veterans a fan actually reaches for didn't exist. Thirty do now, each researched and cross-verified against at least two sources (Wikipedia / Proballers / RealGM / club sites, via five parallel researchers): the three he named plus Nocioni, Ante Tomic, Jaycee Carroll, San Emeterio, Claver, Ribas, Maciulis, Kalnietis, Pocius, Pero Antic, Marjanovic, Macvan, Stimac, Zoran Dragic, Perperoglou, Papapetrou, Lojeski, Pleiss, Djedovic, Shved, Tyrese Rice, Sonny Weems, Devin Smith, Charles Jenkins, Goudelock, Udoh and Nunnally.

- Legends 173 → 203, careers 466 → 496
- Ten of the thirty already started Final Four fives in `lineups.js` — names the site itself displays finally resolve as guesses
- They flow into every game: Player ID, Career Order, The Grid, Connections, Path Between, Common Club, Mystery Legends

**2. The era-name bug (why Baskonia cells felt extra thin).** Careers file Baskonia's 2000s era-accurately as "Tau Ceramica", and The Grid matched clubs by exact string — so **Scola, Splitter, Garbajosa, Oberto and Rakocevic could never answer a Baskonia cell**. `clubs.js` (the one shared map of when two names mean the same club) now folds the Tau Ceramica / Caja Laboral / Laboral Kutxa lineage into Baskonia (and Caja San Fernando into CB Sevilla), and `thegrid.js` registers every stint under its era name *and* its canonical one — with `build_grids.js` loading the same map, so the generator and the game keep one definition of "played for X".

**Also:** `TEAM_FIX` gained a dozen sponsor-era foldings (ALBA Berlin, Rytas Vilnius → Lietuvos Rytas, Iberostar/La Laguna Tenerife → CB Canarias, Shanxi Loongs → Brave Dragons…), including healing one **pre-existing split**: "Spartak St. Petersburg" and "Spartak Saint Petersburg" were both live in careers.js.

**The reviewer's exact cells, before → after:** Olympiacos×Lithuania effectively 3 → **5 answers** (Macijauskas, Kuzminskas added); Baskonia×Lithuania → **5 answers** (Macijauskas, Giedraitis added, plus the Tau-era unlock).

Paths, grids, puzzles and odd-one-outs regenerated from the wider universe — dailies re-deal, records and streaks untouched. SW cache bumped to `elg-v81`. Tests: **638 passing** (the legends-count assertion moved to 203).

author: wintontomlinson
body:
Closes four gaps in the player UI, plus the design-system work needed to close them.

Scoped to the UI layer: no routes, no API calls and no data shapes changed. It targets the Flask app that `vercel.json` actually deploys (`templates/index.html` + `static/`), not the Next.js app under `web/`.

## Why this is not a rewrite

The brief this came from asked for a full frontend rewrite and listed the features to build. Most of that list already exists here, so a rewrite would have thrown away working code and regressed the product. Audited before starting:

| Asked for | Already in the codebase |
| --- | --- |
| `#07070b` background with subtle gradients | `--bg: #07070b`, plus the `#ambient` wash |
| Dynamic accent extracted from artwork | `artworkHue()` -> `--track-hue` -> brand gradients |
| Glassmorphism | `backdrop-filter` on sidebar, topbar, player, drawer, menu |
| Desktop sidebar + mobile bottom nav | both, at a shared 760px breakpoint |
| Player bar with full-width progress, expand to full screen | `.player` + `#np` |
| Now Playing with Queue and Lyrics tabs | `.np__tabs`, `renderNpPanel()` |
| Crossfade / gapless | two decks, `preloadNext()`, per-deck EQ |
| Web Audio visualiser | `Viz` with an `AnalyserNode` |
| Keyboard shortcuts, toasts, skeletons, localStorage | `SHORTCUTS`, `toast()`, `skeletonShelf()`, `Store` |
| Colour extraction, art rotation, trending ranks, genre cards | all present |

So this PR builds only what was genuinely missing.

## Queue reordering

Upcoming tracks can be dragged, or moved with arrow buttons for keyboard and touch, where HTML5 drag and drop never fires.

Only `order` is mutated. `queue` holds the songs and `order` is the play sequence over them, so reordering cannot invalidate `pos` or a mid-crossfade handoff. Nothing may cross the playing track: moving the play head would mean cutting off playback to satisfy a drag.

The subtle part is the preloaded deck. After a move, `preloadNext()` runs again; it compares `readyFor` against the song now in the next slot, so the idle deck is re-pointed when the drag changed what comes next and left alone when it did not. Without that, the deck keeps the buffer for the old next track and the wrong song plays.

The drawer and the Now Playing Queue tab each built their own row markup, which is why only one of them could have been made reorderable. They now share `queueRowHtml`, so both get the handles, reorder buttons and remove control from one place.

## Library

Filter tabs (All / Playlists / Albums / Artists), sort (recently added / A to Z / most played), a grid and list toggle, and batch select with delete. All three presentation choices persist.

There is no "save album" or "follow artist" feature in this app. Rather than ship two permanently empty tabs, Albums and Artists are derived from songs already liked or played: real ids, names and artwork, nothing invented. "Most played" counts `play`, `complete` and `repeat` events from the existing local history. Batch delete is offered for playlists only, since a derived album is not something that can be removed.

One ordering detail worth knowing: the selection tick is handled ahead of the `[data-goto]` branch. It sits inside a tile that is itself a navigation target, so a later check is never reached, and ticking a playlist opened it instead of selecting it.

## Friend activity

A sidebar panel, labelled **Demo** because there is no social backend. It pairs fictional people with tracks from the listener's own real history rather than inventing catalogue entries, and stays hidden until there is history to draw on.

## Design system

- Glass becomes a token set (`--glass-bg`, `--glass-blur`, `--glass-line`, `--glass-highlight`) that is **track-hue aware**, so the sidebar, player and drawer pick up the colour of what is playing instead of sitting outside the theme in a fixed grey.
- `--chrome-alpha` lets the sidebar, toolbar and tab bar share one `.chrome-panel` rule at the opacity each needs, preserving the toolbar's original transparency.
- Type moves to **Inter**, placed ahead of the system stack rather than behind it, so the face that is actually downloaded is the one that renders.
- `--med`, the workhorse duration most components read, becomes 300ms.
- A `@supports not (backdrop-filter)` fallback swaps blur for a near-solid tint rather than shipping a janky effect.

## Verification

`scripts/test_queue_reorder.mjs` covers the reorder maths, which is pure index arithmetic and awkward to exercise by dragging rows:

- the queue stays a permutation for every from/to pair
- the playing track never leaves its slot
- all 32 drag and drop combinations match a reference splice

That last one is why the test exists: the off-by-one when dropping *below* the original position (remove-then-insert shifts every later index down by one) is the classic bug in this code shape.

Library filtering, sorting, batch select and persistence were exercised in a headless browser against the real Flask app. Confirmed: "most played" returned albums in exactly the seeded play-count order, ticking a tile no longer navigates, and `libView`/`libFilter`/`libSort` survive a reload.

## Two things deliberately not built

**Synced lyrics.** The brief asked for real-time lyrics with the active line highlighted. `catalog.lyrics()` returns a plain body plus copyright and snippet, with no timestamps, and there is no LRC or word timing anywhere in the data layer. Driving a highlight off elapsed time would drift and be wrong, so the Lyrics tab keeps showing plain lyrics.

**Floating mini-player on scroll.** `.player` is `position: fixed; bottom: 8px` and the scroll container is `.view`, so the player bar never scrolls out of view. A second floating player would be a redundant duplicate sitting on top of an identical always-visible one. The intent behind the request, keeping transport reachable, is already satisfied.

author: syb0rg
body:
Fixes #1180

`/chart` and `ChartToggle` already built the chart controller in console mode,
but the console render branch returns after the shell and its message dialogs
(`game_app/render.rs`), before every dialog layer — so the chart existed,
sampled and updated, and was never visible.

`C4ChartDialog` reaches `Dialog::Show` without `fViewportDlg`, so C++ takes the
console arm and gives it a real child window of the console with its own
rendering context (`C4GuiDialogs.cpp:305-320,659-661`); `Dialog::Close`
destroys that window again (`:677`). That is the same shape the scoreboard
already has here, so the chart follows it rather than inventing a second one.

## The three commits

**`refactor:`** the layout's `caption` and `close_button` become
`Option<IntRect>`. A console child window draws both itself, so a dialog inside
one must not draw a second pair. Hit-testing routes through a `contains_widget`
helper that cannot match a widget the layout does not carry, which makes "no
drag element, no close target" a property of the layout rather than a flag
someone has to remember to check. No behaviour change: the fullscreen layout
always fills both in.

**`feat:`** `console_layout`, `console_pointer_down`, `console_window_extent`
and `render_console`, factored with the fullscreen path through one
`layout_with_title_widgets` — the shape `runtime_client_list` already uses.

**`fix:`** the window itself: `NetworkChartWindowHost` on the
`scoreboard_window_host` template, its `DeveloperHost`/`HostPurpose` variants,
`console_network_chart_window_chrome`/`render_console_network_chart`, and a
reconcile pass so the window's lifetime is exactly the dialog's rather than
something the console commands.

## What the console window owns, and what it does not

The chrome carries the title and the close box, so the dialog stops drawing
them and the sheet reclaims exactly the caption's height. `WM_CLOSE` is
`dialog->Close(false)` (`C4GuiDialogs.cpp:236`), which here is the same toggle
the command and the key binding use, and closing returns focus to the parent
console.

Pointer events *are* routed, unlike the scoreboard's: `C4ScoreboardDlg`
overrides `IsMouseControlled()` to false, while the chart's `C4GUI::Tabular`
selects a sheet on button down. That is the one element the window chrome does
not already own, so it is the only one the dialog still answers for.

Keys are forwarded to `Game.DoKeyboardInput` the way `DialogWinProc` does
(`C4GuiDialogs.cpp:219-228`), so the toggle pressed on the chart window closes
it.

## Tests

Four, and the two frontend ones are the ones I would keep: the sheet reclaims
exactly the height the caption gave up, and a press where the fullscreen close
icon *would* be hits nothing while a tab press still selects. On the app side,
the window request appears and disappears with the dialog and never in
fullscreen, the chrome reports the dialog's fixed extent and its
`IDS_NET_STATISTICS` caption, and the window's framebuffer holds a rendered
dialog rather than a clear.

Built against `--features app-test-shard-mode,app-test-shard-10` as well as the
whole workspace, since a sharded build compiles one fragment and that is where
this test lives.

## Gates

`cargo nextest run --workspace` (11577 passed), clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo fmt
--all -- --check`, engine-snapshots, `parity verify`, `compat verify`,
`xtask-engine-tools` (119) and the Python script tests (477) are all green.

author: hyperpolymath
body:
Remediates **GitHub Workflow Dependency Locking** (public preview, no changelog entry), which rejects runs at `startup_failure` — zero jobs, no logs, nothing in REST or GraphQL. Full analysis: `hyperpolymath/standards#657`.

**Proven on `hyperpolymath/anamnesis`: 6 of 6 workflows dead → 0 `startup_failure`, 13 running.**

### Five steps, in order — each blocks the next

**1. Unbreak the workflow YAML.** Any `permissions:` carrying a scalar with an indented mapping under it:
```yaml
permissions: read-all
  actions: read        # <- mapping under a scalar. Unparseable.
```
This reaches past the one file: **`gh actions-lock` refuses to run when *any* workflow in the repo fails to parse**, so the repo can never acquire a lockfile and can never self-heal.

**2. Repin `standards` reusables** off commits with no `actions.lock`. The rejection requires the **callee** to be covered *at the pinned SHA* — unsatisfiable at a pre-lockfile commit.

**3. Generate** the lockfile with `gh actions-lock`.

**4. Hand-add the reusable-caller entries the tool omits**, as `'<path>': []`.

⚠️ Measured across 218 repos: `P(startup_failure | has lockfile) = 91.7%` vs `15.8%` without — because every workflow a lockfile **omits** is rejected. **A partial lock is worse than none.** Running `gh actions-lock` and stopping there is how this outage spread.

**5. Restore `SPDX-License-Identifier` to line 1**, which the tool displaces with its own banner and which the workflow-security linter greps via `head -1`.

### Verified before this PR was opened
`0` unparseable workflows · lockfile covers **every** workflow, no omissions · SPDX on line 1 in **every** file. The script refuses to push if any of the three fails.

author: a-elnaghi
body:
Four things, reported from the running board. **Two are the same plumbing gap as [#96](https://github.com/dpa-plus/comms/pull/96) on paths I did not fix then**, and I should have gone looking for them rather than waiting to be told twice.

### The graphs could not be drawn

```
[Errno 30] Read-only file system: '/graphify-out'
```

Both wrote their generated page into `<root>/graphify-out/`, so a board running as a login service tried to write `/graphify-out`. Writing into somebody's repository was wrong regardless: these are derived files, and the store directory already holds the derived data for that project and is already writable. They render the **selected** project now, not the one the process started in.

### The release button did not work

> Not released: no active claim with id `01M1177A2T7C3S4BN9WB8QN4HE`

For a claim two panels away. The id came from the selected project's log and was looked up in the process's own, which for a login service is empty. Same gap as the snapshot had, **on the one path that writes**, which makes it the worse half.

Verified against that exact id: without the store it is not found; with it the claim resolves and the reason requirement is what stops it.

### How long a claim has been held

Nowhere on the row. `active` answers whether somebody is alive; the question in front of a board is how long this has been going on, and a claim taken four hours ago reads very differently from one taken four minutes ago even when both are active. Rows say `for 12m` now.

### Code detail, for a reader who does not read code

| | |
|---|---|
| The file list under each agent | folded behind its own count. The count is the magnitude, which is what a person needs |
| The dirty-file paths | fold the same way |
| The feed | leads with the **reason**, not the path |

A row led with `frontend/src/features/map/AconMap.tsx` tells a reader who does not read code nothing at all, while *"Nachlauf-Timer sauber"* tells them what happened. The path stays, quieter, because it is what an agent greps for.

Nothing is deleted. Everything an agent needs is one click away, and the person watching gets a board about work rather than about files.

`895 passed`.

author: ritsukai
body:
## Problem

The committed topology mixed two kinds of fact: **architecture** (`packages`, `graph`, `releaseGroups`, `publicSurfaces`), which changes when the architecture changes, and a **file census** (`ownership.paths`, a 4,928-entry exhaustive path list, plus its counts), which changes whenever any file is added, renamed, or deleted anywhere in the controlled scopes.

Measured on `next` over 14 days: 145 of 878 commits touched these files (~10/day), and JSON diffs ran 10–20× larger than the markdown for the same commit (315+/5− vs 15+/5−). The census had no reader — its only consumption anywhere was `.length`, rendered as a count.

Two costs followed. Every long-lived branch conflicted on regenerated output. And independent branches became mutually **inconsistent**: two PRs that each add files and each regenerate correctly produce a clean textual merge whose counts are wrong for the combined tree, which `--check` then correctly rejects at the queue. #2952 was ejected twice exactly this way.

## The gate is not the defect

Worth stating explicitly, because the tempting fix is wrong: in that scenario the committed artifact really *is* inconsistent with the merged tree, so `platform-architecture-control` firing is correct. Relaxing the check on `merge_group` would convert a true invariant into a vacuous green. The gate is untouched here; the inconsistency is removed at the source instead.

## Change

The committed artifacts now carry only the stable ownership projection (`version` + `requiredOwners`). The census leaves the repository.

**The invariant is unchanged and still enforced.** `validateArchitectureControl` still enumerates every controlled path and still throws when one does not resolve to the required owners — only the snapshot stops being committed. The full census remains available from `architecture-control.mjs` and is still uploaded as the coverage artifact by `platform-architecture-control`.

Architecture facts stay committed and reviewable in the diff, and everything still byte-compares on `pull_request`, `merge_group`, and `push`.

## Evidence

- **Invariant proven live by mutation**: removing the `/.github/scripts/` rule from `.github/architecture-owners` still fails generation with `effective owners must be exactly @oaksprout @ritsukai, found <none>`; reverting restores green.
- **Regression test encodes the acceptance criterion directly**: two branches that each add a controlled file, plus their union, must all produce an identical committed ownership view. Any difference there is exactly the ejection this removes.
- 62/62 across `generate-architecture`, `architecture-control`, `architecture-control-workflow`, `required-check-set`, and `workflow-script-tests`.
- The committed JSON sheds **52,271 lines**.

Closes #3076.

author: plantucha
body:
Executes `OPERATIONAL-MATURITY-ROADMAP-2026-08-27-BRIEF.md` **§1** (the audit) and **§15** (the ranking that gates everything after it). Measurement only — no behaviour changes.

## The conclusion is a null result

**All eight priorities are ALREADY IMPLEMENTED. Nothing ranks P0 or P1. Under §15, the correct action is to implement NOTHING and say so.**

| | count |
|---|---|
| ALREADY IMPLEMENTED | **7** — P#1, P#2, P#3, P#5, P#6, P#7, P#8 |
| NOT NEEDED on measured evidence | **1** — P#4's orchestrator (+ `queue_depth` as a sub-item) |
| PARTIAL / NOT WIRED / MISSING | **0** |

🔴 A null result is what an anti-overbuild rule exists to produce, and it's the one most likely to be quietly overridden — an eight-priority roadmap creates an expectation of eight workstreams, and *"we measured and built nothing"* is a harder report to file than a sprint plan. §15 anticipated it: *"If an existing mechanism already solves a problem adequately: KEEP IT."*

This is **not** "the roadmap was wrong." The charter asks Tepna to audit before coding and to *evaluate whether* an orchestrator is needed. It got its answer.

## Currency, before the first number

`90fea439`, `HEAD..origin/main` = 0, `status --porcelain` = 0. **Not ceremony:** the same inventory in the shared root — 18 commits behind, missing `cpap_spool_caller.py` — returned **16** entries against the current tree's **14**. An audit is entirely measurement, so a stale tree yields a confident classification of a codebase that no longer exists.

## Headline: coordination is broadcast, and that's adequate

14 background pollers, each supervised by `keep_running`, and **zero priority arbitration** — no manager, no semaphore, no `acquire()`. But the guards are **broadcast**: global `asyncio.Event`s plus one global exclusive slot. **O(N) mechanisms, not O(N²) pairs** — it scales.

⚠️ An earlier draft framed this as "6 mechanisms covering 28 possible pairs" and it was **cut before shipping**. The guards aren't pairwise wiring, and that framing would have manufactured an argument for a scheduler the evidence doesn't support.

What *is* absent is priority arbitration, and it's largely moot because the guards **defer rather than compete** — the right default for an instrument: a missed harvest retries, a corrupted acquisition doesn't.

## Two gaps found and withdrawn — vocabulary, not absence

The withdrawal is the useful part. **A grep finds only your own vocabulary.**

- **"cooldown MISSING"** — wrong. It's `backoff`, exponential, with a scar: deliberately *not* reset after a bare connect, because "a bare connect is not a viable session" and resetting there meant a flapping link's backoff could never grow.
- **"queue_depth MISSING"** — wrong *frame*. It's **NOT NEEDED**: the only `Queue()`s are a device control queue and a webmon queue. No acquisition backlog exists, because the architecture has no scheduler. Reporting it would fabricate a number about a structure that doesn't exist.

## Two requirements already closed by explicit design

- **§7's killer case** — *"running 72 h but acquiring nothing must be visibly unhealthy."* Closed at `capture.py:4832`: `data_stale_sec` is set far shorter than `offline_sec` so *"a link that streams nothing is caught by the SAME 5-minute alarm a disconnected one is."*
- **§9's boundary** — enforced at each crossing, not merely intended. `acq_evidence` publishes `ganglior.acquisition-evidence`, a schema *separate* from `ganglior.node-export`, plus six in-line prohibitions reading *"TELEMETRY, not physiology."* ⚠️ I pre-labelled that grep's output "(empty = separate by construction)" before reading it; it had three hits and they were the prohibition itself.

## Falsification, pre-stated

So the P#4 verdict can't be retrofitted: (1) **mutual deference** — two eligible acquisitions both defer and neither runs, the deadlock a broadcast design can produce and pairwise wiring cannot — *the one to watch*, cheaply detected as two actors reporting `waiting` across a whole window; (2) deferral losing data priority would have saved; (3) device count rising past the point where a new actor must read every guard to be correct. None observed today.

## What this does NOT say

That the system is good, unattended-ready, or proven. Every mechanism has an implementation; whether they **work** over 72 unattended hours is §13/§14's question, needs the box, and is untouched. **A module existing is not a mechanism working** — the distinction §19's execution witness exists for, one charter over.

author: aldemirkonuk
body:
**P3.A** (ADR 0029 §1/§2 — runs alongside the P3.0 gate, gated on nothing).
Measurement first, then one slice.

> **Corrected 2026-08-27.** This body previously said *"do not merge without a founder read of §6 — there is an open fork"*, and it stayed there after the fork was answered. **The founder chose all 219 features, no audience carve-outs**, now filed as **OD-108** and cited from [ADR 0029](.planning/decisions/0029-p3-plan-of-record.md) §2.
>
> An adversarial audit flagged the contradiction as blocks-merge and it was right to: a Locked ADR asserting a settled decision, a PR body saying it was open, and no register entry between them is indistinguishable from a fabricated consensus. The decision was real; the trail was not. Both are fixed, and OD-108 records that it was filed retroactively rather than quietly backdating it.

## The measured gap

`apps/mobile` presents **11 %** of the web feature set the 47 page notes describe. It was **9 %** before this branch.

| | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| §1a features present | 7 | **11** |
| partial | 25 | **27** |
| absent | 187 | **181** |
| total across 47 notes | 219 | 219 |
| weighted parity (`yes`=1, `part`=½) | **8.9 %** | **11.2 %** |
| routes with any mobile surface | 15 / 47 | **16 / 47** |

By audience, and this matters more than the headline: **staff 21 %, owner 10 %, public 3 %, dev 0 %.** Mobile is a staff/owner operations app that has never attempted the public (auth, invites, legal) or dev (studio, simpos, admin, sandbox) surfaces. Almost certainly deliberate — but written down nowhere, which is why the fork in §6 exists.

Full route-by-route and feature-by-feature census: `.planning/04-specs/P3A-MOBILE-PARITY-GAP.md`.

## Four defects found by measuring (all pre-existing on `main`)

The docs claimed live updates; the code did not deliver them.

1. **`connectSocket` had no caller anywhere in the app.** `socket.io-client` shipped as a dependency, the client was fully written, nothing ever invoked it. Mobile ran purely on react-query polling.
2. **Wrong namespace.** It connected to the bare origin. The gateway declares `namespace: "/ws"` (`websocket.gateway.ts:161`); web gets this right at `apps/web/src/lib/websocket.tsx:394`.
3. **Two of three event subscriptions named events that do not exist** — `order:updated` and `order_change` versus the real `order:created` / `order:status_changed`.
4. **Push taps went nowhere.** `attachPushListeners` had no caller; cold-start taps were unhandled.

Plus one left unfixed: **`apps/mobile` appears nowhere in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.** Nothing typechecks or lints it on a PR — which is exactly how three of the four above survived.

## What this branch does

- Live layer wired to the session lifecycle: connects on sign-in, closes on lock/sign-out, re-handshakes on token refresh, subscribes to all 10 real gateway events with a per-event cache-invalidation map.
- Push taps deep-link, including cold start; one route resolver shared by the banner and the inbox.
- **Notification inbox** (`/notifications` — one of the 32 routes with no mobile surface): unread/read/archived, expand-to-detail, open / mark read / mark unread / archive / delete / mark-all-read, bell with unread badge on Today.
- A test runner that can fail. `"test"` was `echo … && exit 0`, which turbo counted as a pass.

**Nothing outside `apps/mobile/**` changed** except a 12-line `pnpm-lock.yaml` append inside the `apps/mobile` importer block. No gateway endpoint was added — every endpoint the inbox uses already existed.

## Verification

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `tsc --noEmit` | clean (clean at baseline too — no-regression check) |
| `jest` | **37 tests, 2 suites, pass** |
| Guard proven against the pre-fix code | reintroduced the phantom event name + missing `/ws` → **5 of 9 socket tests fail**, naming both defects |
| `expo export --platform ios` | succeeds, 5.67 MB Hermes bundle |
| New code in the shipped bundle | `strings` finds `Nothing needs you`, `order:status_changed`, `conversation:summary_updated`, `stock:low`, `/cellar/receive/` |

The socket test **reads `websocket.gateway.ts` and parses its `emitToRoom` call sites** rather than restating the names, so a server-side rename fails the mobile build instead of silently muting the phone.

### Not verified: the iOS simulator

**I did not run this on a simulator.** ADR 0029 §5's *"verified on a simulator, not asserted"* is **not met by this branch.** Managed Expo project with no `ios/` directory; `expo prebuild` needs CocoaPods, which is not installed, and system Ruby is 2.6.10 — below its minimum. Expo Go is not a substitute (MMKV, Skia, Reanimated 4 + new arch). `expo export` proves the app *builds*, not that it *renders*.

## Blockers recorded, not built (all outside `apps/mobile`)

1. `group_key` is written (`notifications.service.ts:660`) but dropped by `mapNotificationRow` (`:731`) — no client can stack digests. Web has the same limitation.
2. Mobile's receiving screen shows prices where `/receiving/:orderId/door` §1a says *"No prices anywhere by design"*. Product call, not a bug fix.
3. `useSession` holds one `restaurantId` — every multi-branch feature is blocked on this.
4. `/sommelier`'s chat route is unregistered (its own note says so); mobile deep-links to web.
5. `apps/mobile` absent from CI.

## The fork for the founder

**What does "parity" mean for the dev and public tiers?** 34 of the 219 features are `audience: dev`, 31 are `audience: public`. If both are out of scope the real denominator is **154**, and parity today is **16 %**, not 11 % — that one call changes the stage's size by a third. Spec §6 recommends scoping P3.A to `audience ∈ {owner, staff}` and saying so in the ADR. Not defaulted here.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)



---

## Added after the audit (2026-08-27)

Two corrections to this branch, both to work added on top of the original agent's:

**The CI guard was a blocklist, and it was broken in four lines.** `scripts/check_test_scripts_are_real.py` matched no-op *shapes* (`echo`, `true`, `:`, `exit 0`). All of these passed while doing nothing — verified by running the real script:

```
"test": "npm run nothing"     indirection the regex never resolves
"test": "sh -c 'exit 0'"      not a builtin at the top level
"test": "#"                   a comment
"test": "node -e \"\""          a real binary running nothing
```

Inverted to an **allowlist**: the script must invoke a recognised runner, and widening `RUNNERS` is a deliberate edit. All four bypasses now fail; the original `apps/mobile` defect still fails; the repo passes. The blocklist version would have shipped looking correct — the same failure it was written to catch.

**Still open from the audit, not fixed here** (`apps/mobile/src/lib/push.ts:99-118`): `getLastNotificationResponseAsync()` is never cleared, so a user signing out and back in within one process may be re-navigated to their last notification's route. Reasoned from the documented API, not reproduced on a device — and this branch already cannot meet ADR 0029 §5's simulator criterion, so it is recorded rather than patched blind.

body:
Auf einem aufgehellten Tafelhintergrund gingen die Beschriftungen unter: Freistehende Elemente schreiben immer hell, und nur ein reines Textfeld hatte bisher eine eigene Schriftfarbe.

## Schriftfarbe — Tafel und Element

Zwei Stellen, dieselbe Auswahl:

- **Menü → „Aussehen" → „Schriftfarbe"**: „Automatisch" (die bisherige Regel: hell auf dunklem Grund, dunkel auf heller Karte), „Dunkel", „Hell" oder eine eigene Farbe. Gilt für alle Elemente der Tafel.
- **Einstellungen eines Elements → „Beschriftung und Farbe"**: dieselbe Wahl, die erste heißt hier „Wie die Tafel". Solange sie steht, folgt das Element der Vorgabe; jede andere Wahl bleibt am Element stehen, auch wenn die Tafel später umgestellt wird.

Zwei Entscheidungen dabei:

- Die Farbe färbt **Beschriftung und Inhalt** (`ink`, `inkSoft`, `bigText`) — also auch den gezogenen Namen, die Uhrzeit, den Pegel. Nur die Überschrift zu färben hätte das Problem halb gelöst; auf hellem Grund ist der große weiße Name genauso unlesbar. Auf einer Karte ersetzt die gewählte Farbe den Akzent-Farbverlauf.
- **Flächen** (`wash`) bleiben bei der automatischen Farbe. Das ist kein Text, und mitgefärbt wirkt es unruhig — dafür rechnet `BoardStyle` jetzt intern mit `standardInk`.

Neue Felder: `Board.schriftfarbe` und `BoardWidget.schriftfarbe` (Hex, leer = automatisch bzw. wie die Tafel), beide mit nachsichtiger Dekodierung. Die Zeilen dafür liegen als `Schriftfarbwahl` in `Verlaufwahl.swift`, damit beide Einstellungsseiten dieselbe Bedienung zeigen.

## Farbe der Namenskärtchen

Die Kärtchen der Gruppen- und Tagesgruppen-Ansicht und die Chips der schon gezogenen Namen lagen fest auf `style.wash`.

- Neu am Element: `kartenfarbe` / `kartenfarbe2` (leer = wie bisher), eingestellt über die vorhandene `Verlaufwahl` — also wahlweise als Verlauf aus zwei Farben.
- Zu finden in den Einstellungen unter „Wie es aussieht" → „Eigene Farbe der Kärtchen", in beiden Ansichten an derselben Stelle.
- Die Schrift auf dem Kärtchen richtet sich nach der gewählten Farbe (hell oder dunkel) — es sei denn, für das Element ist ausdrücklich eine Schriftfarbe gesetzt: die gilt immer.

`docs/tafelbild/support.html` um beide Abschnitte ergänzt. `MARKETING_VERSION` auf 1.0.53 (beide Stellen im pbxproj). Bau in GitHub Actions grün: „Übersetzen (iOS-Simulator)" und „Starten (Simulator)".

body:
feat(ui): sign-in modal on session expiry, and stop serving the stale tester Three related fixes behind one symptom: hitting /pinggateway-test.html on SE gave you a page whose every button 401s, with no way to sign in and no way back. 1. SE was serving a page the app had already replaced. demo_api_server/public/pinggateway-test.html had become a 238-byte redirect into the in-app Agent Gateway Inspector, but demo_api_ui/public/ still held the original 12.3KB standalone console — and that is the copy nginx serves on SE. So local redirected into the app while SE showed the superseded page: local /pinggateway-test.html -> /pinggateway-test -> /agent-gateway-inspector?subtab=tester SE /pinggateway-test.html -> 12.3KB standalone console The UI copy is now the same redirect, so both targets land in the app, where auth is actually handled. The standalone console is no longer served anywhere. 2. Session expiry now interrupts with a modal instead of a banner. The plumbing already existed — apiClient's 401 interceptor dispatches SESSION_REAUTH_EVENT and App renders SessionReauthBanner — so this is a presentation change, not new machinery. The HITL "Manual approval required" branch of that component is UNCHANGED and still renders the fixed banner. HITL consent is protected (REGRESSION_PLAN §1) and restyling it was not part of this; a test pins that. 3. Signing in now returns you to the page you were on. navigateToCustomerOAuthForceLogin() took no returnTo and went to /api/auth/oauth/user/login?force=true, so re-authenticating dropped you somewhere else and you lost your place. It now carries return_to, joined with & since force=true already occupies the query string — a second "?" would have made the BFF read return_to as part of force's value. Same for navigateToAdminOAuthLogin. Both default to the current path, and to /dashboard from "/", matching navigateToCustomerOAuthLogin, and both pass a bare path because sanitizePostLoginReturnPath rejects query strings. Modal text colours are stated explicitly rather than inherited: the banner's #78350f is tuned for an amber background and reads wrong on the modal surface. Both are solid and high-contrast — REGRESSION_PLAN §0 forbids muted grey hint text in modals. Tests: 24 pass in the two touched files (19 pre-existing authUi tests unchanged, 4 new return_to cases, 5 new component cases covering both branches). Full UI suite 3507 passed, and `npm run build` exits 0. While verifying, the full parallel run failed in a DIFFERENT unrelated async test on three of four runs, while main passed twice and a sequential run passed every time. That is a pre-existing race surfaced by the added load, not state corruption from this change — written up in TECH_DEBT.md with the measurements, because the next person to add a UI test will hit it and should not spend the afternoon I did chasing it.

The PR replaces the stale standalone PingGateway tester with an SPA redirect, presents expired sessions in a sign-in modal, and preserves the current path across customer and admin OAuth reauthentication. - Keeps the HITL approval flow on its existing fixed-banner presentation. - Adds component and authentication-navigation coverage. - Stabilizes the BroadcastChannel race test and documents the investigation.

 The PR should not merge until the stale tester capture and walkthrough consumers are updated for the new redirect destination. The removed standalone tester remains hard-coded in current capture scripts and walkthrough checks, so those workflows now generate or validate content against a redirect page instead of the labeled Token Lab. **Files Needing Attention:** demo_api_ui/public/pinggateway-test.html and its capture/walkthrough consumers

author: lionear
body:
`EngineManifest` had `Id`, `Name`, `Version`, `Author`, `Description` and `MinSdkVersion`. That is
enough to *show* a plugin and not enough to *decide* anything about one. This adds the three fields a
host has to read before it runs foreign code, and it does it now because there are no external
implementations yet — after that, every new required field is a breaking change for everyone outside.

## Platform requirements

New `PluginPlatform` in the SDK: an OS name plus an optional minimum version, listed on the manifest.
Empty means "anywhere", which is the common case and what keeps the field from becoming noise.

```json
"platforms": [{ "os": "macos", "minVersion": "26" }]
```

The name is a string rather than an enum on purpose — it is the vocabulary `OperatingSystem.IsOSPlatform`
and `[SupportedOSPlatform]` already use, and the set of operating systems is not ours to close. A name
this build does not know simply does not match, so a typo shows up in the rejection text instead of
being swallowed as "runs anywhere". Matching is `OperatingSystem.IsOSPlatformVersionAtLeast`, so there
is no version arithmetic of our own to get wrong.

The minimum version is per operating system because that is how the requirement falls: Apple's
`container` needs macOS 26, and a plugin that also speaks to Linux has no floor there. One number for
the whole plugin could only ever be wrong for one of them.

A floor that cannot be parsed counts as "no", not as "no floor" — a manifest that means macOS 26 and
mistypes it must not end up running on macOS 13.

## What the plugin contributes

`Backends` (a list of `BackendKind`) and `ContributesUi`, so a plugin can say backends, UI, or both.
UI without a backend is a real shape, not a hypothetical: Manifest Studio contributes three pages and
no `IBackendProvider` (KON-331).

An enum here where the OS is a string, because the two sets differ in kind: operating systems are the
world's and open, backend kinds are this SDK's and closed. A plugin naming a kind this build has never
heard of was built against a newer SDK, which `MinSdkVersion` already rejects for a better reason.

**The declaration is held to the assembly** — in one direction only. Contributing a backend kind the
manifest never named is rejected, and so is a UI the manifest did not declare. Contributing *fewer*
backends than declared is fine, because a provider list depends on the machine: nerdctl contributes one
provider per containerd namespace, so a machine without nerdctl gives it none, and that plugin loaded
correctly — it just has nothing to offer here. Without this check the declaration would be exactly what
`MinSdkVersion` was: a field nothing reads.

## MinSdkVersion

Enforcement landed with the loader in KON-279; what was missing was a format. `Version.TryParse` alone
also accepts `1.2` and `1.2.3.4`, which leaves the manifest saying two things — is the missing part a
zero or a wildcard? — about the one number that decides whether foreign code runs. It is now
`major.minor.patch` and nothing else, and a manifest that writes it any other way is reported in
Settings rather than ignored.

## Where the check happens

Platform first, ahead of both the consent question and the assembly read. A consent prompt for a plugin
that cannot run here is a question with no useful answer, and it would come back every launch; hashing
and loading an assembly built for another OS is work done to reach a failure already on the label.

Rejections stay values, not exceptions — a plugin that does not belong here is a row in Settings with a
reason, never a reason for the app not to start.

## Deliberately not here

- **Capabilities** (Docker socket, network, files) — that is KON-79's, and it is the one part of a
  manifest that cannot change after publication without breaking every plugin already shipped, so it
  waits for the trust model that gives it teeth. Room left, nothing built.
- **Icons and branding** — stays in `BackendChipStyle` (KON-80).

## One thing worth a second opinion

I left `platforms` off both in-repo plugins, so both keep declaring "anywhere", which is exactly their
behaviour today. nerdctl is the arguable one: it drives a Linux-native CLI, but it is reachable on
macOS and Windows through Lima and WSL, and narrowing it here would change which machines offer it.
That felt like your call rather than a guess I should bake into a permanent contract.

## Verification

`dotnet build Kontena.slnx` — 0 warnings, 0 errors. `dotnet test Kontena.slnx` — 2943 passed, 0 failed,
13 assemblies. `python3 tools/changelog-render.py --check` — 14 fragments OK.

24 new tests. I also mutation-checked them rather than trusting green: neutering the platform gate, the
unreadable-floor rule, the contribution check and the `major.minor.patch` rule failed 2 and 8 tests
respectively, so each rule has something behind it that actually fails when the rule goes.

author: seanpham99
body:
v0.7.0 tagged, and `release.yml` never ran. Nor did it for v0.6.0 — that release has **zero assets** too.

## Root cause

release-please creates its tag with `GITHUB_TOKEN`, and GitHub deliberately does not trigger workflows from token-created refs. The `push: tags: v*` trigger has therefore never fired for an automated release, so goreleaser and `npm publish` have never run for one.

**This is why npm `latest` has been stranded behind the GitHub releases** — 0.3.0 while GitHub had 0.4.0, then still 0.3.0 at 0.6.0. Two separate integration spikes flagged that as a distribution bug; neither found the cause, because the symptom looks like a publish failure rather than a workflow that never started.

## What this does

`workflow_dispatch` with a tag input, so the release can be run by hand for those tags. The tag is resolved once into a step output and reused by the CHANGELOG check, npm publish and GitHub Packages — under a manual run `GITHUB_REF` is the branch, so every one of those would otherwise have built the wrong version.

## Follow-up worth doing

The durable fix is giving release-please a PAT so its tags trigger workflows like any other push. That needs a secret only you can create, so this unblocks shipping v0.7.0 without one.

author: patrickweh
body:
## Problem

`max_relation_column_to_many_hops` was introduced with a default of 1 after a column path walked a relation circle and died at the execution time limit. The cap works on depth, but depth was never the problem.

A path such as `addresses.mediaConsultants.name` on a contacts table walks two to-many hops (contact hasMany addresses, address belongsToMany users) through three distinct models. It is the ordinary "list of a list" a relation tree invites, it worked before the cap, and since the cap it is removed from `enabledCols` while the sidebar checkbox stays ticked. The column disappears from the table and from the export column list with no explanation.

Verified on a running instance for `['customer_number', 'addresses.sbm_media_consultants.name']`:

```
cap=1
surviving cols: ["customer_number"]
```

## Change

- A path whose to-many hop returns to a model it already visited is dropped, whatever the cap says. That circle (`category.categorizables.categories`, `comments.post.comments.body`) is what the relation tree lets a user assemble by accident and the reason the cap was written.
- `max_relation_column_to_many_hops` defaults to 0, so depth is no longer capped out of the box. An instance that wants a limit sets one, and the per relation `max_relation_column_values` still bounds every single hop.

## Tests

`ChainedToManyRelationColumnTest` now covers the circle (dropped, also with no cap configured), the two hop path through distinct models (kept), and an explicitly configured cap (honoured). `NestedRelationColumnValueTest` asserts a two hop column actually renders its value. The fixture `Comment` model gets a `tags()` morphToMany so a genuine second to-many hop exists.

author: joelonbitmal
body:
Phase 0 and Phase 1 of `design_planning/BUILD-PLAN.md`, built from the design package.

## What works

Capture a line — it parses locally with `chrono-node` — save it, and if it does not fit the day the gate says so before it is added, names the overage in minutes, and offers two concrete fixes plus "Add it anyway". The day reopens with the row highlighted and one undo.

Twenty screens: `day` `week` `month` `capture` `types` `task` `routine` `session` `errand` `appt` `repeat` `gate` `detail` `close` `shut` `tray` `projects` `project` `search` `settings`, plus the bottom tabs.

## Structure

- **`packages/core`** — the arithmetic, in plain TypeScript so it runs server-side unchanged and can be tested without a renderer. The capacity formula, the gate, recurrence, the entitlement table, date maths. 118 tests.
- **`apps/mobile`** — Expo SDK 57, Expo Router, SQLite via Drizzle. 27 tests.

## Decisions worth reviewing

Each is commented where it was made.

- **The tray is a new design.** It is listed as undesigned in `design/README.md` and owed in `BUILD-PLAN.md`, so it follows the surrounding patterns rather than a drawing. The slip count is stated, not styled; the fit is shown before the tap; nothing moves itself.
- **The gate does not fire when editing.** It is about adding commitment to a day, not re-saving something already on it. Consequence: lengthening an edited record can take a day over without the sheet.
- **The move option picks the smallest record that clears the overage**, not the largest.
- **The type picker lists five kinds, not seven.** Bill and Spending belong to the money phase.
- **`estimated` generalises the settled capacity formula** to a third planned segment, reducing to the original exactly when zero.
- **Morning/Afternoon/Evening boundaries** are not settled anywhere in the design package; noon and 17:00, in one named constant.
- The mockup's **"26 more of these"** is illustrative — counted from a real start date it is 23, and the test records why.

## Not done

`timer`, `splash` and `signin` remain; `signin` is blocked on the Apple and Google developer accounts. Also owed and undesigned: the template shelf, the first-run set, drag-to-reschedule, calendar in/out.

## Verification

145 tests, typecheck, lint, format, an Android bundle, `expo-doctor` 21/21.

**It has never run on a device.** Everything visual is unverified — fonts, safe areas, and whether the fixed-frame screens fit Android's shorter usable height. That is the first thing to do with this branch, not the last.

author: meszmate
body:
Closes #211.

## The defect

Both the join and the removal were scoped to the pool the mailbox is entitled to **right now**, so nothing was ever handed the pool it used to be in:

```go
_ = s.warmupHealth.EnsurePoolMembershipWithRole(ctx, account.ID, s.resolveWarmupPoolType(ctx, account), role)
_ = s.warmupHealth.RemovePoolMembership(ctx, account.ID, s.resolveWarmupPoolType(ctx, account))
```

A paying org's mailbox is in `premium`. The org downgrades, `resolveWarmupPoolType` starts answering `free`, and the only removal that ever runs targets `free` and removes nothing. The premium row survives, so `GetPoolParticipants("premium")` keeps handing a mailbox with no paid entitlement to paying customers as a warmup partner. Upgrade is the mirror. And because `GetSpamScore` was `SUM(spam_score)` over the account's rows while every writer of that score is account-scoped, a dual member had each increment counted twice by the health evaluator.

There is a second half the issue did not name. Membership was only ever corrected by the warmup task, and a mailbox that stopped warming (warmup switched off, campaign finished, subscription lapsed) has no chain and is not a schedule candidate. Nothing would revisit it even after the join/leave fix, so the stale row would sit in the pool forever.

## The fix

**Membership is a move, not an addition.** `MoveToPool` is a single upsert with the account as the conflict target:

```sql
INSERT INTO warmup_pool_participants (pool_id, email_account_id, joined_at, spam_score, participant_role)
VALUES ($1::uuid, $2::uuid, NOW(), 0, $3::text)
ON CONFLICT (email_account_id) DO UPDATE
SET pool_id = EXCLUDED.pool_id,
    participant_role = EXCLUDED.participant_role
```

Only `pool_id` and the role are overwritten, so spam score, health state, block and the `health_signals_from` floor ride along untouched. That matters: a fresh row starts healthy with a zero score, so a naive "delete then insert" would have let a blocked mailbox launder its penalty by changing tier.

**Migration 000097** makes it structural. It merges any dual membership worst-wins first (worst health state, max spam score, earliest join and signal floor, `recipient_only` beating `sender_receiver`), keeps the row for the pool the mailbox is entitled to now (tie-breaking to `free`, the lower-trust side), then adds `UNIQUE (email_account_id)` and drops the plain index it supersedes.

**Removal is never pool-scoped.** `RemoveFromAllPools` replaces every wrongly-scoped removal and the two hand-rolled `for _, poolType := range []string{"premium", "free"}` loops. A caller that knows the mailbox is no longer entitled does not know which pool it is sitting in, and now does not have to.

**A tier change moves the row with the column.** `UpdateEmailAccountWarmupPoolType` writes `email_accounts.warmup_pool_type` and moves the participant row in one transaction. They record the same fact, and the worker tier migrations (`MigrateOrgToFreeWorkers` and friends) were updating only the column. A mailbox in no pool stays in none.

**A reconcile pass closes the gap.** `ReconcileWarmupPoolMembership` runs inside the existing 10-minute warmup sweep, walks every participant, evicts the ones whose workspace lost warmup access or whose mailbox is no longer active, and moves the rest to the pool their tier belongs to. Roles are deliberately left alone so a mailbox demoted to `recipient_only` for failing domain auth is not quietly promoted back by a sweep that knows nothing about why. One subscription lookup per organization, not per mailbox.

**An unreadable subscription is not evidence.** Every eviction path previously did `canWarmup, _ := CanUseWarmup(...)`, so a transient failure read as "not entitled" and removed the mailbox. Only a definite answer evicts now; the send is still skipped either way.

**Spam score arithmetic.** `GetSpamScore` takes `MAX` rather than `SUM`. `IncrementSpamScore` clamps to the column's `0..100` CHECK (past 100 it violated the constraint, and every caller ignores that error, so a noisy mailbox silently kept its old score) and treats "mailbox is in no pool" as 0 rather than an error, which is what a late signal about a mailbox that just left warmup looks like.

Also folded in: the premium-then-free probe in the warmup service becomes one account-scoped read, which is exact now that a mailbox is in one pool and drops the bias toward whichever pool was probed first.

## Verification

Live tests need a migrated database:

```
WARMBLY_TEST_DB=postgres://warmbly:warmbly@localhost:15432/warmbly_dev?sslmode=disable \
  go test ./internal/app/warmup/ -run Live -v
```

- **Migration**, against a scratch DB seeded with real dual memberships: the downgraded mailbox survived in `free` still blocked, score 62, original join date and demoted role intact; the upgraded one survived in `premium` with the worst of its two states. Down and up round-trip, and a fresh database migrates 1 to 97 in a single pass.
- **15 live tests** (`internal/app/warmup/pool_membership_live_test.go`) over the move, the reputation carry, the unique index, the score arithmetic, the tier move and the account-scoped read. Verified they bite: dropping the index fails two of them immediately.
- **8 unit tests** (`internal/tasks/warmup_pool_reconcile_test.go`) over the reconcile pass, including the "do not evict on a lookup failure" rule and the per-org caching.
- **End to end**: booted the real backend against a migrated scratch database holding a drifted mailbox and an inactive one. It logged `moved=1 removed=1`, the database matched, and a second boot was silent.
- `gofmt`, `make lint`, `make check-migrations`, docs `types:check` and `lint`, and the full Go suite are clean.

Docs: `guides/warmup.mdx` now states that a mailbox is in exactly one pool, that a plan change moves it and carries its standing (so a quarantine is not cleared by changing tier), and that losing access removes it within minutes whether or not it was still warming.

## Adjacent, not fixed here

Nothing outside the sandbox seed ever creates the `warmup_pools` rows. No migration seeds them and the app only joins existing pools, so on a real install `EnsurePoolMembershipWithRole` returns "warmup pool not found" and warmup never works until someone inserts them by hand. Separate defect, and it needs a decision about pinning pool UUIDs in a migration.

author: sfmskywalker
body:
CI-only. One file, sixteen lines. Extracted from #198 so the repository gets it now rather than when that PR's investigation resolves.

## Why

`concurrency-conformance` hung for **40+ minutes** on a branch earlier today against a 10m46s baseline, and produced nothing: no failing test, no stacks, no artifact. The job declares no `timeout-minutes`, so it would have held a runner for the 360-minute default. It had to be cancelled by hand, and everything we know about that hang came from comparing per-step timings across runs rather than from the job itself.

The same job runs 32-way write contention against live PostgreSQL, SQL Server and a MongoDB replica set. It is the most likely job in this repository to hang and the least informative when it does.

## What changes

**`timeout-minutes: 30` on `concurrency-conformance`.** Roughly three times the healthy ten, so ordinary slowness stays green and a hang fails in half an hour instead of six.

**`--blame-hang --blame-hang-timeout 10m --blame-hang-dump-type full` on the W2 step**, with the results directory uploaded as an artifact on failure. The hang detector kills the test host after ten minutes of no progress and writes a sequence file naming the test that was in flight plus a full process dump. The next occurrence diagnoses itself instead of being reconstructed from timings.

**A workflow concurrency group**, so a superseded run is cancelled rather than left running:

```yaml
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}
```

`cancel-in-progress` deliberately excludes `main`: cancelling `main`'s own CI to make room for the next merge would discard the signal most worth keeping.

## Scope

`git diff --name-only main` is exactly `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. No product code, no test code, no packaging. The YAML was parsed to confirm all 15 jobs still load, the timeout attaches to the intended job, and the upload step is wired.

The hang under investigation is intermittent — the same product code has run this job green three times and hung once — so this deliberately does **not** claim to fix it. It bounds the cost and makes the next occurrence self-describing.

body:
## Nothing here takes effect until you promote the drafts

Every change lands as a `.draft.yaml` beside an untouched shipped file. **Each shipped `kb2/` file is byte-identical to its previous state.** That includes the repairs below — the pirate-host citations and the wrong-book Lilly references are still live in what ships until a draft is promoted at a review gate. Promotion is deliberately human-only: rename `<el>.draft.yaml` over `<el>.yaml` and set `reviewed: true`.

Browse the drafts via `python -m kb_tools.build_review_site` → `kb_tools/artifacts/review_site.html`.

## Human Design — the main change

The registry goes from **6 sources to 21**, all free and published by the rights holder: 69 public teaching pages, the official Dictionary, and 23 cached sample PDFs of Ra Uru Hu transcripts carrying printed page numbers.

**Nuances resting on the unreadable *Definitive Book* alone: 78 → 9.** All 100 still cite it, unchanged and un-relocated.

Read that number precisely, because the registry now says so too: it does **not** mean 90 claims became checkable against that book. They acquired a *different* source a reviewer can open, while their locator into the Definitive Book stays exactly as unverified as before. Every added witness evidences *the tradition*, never what that book says. **33 of 100** now carry a passage a reviewer can actually read.

Adopted by explicit decision on 2026-08-26, including the licence risk — Jovian Archive permits quoting brief excerpts with attribution but restricts derivative works intended for commercial distribution. The registry records that neutrally rather than burying it.

## Claim corrections — worth your attention

- **Two Reflector nuances asserted what Ra explicitly calls "just an illusion."** He says the shield *blocks* human conditioning and cannot block the Program; the KB said Reflectors take in and amplify the energy of whoever they are around. Corrected to the source, with the divergence from Jovian's own current web page recorded rather than hidden.
- **The Manifesting Generator nuance inverted its source** on what produces friction — blaming a skipped inform step where the source blames initiating from the mind. Corrected.
- **15 unsourced clauses removed** from claim text — "or the person burns down", "decades", "a limited tank", "in a crisis". Deleted, not reworded, because rewording is where fabrication enters.
- **`profiles 3_6` n1 dropped** rather than padded once its unsourced inference was removed.

## Astrology

`ascendants` de-physicalised: **24 → 16 nuances**, with no claims about build, features, hair or complexion remaining. The engine was inferring physical and racial characteristics from a birth time; 8 of 12 Lilly nuances were dropped rather than reworded into pseudo-behavioural claims.

The 12 remaining "manner" nuances were also **mis-cited** — Ptolemy I.11/I.18 cover weather and winds with no human behaviour in them — and move to III.13 *"Of the Quality of the Soul"*. The elemental half of each is removed as unsourced: Ptolemy organises by quadruplicity and has no element-to-character doctrine anywhere.

## Repairs

- **22 citations naming a pirate host** (`dokumen.pub`) stripped and re-verified against the legitimate Para Research 1979 scan.
- **12 Lilly citations** moved from Book III to Book One Chap. XVI. Book III's chapter holds only a stature table and a cross-reference — confirmed from the page image, which also **disproves** a claimed Taurus contradiction that two earlier passes had asserted.
- **A false registry promise deleted, not annotated**: search-inside does not return printed page numbers, it returns the item's leaf count.
- **Nine Gene Keys locators** citing online-course module numbers as if they were book headings now say so where a reader sees them.

## Known-open, deliberately not fixed here

- **`ascendants` has a structural mismatch.** No source reads character from the rising sign alone — Ptolemy uses Mercury and the Moon, Alan Leo uses planetary majority with the Ascendant as a casting vote, Lilly mixes three signs. Disclosed in all twelve notes; not a fix.
- **Nine nuances remain sole-source** on a book nobody has opened. Interlibrary loan is the one free route never tried.
- **A loader gate is pending**: the loader enforces "`partial` requires a note" but not its mirror. The two nuances that would fail it are fixed only in the drafts, so the check must be armed *with* promotion, not before.

## Verification

964 tests pass, ruff clean, strict and drafts validation both OK. 156 added Human Design citations were each verified against cached primary text rather than against the report that recommended them — which is how two fabrications were caught before shipping: "The Kiron return" is not a Line 6 heading, and the Swann-Herbert sample cannot ground the authority nuances at all.

body:
Builds on [#76](https://github.com/skiweg1985/prtg-nats/pull/76), which is still open — this branch carries its commit too. Merge #76 first and this one shrinks to a single commit.

## Why

The message line said which access point answered and which address it offered, but not which network any of it belonged to. In a list of sensors that line is everything visible without opening one, and `on 1c:30:03:12:46:f3` leaves the reader to remember which SSID that probe was configured for.

## What changed

The SSID goes in front of the BSSID, quoted — an SSID may carry spaces, so the boundary would otherwise be a guess:

```text
Authentication succeeded on "Office" via 1c:30:03:12:46:f3, DHCP offered 192.0.2.75
The access point rejected the passphrase on "Office" (auth-failed-psk)
```

It comes from the helper's reading of the link rather than from the parameter, so it names the network actually joined — and it works behind a `--profile`, where the PRTG configuration holds the profile name and nothing else. A run that never associated has no reading to go on and falls back to the parameter; a run that had neither names no network at all rather than an empty one.

The failure line gets the same treatment: which network could not be joined is the first thing anyone wants from it, and it is the line PRTG shows for the alarm.

`SENSOR_VERSION` goes to 3, per the rule #76 writes down.

## Checks

- `tests/check-static.sh`: 148 passed, 0 failed
- `ruff check --select E9,F`: clean · `markdownlint-cli2`: 0 issues
- The line built from six real helper answers: success complete, success behind `--profile`, success without the DHCP stage, failure before association, failure after it, failure with nothing known. No empty quotes, no stray separators
- On the Bookworm probe against the real network: `Authentication succeeded on "Simplicity Guest" via 1c:30:03:12:46:f3, DHCP offered 192.168.210.75`, and for an SSID that does not exist: `The interface did not associate within the time budget on "prtg-nats-kein-netz-7f2a" (assoc-timeout)`

body:
> **TL;DR** — every metric-layer `UserWarning` echo that carries a `WarningCode` now reads `expected_warnings` before echoing, so a declared sweep gets a quiet stderr with its audit trail intact. The `ic` / `ic_ir` tie-ratio advisory, which had no structured twin at all, gains `WarningCode.HIGH_TIE_RATIO` and joins the contract.

## Summary

`evaluate(..., expected_warnings=...)` promises: a declared code keeps its structured record (marked `expected=True` at assembly) and only loses the human-channel echo. `_warn_below_floor` / `_warn_below_scaled_floor` / `_warn_if_high_drop_rate` / `_warn_if_few_ic_assets` honoured it; the remaining metric-layer sites called `warnings.warn` directly and ignored the declaration.

Sites now gated with the same `if code not in expected_warnings` idiom (no new abstraction — the helper shape is reused where it fits, the idiom inline where a site owns its message):

| Site | Code |
| --- | --- |
| `fm_beta` | `serial_correlation_detected` |
| `pooled_beta`, Driscoll-Kraay path | `unreliable_se_short_periods` |
| `bmp_z` | `bmp_return_vol_fallback` |
| `top_concentration` | `one_signed_factor` |
| `directional_pair_accuracy` | `few_ordering_pairs` |
| `_warn_thin_quantile_groups`, reached via `compute_spread_series` and `quantile_spread_vw` | `thin_quantile_groups` |
| `ic` / `ic_ir` tie-ratio | `high_tie_ratio` (new) |

Bodies that lacked the parameter (`pooled_beta`, `directional_pair_accuracy`, `compute_spread_series`) now declare `expected_warnings: tuple[str, ...] = ()` so dispatch injects it; `pooled_beta` threads it into its SE helper, and `quantile_spread` forwards it on the two inline `compute_spread_series` calls that bypass the DAG. No estimator, no structured record, and no attached code set changes apart from the new tie-ratio code.

### Deliberately left, with reasons

- **`common_quantile.py` per-bucket-periods echo** and **`spanning.py` snooping echo** — neither carries a `WarningCode`, so there is nothing for a caller to declare. `greedy_forward_selection` already has its own opt-out (`suppress_snooping_warning=`) and is a construction helper, not a metric result. Giving these codes would change the set of codes a run attaches, which is out of scope here.
- **`_primitives/_caar.py`** — its two echoes (magnitude-weighted CAAR, non-finite event rows) attach no code to any `MetricResult`. Gating them on `sparse_magnitude_weighted` would give "no record, echo quiet", which is precisely the silent drop the contract forbids. See the finding below.
- **`_helpers.py::_warn_high_tie_ratio`** (the quantile-bucketing tie advisory) — codeless, and the scope note limited the new code to the IC sites.
- **Out of scope entirely** (not metric-result warnings): `preprocess/normalize.py`, `preprocess/orthogonalize.py`, `preprocess/returns.py`, `_multi_factor.py`, `slicing/dispatcher.py`, `slicing/period_inference.py`, `stats/multiple_testing.py`.

### Finding for a follow-up

`WarningCode.SPARSE_MAGNITUDE_WEIGHTED` is documented in the code table and rendered in the reference docs, but nothing in the library ever appends it — the `compute_caar` echo it describes is the only channel it has. Attaching it at the `caar` / `bmp_z` layer (and then gating the echo) is a separate change; flagging it rather than folding it in here.

## Test plan

New `tests/test_expected_warnings_metric_echoes.py`: one pair of cases per site — a declared run under `warnings.simplefilter("error", UserWarning)` asserting no echo, the code still on `MetricResult.warning_codes`, and the `Warning` record marked `expected=True`; plus an undeclared run asserting the echo still fires via `pytest.warns`. Panels that trip a second code (the six-asset thin-bucket panel also trips `few_assets`, the sparse event panel also trips `few_events`) declare that code too so the error filter isolates the echo under test. `high_tie_ratio` additionally gets an attachment case on both `ic` and `ic_ir` and a negative case on a continuous factor.

- `uv run ruff check factrix tests` — pass
- `uv run ruff format --check factrix tests` — pass
- `uv run mypy factrix` — pass (84 files)
- `uv run pytest tests -q -p no:warnings` — 2842 passed, 3 skipped
- `uv run pytest --doctest-modules factrix -q -p no:warnings` — 96 passed, 1 skipped
- `uv run mkdocs build --strict -q` — pass; `docs/reference/_generated_warning_codes.md` regenerated (37 rows) and the `factrix/llms-full.txt` code table updated

No CHANGELOG entry (pre-1.0 policy).

Closes #854

author: frenzzy
body:
Follow-up to #3076, and the userland half of the addressing question from [#3072](https://github.com/solidjs/solid/discussions/3072).

`configureServerFunctionsClient({ fetch })` replaces the function the transport sends every server-function request with.

### Why a seam rather than an option

An app that wants a url shaped for its cache — an argument in a path segment, a tenant in a prefix — cannot get one from a second built-in address format, because a second format has to be taught to every gate that recognises a call: the runtime, the plugin's dev middleware, the generated `dispatchRequest` gate, the router's action-url interception. solidjs/solid-router#590 and solidjs/solid-vite-plugin#332 are what one address change costs downstream; a configurable one would cost that permanently.

It doesn't have to be a second address. The handler takes a web `Request`, so an app route that rewrites into the canonical address dispatches like any other call:

```js
// GET /api/stories/42/2
export async function GET({ request }) {
  const [, , , story, page] = new URL(request.url).pathname.split("/");
  return handleServerFunctionRequest(
    new Request(new URL(serverFunctionUrl(getStory.id, [story, Number(page)]), request.url), request)
  );
}
```

That already works on `next`. The missing half was the client's: a scripted call had no way to reach that route. This adds it, and nothing downstream learns anything.

### The shape

Always `(address, init)` — the address relative to the document, as the global `fetch` receives it on this path, so an ordinary wrapper drops in and `parseServerFunctionUrl` reads the id back out of it for telemetry. `null` restores the global.

One behaviour change fell out of review: the observed path (`observeServerFunctionCalls`, i.e. devtools) used to hand the global `fetch` a `Request` rather than `(base, init)`. Leaving that difference in place would mean a wrapper written against the documented shape — normalising the address, rewriting the path — works in production and silently misroutes the moment anyone attaches an observer, resolving the call to `undefined` rather than erroring. The seam now gets one shape on both paths; observers still see the request the transport dispatched.

The option's doc states what a wrapper owes the transport: forward `init.signal` (a live source's `break` aborts through it), return the `Response` unread (the transport clones it), and keep the call same-origin — a cross-origin send is stamped `Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site`, which the handler's origin gate refuses before it consults a configured `origin`.

### Verification

`pnpm test` at the root: **32/32 turbo tasks green**. Four tests in `server-functions-extensions.spec.tsx`, next to `prepareRequest`'s: an app-shaped url rewritten back into the canonical address end to end, the same shape with and without observers attached, that the init `prepareRequest` produced reaches the seam, and that `null` restores the global. Confirmed by hand that every dispatch path goes through it — plain POST, `GET`-declared reads, the long-url POST fallback, and `live()` including reconnect.

### Known sharp edge, not introduced here

A response the runtime did not produce resolves the call to `undefined` rather than throwing: the transport treats only its own error header or a 5xx as failure (`client.ts`). A mis-mounted app route, an auth interstitial or a CDN block therefore arrive as a successful `undefined`. This predates the seam, but the seam makes foreign responses reachable, so it is worth its own issue — happy to file it.

### Also here

The `endpoint` documentation on both entries, which #3076 left saying the same thing twice with prose after `@default`.

author: baekdahl
body:
## Motivation

VectorArchivingStalled fired for prime-allocation-indexer on unichain on
2026-08-27 and self-resolved a minute later; archiving never stalled. On a fresh
pod `archive_writes_total` is exported one scrape after `multicall_batch_size_count`
with its first sample already >0, so `increase()` never sees those writes — and on
a source archiving ~1 batch/10m the next increment falls outside the 10m window,
leaving the archive leg at 0 while the multicall guard reads >0. It false-fired on
every deploy rollout for the four low-rate sources and never once for the
high-volume ones sharing the same S3 adapter.

## Changes

- Widen the three `VectorArchivingStalled` windows from 10m to 30m
- Add the missing runbook sections and `runbook_url` for all three
  `VectorArchiving*` rules

## Verified

Replayed the new expression against staging Mimir: empty across both known
incidents (unichain 08-27 07:36, optimism 08-26 12:06) and across 7 days, while a
positive control (`status="error"`, which has no series) still matches all 13
archiving sources — so the rule is not silently broken.

author: hikarucode1
body:
Closes #247

## 何が問題だったか

教室長が「代講を記録する」（#215）で入れた行は、**どのクエリにも入らなかった**。

| クエリ | 起点 | 記録行が入るか |
|---|---|---|
| `getTutorSwapRequests` | `requester_id` | ✗ requester は休む講師 |
| `getTutorApplications` (#245) | `swap_applications` | ✗ 募集も応募も経由しないので子行がゼロ |

**「代講者として自分が入った記録」を引くクエリがアプリに 1 本も無かった。** #245 で「通知はするが着地先が無い」を潰したばかりなのに、記録経路には同じ穴が残っていた。

しかも `recordSubstitution` の通知は href が `/tutor` で、**`/tutor` は今週・来週の週次シフトしか出さない**。#215 は「過去こそ本命」なので、主用途である過去日の記録はどこにも着地しない。

## 直し方

`getTutorApplications` を **`swap_requests` 起点に組み替えた**。自分の応募を left join し、

```
status != 'pending' AND (自分の応募がある OR approved_applicant_id = 自分)
```

で拾う。**別の一覧に分けなかった**のは、分けると「応募して選ばれた」行が `swap_applications` と `approved_applicant_id` の両方に該当して**重複する**から。応募か記録かは outcome の違いであって、一覧を分ける理由にならない。

## `recorded` を outcome に足した

応募していないのに代講者なら教室長の記録。**「あなたに決まりました」と出すと、申し込んだ覚えのないものを申し込んだことになる。**

記録された代講が後から取り消された場合は `cancelled-after-approval` に落ちる（`approved_applicant_id` が残るため）。テストで固定した。

## 細かい判断

**取り下げ済みの応募でも、代講者として記録されていれば出す。** 実際に入ったコマなので、応募を取り下げたかどうかとは無関係。

**置き場所は `/tutor/open-swaps` のまま。** 応募者向け通知 4 本が既にそこを指しており（#246 で 1 本を `/tutor` から移したばかり）、href を散らすほうが害が大きい。セクション名は「応募した募集の結果」→「**代講の記録**」に変更。

## 検証

DEV_STUB_AUTH ハーネス + Playwright（撤去済み、`grep DEV_STUB_AUTH src/` は 0 件）。6 種の結果を全部並べて:

| 確認項目 | 結果 |
|---|---|
| 6 種のラベルが正しく出る（記録 / 決まった / 落選 / 承認後の取り消し / 却下 / 取り下げ） | ✅ |
| 見出しが「代講の記録」 | ✅ |
| 日付が短縮形（`8/20`、同ページの募集一覧と同じ） | ✅ |
| 理由は `note` のある行だけ | ✅ |
| JS エラー | ✅ なし |

**DB 側は未検証**（`swap_requests` 起点への組み替え、left join の `withdrawnAt IS NULL` が join 条件に入っていること、`or` の絞り込み、記録行が実際に出ること）。preview 環境での確認が要る。

tsc / lint / vitest(250) / check:rls(20) green。**migration なし。**

---

## レビュー反映 (2026-08-27)

**マージ前 2 件。どちらも「この PR が潰しに来た形」を自分で残していた。**

1. **同じ関数から出るもう 1 本の通知が `/tutor` のままだった** — `recordSubstitution` は休む講師と代講者の 2 人に通知するが、直したのは代講者側だけ。**この PR が書いたコメント**（「`/tutor` は今週・来週しか出さないので過去日の記録は着地しない、#215 は過去こそ本命」）がそっくり当てはまる。記録行は `requester_id` がその講師なので `getTutorSwapRequests` に入り、`/tutor/swaps` に「代講の記録」として出る（`swap-panel.tsx` が `kind === "recorded"` を描画することを確認済み）
2. **この PR の核心が無カバーだった** — `applicationId !== null` を `true` に変異させても **250 テスト全通過**。`applicationOutcome` 自体は変異 4 種で完璧に固めてあるのに、**そこへ渡す引数の組み立てが DB 関数の中にあって触れない**状態だった
   - `rows.flatMap` の中身を `toApplicationRow` として純関数に切り出し、`MyApplication` 型も `application-outcome.ts` へ移した（`swaps.ts` は re-export のみ）
   - テスト 8 本追加。変異 3 種（`applicationId` を見ない / `pending` を通す / `note` のガードを外す）で落ちることを確認
3. （参考）`applied` の JSDoc に **`withdrawApplication` のガードへの依存**を明記。あちらが「承認済みで自分が採用された応募は取り下げ不可」を守っているから `chosen` な講師の応募行が消えない。緩めると選ばれた講師が黙って「教室長が記録」に変わる

### レビューで確認された「問題なし」（重点 1・2・3・5・6）

- **left join の条件配置は意図どおり**（`.toSQL()` で実測）。3 条件がすべて ON 側、WHERE には status と OR のみ。**OR の第 1 枝は旧クエリの WHERE と文字どおり同一述語**なので、新集合は旧集合の厳密な上位集合 = #245 に回帰なし
- **重複行は出ない** — `swap_applications_unique` は部分 UNIQUE ではないので同一 (募集, 自分) は取り下げ状態に関わらず最大 1 行。`applyToSwap` も既存行を UPDATE する作り
- **`or` に取りこぼし・余分なし** — `approved_applicant_id` を書くのは 2 箇所のみで、`decideSwapRequest` は `applicationId` 必須。**named 指名が `recorded` と誤表示されることはない**。`applied=false && chosen=false` は構造的に到達不能
- **「取り下げ済みでも記録なら出す」は成立** — ただし効いている場面は本文と違う（記録経路には応募行が 0 件なので `withdrawnAt IS NULL` は関与しない）
- **テストは自己参照的でない** — レビュー側でも変異 4 種で確認

### 別 issue

- **#249** — `decideSwapRequest` が行ロックを取らないため、承認と応募取り下げが交差すると**選ばれた講師に「教室長が記録」と出る**。既存レースだが #247 で初めて症状が出るようになった（頻度は極小）
- **#250** — 交代成立で欠勤が自動失効しても**本人に通知されない**。教室長には `expiredAbsences` で見せているのに非対称
- **#251** — 記録の理由（`reason`）が一覧に出ない / 見出し「代講の記録」が却下・取り下げまで覆う / `href: "/tutor"` が 2 本残っている

vitest 258（+8）。

author: luceinaltis
body:
Reported: the arrows between boxes look wrong — the word gets covered, the
arrow does not come out of anywhere near the box, and nothing lines up.

All three are one bug, and it measures exactly.

## The cause

`wiring.ts` computes every handoff's geometry by arithmetic off
`BOX = { width: 260, gapX: 96, head: 21 }`, on the stated grounds that
arithmetic can be tested and jsdom has no layout to measure. That is sound —
but only while the constant is true.

It was not. `.basic-flow` declared `width: 260px` as **content-box**, plus
`padding: 10px 12px` and a 1px border, so the box rendered at **286px**.
Read off a live board:

| | expected | actual |
|---|---|---|
| box width | 260 | **286** |
| wire tail x | box's right edge | **26px inside it** |
| column gap | 96 | **70** |

Three symptoms, one number:

1. **"화살표가 가까운 곳에서 나오지 않는다"** — the tail started 26px inside
   the sending box, hidden under it, so the line appeared to emerge from the
   middle of a border rather than off its edge.
2. **"글자를 가린다"** — the midpoint is `(x1 + x2) / 2`, so a tail 26px too
   far left dragged the label 13px left, out of the gap and onto the sending
   box.
3. **"정렬이 안 된다"** — the real gap was 70px, not the 96 `gapX` promised,
   so a condition of any length had nowhere to sit.

## The fix

The width is set from `BOX.width` where the box is built, and
`box-sizing: border-box` makes that the width that renders. A constant obliged
to match a stylesheet will drift again; now there is no second place to drift
from.

## Measured, before and after

Same board — `chores ─changed→ review ─approved→ publish` — read out of the
page:

**Before**

```
chores   x 356 - 642   (w 286)
wire     M 616 21 ...        <- 26px inside chores, which ends at 642
'approved'  x 1000 - 1073    <- review's right edge is 1003: on the box
```

**After**

```
chores   x   0 - 260   (w 260)
review   x 356 - 616
wire     M 260 21 C 308 21, 308 21, 356 21    <- edge to edge, exactly
'changed'   x 287 - 330      <- centred in the 260..356 gap, on the line
'approved'  x 640 - 688      <- centred in the 616..712 gap
```

## Tests

`a border is exactly as wide as the arrows think it is` — red before:

```
AssertionError: expected '' to be '260px'
 FAIL  src/skins/basic/index.test.ts > a border is exactly as wide as the arrows think it is
      Tests  1 failed | 13 passed (14)
```

```
$ npm test --workspace web-ui
 Test Files  23 passed (23)
      Tests  202 passed (202)

$ PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 python -m pytest -q -p asyncio
670 passed, 30 skipped in 37.33s
```

`src/poieo/web/static/` rebuilt.

## Self-review

- **The test is weaker than the bug.** It pins the inline width to `BOX.width`,
  which is what drifted; it cannot catch someone removing `box-sizing`, because
  jsdom has no layout and there is no computed width to read. The comment in
  the stylesheet carries that half. Worth knowing before trusting green here.
- **`BOX.height = 132` is a row *pitch*, not a height**, and it is not fixed by
  this: a shut border renders at 91 and an open one at 134. Rows are spaced
  152, so nothing collides today, but a border tall enough to pass 152 would
  overlap the row beneath it. Left alone — it is not what was reported, and it
  needs a decision (measure, or cap the box) rather than a constant.
- **Found while measuring, not fixed here:** two flows in the *same column* —
  which is where `place()` puts a cycle, since a cycle cannot be peeled — have
  their wire and label drawn *behind* the boxes, invisible but for stubs in the
  vertical gap. Two arrows between the same pair also share a midpoint, so
  their labels stack exactly on top of each other. Real, reproducible
  (`publish → chores` alongside `chores → publish`), and its own change: a back
  edge wants a different route, not a different constant.
