author: poppin-mice
body:
## What changed

### VA_center_opt 1.4.0 → 1.5.0 — adaptive catch-trial scheduler
The 1.4.0 scheduler drew N catch slots from a fixed window (trials 2–13). A subject who passes everything finishes in 9 trials, so a third of that window was dead and catch trials landed as a block **after** the staircase — seen in the first field session (A01, 2026-08-25: both catch trials were trials 10 and 11).

New `CatchScheduler` (`ntuh/vavf/stimuli.py`), decided trial by trial:
- trials 1–2 always normal; a **failed** normal trial is always followed by a normal one;
- otherwise `P(catch) = k/(k+m−1)` — k = catch trials still needed, m = passes still needed to finish the staircase (a uniform shuffle of the remaining catches among the slots before the final normal trial);
- the setting now means **N negative samples wanted**: real FAILs count toward it, and only what is still owed is forced in when the staircase ends early (a low-VA subject gets few or no catch trials instead of a block at the end).

Chosen by Monte-Carlo simulation over the real `Staircase` (20k sessions per cell; perfect / 14 cpd / 8 cpd / low-VA subjects; N = 3 and 6) against the fixed window and two fixed-75% variants. Good-vision subject, N = 6:

| scheduler | trailing catches/session | catches in 1st/2nd/3rd third | next-trial guessable? |
|---|---|---|---|
| fixed window (1.4.0) | 0.00 | .33/.42/.25 | no (58% = base) |
| strict "no consecutive", 75% | 0.87 | .26/.34/.40 | **yes** (85% vs 58%) |
| symmetric 75%/75% | 0.40 | .28/.41/.31 | partly (70% vs 56%) |
| **this PR** `k/(k+m−1)` | **0.00** | .25/.42/.33 | **no** (54% = base) |

author: ruhex
body:
Closes #307

## Problem

`RouteAssembler.BuildOutboundRoutesAsync` takes the per-peer decision tree only when all three of `IPeerStore`, `IPrefixService` and `AppConfig` are present — each an optional constructor parameter defaulting to `null` (`RouteAssembler.cs:35-39`, reached via `BgpSession.cs:246-248`, `BgpServer.cs:52-53`) — and otherwise advertises the shared `RouteTable` verbatim.

That table is not a per-peer route set. Alongside the startup seed from `RouteSeedingService`, it holds **every NLRI any peer announced inbound**, because `BgpSession.HandleUpdateAsync` installs accepted routes straight into it.

So one missing DI registration silently changes what every session receives, from *"the prefixes this user selected"* to *"one global list including what other users' sessions injected"*. No exception, no distinguishing log line, sessions establish normally.

BGPLite is deployed as a service where each user picks their own prefix set in the management UI and the session exists to hand that user their selection. Under that model this is a **tenant-isolation failure**, not a disabled feature: a peer can place a prefix into another peer's advertisement simply by announcing it inbound.

The branch is unreachable in the current `Program.cs`, which registers all three. Nothing in the type system keeps it that way — that is #263's subject; what this PR addresses is the blast radius when it does happen.

## Fix

**1. `RouteTable.EnumerateUnowned()`** yields only entries installed with no owner — in practice the startup seed. The owner tag added in #289 already separates those from peer-installed routes, so the fallback stops being a cross-tenant path *outright*, rather than depending on the composition being correct:

```csharp
foreach (var r in _routeTable.EnumerateUnowned())   // was: Enumerate()
```

This is the advertise-side counterpart of `RemoveOwnedBy`. The tag now carries one coherent meaning in both directions: a peer can neither delete what it does not own, nor have what it injected handed to somebody else.

**2. Taking the fallback logs a Warning** naming which dependency is missing. Until now the only symptom was "the peer got the wrong prefixes", which is indistinguishable from a configuration mistake on the user's side.

## Deliberately not a throw

Several existing tests construct `BgpSession` without a peer store and legitimately exercise this path (`BgpSessionShutdownTests`, `MalformedUpdateResilienceTests`, `SendTimeoutTests`, `BgpSessionHoldTimerTests`, and the ownership tests here). Turning the fallback into a failure would need those to be given a null-object to inject first — that is #263's fix (1), and it belongs there. This PR closes the isolation hole independently of whether that lands, which seemed the right order given the two have very different sizes.

## Verification

`dotnet build BGPLite.sln` + `dotnet test BGPLite.sln`: **684 passed, 0 failed** (683 before, 1 added). `dotnet format --severity warn` clean. No existing test changed behaviour — the two that seed the table already use the owner-less `AddOrUpdate(route)` overload, which is exactly what the fallback still serves.

Confirmed to catch the regression — reverting `EnumerateUnowned()` to `Enumerate()`:

```
Failed SharedTableFallback_DoesNotAdvertiseRoutesInjectedByAnotherPeer
  Assert.DoesNotContain() Failure: Item found in collection
```

## Test added

`SharedTableFallback_DoesNotAdvertiseRoutesInjectedByAnotherPeer` — seeds `192.0.2.0/24`, has one peer announce `10.0.0.0/8` inbound (asserting it *is* in the shared table, so the test cannot pass by the injection having failed), then connects a second peer and reads the NLRI it actually put on the wire. The seed must be there; the other peer's injection must not.

`ScriptedConnection` now captures outbound frames so that last assertion is against real wire bytes rather than internal state.

## Note

Nothing bounds what a peer may *add* to that table — see #304. This PR stops those additions leaking into other peers' advertisements; it does not stop them accumulating.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Corrected fallback route announcements so peers receive only configured startup routes.
  * Prevented routes learned from other peer sessions from being advertised during an initial dump.
  * Added a warning when peer-specific configuration is unavailable and configured prefixes cannot be served.

* **Tests**
  * Added coverage verifying route ownership and outbound route announcements.

author: unidoc-ahall
body:
Fixes https://github.com/unidoc/isms/issues/230.

Documents.vue's read view splits every list item into its own commentable block. Each `<li>` ends up alone in a brand-new `<ol>` with no `start` attribute, so the browser renders every item as "1." regardless of its real position — confirmed against a real customer document (a 14-item list, every item showing "1." in the read view).

Traced it precisely rather than guessing: fed the exact markdown to `marked` directly (same instance `useRenderMd.js` uses) and it correctly parses a single `<ol>` with all 14 `<li>` in order — including across a blank line between two items, which CommonMark keeps as one "loose" list rather than splitting it. The bug is entirely in `contentBlocks`' per-item split that runs on the already-correct HTML, not in markdown parsing.

This also explains why edit and read view disagreed (the second part of the report): the editor (tiptap) renders the whole list as one WYSIWYG list and never splits it, so only the read view was affected.

**Fix:** each split `<li>` now carries `start="N"` on its wrapper `<ol>`, computed from the original list's own `start` (default 1, but respects a source list that legitimately starts elsewhere) plus the item's position within it.

**Also:** extracted the split logic out of the `.vue` file into `web/src/utils/contentBlocks.js` — it runs against `document.createElement`, so it had no real test coverage before (would have needed transplanting into a test file by hand, the way `router.test.js` documents having to do for router.js). New `web/test/contentBlocks.test.js` covers: numbering across a blank-line-separated loose list, a list with a non-1 `start`, unordered lists staying unaffected, and the other block types (tables, headings/paragraphs) unaffected by the change.

**Verified:** mutation-checked — reverted just the `start`-threading and confirmed exactly the 3 numbering-related tests fail, nothing else. `just build-web` clean, full `npm test` 83/83 (76 existing + 7 new).

author: arealmaas
body:
## What broke

The publish for `0a513e2` ([run 33060603631](https://github.com/Altinn/altinn-dashboards-grafana/actions/runs/33060603631)) failed:

```
► logging in to registry with provider credentials
✗ pushing artifact failed: POST https://altinncr.azurecr.io/v2/monitoring/grafana/blobs/uploads/:
  UNAUTHORIZED: authentication required
```

…on the line immediately after `az login` reported **"Subscription is set successfully"**.

## Why

`flux --provider=azure` does not use the session `az login` establishes. It resolves an ACR
credential through the Azure SDK's `DefaultAzureCredential` **by discovery** and authenticates as
whatever that chain lands on — so the push can fail as the wrong identity while `az login` looks
perfectly healthy.

Upstream fixed this in [`setup-flux-acr@b0c9762`](https://github.com/Altinn/altinn-platform/pull/3912)
(2026-08-20) by exporting the same federated credentials `azure/login` uses
(`AZURE_CLIENT_ID` / `AZURE_TENANT_ID` / `AZURE_FEDERATED_TOKEN_FILE`), so
`WorkloadIdentityCredential` resolves first, and repinned `build-push-image` onto it in
[`523f141d`](https://github.com/Altinn/altinn-platform/pull/3935) (2026-08-26).

Our pin `fb059cc6` predates both — the run log shows it still pulling in
`setup-flux-acr@0be6bf2f` from **2026-01-21**. Timeline matches: last green publish 2026-08-05,
first red 2026-08-27.

## Why this pin

`523f141d` is exactly what `Altinn/dialogporten-manifests` moved to after hitting the identical
failure on 2026-08-25 ([their #74](https://github.com/Altinn/dialogporten-manifests/pull/74)).
Its publishes have been green since, most recently today.

## Changes

- `build-push-image` pin `fb059cc6` → `523f141d`, with a comment recording the pin floor so it
  doesn't get rolled back.
- `actions/checkout` `v4` → `v5` (6 usages), clearing the *"Node 20 is deprecated"* warning.

## Verification

- New pin resolves and references `setup-flux-acr@b0c9762`.
- Input surface unchanged — `image_name` / `workdir` / `tag` / `azure_*` all still accepted.
- The new step hard-fails without `id-token: write`; this workflow already grants it.
- No workflow here uses `pull_request_target`, so checkout v5's `allow-unsafe-pr-checkout`
  breaking change does not apply. All four workflow files parse.

The real proof is the publish run on merge to `main` — this workflow only fires on push to
`main`/`release`, so it can't be exercised from the PR.

## Worth a follow-up

**Renovate isn't running on this repo.** `renovate.json` exists, but the onboarding PR (#3) was
closed in 2023 and no Renovate PR has ever landed. Every digest here is hand-maintained, so pins
will go stale again the same way.

author: dannbleeker
body:
## The blocker

`src/pane/taskpane.html` never referenced Office.js. A task pane is an ordinary web page and the host injects nothing into it, so `Office` was undefined, `main.ts` threw `ReferenceError` on its first statement, and the pane rendered its header and stopped — **on every host, with no message anywhere.**

Verified in a browser against the built output, before and after:

```
pageerror: Office is not defined
PANE innerHTML length: 0
```

This has been true of every build the site has served.

## Why nothing here could see it

`test/pane-render.test.ts` calls `render` in jsdom. `scripts/pane-shots.mjs` imports `render.ts` directly in a real browser and photographs the result. Both are useful; neither loads `main.ts`. So the pane's actual entry point had never run anywhere, and fourteen screenshots looked perfect.

The lesson generalises past this bug: **a harness that mounts a component bypasses the document that mounts it in production, so the document needs a guard of its own.** `test/pane-boot.test.ts` is that guard — the CDN path, the ordering against the deferred module, and that the tag is not marked `async`, which would turn the ordering into a race that works on the machine you test it on.

## What the pane says when Office.js does not arrive

A blocked CDN, an offline laptop or a corporate proxy rule all ended as the same blank pane — nothing to report and nothing to search for. It now names the address that failed and says it is usually a network rule rather than a fault in the add-in.

Conditioned on both `Office` being undefined **and** `#pane` being empty, never on the timer alone, so it cannot paint over a pane `main.ts` already drew. This environment's egress proxy refuses that CDN, so the fallback was checked against a real failure rather than a mocked one.

## Two pieces of stale documentation, both on the install path

- **The manifests said the floor is PowerPointApi 1.3.** The code corrected that to 1.2 — the 1.3 was justified by `slide.tags`, which nothing here calls — and the file a user installs kept the old number. The comment is generated from a `FLOOR` constant now, and a test holds it against `API_FLOOR`.
- **The manual's status block said "the task pane is not written yet"**, and marked three shipped sections as planned. The existing guard asserts the word "planned" *appears*, which is satisfied by a manual describing shipped work as unbuilt. Claiming less than you have is not the harmless direction: it tells a reader not to look for the thing that is there.

The manual also told people to download the manifest from the latest release. **There are no releases**, so that link is a 404 today; it points at the file on `main` first now, with the release as the versioned route once one is cut.

## Verification

Every guard proven by a faithful revert, red on its own assertion — including the `async` mutation and both directions of the manual guard. Gate run by name checking exit codes: build 0, eslint 0, prettier 0, tsc 0, coverage 0. Test floor 532 → 540.

author: meszmate
body:
Closes #209.

The prepare sweep added in #208 asks Postgres to `PREPARE` every parameterised statement in `internal/repository`. #208 fixed the parameter-type failures. These are the rest, and they are a different class: queries naming schema that no longer exists. Each failed 100% of the time.

## Per query, renamed or dead

The issue asks to decide per query whether the column was renamed and the query missed it, or the feature is dead and the query should go.

| Query | Verdict | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GetUserPreview` email accounts (`pg_admin.go:404`) | rename miss | `WHERE user_id = $1`. The column is `uuid`, not text. |
| `StopCampaign` (`:1575`) | schema drift | `campaign_status` has never had `stopped` and `campaigns` has never had `stopped_at`. A stop now parks the campaign at `paused`, the same state the owner-facing stop uses, and stamps `last_status_change_at`. |
| `CreatePlan` / `GetPlan` / `UpdatePlan` (`:2081`, `:2101`, `:2129`) | rename miss | `plans.duration_id` is an FK to `durations`. Resolved through a new `DurationIDByTitle`, so an unknown period answers 400 instead of a NOT NULL violation. `pg_plan.go` and `SearchPlansForAdmin` already did this correctly; these three missed it. |
| `GetUserRateLimits` / `UpdateUserRateLimits` (`:2414`, `:2437`) | dead column, and the feature behind it never existed | `user_rate_limits` governs API and realtime throughput. Outbound mail volume is a per-mailbox budget (`email_accounts.campaign_limit`) plus the plan's `daily_emails`, neither of which lives in this table. Replaced `daily_email_limit` with the seven real limit columns and removed the phantom "Daily emails" field from the operator dialog, rather than adding a column so a control that does nothing could keep existing. |

The plan CRUD stays rather than being deleted: `897da46e` dropped its routes along with roughly fifty other admin handlers (cloud provisioning, discount codes, enterprise inquiries), so removing only this one would be inconsistent with every sibling.

## One more of the same class, which the sweep cannot see

`GetUserEmails` had the identical `user_id = $1::text` comparison. The sweep misses it because that `WHERE` clause is concatenated at runtime, so the extractor only sees a fragment with no placeholders in it. Unlike the preview, this one does not swallow the error: `GET /admin/users/:id/emails` was a 500 on every call.

## What the fixes forced

- `AdminWorkerEmail.LastSyncedAt` is now `*time.Time`. It was `time.Time` against a nullable column, so a mailbox that had never synced failed to scan and was silently dropped from every admin mailbox list.
- The rate-limit write is insert-then-patch inside a transaction. Every column is NOT NULL with a default, so the old `INSERT ... VALUES ($2..$6)` would have violated those constraints the first time an operator overrode a single limit. It also records `updated_by`, which this path never set, and returns the updated row so the `PATCH` matches the type the client already declared.
- `AdminStopCampaign` reads the reason the dialog has always sent and the handler has always dropped, writes it to the audit log and to the owner's campaign activity feed, and refuses a draft or completed campaign with a 400 instead of silently succeeding.
- `GetUserPreview` propagates query errors instead of swallowing them. That swallow is the reason the mailbox bug survived this long.

## Regression guard

`TestLiveEveryQueryPrepares` now fails on `42703`, `42P01`, `42883`, `42704` and `22P02`, not only on `42P08`. Syntax errors stay tolerated because those are the runtime-assembled fragments. Reintroducing `status = 'stopped'` makes it fail with the original error.

`internal/repository/admin_schema_live_test.go` covers all six paths behaviorally: the preview and the paginated mailbox list return the mailbox that was connected and handle a null `last_synced_at`, a force-stop leaves the campaign paused with `last_status_change_at` set, a plan round-trips `month` then `year` through `duration_id`, and two successive partial rate-limit patches each land without resetting the other or zeroing the columns they do not mention.

## Verification

Against a scratch database migrated from this branch alone, which also confirmed the shared dev database has drifted (it carries a `paused_suspended` enum value that exists in no migration):

- every live test in `internal/repository` passes, prepare sweep clean
- backend booted against it: all 49 admin `GET` routes return 200, including `/admin/users/:id/emails`
- `PATCH /admin/users/:id/rate-limits` round-trips a partial patch and leaves the untouched columns alone; a user with no override row reads back the defaults the enforcement path applies
- `POST /admin/campaigns/:id/stop` answers 400 with no reason, 400 on a draft, and 200 on the active campaign, leaving `status = paused` with the reason in both `campaign_logs` and `admin_audit_logs`

`make lint`, `gofmt -l`, and `pnpm typecheck` / `pnpm lint` in `admin/` are all clean. No migrations, no `orgtransfer` tables, and no docs changes: every surface here is operator-only and not covered by `docs/`.

## Left alone, both pre-existing and outside this issue

- `admin/src` still calls `GET /admin/plans` to fill the plan filter on the Users and Organizations pages. That route went away in `897da46e`, so the dropdown is empty. Restoring it or dropping the filter is a product call.
- `internal/app/warmup/health_evaluation_live_test.go:151` segfaults rather than failing cleanly when the target database has no `warmup_pools` rows. It passes against the dev database.

### What this PR does

Before this PR:

The provider-registry sync workflow passed each Base64-encoded catalog through a single command-line argument. `models.json` and `provider-models.json` exceeded Linux's per-argument limit, so both `jq` processes failed inside a pipeline while the workflow still published a manifest-only commit and reported success.

After this PR:

The workflow builds its GraphQL request in a file through a tested Node helper, preserving every staged catalog file without using large argv values. Changes to the workflow or helper also trigger a sync, so merging this PR republishes a complete snapshot.

<!-- (optional, in `fixes #<issue number>(, fixes #<issue_number>, ...)` format, will close the issue(s) when PR gets merged)*: -->

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

The following tradeoffs were made:

The helper reads the staged catalog files into memory while constructing the request. The current request is about 2 MB, which is small enough for the workflow and avoids shell argument limits.

The following alternatives were considered:

Publishing each file in a separate commit was rejected because the catalog contract requires the manifest to bind one atomic snapshot. A normal Git push was rejected because the branch requires GitHub-verified signatures; `createCommitOnBranch` preserves the existing signed publication path.

None.

The failed sync left the remote manifest newer than the two large JSON files. Merging this PR triggers the repaired workflow and republishes them together. The regression test uses a 200 KB catalog fixture, above Linux's single-argument limit, and verifies lossless Base64 round-tripping.

author: batuhanzorbeyzengin
body:
Three things this branch fixes, in the order they would have bitten.

## The release would have shipped an unchanged changelog

`semantic-release` was called with `--no-changelog` and a comment saying
towncrier owns `CHANGELOG.md` — which is the right design, and the reason two
writers on one file is the wrong one. Nothing then called towncrier. Not
`release.yml`, not `docs/development/release.md`; the `justfile` had only
`--draft`, which previews without writing. Cutting `0.1.0` as things stood would
have published an unchanged changelog and left 108 news fragments in
`changelog.d/`.

The assembly is now the release commit, so the tag lands on a tree that contains
the changelog rather than one commit behind it. `verify` refuses to release when
`changelog.d/` is empty, because an empty directory means either nothing
user-visible changed or somebody forgot the fragment, and the second is the one
worth catching.

## The release would probably have gone red on noise

`verify` ran `-m "not gpu and not slow and not network"` — no `not perf`. So a
release ran exactly the wall-clock assertions `ci.yml` removed as unmeasurable
on a shared runner, `test_batching_amortises_the_per_call_cost` included, which
had already failed twice by 1% and 2.6%. A release blocked by a 2.6% timing
wobble is a release blocked by nothing. Those numbers are gated on the host
before a release instead, as `docs/development/testing.md` already says.

## The memory ceilings gated nothing, and three documents said they did

`benchmarks/README.md` claimed `test_memory_ceiling.py` runs on "every PR" with
an "absolute — exceeding blocks" gate, and closed with "Only the absolute-memory
ceilings are gates". Every test in it and in `test_hot_path.py` carried `perf`;
CI runs `-m "not network and not perf"`. The one guard against the `O(N x d)`
class of bug — a `list(iter_records())` that fails only on corpora nobody has in
development — ran on no pull request at all. `test_macro_budgets.py` pointed at
an instruction-count benchmark as the real gate; there is none, the CodSpeed job
that would have been it collected nothing and was removed.

The marker now follows what a test asserts on. `perf` asserts wall clock and
stays on the measurement host; the new `memory` marker asserts peak allocation,
which `tracemalloc` measures identically on a loaded runner and a quiet one, so
CI gates on it. Ten tests moved. A test must not carry both, since `perf` is
what keeps it off the merge path — and `benchmarks/README.md` no longer tells
contributors to mark every new benchmark `perf`, which is the instruction that
would have re-opened this quietly.

## New: rehearsing a release

`Release` takes a `mode` — `dry-run`, `rehearse`, `release` — instead of a
`dry_run` boolean. `rehearse` assembles, commits, tags and builds on the
runner's throwaway checkout and uploads to TestPyPI: everything the real run
does except the two irreversible parts. It is not granted `contents: write`,
which makes "nothing is pushed" a property rather than a promise. What it proves
is what a dry run cannot — that towncrier assembles, that `hatch-vcs` reads the
tag, and that Trusted Publishing works end to end here.

It commits before tagging rather than building the tree as it stands, because
`hatch-vcs` appends a local version segment to a build from uncommitted changes
and PyPI rejects local version identifiers. Both publishing jobs check the built
filenames for that segment and name it, rather than letting it surface as a
rejected upload.

The version and tag come from `--print` and `--print-tag`, which exit before
changing anything, and `git` places the tag. The commits still choose the version
and `tag_format` still decides the tag's shape; what is gone is a dependency on
how the release tool behaves when there is no version file to rewrite, which
this project does not have.

## What this PR is itself testing

**The `memory` layer has never run on a GitHub runner.** Its budgets were
measured on the project's own host. `tracemalloc` is machine-independent so the
assertions should hold, but the runtime is unknown — the scaling invariant builds
corpora at 60,000, 150,000 and 400,000 records. If the `tests and coverage
floors` job goes red or slow here, that is this branch reporting on itself, and
the budgets get adjusted before any of it reaches `main`.

## Checked locally

`ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean over 224 files. `pyproject.toml`
and both workflows parse. `mkdocs build --strict` succeeds. `towncrier build
--draft` assembles 391 lines. `uv.lock` unchanged. Marker selection verified by
collection: `-m memory` is 10 tests, `-m perf` is 12, and CI's expression now
collects 1302 of 1314 where it previously excluded all 22.

The suite was not run locally — it runs on the GPU host.

author: hubbersbi
body:
Makes the app publishable as a static site, and fixes the bar-height bug found while checking it.

## What changed

**No backend when published.** The read endpoints answer the same thing between two fetches, so `app/export_static.py` writes them out as flat JSON at build time and the frontend reads those files when `NEXT_PUBLIC_WACHTTIJD_STATIC` is set. Unset, everything is the live API exactly as before — Docker is untouched.

The exporter calls the same `queries` and the same `main._answer` the API does. `test_export_static.py` asserts file-for-response equality across all 113 treatments, because a figure assembled twice will eventually be assembled two different ways.

**The assistant now runs in the browser.** This is what closes the Groq gap rather than managing it: a backend on the public internet meant either a model key in a serverless function — strangers' health questions going to a vendor with no processor agreement — or no assistant. `parse_with_rules` is ported to `lib/assistant.ts`, so the question never leaves the page.

**It says what it is before it is used.** A focus-trapping notice on first visit, a marker in the header after that, both linking to ZorgkaartNederland. The site is `noindex`: a visitor arriving from a search result rather than a portfolio would take it for a service.

**Deploy** runs on push and twice a month, matching the source's cadence.

## Verified

- Static export served by a plain file server, no FastAPI: 117 locations, 0–240 dagen, 53 over the norm — identical to Docker.
- Same question on both paths returns the same treatment key and the same "7 van de 9". Static build's network log shows **only GETs for JSON** — no request carries the question.
- Both parsers agree on all 20 questions checked against the real 113-treatment catalogue.
- `basePath` build served from a subdirectory: assets and JSON both resolve.
- 52 backend + 80 frontend tests pass, ruff clean, Docker rebuilt and unaffected.

## Costs, recorded in PLAN.md

- Figures are as old as the last workflow run. `fetched_at` stays on the page, which is what makes that honest.
- Snapshot history depends on the CI cache surviving. No screen shows history in v1.
- The published assistant is rules-only, and says so on screen.

author: satriabw
body:
Fourth of five, on top of #36. A fifth distribution, `workers/evidence-worker`, and the thing the queue in the previous PR was built for. Nothing enqueues to it yet — that is PR5 — so this lands with the worker complete and idle.

### One dependency

`shared`, for boto3, the job model, the queue and the database connection. That is the argument for this not being a module inside detection-worker: that package pulls onnxruntime, supervision and three local distributions, and its image adds a CUDA 12.2 runtime, a deadsnakes interpreter, an onnxruntime-gpu pinned to the workstation's driver and a cuDNN from pip whose directory has to be on `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`. None of it seeks a video.

This image is the same `python:3.11-slim` the API runs on plus ffmpeg, it builds on any machine, and `--scale evidence-worker=3` works because nothing here touches the GPU.

Separate service ≠ separate host: it is the third process on the one SQLite file and the second that writes. The filesystem is still the constraint, same as detection-worker.

### The clip is the span the record covers

`window()` takes `evidence_seconds` off the job — the site's own number, the one the detector sized its ring buffer with — and **nothing in config sizes a clip**. The blob holds boxes for exactly those frames, so a clip of any other length is either missing footage the record describes or showing footage it does not, and a reviewer drawing those boxes over it would watch them start late or run out early. A setting here would be a second source of truth for one number, free to drift from the one that produced the evidence.

It ends *on* the violation, like the buffer and for the buffer's own reason: the approach is what a reviewer needs, and the aftermath is still in the source. The `+ 1/fps` is `FrameBuffer.over`'s `+ 1` in seconds — the frame a rule fires on is part of its window, so the clip reaches the far side of that frame rather than stopping at its leading edge.

### Two subprocess calls, no pixels in Python

`-ss` before `-i`, so ffmpeg seeks the container rather than decoding everything up to the moment asked for. `-c copy` for the clip, so frames are remuxed rather than re-encoded — a clip costs roughly its own bytes off the network and nothing on the CPU.

The price is that a stream copy can only start on a keyframe, so a clip begins at or before the requested second by up to one GOP. That is more lead-up, never less, and a test pins the direction: it can never cut off the violation itself.

**Nothing is drawn on either object**, and that is what keeps the property the read-time design was protecting. The blob already holds every box and frame index, so the detail view draws them over the clip — fix the drawing and every violation ever recorded improves, while the expensive half is baked once.

### Failure handling

**The exit code is not enough to trust.** Asked to seek past the end, ffmpeg exits 0 and writes a zero-byte file, so `_run` checks the output exists and is non-empty. Without it, a violation whose frame index does not match its footage would upload an empty object and record it as ready evidence.

**A failed cut marks the violation and the worker carries on**, which diverges from detection-worker's raise-and-stop contract deliberately: the failure has somewhere to go now. What still stops the worker is everything that is *not* about one violation — no database, no credentials, a bucket that refuses a write — so uploads sit outside the `except`. A test pins that an AccessDenied does not quietly mark the row failed and go on to do the same to every job behind it.

**A source with no probed frame rate is failed rather than cut at an assumed 25 or 30.** A guessed rate seeks to the wrong second of a real video, which is evidence of something that did not happen.

### Worth review

`shared.s3.client` grows `upload()`, against a docstring that said there deliberately was none. That rule is about a *request path* — a client's bytes never pass through a service, which is why presigned PUTs exist and why there is still no `download()`. A worker that produced an artifact is the origin of those bytes, not a relay for somebody else's, and has nowhere to put them but storage. The docstring now says which of the two lines it is drawing.

### Testing

The cut tests run real ffmpeg against a generated video and probe the result with the same reader site-service uses, skipping rather than failing where ffmpeg is absent. The window arithmetic is tested on its own: a violation in the first seconds of a video clamps to zero and comes out short rather than wrong, which is the same truncation the record itself carries.

Not built here: the Docker image. `docker compose config` parses; the image's own import check will be the first real test of it.

Suite: **846 passed, 1 skipped**.

author: inprimex
body:
## Why
bridge 1.2's `/api/auth/refresh` receives only `{refresh_token}` — after a browser reload the session JWT is gone (memory-only per F128). To return a rotated session it must mint a **fresh session JWT without a password**. `login()` is the only minter and `_secret` + the claim shape are private (correctly) — so bridge duplicating `jwt.encode` would create the second implementation the extract-to-core decision exists to prevent. bridge requested this exact seam (msg 20260827T123622); it's the last gate before their PR.

## What
- **`CeAuthManager.issue_session_token(username) -> session_jwt`** — password-free counterpart to `login()`. Role is **re-looked-up from config** (stays authoritative; a removed/disabled user raises `AuthError`, so the caller 401s and falls back to the password prompt — the spec's revoked-token scenario). Payload byte-for-byte identical to `login()`.
- Refactor: `login()` and `issue_session_token()` both mint via a shared private `_issue_session_for(user)` — the password and password-free paths **cannot diverge**.

## Tests
`tests/test_web_auth.py` +6 (`TestIssueSessionToken`): valid mint, payload-matches-login, unknown-user raises, disabled raises, role re-authoritative, and the end-to-end mint→attach refresh flow. Full suite **883 passed**, mypy + ruff clean.

Isolated + additive; no change to existing behavior.

author: leylabernie
body:
## Confirmed production routing defect

The LuxeMia frontend is a Vite SPA. Vercel evaluates `vercel.json` for redirects and rewrites; the repository-root `middleware.ts` is not the effective production routing layer. Therefore, the middleware-only correction in PR #167 compiled successfully but did not change the public 404 responses.

## Controlled correction

This PR:

- Adds all eight exact permanent redirects to the deployable `vercel.json` redirect array:
  - `/collections/earrings` → `/jewelry`
  - `/collections/evening-gowns` → `/collections`
  - `/collections/frontpage` → `/`
  - `/collections/indo-western` → `/indowestern`
  - `/collections/jacket-sets` → `/suits`
  - `/collections/kurta-pajama-vest` → `/menswear`
  - `/collections/manthrakodi-sarees` → `/sarees`
  - `/collections/saree-gowns` → `/sarees`
- Enforces `statusCode: 301` for every route.
- Deduplicates the route sources before writing them.
- Updates `finalize-empty-collection-redirects.cjs` to validate `vercel.json`, the actual production routing source, rather than the non-operative middleware layer.
- Leaves all unrelated Vercel redirects, rewrites, headers, and SPA fallback behavior unchanged.

The controlled patch workflow and patch script removed themselves after writing and validating the two-file final diff.

No Shopify products, prices, inventory, variants, SKUs, images, publication status, discounts, policies, orders, customers, or unrelated site content were changed.

author: shuaimxu
body:
## 问题

用户 `fangxinhao`（飞书渠道账号 `8b82d094-26f2-4f03-af70-6c4570224916`，自建应用凭据模式）新开的第二个飞书私聊一直无法绑定/激活，每条消息都在日志里报：

```
ChannelRouteRejectedError: Channel binding resolver rejected route for feishu:oc_f0ad14fcd1b354dbfe3f7f30d714327f#account:8b82d094-...
```

Inbox 无限重试同一条消息，永远失败。该账号的第一个私聊（被启动时的 `syncGroupMetadata` 群同步预先注册过）工作正常，掩盖了这个问题；第二个私聊在账号已连接之后才打开，没有预注册，直接触发 bug。

## 根因

`createFeishuConnection()` 里 P2P 新聊天的 bootstrap 预检查直接调用 `resolveEffectiveChatJid(chatJid)`，其声明类型是 `{...} | null`，代码按"返回假值"处理未绑定情况。但当渠道账号是 scoped connection（`scopeIncomingJids: true`，即非旧版默认的自定义凭据账号）时，实际注入的 resolver 是 `im-manager.ts#scopeConnectOpts` 包装过的实例——对未绑定的路由它是**抛出** `ChannelRouteRejectedError`，而不是返回 `null`。这个抛出对下方 `resolveAdmittedChannelRoute`（外层有 catch，转成 Inbox 定时重试）是符合预期的；但在 bootstrap 预检查里不加保护地调用，异常直接跳过 `onNewChat`，导致该聊天永远无法完成注册——Inbox 一直重试同一条消息，一直命中同样的抛出，无限循环。

## 修复

把 bootstrap 预检查里 `resolveEffectiveChatJid` 抛出的 `ChannelRouteRejectedError` 当作未绑定（等同 `null`）处理，让 `onNewChat`/`onP2pSender` 能正常执行，聊天在收到第一条消息时就完成注册，不管底层 resolver 是返回 `null` 还是抛异常。

同步更新了 `tests/feishu-route-safety.test.ts`，覆盖抛出异常的场景。

## 验证

- 已在生产环境编译并通过 PM2 重启（`happyclaw` 进程，pid 变化前后见部署记录）。
- 重启后 fangxinhao 该私聊的下一条消息（`om_x100b663704a3cca8ddc06da4eec1970`）日志显示 `Group registered` → `Auto-registered IM chat` → `Feishu message routed to workspace main conversation`，不再出现 `ChannelRouteRejectedError` 重试。
- `tests/feishu-route-safety.test.ts` 本地跑通（3 passed）。

## 备注

排查过程中发现上游仓库 `riba2534/happyclaw`（本仓库的 upstream，非本 fork 的 main）今天刚合并了同一根因问题的一个更完整的历史修复（`a40285a3`，2026-08-09 提交，额外订阅了 `bot_p2p_chat_entered_v1` 事件做首条 DM 到达前的预注册）。由于两个仓库的 `main` 已经分叉较远（此 fork 领先 3 个 commit，落后 upstream 248 个 commit），后续如果要同步吸收 upstream 的完整方案，需要专门评估合并/移植，不在本 PR 范围内。

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

---

## 追加修复：P2P 账号级 owner 泄漏到同事的私聊（第二个 commit）

### 问题

同一渠道账号下，方昕皓自己新开的私聊也一直"已读不回"，日志显示 `audience_rejected`，不是路由问题（上面那个 bug 已经修复）。

### 根因

`onNewChat` 给全新 P2P 聊天赋值 `owner_im_id` 时，用的是**整个渠道账号共享**的 `ownerOpenId`（第一个曾经 DM 过这个 bot 的人学习得到的值）。这个逻辑对群聊合理（没有更好的信号），但对 P2P 是错的：P2P 天生 1:1，一旦账号已经从"另一个人"的更早 DM 学到了 owner，同一个 bot 下**任何新开私聊的人**都会被强行套上那个别人的 owner_im_id，之后自己在自己的私聊里发消息全部被 `owner_only` + `audience_rejected` 拦截。

### 修复

新增 `correctP2pChatOwner()`：每次收到某个 P2P 聊天的入站消息时，把**这个聊天自己的** `owner_im_id`/`sender_allowlist` 强制纠正为它的真实发送者（幂等、已经正确时是 no-op；对已经 `transfer_reset` 隔离的聊天不生效）。把 `chatJid` 穿透进 `onP2pSender` 回调链（`feishu.ts` → `im-manager.ts`/`im-channel.ts` → `index.ts`），让纠正能定位到具体聊天而不是账号级共享值。

### 验证

- `tests/feishu-allowlist-backfill.test.ts`、`tests/feishu-channel-account-owner.test.ts` 本地跑通（25 passed）。
- `make typecheck`、`npm run docs:check` 干净。
- 已编译并重启生产 `happyclaw` PM2 进程；重启后日志已出现 `Corrected P2P chat owner to its actual DM sender` 的正常纠正/no-op 日志。
- 数据库核对：方昕皓自己的私聊（`oc_2cc0f905081834aac97abe63b3478e19`）`owner_im_id` 现在等于他自己的 open_id，不再是别人的值。

'…' + t.price + '…今だけお試し価格' : ""; ``` 条件がありません。10月の回に `price: "3,000円"` と書くと **「3,000円 今だけお試し価格」** と表示されます。**正規価格にお試しバッジが付く＝嘘の表示**になるので、10月分を入れる前にバッジ側を直す必要があります。 **⚠️ 告知より先にLPの金額を上げてはいけない** **まだ告知していません**（インスタ画像が未制作）。先に金額だけ書き換えると、**説明のないまま値上げが見えてしまいます。** 10月の回（10/11・10/23）は現在 timetable だけ入って `price` が空ですが、これが**未着手に見えて親切に埋められてしまう**のが怖いところです。**意図的に空**だと書き添えました。 ## CLAUDE.md（新規・31行） 毎回読み込まれるので短くしています。AGENTS.mdへの導線と、事故が起きやすい4点だけ。 ``` ① 料金は SCHEDULE-PATTERNS.md が正（告知原稿から写さない） ② このリポジトリはPUBLIC（広告実績・SNSインサイトの数値を書かない） ③ 個人情報をAIに渡さない ④ 1ページのLPではなく7ページのホームページ（日程追加は4か所） ``` ## このPRに入れていないもの **`AGENTS.md`** … `price` の警告を追記済みですが、**別セッションの未コミット作業が同じファイルにあります**（GA4のサブアクション、Canvaのスケジュール差し替え、HANDOFFのPRIVATE移設）。巻き込まないよう、作業ツリーに残してあります。そちらのセッションのコミットに一緒に乗ります。 **メモリ** … リポジトリ外（`~/.claude`）なので反映済みです。`pricing-source-of-truth` を追加し、`lp-pending-decisions`（「金額はまだ聞いていない」が古くなっていた）と `pricing-unification-plan` を更新しました。 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: sgeos
body:
## The milestone

**`wire.kel` self-compiles byte-identically.** 486 chunks, **125,540 bytes on both sides, zero chunks differing.**

The byte-identity corpus goes from **ten stages to eleven**, and the largest stage — the last one outside the oracle — is now in it.

That sentence was once **invented** on this line and reached a doc comment, a pull-request body and all three channels while the compile still panicked. It is now the output of `self_host_compiles_wire_kel_byte_identically`, not a recollection.

## The cause was one line, and it was a symmetry gap

`forin_count` — the bare `for` form's program-order counter — was never added to the per-function reset that already cleared its own documented analogue, `forlimit_count`. The stage's own comment calls it *"the analogue of `forlimit_count`"*; the analogue was reset and it was not.

It indexes an emitted record as `7 * forin_count`, so the **second and every later function** containing a bare `for` emitted a record pointing past its own parts. **That is why the stage emitted FEWER operations rather than different ones** — and that direction was the most useful fact in the whole diagnosis.

## Four causes over three sessions, two first diagnosed wrongly

| recorded cause | verdict |
|---|---|
| a capacity bound, read off the `1024` in an index message | **wrong** |
| the lexer having no hexadecimal or binary literal support | correct |
| a cap of 256 on the declaration count | **wrong** |
| a `Call` record whose chunk field overflowed at index 256 | correct |
| `forin_count` not reset between functions | correct |

Both wrong readings took **a number in a message for a cause**.

## The method, which is the transferable part

1. **Prefix bisection with the right predicate** — *do these chunks match*, **not** *does it compile*, which passes everywhere once the file compiles at all. Choosing it wrongly would have produced a table that looked like data.
2. **The real dependency chain**, not simplified stand-ins. An earlier extract of the same function came back IDENTICAL for exactly that reason; rebuilt verbatim it reproduced at 40 against 59 — the precise stage figures.
3. **Delta-debugging** to the loop alone: 14 against 33, the same 19-operation delta.
4. **A five-line synthetic** separating one bare loop from two in separate functions.

**It then predicted the file before I looked.** The rule says every bare-`for` function after the first diverges; `wire.kel` has three, and the two after the first are exactly the pair that diverged.

**And it nearly failed for the wrong reason** — my detector matched a *comment* reading `for k in 0..3` and reported four functions against an observed two. The instrument was broken, not the finding.

**Tally across all four causes: guessing failed seventeen times; prefix bisection succeeded three out of three.** That is now guidance in the handoff, not just history.

## A stale open item whose evidence did not exist

Separately: the handoff's **correctness item 4** claimed an arithmetic result is still unknown to the type-rejection rules, citing a pin that **no test defines**. Commit `63574d1f` closed that half with a bounded fixpoint.

**Three live comments cited the same dead name**, and the `UNRESOLVED` register excused all three — so nothing failed while four places in the tree asserted something untrue. The comments now name the test holding the edge that genuinely remains, and the register shrank **13 → 12**.

**A citation in a debt register is not a citation that is right. It is one excused from being checked.**

The guard then caught me spelling the dead name *in the comment explaining its retirement* — the third time that has happened here — so the identifier is deliberately not spelled.

## Verification

Green with cargo's own exit status on every segment: **41 + 41 binaries** in two runs, plus `selfhost_codegen` (142), `selfhost_typecheck` (16), `comment_citations` (5), `wire_self_compile_status` (3). Clippy, fmt and the documentation gate clean; the feature sets without `self-host` build.

**No new opcode, no `BYTECODE_VERSION` change.**

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: mkonda
body:
## Summary

Phase 2 of the review system roadmap — the versioned, self-contained JSON artifact that is the seam between the plugin and every consumer (solo dev, CI, Drupal catalog).

Phase 1 (PR #37) delivered the inner core (`.findings.json`). This PR wraps it in the full artifact envelope: `schema_version`, `reviewed{}`, `recommendation{}`, repo-level / per-app nesting with derived criteria, report paths, and `run_meta`.

### Architecture: three files in, one artifact out

The LLM produces judgment; scripts produce structure:

| File | Producer | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `review-<slug>.md` | Orchestrator (LLM) | Human-readable Markdown report |
| `review-<slug>.findings.json` | Aspect skills (LLM) | Structured finding records |
| `review-<slug>.meta.json` | Orchestrator (LLM) | Review context, recommendation, per-app decisions, model |

Pipeline: `compute-ids.py` → `assemble-artifact.py` → `review-<slug>.artifact.json`

### New files
- **`references/assemble-artifact.py`** — merges meta + findings into the artifact envelope. Splits findings by `app_id` (maintenance → repo-level, rest → per-app), derives criteria from finding rules (STR-03 FAIL → `yaml_valid: "fail"`), normalizes decision strings to snake_case.
- **`references/artifact-envelope.md`** — documents the artifact shape, production pipeline, field notes, versioning contract.

### Stable-anchor HTML report
- `md2pdf.sh` now generates an HTML report alongside the PDF
- Pandoc produces deterministic heading `id` attributes from heading text (`## Security` → `id="security"`)
- These are the deep-link targets the artifact's `anchor` fields will reference when indicators land
- Self-contained HTML with table of contents and clean CSS

### Cost tracking
- `run_meta.model` captured from the orchestrator's self-reported model ID
- Token counts and USD are **not available** — the `claude-code-action` deliberately sanitizes usage data from the execution output (`sanitizeModelUsage()` strips everything except context window / max output tokens)
- Cost tracking is external (API provider billing) until the action or SDK exposes per-run usage

### CI pipeline (5 outputs per review)
`.md` → `.pdf` → `.html` → `.findings.json` (with IDs) → `.artifact.json`

### Deferred
- **Per-category indicators** (`level` / `summary` / `anchor`) — requires an indicator-level mapping spike (findings → solid / some_notes / needs_attention). The `indicators` field will be added to `repo_level` and each `apps[]` entry when that design lands.

## Depends on

- **PR #37** (Phase 1) for structured findings. Should merge after #37.

## Test plan

- [ ] Run `assemble-artifact.py` with sample meta + findings — verify artifact shape, criteria derivation, decision normalization
- [ ] Run `md2pdf.sh` on a review markdown — verify `.html` output with correct heading `id` attributes
- [ ] Run CI workflow (dry-run) — verify new steps don't break the pipeline
- [ ] Verify `assemble-artifact.py` handles missing findings gracefully (empty arrays)

author: satriabw
body:
Last of five, on top of #37. The two lines that connect the worker to the pipeline.

### Ordering

The handler queues by the id `save` handed back, **after the write and never before**: a job naming a violation that is not in the database yet is one evidence-worker picks up, fails to find, and marks failed — a row poisoned by the order it was written in rather than by anything about it.

Violations drained at the end of a chunk are queued the same way. The clip comes out of the source rather than out of what the ring held, so one with no window has exactly as much evidence available as one that fired mid-chunk.

The site's `evidence_seconds` goes with the id — the same number the analyzer sized its ring buffer with, one line above. That is what makes the clip cover exactly the frames the record it just wrote holds boxes for.

### `pending` is written before the job is handed over

The order is the whole of the design. Evidence-worker is a different process and may be idle; enqueue first and it can finish the cut and write `ready` before this line runs, at which point `pending` overwrites a violation that already has its evidence. Writing first cannot lose that race — the only thing that can follow it is the worker's own verdict.

### A queue that will not take the job does not stop the detector

This is the one place in the worker that swallows an exception, against a module where everything else raises because losing a job silently is worse than stopping loudly. The difference is that this job is already recorded: the violation is safe on disk, and giving up GPU throughput because a second queue is unreachable trades the expensive half of the pipeline for the cheap one.

The row is marked `failed` instead — true, since nothing is going to produce this evidence, and something a backfill can find. `logger.exception` rather than a message, because a broad `except` that hides its traceback makes a bug in here look exactly like Redis being down.

### Notes

`make_handler` grows a fourth required collaborator rather than a defaulted one, for the reason its docstring already gives about the first two: it needs a Redis connection and the same database handle `save` writes through, and defaulting it would mean quietly opening both.

Also clears out the last comments that still said evidence was re-derived at read time — in `ViolationCreate`, `ViolationResponse`, `to_create` and the README.

### Verified end to end

Real ffmpeg, a real generated video, a real SQLite file, faking only the S3 upload:

```
after enqueue: pending
  uploaded evidence/{id}/thumbnail.jpg   8,498 bytes  image/jpeg
  uploaded evidence/{id}/clip.mp4       43,013 bytes  video/mp4
row: ('ready', 'evidence/{id}/thumbnail.jpg', 'evidence/{id}/clip.mp4')
clip: 5.12s   (5s of lead-up + the firing frame, ending at 20.0s)
```

Suite: **856 passed, 1 skipped** (baseline on `main` is 792).

author: calmacx
body:
> _Disclaimer: AI (Claude) was used to assist with implementing and documenting the changes in this PR._

## Summary


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8f2d20dc-56a6-4ae1-a8df-17278e555fbd



The Demographics panel (Age / Sex / Race / Location rows) used to write straight into `queryBuilderJson.demographics` on every interaction — a checkbox tick, a slider drag, a map pin drop all committed immediately. The "Save Selection and Collapse" button was purely cosmetic: it just collapsed the row, since nothing wired an `onSave` handler up to it.

This PR converts each row to draft-until-save editing via `react-hook-form`, so the demographics JSON block is only written to the store when Save is actually clicked:

- Editing a row now only mutates a local form draft. Reset discards it; Save commits it.
- Only one row can be edited at a time — the other rows' Edit buttons are disabled while a row is open.
- The one exception: the very first time a demographic rule is added (the block is still empty), all rows open at once with a single Save button at the bottom, so a first-time user can set everything in one pass instead of round-tripping through Edit/Save four times.
- "Clear all" (shown on a collapsed row with a value) is unchanged — still an immediate store write, not gated behind Save, since it's a deliberate one-shot action rather than an in-progress edit.

### Decisions worth noting

- **`FormProvider`/`useFormContext<Demographics>()`, not prop-drilled `control`.** Matches the codebase's existing pattern for this shape (`UpdateCollection` owns the form, `CollectionConfig` consumes it via context) rather than threading `control` through every section as a prop.
- **One custom hook (`useDemographicFieldEditing`) instead of a pile of `useState`/helpers in the panel.** It owns the form, which field (if any) is active, and whether every row is forced open; `propsFor(field)` hands back the settled set of coordination props for one row, so `DemographicsPanel.tsx` reads as `<DemographicAgeSection {...propsFor("age")} />` rather than eight named props per row.
- **No resync `useEffect`.** A row's draft only needs to be fresh the moment its edit session starts — `onEditStart` already re-reads the current committed value at that point, and non-active rows never render their form-bound UI, so there's nothing to keep in sync reactively.
- **Per-row Save commits only that field, not the whole form.** The first pass called `form.handleSubmit(values => setDemographics(values))` for every Save, on the assumption that non-active fields' form values always equal their committed values. That assumption breaks for `Controller`s that aren't currently mounted (a row that isn't being edited doesn't render its `Controller`, and `resetField` on an unmounted field doesn't reliably update what `handleSubmit` reads back) — concretely: clear Sex, then edit-and-save Age, and Age's save would silently resubmit Sex's stale pre-clear value, reverting the clear. Caught by `DemographicsPanel.test.tsx`'s "Clear all ... survives a later Save elsewhere" test. Fixed by having per-row Save read and commit only its own field (`form.getValues(field)`) merged onto the latest committed block; the bottom-of-panel global Save (first-open mode) still uses `handleSubmit` since every row's `Controller` is mounted in that mode.
- **Store simplified to one action.** `setDemographicsAge`/`setDemographicsLocation`/`toggleDemographicsConcept`/`setDemographicsConcept`/`clearDemographicsConcept` (and the `withDemographics` helper) are replaced by a single `setDemographics(demographics: Demographics)` — the granular setters existed to support immediate-write editing, which no longer happens.

## Jira

https://hdruk.atlassian.net/browse/DP-1091

## PR Type

- [ ] `feat`
- [x] `refactor`
- [ ] `fix`
- [ ] `chore`
- [ ] `docs`
- [ ] `test`
- [ ] `perf`

## PR Title Check

`refactor(DP-1091): draft-until-save editing for the demographics panel`

## Changes Included

- [x] UI changes
- [ ] API integration changes (`src/actions/*`)
- [ ] Routing/navigation changes (`src/config/routes.ts`, app router pages)
- [x] State management changes (hooks/store)
- [x] Test updates
- [ ] Documentation updates

### Files

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `src/modules/DemographicsPanel/useDemographicFieldEditing.ts` | **new** — owns the shared `useForm<Demographics>()`, which field is active, first-open state, and `propsFor(field)` |
| `src/modules/DemographicsPanel/DemographicsPanel.tsx` | wraps rows in `<FormProvider>`, spreads `propsFor(field)` into each section, renders the bottom Save button while first-open |
| `src/modules/DemographicsPanel/DemographicRow.tsx` | dropped its own `editing` state — now fully controlled; exports the shared `DemographicRowActionProps` type |
| `src/modules/DemographicsPanel/DemographicSaveButton.tsx` | now holds the actual Reset/Save button pair (previously an in-progress, unused duplicate of the row's Edit/Clear controls) |
| `src/modules/DemographicsPanel/DemographicAgeSection.tsx`, `DemographicCheckboxSection.tsx`, `DemographicLocationSection.tsx` | pull `control` via `useFormContext<Demographics>()` instead of taking it as a prop; checkbox toggle/select-all logic now operates on the draft, not the committed store value |
| `src/modules/DemographicsPanel/DemographicConceptSection.tsx` | unused elsewhere in the app; updated to the same controlled-row contract so it isn't left broken |
| `src/store/queryBuilderStore.ts` | five granular demographics actions collapsed into one `setDemographics`; `EMPTY_DEMOGRAPHICS` now exported |
| `src/store/queryBuilderStore.demographics.test.ts` | updated for `setDemographics` |
| `src/modules/DemographicsPanel/DemographicsPanel.test.tsx` | **new** — first-open-all-editable, single-row coordination, Reset/Save/Clear-all behaviour, and the stale-draft regression above |
| `src/modules/DemographicsPanel/DemographicLocationSection.test.tsx` | updated to wrap the section in a local `FormProvider` instead of passing `control` directly |

## Validation

Run locally before requesting review:

- [x] `npm run lint` passes
- [x] `npm run test` passes (247 tests, including 7 new tests in `DemographicsPanel.test.tsx`)
- [x] `npm run build` passes
- [ ] `npm run build-storybook` passes (Storybook is not used in this project)
- [ ] Manual browser walkthrough — not completed in this session (no local login credentials to hand); please exercise the golden path below before merging

## Coding Conventions Checklist

- [x] New components/modules use existing naming conventions (PascalCase component files, `use*` hooks, action files in `src/actions`)
- [x] Imports follow existing ordering and alias usage (`@/` for internal imports)
- [x] Routes are built with helpers in `src/config/routes.ts` (no scattered hard-coded dashboard URLs) — n/a, no routing changes
- [x] API calls follow existing patterns (`apiGet/apiPost/...` in server actions, not ad-hoc fetch in client components) — n/a, no API changes
- [x] Side-effectful endpoints are not cached unintentionally — n/a, no API changes
- [x] No sensitive values, secrets, or debug-only code left behind

## Screenshots / Evidence

None captured — this session didn't have login credentials for a local walkthrough. See the manual test plan below.

## Risk and Rollback

- Risk level: medium
- Main risk areas:
  - Demographics panel editing flow (Age/Sex/Race/Location) — behaviour change from immediate-write to draft-until-save
  - `setDemographics` replacing the five granular store actions — anything outside this module that called `setDemographicsAge`/`toggleDemographicsConcept`/etc. would break at compile time (grepped repo-wide; nothing else called them)
- Rollback plan:
  - Revert PR — no data migration or persisted-state shape change involved (`Demographics` type is unchanged, only how it gets written)

## Notes for Reviewers

body:
## Summary

- **B-8 [CONFIRMED, P1]** (`audits/review-2026-08-26/B/collated-findings.md` §B-8): the belief row's `last seen in ROOM at tick T` had exactly one production writer, `_record_movement_sightings`, which skipped every episodic row that was not a witnessed `saw_player_move` transition — so an ordinary look at the subject never refreshed it and the non-elastic belief block asserted a room the same prompt's own observations contradicted two lines above. The writer is now `_record_last_seen_sightings` and records each subject's **latest** non-suppressed first-hand sighting (`room` from a `saw_player` row, `to_room` from a `saw_player_move` row — the two-branch extraction `agents/tactical/features.py:472-481` already performs), through the same §4.7 firewall with the row's OWN `action`.
- **B-35 [ADJUSTED, P3]** (same file §B-35): `_collect_movement_breadcrumbs` dropped `vent`/`kill` rows from the subject's path, justifying the skip as "never suffixed" — a property `_render_saw_player` already enforces by returning the vent line at :1810-1816 and the kill line at :1817-1823 *before* `_movement_suffix_for` is called. The drop was an undeclared second effect: it erased the placement those rows carry. Vent/kill rows now feed the path as prior-room candidates while the ANCHOR stays the subject's most recent ORDINARY sighting and priors are restricted to ticks at or before it — so exactly one line per moving subject is still suffixed and the vent/kill lines stay clean.
- **Both halves ship behind ONE default-OFF repair gate**, never two, because they are one sentence in one render fed by one argmax question: substrate key `last_seen_from_sightings`, variable `AILIBI_LAST_SEEN_FROM_SIGHTINGS`, registered in `orchestrator/replay.py::_TOGGLEABLE_LEVER_RESOLVERS` and documented in `.env.example`. **No committed byte moves in this PR** and every committed byte keeps reconstructing; `replays/samples/` and `replays/ml_corpus/` remain the baseline-7 record — canon by explicit owner override of a **FINDING** verdict, bars 1 and 2 missed (`audits/audit-phase-20-baseline-7.md` §6.1). Task 21.15 flips the gate unconditional, DELETES its mechanism outright (it is a repair, not a lever — no record runs it ON, so nothing graduates into `_RETIRED_ALWAYS_ON_LEVERS`) and re-records the four sets on the corrected render.

### Measurement — the OFF path (the merge condition)

The OFF path is not "approximately unchanged": it is the code that exists today, so the 47 tests the reverification's simulation of the *ungated* change turned red are green by construction rather than by re-blessing.

```
$ uv run pytest tests/meetings/test_prompt_byte_golden.py tests/agents tests/eval/test_evidence_honesty.py -q
1141 passed in 207.60s (0:03:27)

$ bash scripts/verify_samples.sh
=== verifying .../replays/samples/4p1i/ ===
All 50 samples verified clean.
=== verifying .../replays/samples/9p2i/ ===
All 50 samples verified clean.
```

That covers every file on the verifier's measured red list — `tests/meetings/test_prompt_byte_golden.py` (2 failed + 14 errors, first signature `headless-seed-0:meeting-0: reconstructed state_hash_after … != recorded …` from :611), `tests/agents/test_absence_prior.py` (14 errors), `tests/agents/test_beliefs_hard_evidence_gate.py` (6), `tests/eval/test_evidence_honesty.py` (4), `tests/agents/test_episodic_ids.py` (1 + 2), `tests/agents/test_reported_testimony.py` (1), `tests/agents/test_memory_store.py` (1 — the committed `_EXPECTED_FIXTURE_RENDER` at :934-948, the one uncontracted casualty, which never moves at all), plus the two `tests/agents/test_memory_rendering.py` goldens this task owns. 100/100 committed samples reconstruct byte-identically.

### Measurement — the ON path

```
$ AILIBI_LAST_SEEN_FROM_SIGHTINGS=1 uv run pytest tests/agents/test_memory_rendering.py tests/agents/test_memory.py tests/agents/test_features.py -q
174 passed

$ uv run pytest tests/agents/test_memory_rendering.py tests/agents/test_memory.py tests/agents/test_features.py -q
174 passed
```

**These two runs are identical, and that is not ON-path verification — see Decision 2.** `tests/conftest.py`'s hermetic guard strips every `AILIBI_*` name at `pytest_configure`, so the export never reaches a render inside pytest. Rather than assert the DoD item on that, here is the measurement that earns it — the guard temporarily patched to let the export through, so the whole advertised suite really does run ON:

```
$ AILIBI_LAST_SEEN_FROM_SIGHTINGS=1 uv run pytest ... -q     # guard patched, probe only
FAILED ...::TestSelfLocationTrail::test_render_matches_the_trail_golden
FAILED ...::TestCoalescedMemoryRender::test_render_matches_the_coalesced_golden
2 failed, 172 passed in 9.86s
```

**172 of 174 pass with the gate genuinely ON**, and the two failures are the committed-golden comparisons — which MUST fail, because those `.expected.md` files are the OFF render and this contract puts them in Files-NOT-in-scope so they stay byte-identical until Task 21.15. A whole-suite ON entry point is therefore contradictory by construction, and the patch was reverted; `tests/conftest.py` is untouched in this PR.

The ON arm's real gate is the in-module two-arm cases the contract itself prescribes, and they can fail: all four planted cases were written first and were red at HEAD (`'- p-3: suspicion 0.80 (last seen in ADMIN at tick 2)'` where `LABS at tick 5` was expected). The golden surface gets ON coverage without moving: `_sole_changed_line` pins each moving fixture's ON render as a one-line diff, and the three non-moving fixtures are pinned identical on both arms.

### Measurement — registration

```
$ uv run pytest tests/orchestrator/test_replay.py -q
87 passed in 1.50s
```

A bare environment stamps the new key `False`; the committed `_BASELINE7_STAMP` — which predates the key and does not name it — still reconstructs in a bare shell through the missing-key rule, and is REFUSED with the gate exported (the perturbation that proves the seam is a match, not an omission).

### Measurement — behaviour, on freshly rendered bytes

One fake-provider 9p2i game per arm at the contract's seed, then the register's own row-versus-observations comparison (scan script quoted below, run from the scratchpad under craft rule 5, not committed):

```
$ uv run python scripts/run_game.py --seed 4104 --num-players 9 --num-impostors 2 \
    --replay-path <scratch>/lastseen-off.jsonl
$ AILIBI_LAST_SEEN_FROM_SIGHTINGS=1 uv run python scripts/run_game.py --seed 4104 \
    --num-players 9 --num-impostors 2 --replay-path <scratch>/lastseen-check.jsonl
$ python3 scan_last_seen.py lastseen-off.jsonl lastseen-check.jsonl

lastseen-off.jsonl                          lastseen-check.jsonl
  prompts scanned                  : 32       prompts scanned                  : 32
  belief rows carrying a last-seen : 22       belief rows carrying a last-seen : 22
  ... contradicted                 : 12       ... contradicted                 : 0
  breadcrumb suffixes              : 148      breadcrumb suffixes              : 148
  ... contradicted                 : 0        ... contradicted                 : 0
```

Both arms end `IMPOSTORS` at tick 21 with 32 prompts, so the games did not diverge. **Zero contradictions in both classes on the ON arm, against 12 on the OFF arm.**

**Newly-suffixed belief rows and newly-minted breadcrumbs on that one game: 0 and 0.** Seed 4104's byte-widening is a *changed* suffix, not an added one — 12 belief rows across 30 prompts move from `(last seen in STORAGE at tick 8)` to `(last seen in ENGINEERING at tick 11)`, and 0 breadcrumb lines move. (The other 27 changed lines are fake-provider `free_text` hashes, which are a deterministic function of the prompt: downstream of the render change, not part of it.)

Seed 4104 happens to carry no B-35 instance (its crew never witnessed a vent in a room the subject was later ordinarily seen in), so the 0→0 breadcrumb column there is honest but uninformative for t

body:
## Summary

Fixes a layout issue in the multi-column information view where sections opening in the second column were misaligned vertically due to CSS column fragment behavior truncating top margins.

## Changes

- **InformationView.tsx**: Updated the column wrapper to use top padding (`md:pt-9`) instead of relying on the heading's top margin, and neutralize the heading's margin within columns using a CSS selector (`md:[&_.sheet-heading]:mt-0`)
- **SheetUi.tsx**: Added a `sheet-heading` class marker to the heading element to enable the parent container to target and neutralize its top margin

## Implementation Details

CSS multi-column layout truncates margins at the top of column fragments, causing sections that open a new column to sit 36px higher than sections in the first column. By moving the spacing from the heading's `mt-7 sm:mt-9` margin to padding on the wrapper (`md:pt-9`), the spacing is preserved across column breaks. The heading's margin is then neutralized within columns using the `sheet-heading` class selector, ensuring consistent vertical alignment while maintaining the gap between stacked sections.

author: teknium1
body:
Campaign entry (#95681). NOTE: the tracker's old 651-tok figure was the static stub — this tool builds its real text via dynamic_schema_overrides; AS-SERVED on a default config is **1,201 tok/call**. All numbers measured through `model_tools.get_tool_definitions()` (the wire path).

Three maintainer-directed interface changes + diet, in commit order:

## Commit 1 — depth-derived delegation, session-filtered rules, background unadvertised

**`role` retired.** The old model made the CALLER declare `role='leaf'|'orchestrator'`, then silently coerced it when config disagreed. Now the runtime derives it: a child may itself delegate iff `delegation.orchestrator_enabled` and its depth < `max_spawn_depth` (`_build_child_agent`, the existing enforcement point). `role`/`tasks[].role` leave the schema; handler accepts+ignores them (old transcripts, kanban dispatcher). Depth-1 installs (default): the word "orchestrator" appears NOWHERE in the served schema. Behavior delta on nesting-enabled installs only: children with depth budget now always get delegate_task (previously only when the caller remembered to ask).

**Restrictions rule session-filtered.** The "children cannot call X" line now names only tools the SESSION actually has (same model_tools seam as the browser_exec terminal-gate; memo key already includes toolsets): full kit → full list · partial → filtered · none → line dropped. **send_message is never named** — gateway-internal vocabulary; enforcement unchanged (DELEGATE_BLOCKED_TOOLS still strips all five).

**`background` (86 tok of "DEPRECATED / IGNORED") unadvertised**; handler unchanged.

## Commit 2 — tasks[] is the only advertised shape (the clarify #95907 pattern)

The runtime already wrapped single-goal calls into a one-entry task list internally; the schema was the only place the two-shape fiction lived — and it bred real confusion (top-level `context` looked like shared/broadcast context; it never was: each child sees only its own `tasks[i].context`).

- Top-level `goal`/`context`/`output_schema` leave the schema (handler-accepted legacy, wrapped at dispatch as before; do-not-re-add comments in place).
- `tasks[]` (minItems 1) is the one shape; item fields now carry the full teaching, including the context-isolation rule models previously had to guess: "Each child sees only its own context — repeat shared background in every task that needs it."
- The min-2 batch gate is gone (a one-entry array is now canonical, matching the runtime's internal shape); the placeholder/template goal checks still run on every entry, and the short-goal check applies only to multi-task fan-outs (single tasks legitimately use short goals — preserves the historical exemption including the gpt-5.4-mini `tasks=[]`+goal regression case).
- Missing-input error teaches the canonical shape.

## Numbers (as served, o200k_base, default config)
| | tok/call |
|---|---|
| main | 1,201 |
| commit 1 | 819 |
| commit 2 | **773 (−428, −36%)** |

**4 advertised params** (tasks, action, subagent_id, message), down from 9.

## Verification
- E2E (wire path): depth-1 + depth-3 (temp HERMES_HOME) variants; all four session-filter shapes; `role`/`orchestrator`/`leaf`/`send_message` asserted absent from serialized schema.
- E2E (dispatch): one-entry array with short goal spawns clean; legacy `goal=`/`context=`/`role=` still flow; bare call gets the teaching error.
- 153/156 delegate tests pass — 3 failures are the pre-existing output_schema trio (reproduced identically on clean origin/main via stash). 5 contract tests updated to pin the new interface, incl. flipping the one that REQUIRED the min-2 rejection into one that requires one-entry acceptance.

author: fcoury-oai
body:
## Why

Recent releases hide Red's most distinctive Agent, inline-assist, Vim, and performance improvements inside commit-ordered changelogs. GitHub releases, Discord, and the in-app What's New panel also choose highlights independently, so users miss the same flagship work across every surface.

## What Changed

- Add a reviewed, version-specific `release/campaign.toml` with six ordered stories covering source-linked Agent explanations, inline assistance, Vim-style multi-cursor editing, conversation model selection, large-repository performance, and external-file protection.
- Render the same editorial campaign for GitHub release introductions, Discord, in-app highlights, X, and Bluesky while preserving complete contributor-attributed changelogs and falling back safely when versions do not match.
- Resolve and validate the campaign version during release preparation; prioritize features and performance in public changelogs; and preserve the latest upstream CI planning and branch-ruleset checks.
- Add dependency-free X and Bluesky adapters with optional images, X video, accessible alt text, bounded post lengths, and credential-safe errors. Workflows generate offline previews only: authenticated posting requires a separate explicit `--publish` invocation.
- Update release-review checklists and document the real Agent/inline safety boundaries, campaign review requirements, and promotion of upcoming-feature language.

Merging this change does not publish a release or a social post. Release publication still starts only through the existing separate tag action; Discord retains its existing release-published behavior.

## How to Test

1. Run `python3 -m unittest tests.test_release_campaign tests.test_discord_release tests.test_social_release`; all 39 tests should pass, including mismatched-version rejection, no-network social previews, media handling, and credential-safe failures.
2. Run `cargo test --lib whats_new`; all 21 release-panel tests should pass, including exact-version campaign highlights and fallback for unresolved, mismatched, or invalid campaigns.
3. Run `python3 scripts/release_campaign.py validate` and `python3 scripts/release_campaign.py render --channel github`; confirm the six reviewed stories appear before the full changelog and genuinely new features are distinguished from improvements.
4. Render X or Bluesky copy and pass it to `scripts/social_release.py --platform <x|bluesky> --text-file <rendered-file> --json` without `--publish`; confirm the result reports `"published": false` and requires no credentials.

author: gunbai-bot[bot]
body:
One row in the rung census. No behaviour change, no witness edit, no typecheck change.

## The finding

`test.claim.record_literal_call_arg_handoff_witness.record_literal_container_element_mismatch_at_call_arg_still_refuses` asserts that `FreeMonoid<Node>` handed to a declared `FreeMonoid<NormalizedTree>` parameter must refuse. It is green on main. **The judgment it names does not fire.**

Measured 2026-08-27 with the witness's own oracle (`compile_dag_rust_emit_check`) alongside `compile_dag_diagnostic_census`, over two corpora in two remote dispatches — `main` @ `ddb7f533e4e` and gunbc#9428's head:

| fixture | on `main` | on #9428's head |
|---|---|---|
| main's exact fixture text | **refuses** — `UnresolvedType std.occurrence_identity.OccurrenceId` ×2, `ScopedOccurrenceRef` ×1 | refuses — `MissingExport SyntheticOccurrence` |
| `NormalizedTree` + local record | **compiles clean** | compiles clean |
| corpus-unique wrapper + local record | **compiles clean** | compiles clean |

The last two are the identical container-element mismatch with **no `Node`, no `v2.std.node`, no occurrence identity** anywhere in them, and a corpus-unique wrapper name. They compile clean on `main`, zero blocking. The argument surfaces only as advisory `DeclaredTypeInhabitanceUndecided`.

Main's refusal of the real fixture is **exactly** the two `UnresolvedType` diagnostics and contains no type-mismatch diagnostic at all: `v2.std.node` referenced `std.occurrence_identity.OccurrenceId` and `ScopedOccurrenceRef` fully qualified without importing that module, so every closure importing `v2.std.node` inherited them. gunbc#9428 adds the import; those resolve, and the accidental refusal goes with them.

## Why this is 4b(1) and not 4b(3)

Nothing regressed. The check was never firing, before or after. What is corrected is a rung **reported higher than it ever was** — DESIGN's rung inflation, which it calls worse than sitting low because an inflated class never ranks for climbing.

Framing matters here operationally: a §4b(3) regression row invites *restore the previous behaviour*, and the previous behaviour was an accident. Re-adding unresolved references to buy back the red is the one remedy that must not happen.

## The generalisable part

**A witness green on a defect in its own closure is not weak coverage — it is negative coverage.** It is cited as evidence the wall is live, so the class never ranks. That is DESIGN §4b's worse-than-absent case reached from a direction the document does not currently record: not an *unauthorable* RED, but an **authorable one satisfied by the wrong cause**, which no reader of the witness can distinguish from the right one.

The family read as coherent because the nominal sibling `record_literal_nominal_mismatch_at_call_arg_still_refuses` is genuinely green — through a different path (`literal_introduction_type_mismatch`, whose actual is a record literal rather than a call).

## Scope

Declares the class, names the trigger, stops. It does **not** attempt to make `container_element_nominal_brand_mismatch` fire — that is a typecheck change with its own blast radius and its own owner.

The enrolment of the witness as expected-red lands in gunbc#9428, not here, and the reason is mechanical: on `main` the witness still **passes** (on the accident), and `required_floor_outcome_is_clean` requires `stale_quarantine` to be empty — an enrolled row that passes reds the build. Enrolling here would red main's own required floor. It fails on #9428's head, which is where it is honestly enrollable.

Sequencing ruled by `snappy-dove-250`; gunbc#9428 waits on this.
