author: nimeshjm
body:
Closes #42

Top of a 2-PR stack; based on #53, which carries the `filled_at` anchor and the Stage 2
report fields. This PR is the emission half: the span, the board spec, the human-readable
columns and the docs.

## What changes

- **`sdlc.design.snapshot`**, one per feature, a **sibling root span** of the existing
  `sdlc.plan.snapshot` / `sdlc.plan.rollup`, in the same `emit_spans()` call. A third span
  name rather than more attributes on the Stage 1 snapshot, because the existing rationale
  is that every board widget queries by `name` alone.
- **No `sdlc.design.rollup`.** Both Stage 2 indicators are per-feature; there is no
  accepted/rejected/survival analogue to aggregate, and a rollup restating counts already
  visible per feature would be a span with nothing to say. Written down in the module
  docstring so it does not get added later to "match" the Stage 1 shape.
- `PANELS_DESIGN`, `BOARD_NAME_DESIGN`, `BOARD_DESCRIPTION_DESIGN`, `TRIGGER_DESIGN` —
  spec-in-file next to the emitter, same convention as `PANELS`.
- Stage 2 columns in `print_table`, a `## Measuring stage 2` section in
  `features/README.md`, and one line in `CLAUDE.md`.

## The board is still not created — but #42's reason for waiting only half holds

The issue says every Stage 2 numeric column is omitted while no feature is measurable, so
hand-creating a column to make a panel render reproduces #29's measured failure: `P50`/`MAX`
come back a fabricated `0` and the panel shows a flat zero line.

That is true of the three **lead-time** panels — `sdlc.design.lead_time_hours` is never
emitted while every feature is `design_measurable = false`, and 001 is, by construction. It
is **not** true of the churn side: 001 emits `sdlc.spec.post_plan_edits = 3` and
`sdlc.design.anchor_source = "plan-filled"` today, so "Post-plan spec churn" and "Build not
started" have real data on the first emit. The accurate split is recorded above
`PANELS_DESIGN` rather than the stale blanket version.

## The test gap this closes

The 24 rows from #53 assert only the `--json` report. **Nothing exercised `_build_specs` or
the board specs**, so a span-attribute typo, or a panel naming a field nothing emits, would
have shipped green — a board that silently returns no data, with no failing test anywhere.

- **Row 24** pins the design span's exact attribute key set for a fully-filled feature,
  that `sdlc.measurable` and `sdlc.design.anchor_source` are always present, that no value
  is `None`, and that no `sdlc.design.rollup` exists.
- **Row 25** checks every `sdlc.*` column in *both* boards' panels and triggers against what
  `_build_specs` can actually emit, plus that every panel's `name` filter names a real span.
  This is the row that catches the naming trap #42 flags: in this namespace `sdlc.plan.*` is
  the Stage 1 *stage*, while `plan.md` is the Stage 3 *artifact*, so the artifact's date is
  `sdlc.design.plan_filled_at` and never `sdlc.plan.filled_at`.

## Verification

`npm run test:plan-metrics`: 26 rows green. A green run is not the check — each new row was
confirmed to fail with its guard removed, and the verifying model re-ran three mutations
independently rather than taking the implementer's word:

| Mutation | Effect |
|---|---|
| rename `sdlc.design.plan_filled_at` → `sdlc.plan.filled_at` in `_build_specs` | row 24 red |
| typo a `PANELS_DESIGN` breakdown column | row 25 red |
| emit `None` for an absent design field instead of omitting the key | row 24 red |

Also green: `npm run typecheck`, `npx wrangler deploy --dry-run` (no `src/**` change),
`npm run review:checks`, and — via `core.hooksPath` on every push — `lint:ast`,
`test:ast`, `lint:ts`, `test:checks` and `npm test`.

A follow-up commit records one thing the mutation table cannot: the synthetic fixtures are
dated October 2026 so they land after every commit in this repo's real history, because
`--follow -M25%` pairs a still-template artifact as a *copy* of `features/_template/` and
walks into the template's own history. Those dates are therefore perishable — real history
keeps growing — so the row now says that a red row means "move the dates forward", not
"weaken the assertion".

Two corrections to #42 found while implementing:

- The issue's `### Attributes` block lists `sdlc.intent.committed_at` on the design span. It
  is not emitted there; row 24's exact-key-set assertion pins its absence. A board built
  from the issue's literal list would query a field that returns nothing.
- A comment credited the wrong mutation row with enforcing the `name` filter; it now refers
  to the row by name, since a row number drifts as rows are added.

`__pycache__/` is gitignored: the new module-level import of `plan_metrics` leaves bytecode
behind when the pre-push hook runs the suite.

## Roles

Per the delegation split recorded in #52: orchestrated and verified by Opus, implemented by
Sonnet.

author: davonlemar30
body:
## Summary
- Home's three intent buttons (LOOK FOR WORK / LOOK FOR A DEAL / SEE WHO IS OUT) collapse into one **WALK AROUND** button dispatching READ, plus a conditional **GO TO WORK** button that appears only once employed and routes to the Jobs screen. WORK and DEAL stay real, dispatchable intents (the parity economy profiles still use them directly) — only the UI stopped asking the player to choose upfront.
- `wander.gd::_wander()` broadens READ into WORK's and DEAL's own discovery pools, so a single WALK AROUND tap can turn up a job or a boost target on top of everything READ already found. WORK and DEAL still answer to only their own pool, never each other's — the choice between them still means something underneath the UI that stopped asking for it.
- Market gets a **POST UP** button: spend a slot standing in place and find out what a hot corner costs. Its dispatch lives on `ConsequenceEngine` as a new `post_up` action rather than a bare `time_system.handle()` call from the screen — every UI-initiated mutation in this codebase goes through `GameManager.dispatch()` without exception (verified across all ~20 screen files), and calling a system method directly from a screen would spend the hour without `notify_changed()` ever firing. The action does exactly what Wander does for its own slot — advance the clock, then `try_surface_delayed()` — same call, no parallel encounter system.
- **Task 3 (ModalSheet encounter presentation) is deferred**, not attempted halfway. It's the PR's own explicit stretch goal. `consequence.gd` is 622 lines implementing a carefully rule-bound presentation contract (odds as bands never percentages, arrest warnings without thresholds, signed result deltas); reimplementing that for a modal risks silently diverging from it, and embedding the existing full-chrome scene in a card-sized sheet fights its own design. A half-measure (modal the decision, then jump to the full screen for the result) would be a worse, more inconsistent UX than what ships today. Filed as a follow-up with the assessment attached.

## Test plan

author: jihoon22-lee
body:
`ICI-GAPS` **C-8** 입니다. 남은 것 중 마지막 소소한 건입니다.

## 문제

ruff 가 없을 때 내려가는 AST 폴백은 `SyntaxError` 가 났을 때만 타깃을 남깁니다. 그래서:

```
깨끗한 프로젝트        → 타깃 0건
아무것도 안 본 프로젝트  → 타깃 0건
```

**둘이 구분되지 않았습니다.** 이건 이 세션에서 찾은 버그들과 똑같은 모양입니다 — 게이트가 초록불인 이유가 "검사해서 깨끗해서"가 아니라 "검사를 안 해서"인 경우. C-6(CI 에서 lint 가 한 번도 실행된 적 없음)을 눈치채기 어렵게 만든 직접적 원인이기도 했습니다.

## 수정

```
[PASS] ASTSyntaxFallback: Ruff was unavailable; parsed 2 Python file(s)
       for syntax errors only. Style and lint rules were not checked.
```

파싱한 파일 수를 `extra.python_files_parsed` 와 타깃 메트릭에 기록합니다.

**무엇을 검사하지 않았는지도 말합니다.** 그러지 않으면 읽는 사람이 lint 가 돌았다고 가정합니다 — 실제로 그 가정 때문에 CI 에서 lint 가 안 도는 걸 오래 못 봤습니다.

## 검증

ruff 를 숨기고 두 프로젝트를 비교:

```
파일 2개 파싱 | 타깃 1건   ← 코드가 있는 프로젝트
파일 0개 파싱 | 타깃 1건   ← 빈 프로젝트
```

테스트 3건 추가 — 검사량 보고, 빈 프로젝트 구분, 그리고 **SyntaxError 는 여전히 잡히는지**.

`pytest` 전체 통과 · `ruff` 통과 · 자체 검증 exit 0.

body:
> _Disclaimer: AI (Claude) was used to assist with implementing and documenting the changes in this PR._

## Summary


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/466f5c71-ffc2-4274-9688-3d4785da5d67



Redesigns the Location demographics filter's map picker (`GeoMapPicker`) to match the latest design: the address search bar now overlays the top of the map instead of sitting in a row above it, the "LSOA boundaries" toggle moved into that same overlay bar next to the search box (using the shared `ToggleAction` component instead of a plain MUI `Switch`), and the radius slider is now a compact overlay pinned to the bottom-left of the map that only appears once a location has actually been picked (pin dropped or address searched) rather than always being visible. Leaflet's zoom control moved from its default top-left position to bottom-right so it no longer sits under the new search overlay.

Also fixes two real bugs surfaced while building this:

- **Wrong initial zoom when editing an existing location.** The map always opened at a fixed zoom level regardless of the saved radius, so a wide radius (e.g. 500 km) opened tightly zoomed in with the radius circle nowhere in view. `GeoMapPicker` now computes an initial Leaflet `fitBounds` from the saved `lat/lon` + `radius` on mount (`L.latLng(...).toBounds(radius * 2)`), so opening a saved location frames its full radius.
- **Search bar not reflecting a pin drop.** Dropping a pin directly on the map (without searching an address) left the search box empty. `AddressSearch` now accepts a `value` prop and `GeoMapPicker` feeds it a formatted `"lat, lon"` string whenever there's a position with no address. This uncovered a subtler MUI `Autocomplete` issue: without `freeSolo`, Autocomplete resets `inputValue` back to match the selected `value` (`null`) on every render, silently undoing the externally-set text — `freeSolo` had to be added, with `getOptionLabel`/`onChange` guarded against the free-typed-string case that `freeSolo` introduces (otherwise a raw string could reach `.lat`/`.lon` and crash, or trip an MUI console warning).

`DemographicRow.tsx` (shared by Age/Sex/Race/Location) also got two small fixes needed to support the above and to match the same design language across all four rows: an invalid CSS `alignItems="space-between"` value was corrected to `"flex-start"`, and the editing content now sits as a flex sibling to the right of the row's label (`flexShrink={0}` on the label, `flex: 1, minWidth: 0` on the content) instead of stacked awkwardly underneath it.

### Decisions worth noting

- **`freeSolo` on `AddressSearch`'s `Autocomplete`.** Required to let the input display arbitrary text (a lat/lng readout) that doesn't correspond to any selected option — MUI actively fights a controlled `inputValue` otherwise. This is a genuinely subtle MUI behaviour: it wasn't caught by reading the code, only by writing a test that re-rendered `AddressSearch` with a changed `value` prop and watching the DOM input value get silently reset.
- **`showBoundaries` stayed local `useState` in `GeoMapPicker`**, not lifted to the parent. An earlier iteration lifted it (and a live lat/lng readout) into the outer `DemographicRow` header to match an intermediate design, but the design settled on keeping both in the map overlay instead — see Known follow-ups below for the one leftover from that direction that's now dead weight in `DemographicRow`.
- **`ToggleAction` reused as-is** for "LSOA boundaries" rather than styling a new control, matching its only other consumer (`SelectDatasets.tsx`). It renders as two segmented icon buttons (X / check) rather than a sliding switch — a different interaction pattern than the `Switch` it replaces (see Known follow-ups).

https://hdruk.atlassian.net/browse/DP-1092

| `src/components/GeoMap/GeoMapPicker.tsx` | overlay search bar + boundaries toggle, conditional radius overlay, repositioned zoom control, `fitBounds` framing for saved locations, feeds `AddressSearch` a lat/lng readout |

author: ahmedsaed
body:
Three things prod found within an hour of #8, plus the homepage decision. Recorded as an [amendment to ADR-0017](docs/adr/0017-rate-limits-pause-games.md).

## 1. A shared pool is the *provider's*, not the model's

I keyed the cooldown by `(model, provider)`. So `gemma-4-26b` was cooled down and correctly skipped — and the matchmaker paired `gemma-4-31b`, **a different model on the same hot Google AI Studio pool**, which paused a minute later for the same reason. Then a third, on GMICloud:

```
paused  cc48ab6e  minimax-m2.7  · GMICloud
        f64915b6  gemma-4-26b   · Google AI Studio
        c8687dd8  gemma-4-31b   · Google AI Studio
        c7d97ea3  gemma-4-26b   · Google AI Studio
```

`limit_source: upstream_provider_shared_pool` is a statement about a pool serving many models. A refusal naming it now rests the **whole provider**, and an entrant is skipped when *every* endpoint it has is on a resting provider — "every", not "any", because a paid model on nineteen providers isn't unavailable because one rests.

## 2. Freeing the slot needed a ceiling

Not counting paused games against concurrency was right — they spend nothing. But with nothing bounding the **inactive** pile, a hot provider gets absorbed by opening more games instead of by waiting. Four paused games against `max_concurrent: 1`, each destined to wake, be refused, and eventually abandon: the original failure at a slower tempo.

A pool now holds once `max_concurrent + 2` games are paused. The headroom is small deliberately — it exists so one unlucky pause doesn't stall a healthy pool, not so an outage can be spread across the field.

## 3. The last abandoned game was never a rate limit

`f8768830` played 10 plies of a real Scotch Game and died on a 400:

```
This endpoint's maximum context length is 65536 tokens. However, you requested about 65810
tokens (1430 of text input, 380 of tool input, 64000 in the output).
```

Three layers:

- **`liquid/lfm-2.5-2.6b:free` should never have been registered.** Its window is 65,536, under AGENT-14's 128k floor.
- **How it got in:** `fetch_catalogue(min_context=…)` defaults to **0, meaning no filter**. `refresh_catalogue.py` passed it; `seed_models.py` did not. So the rule held or not depending on which command you last ran. Fixed. Also, CLAUDE.md cited a `MIN_CONTEXT_TOKENS` constant that **does not exist** — corrected.
- **The worker retried a fatal 400 five times.** The gateway classified it correctly (`attempts=1`), but `TurnResult` carried the error's *text* and nothing that could be reasoned about. A refusal of the *request* is now abandoned at once.

That last one is deliberately narrower than the gateway's `retryable`: a deadline is fatal to a *call* but a fresh turn may succeed, and an auth blip must not abandon every game in flight. Only request-shape rejections short-circuit.

## 4. Paused games are off the homepage

Reversing half of #9 at your call — and I agree: the front page is a shop window and a stopped board is a poor introduction. `HeroGame`'s three-state fix stays, because a featured game can still pause while someone is watching it.

## An unpleasant find

`make_tournament` returns `Entrant` objects, not slugs. An assertion I added yesterday compared an `Entrant` to a `str` — it could never fail, and had been testing nothing. Fixed, with a comment so it doesn't recur.

## Still open, stated not fixed

`max_completion_tokens` is a flat **64,000** reconciled against nothing. Clamping it to `context_length - prompt - margin` is the real fix; enforcing the floor only keeps models that can't hold it out of the field. I'd do both, and it's a separate change.

Note the floor fix prevents *future* admissions — `liquid/lfm-2.5-2.6b:free` is already an entrant in `pool-free`. Withdraw it: `make tournament ARGS="withdraw pool-free liquid/lfm-2.5-2.6b:free"`.

`make check`: **1063** backend (was 1052) + 133 frontend, lint and strict mypy clean.

body:
## Summary

- reassert the root conversation viewport's follow-to-tail policy after live history is replaced with its durable projection
- repeat tail resolution when terminal focus returns, since hidden-tab redraw suppression can discard an earlier Brick scroll request
- preserve paused scrollback instead of forcing users back to the tail
- add a deterministic Brick/Vty regression harness for focused and hidden-tab history replacement

## Why

History compaction can replace a long live turn with a much shorter durable projection. Brick retains the old viewport top when the replacement still exceeds the viewport height, so the viewport can point past the new content and appear blank. A manual scroll clamps the offset, which is why scrolling up made the text reappear.

## Testing

- compiled regression test drives the real Brick event handler through history start, long live output, durable replacement, focus loss/gain, and a later hidden reflow: 2 examples, 0 failures
- verified both regression scenarios fail when the two viewport-resolution hooks are removed
- `TUIScrollSpec`: 17 examples, 0 failures
- production TUI source loaded/typechecked in GHCi
- reproduced and verified the fix in Ghostty using focus-out/focus-in events
- tmux smoke test confirmed the final answer remains visible after hidden history replacement

The broader agent-cli suite compiled and ran 1,118 examples; 26 database tests failed because the temporary PostgreSQL Unix socket path exceeded the platform path limit, unrelated to this change.

The concurrent TUI module-refactor merge dropped the `AppAgentSnapshot` case label while moving the handler; this branch restores that label so the merged code continues to compile.

author: geodro
body:
Only Laravel 11 and up and Tempest declared the vite worker, so a site on any other definition never got a dev server worker and never got the generated wrapper config that puts vite behind the site's own domain. That left people wiring the site certificate, the hostname and the HMR host into vite.config by hand, which is what came up in discussion 1558 on a Laravel 10 project.

Serving a dev server under the site domain is a property of the tool rather than of the framework running it, and everything the mechanism needs was already framework agnostic. The wrapper writer and the nginx proxy both key off vite being installed, not off a framework name. So the same declaration now goes to every definition whose asset pipeline is vite: Laravel 9 and 10, Statamic 4 and up, Symfony 5 and up through vite-bundle, and CakePHP 4 and up through ViteHelper.

The check on node_modules/vite is what makes this safe to declare broadly. A project that never added a dev server never sees the worker, so a definition whose scaffolding does not ship vite still carries the block without showing anything.

Definitions from the webpack era are left alone on purpose. Laravel 6 to 8, Statamic 3, Symfony 4 and CakePHP 3 shipped Mix or Encore, and CodeIgniter, Drupal, Magento, TYPO3 and WordPress declare no npm pipeline at all.

The health probe on public/hot goes only to Laravel and Statamic. That file is written by the Laravel vite plugin, and pointing the probe at a file nothing writes would report a perfectly healthy dev server as dead.

author: r-tome
body:
## 🎟️ Tracking

https://bitwarden.atlassian.net/browse/PM-42605

Stacked on #8211 (PM-12473). Review that one first — this PR only adds a caller.

## 📔 Objective

`CollectionsController.PostBulkCollectionAccess` was the last place in
`CollectionsController` still using `BulkCollectionAuthorizationHandler` for
collection access. This PR points it at `ICollectionAuthorizationService`,
which #8211 added, behind the same `pm-35160-authorization-services` flag.

The old call passed both `ModifyUserAccess` and `ModifyGroupAccess` to a
single `AuthorizeAsync`, so both operations had to succeed across the whole
collection set. The flag-on path intersects `AuthorizeModifyUserAccessManyAsync`
and `AuthorizeModifyGroupAccessManyAsync`, which is the same all-or-nothing
decision. This also gives those two methods their first caller.

Three things stay as they are:

- **The count pre-check.** It rejects unknown, cross-organization and duplicate
  collection ids with a 404. `ICollectionAuthorizationService` leaves such ids
  out of its result rather than failing on them, so removing this check would
  turn a rejection into a silent ignore.
- **The collection fetch.** `BulkAddCollectionAccessCommand.AddAccessAsync`
  takes the `Collection` entities and needs them for event logging and for its
  default-collection check. The authorization service resolves the same ids
  again, so this request reads collections twice. That is the cost of an
  authorization layer that fetches its own data, instead of threading
  pre-fetched entities into it — the pattern rejected on #8075.
- **The 404 on an empty request.** This one needs an explicit guard. The old
  handler fails an empty resource list, while the service returns an empty
  result, and "every id is authorized" is vacuously true over an empty list.
  Without the guard the flag-on path would fail open and reach the command.

No behavior change is expected on either path.

## 📸 Screenshots

author: backspace
body:
This is a Percy stability step, though it mostly would help diagnosis of diffs, as pinning the `boxel-skills` version would be the real stability fix but would be too annoying, I think.

Claude: Three things about `skills:setup` were worth fixing, none of them the version it clones.

An existing `contents/` was never looked at again, so a machine that cloned it once kept that content indefinitely while CI — which clones fresh every run — served current skills. It is now brought up to date. Two cases are deliberately left alone: uncommitted changes, so trying something out in place is not overwritten, and a detached HEAD. Being offline costs the update rather than the ability to start a dev stack, since this runs on the way into one.

A failed clone left an empty realm behind to be discovered later as something else entirely. It now fails immediately, naming both attempts, which is what the neighbouring catalog clone already did.

The SSH attempt's output is dropped. It is expected to fail wherever there is no key, and in CI it printed `Permission denied (publickey)` on every run — which reads like the cause when you are scanning a log for a real failure, and recently was mistaken for one.

Not pinning the revision is deliberate, and the README says so. Upstream is iterated on daily, so a pin would need moving every week; measured against twelve weeks of Percy history, unpinned upstream accounts for roughly one diff every three weeks on a single snapshot. That is not worth a weekly chore, and the fix for it belongs in the tests that render third-party content.

body:
2026-08-27 語料復原過程中踩到的兩個坑，都在 `scripts/ops/rebackfill.sh`。

## 1. `grounding_verdicts.csv` 沒被 commit

它是唯一一個沒進 `git add` 清單的 label cache。第 0 步的 `reset --hard` 會把未 commit 的檔案清掉，所以**每天花錢跑出來的 grounding 判定隔天就被丟掉、重判一次**。這週已經手動補 commit 兩次（`dcab9ae`、`d746231`）。

## 2. checkout 失敗還是會繼續跑，而且跑在錯的分支上

git 不允許同一分支被兩個工作區同時 checkout，兩次 checkout 都會安靜失敗——但接在後面的 `reset --hard origin/$BRANCH` 照樣成功，**把 worktree 當下所在的分支移到 BRANCH 的 commit**。然後整輪爬取、標註、重算、commit 就落在錯的分支上，一句話都不會說。

2026-08-27 就這樣把一次 refresh 的資料 commit 放到了 feature branch 的 ref 上。

修法：在任何東西寫入之前，確認 checkout 真的成功了。

## 驗證

```
$ bash -n scripts/ops/rebackfill.sh
bash syntax OK
$ python3 -m pytest tests/test_label_importers.py -q
24 passed
$ ruff check .
All checks passed!
```

另外用一個臨時 git repo 實際跑過 guard（clone 持有 `feature`、worktree 持有 `main`）：

author: rsteenwyk
body:
## Summary

- dispatch cancellation from the target completion state rather than the cancel request state
- make cancellation of dead or already-deleting completions a no-op
- close and clear epoll-owned duplicate file descriptors after cancellation and failed registration
- add regression coverage for dead-target cancellation and both duplicate-fd retirement paths

## Why

The existing cancellation guard checks the cancellation completion itself. Since `start` only processes `.adding` completions, that condition is always true and `stop_completion` can run against a dead or never-registered target. For active targets, `stop_completion` removes the duplicate fd from epoll but does not close it. Failed epoll registration similarly leaves an owned duplicate open.

This change follows the target-state dispatch already used by the kqueue backend and keeps duplicate-fd ownership cleanup in one helper. It addresses the lifecycle defects reported in #230 and #231. Those defects are implicated in the stale epoll delivery tracked by #234, but this PR does not claim to resolve issue 234.

Fixes #230
Fixes #231
Related to #234

## Tests

- `zig build test`
- `zig build test -Doptimize=ReleaseSafe`
- `zig build test -Doptimize=ReleaseFast`
- `zig fmt --check src/backend/epoll.zig`
- `git diff --check`

## Ghostty validation

I also tested Ghostty 1.3.1 with this patch backported onto its pinned libxev revision (`34fa5087`), using the epoll backend and a terminal-query stress workload.

- patched: 3 clean runs, 2 ReleaseSafe aborts
- unpatched control: 2 clean runs, 3 ReleaseSafe aborts
- both aborted in `epoll_ctl(EPOLL_CTL_DEL)` with `FileDescriptorIncompatibleWithEpoll`
- neither reproduced the `queue.zig:48` queued-write null dereference

This confirms that the cancellation and duplicate-fd fixes in this PR are not sufficient to resolve the broader stale-registration problem tracked by #234. That issue appears to require registration identity and lifetime changes beyond this PR's scope.

author: huamick
body:
## What

The `next:` block every `storytree library artifact <id>` read prints is the artifact's own **citation list** — provenance, *"what this was written from"* — presented as **navigation**. There is no ranking, filtering or relevance step in that path: `renderOfferFollowUps` loops the list and prints one command per entry. So its size measures how many artifacts happened to cite a thing, never how useful it is to the session being handed it.

Measured (frozen, `docs/research/decision-read-baseline-2026-08-23.md` §4): **4.7%** of decision pointers ever followed — an upper bound, the join is deliberately generous — and **111 of 151** offered decisions never followed once.

**The cost is alignment, not context length.** The block is ~1% of a read; the widest measured is 3,537 chars under a 62,386-char document. Any future proposal selling a change here as a context saving is wrong on the numbers.

Owner-directed 2026-08-27: **delete it.** Discovery becomes `library search`, `library related --unlinked`, and the deliberately authored `depends_on` edge.

## Why it is cheaper than authoring a new field

`depends_on` is not a rename of the citation list — it is a different, narrower, already-populated one: 339 of 452 decisions, all 13 agents, all 21 processes, 53 of 95 principles. On decisions it averages **1.7** edges against the citation list's **6.6**, and a person chose those 1.7.

## The order is part of the decision

ADR-0464 D6, and D3 refuses the reverse explicitly — deleting first is the one order that cannot be checked, because the fallback would be under repair at the moment it became the only route.

1. **Repair the ranked population** — `library search "bypass gate"` does not return `never-bypass-the-gate` in its top five; `--kind guardrail` ranks it first. BM25 is sound, the population is wrong: 1,667 of 2,529 rows (66%) are `increment`+`friction` ranked as knowledge. Same fault in `related --unlinked`. Plus stemming.
2. **Render `depends_on` from the field** — today it survives only as authored prose. The one thing this decision builds; follows ADR-0161's derived-`next:` precedent.
3. **Backfill the 53 definitions** — the only tier with zero edges, and it holds the orientation reads.
4. **Delete** — blocked on all three.

Four increments parked on `linked-session-context-arc`; a session is cut for step 1.

## Decision-log work (live store, ADR-0403 — not in this diff)

author: hyperpolymath
body:
**Measured 2026-08-27: this gate caught 0 of 6 invisible-character test cases.** It has never detected an NBSP, zero-width space, BOM, soft hyphen, bidi override or word joiner.

## Root cause

The pattern used UTF-8 **byte sequences** (`\xc2\xa0`) while `grep -P` matches **characters**. Bytes `c2 a0` are *one* character U+00A0; `\xc2\xa0` asks for *two*, U+00C2 then U+00A0 — never present.

```
grep -P '\xc2\xa0'  ->  miss
grep -P '\x{a0}'    ->  MATCH
```

Only `\x00` worked, being single-byte in both readings. The gate ran, passed, and could not see what it exists to see.

## Fixed

- **codepoint escapes** in place of byte sequences
- **C0 controls** `\x01-\x08,\x0B,\x0C,\x0E-\x1F` added (TAB/LF/CR excluded)
- **`grep -a`** — without it grep skips any NUL-bearing file as binary

The C0 range matters: a stray **backspace byte** made a workflow unparseable in `developer-ecosystem`, so it never ran — and this linter called it clean.

Canonical fix: hyperpolymath/empty-linter#70. **1 file(s)** here.

**Verified:** YAML re-parsed, and the corrected pattern was confirmed to catch a real NBSP before the change was kept.

author: copilot
body:
After a successful Shopify OAuth flow, clicking "Load Shopify Products" failed with `"Shopify session token is required."` because the universal products endpoint blocked requests that lacked an Authorization/session-token header, and the Shopify-specific route had no GET handler at all.

## Changes

### `app/api/shopify/products/route.ts`
- Added `GET` handler that authenticates via `virello_shopify_access_token` / `virello_shopify_shop` HttpOnly cookies (set by the OAuth callback)
- Queries `https://${shop}/admin/api/2026-07/graphql.json` with `X-Shopify-Access-Token`
- Returns `{ success: true, products: [...] }` with `id`, `title`, `description`, `productType`, `tags`, `status`, `vendor`, `price`, `featuredImage`, `images` per product
- Improved HTTP-error extraction to check `data.error` / `data.message` before `data.errors[0].message` (HTTP errors and GraphQL errors have different shapes)

### `app/api/stores/products/route.ts` — Shopify branch only
- Checks `virello_shopify_access_token` + `virello_shopify_shop` cookies alongside the existing header checks before deciding to block
- Removed the hard 401 gate that fired whenever no `Authorization` or `x-shopify-session-token` header was present
- Forwards the `cookie` header to the internal `/api/shopify/products` fetch so the new GET handler can read the HttpOnly cookies server-side
- All other platforms (WooCommerce, BigCommerce, Wix) are untouched

```
GET /api/stores/products?platform=shopify
  → checks cookies first
  → forwards to GET /api/shopify/products (new handler)
    → reads virello_shopify_access_token / virello_shopify_shop
    → queries Shopify Admin GraphQL
    → returns { success: true, products: [...] }
```

author: kamyar-finlex
body:
Closes #461. Phase 0 of epic #458, the counterpart to ADR 0012 (#460) — which
ends by saying the gate on a plan a human has not read is a separate decision,
recorded here.

## What it records

- **Existing-repo projects only.** Greenfield plans and builds in one go,
  unchanged. A generated repository has no value to protect and is surveyed by
  construction; the gate is a price, and charging it there costs the wait `--new`
  exists to remove. The mirror drift ("let the gate grow into an approval
  workflow") is refused in its own section.
- **The gate is `--plan-only`, not a new state.** No run mode, no ledger state,
  nothing derived differently. Invariant 4 untouched: no label, and no fourth
  thing `derived.py` recomputes. The rejected alternative is a real `proposed`
  state — refused because it puts the pause inside the loop and gets the
  direction of authority backwards. The cheapest correct implementation of "the
  swarm has not started" is that the swarm is not running.
- **Where waiting is stored, and why it is legitimate.** `setup` on
  `console_projects`' `projects` table, through the `_ADDED_COLUMNS` path that
  exists for this. Legitimate on a test rather than an assurance: nothing under
  `src/swarm/orchestrator/` imports `console_projects` (the dependency runs the
  other way, `console_board` → `authority`), and GitHub has no field this could
  drift from. ADR 0002's line one level out. A second column beside `state` and
  not a value in it, because `state` is standing dispatch intent and the two
  compose.
- **The plan is editable between the gate and the Run, and needs no code**, since
  the ledger is re-read on every attach. With the corollary said out loud: there
  is **no approval record**, so what runs is whatever the issues say when Run is
  pressed.
- **What the gate does not become**, and **the cost unhedged** — an adopted
  project cannot be run unattended end to end. That is the purchase, not a
  rounded corner.

`CLAUDE.md`'s ADR table gains the 0013 row `tests/test_docs.py` requires.

## Verified against the tree, not from the plan doc

`--plan-only` at `cli.py:194`/`cli.py:793` (readiness, then `return 0` before
`_loop`); `Attachment.mode` at `run.py:267`; `build_argv` never emits
`--plan-only`, so the flag is terminal-only today; `_ADDED_COLUMNS`,
`PROJECT_STATES` and `HELD_STATES` in `console_projects.py`; and `grep -rn
console src/swarm/orchestrator/` finds one comment and no import.

## Verify

`pytest -q -s tests/test_docs.py` — 5 passed. Full suite 3751 passed, `mypy`
clean (81 files). Docs-only change.

Closes #351.

`test_a_failing_stats_read_does_not_kill_the_heartbeat` asserts on **iterations** ("at least two passes") while waiting on **wall-clock time** (`sleep(0.1)` at a 0.02 s interval). On a loaded machine one pass can consume the window, and the test then reports that a failed stats read killed the heartbeat — which is not what happened, and reads exactly like a real regression in the heartbeat's error handling.

Every wait in the file now waits for the thing itself:

| test | waits for |
|---|---|
| writes the queue depth | the first heartbeat record |
| survives the JSON allowlist | the first heartbeat record |
| repeats on its interval | three records |
| a failing stats read | a second stats read |
| slots inside a job | a record written while the slot is busy |
| a slow heartbeat vs the claim loop | the loop draining all three jobs |

The 5 s timeout inside `_wait_until` is the **failsafe, not the measurement**, and it names what never happened:

```
AssertionError: timed out after 5.0s waiting for a second stats read after the first one raised
```

## One deviation from the issue

The issue suggested keeping `for_seconds` available "for the tests that genuinely want a duration". There are none — all four callers passed one to buy a number of passes — so it is gone rather than kept. A wall-clock parameter left in place is the door this flake walks back in through.

The last two rows of the table are the other two tests the issue flagged as "worth reading at the same time"; both had the same shape (`sleep(0.05)` / `sleep(0.1)` then assert). In the slow-heartbeat test the assertion and the wait are now the same condition, which is the point: a genuinely blocked claim loop hits the 5 s failsafe instead of being judged against a 0.1 s guess.

## Verification

Mutation-tested against the property rather than the clock:

| mutant | result |
|---|---|
| heartbeat returns out of the loop after a failed pass | fails on the timeout, with the message above |
| failure swallowed without logging | fails on the `WARNING` assertion |

Full suite: 2797 passed. `scripts/preflight.sh`: all gates passed. The heartbeat tests now take 0.15 s instead of 0.96 s, since they stop the moment the property holds.

author: gerrrt
body:
## ⚠️ Draft — blocked on a Core release

This caller pins `@v5`, and **`v5` does not yet contain [dotfiles-core#754](https://github.com/dotgibson/dotfiles-core/pull/754)**:

```
v5      -> 9312d81      bootstrap_postcheck present in v5's bootstrap-test.yml: 0
main    -> b8af66b      (the hook)
```

Merging before the tag moves fails the leg with an unknown-input error. Ready the moment `v5` includes #754.

## What and why

One line of YAML, and it is the line that finishes #133.

The sweep asserts two things after a genuinely unstubbed `./bootstrap.sh`: that it returned 0, and that the wiring survived. Neither can see whether the packages arrived. So the first Gentoo leg ever to run to completion emerged 131 packages over 75 minutes, printed a ledger naming `dev-util/shellcheck` and `ouch` as **not** installed, and reported success ([dotfiles-core#742](https://github.com/dotgibson/dotfiles-core/issues/742)).

#133 fixed those two tools and added `scripts/assert-provisioned.sh` as the check that would have caught them. It could not be wired in from here — `real-bootstrap.yml`'s `docker run` lives in dotfiles-core and ran a bare `./bootstrap.sh` for every leg. That gap was [dotfiles-core#750](https://github.com/dotgibson/dotfiles-core/issues/750), now closed by #754, which added a `bootstrap_postcheck` input read statically out of this caller — the same way `image`, `prep` and `bootstrap_timeout` already are.

**So: declare it.** Until this lands, the hook exists, the script exists, and this leg still asserts nothing about packages — an advisory gate that never runs, which reads as coverage. That is the failure mode both repos keep warning about in comments, and leaving the switch off after building the mechanism would be a fresh instance of it.

## Not `--strict`

`bootstrap.sh`'s `usage()` already records this decision at length. The end-of-run ledger deliberately mixes a **genuine provisioning gap** with an **infrastructure blip** (a rate-limited `mise.run`, a GURU sync hiccup, a failed `tpm` clone), and `--strict` cannot tell them apart — it would red an advisory lane over somebody else's outage. `assert-provisioned.sh` *can* tell them apart, because it knows what `install/packages.txt` promises: hard-fail on those atoms, warn on the overlay/cargo/go/opt-in tools that no run promises.

## Verification

Verified against Core's actual consumer rather than assumed. `scripts/fleet-bootstrap-matrix.py` run over the local fleet:

```
8 legs derived
     —     dotfiles-Alpine      timeout=45   postcheck=''
     —     dotfiles-Arch        timeout=45   postcheck=''
     —     dotfiles-Debian      timeout=45   postcheck=''   (x2)
     —     dotfiles-Fedora      timeout=45   postcheck=''
  ASSERTS  dotfiles-Gentoo      timeout=240  postcheck='./scripts/assert-provisioned.sh'
     —     dotfiles-Offense     timeout=45   postcheck=''
     —     dotfiles-openSUSE    timeout=45   postcheck=''
```

- The script exits 0 run directly **and** under `sh -c` from the repo root, which is how the sweep invokes it.
- It is tracked `100755`, so the `./` form resolves. (If that ever changes, switch the value to `sh scripts/assert-provisioned.sh`.)
- `make lint` passes.

Gentoo is deliberately the only leg asserting: #754's own docs name this script as the reference shape, and every other repo needs one written against its own package list.

## Blast radius

`real-bootstrap.yml` is weekly and advisory — a red leg files an issue and blocks nothing. Turning this on **cannot** red a PR.

## Layer check

- [x] Genuinely Gentoo-specific (it declares this repo's own postcheck for this repo's own leg).
- [x] Does not hand-edit `core/`.

Refs #133, dotgibson/dotfiles-core#750, dotgibson/dotfiles-core#754.

author: mgriffioen
body:
Replace the simple spinning animation with a full physics simulation where dice travel across the tray, bounce off walls and each other, and gradually settle into their reading positions.

## Summary
This change transforms dice rolling from a visual-only animation into a physically-simulated throw. Dice now have velocity, gravity, collision detection, and friction. The crank feeds energy into the system as discrete kicks rather than continuous spin, and dice settle naturally based on physics rather than on a timer.

## Key Changes

- **Physics simulation**: Added gravity, air/ground drag, bounce coefficients, and speed caps. Dice fall under gravity, bounce when hitting the table, and lose speed to friction.

- **Velocity and collision system**: Each die tracks horizontal velocity (vx, vy), vertical position (z), and vertical velocity (zv). Dice collide with tray walls and with each other, bouncing elastically and being pushed apart when overlapping.

- **Steering kicks**: The crank no longer spins dice in place. Instead, each frame of crank input applies a kick that steers the velocity (not just adds speed) to prevent dice from running on rails between walls.

- **Settling behavior**: When dice stop moving, they glide back to their home positions over a distance-based duration, then squash briefly as they land. Dice rotate to the nearest symmetry-aligned angle rather than unwinding completely.

- **Collision detection and response**: `Dice.collide()` handles die-to-die collisions with proper elastic bounce physics and die-to-wall bounces. Returns impact count for audio feedback tied to actual collisions rather than a timer.

- **Constants tuning**: Added comprehensive physics constants (gravity, bounce coefficients, drag values, speed/spin caps, etc.) all tuned by eye for visual believability rather than physical accuracy.

## Notable Implementation Details

- Shoves steer the velocity vector rather than just adding speed along the current heading, preventing dice from bouncing in straight lines between walls
- Dice seat themselves on the nearest rotation angle that preserves their silhouette (e.g., 90° for squares), avoiding long spin-downs
- The gather-back animation is distance-based so dice near their slots nudge in quickly while distant ones take longer
- Collision impacts drive sound effects, so audio feedback is synchronized with visible collisions
- Settled dice are excluded from collision detection to prevent interference with the gathering animation
- Layout system now manages both the reading grid and the tray boundaries that constrain dice movement

## Testing
Added comprehensive tests verifying:
- Dice stay within tray boundaries during throws
- Dice actually travel (not just jiggle in place)
- Different dice follow different paths (not locked in formation)
- Dice return to home positions and settle properly
- Crank speed is capped to prevent dice flying off screen
- Reset properly clears all physics state

author: v-positronic
body:
`Scores` is what a finished submission publishes and what a board row carries. It held five
fields: `primary`, `success_rate`, `per_task`, `episodes` and `unscored`. It now holds
`primary` and nothing else.

## Why each field leaves

A board ranks on `primary` alone (`rankings.py`, `PRIMARY_SCORE_KEY`). Every board is public,
so each field here is republished for every competitor's best submission.

- **`per_task`** decides nothing the platform does. It tells every competitor which task of the
  eval is the hard one, which is an overfitting hint. The submitter can already build it from
  the redacted episodes they receive: each `meta.json` carries the task and `eval.success`. So
  the field adds nothing for its owner and adds a hint for everybody else.
- **`success_rate`** is `primary` under a second name. The scorer computes one rate and assigns
  it to both fields. One fact under two names, with two owners, is the shape that caused the
  defect this branch started from.
- **`episodes`** and **`unscored`** are inputs to the ranking decision, not outputs for
  publication. One eval is live at a time, it pins a fixed trial list, and the platform fails a
  run that does not score every trial. So both values are the same on every row a board ranks.

## What keeps the full record

`platform_runner.scorer.Scores` is unchanged. It still writes `primary`, `success_rate`,
`per_task`, `episodes` and `unscored` into the participant's own `scores.json`, and the
platform reads the completeness facts from that blob. The two models now differ on purpose:
the scorer records, the client publishes a subset. The platform repository pins that as a
subset test, so a field added here that the scorer does not write fails a build.

## Breaking change

This narrows a published response shape. A consumer that reads `scores.success_rate`,
`scores.per_task`, `scores.episodes` or `scores.unscored` breaks. The client goes 0.2.0 to
0.3.0 and the root pin follows it.

Both example scripts read `view.scores.episodes` and now print `primary` alone:
`positronic/cli/examples/walkthrough.py` and
`positronic/cli/examples/nebius_competition/submit_sample.py`.

## The second commit

`848a7032` is an unrelated fix that this branch already carried: the raise-path test doubles in
`positronic/policy/tests/test_harness.py` now match the base class signatures.

## Checks

`pytest client` — 239 passed.

author: antonioventilii
body:
# Motivation

The Solana WalletConnect review shows a message's balance changes but never what the message actually does, and the raw instruction list is not a substitute: a four-hop swap carries around thirty instructions, of which a dozen concern the signer at all and the rest is account plumbing and transfers between accounts that are not theirs. Showing that list unfiltered would be honest and useless.

This is the derivation that turns those instructions into something a person can read. It ships on its own, without UI, because it is the part with the judgement in it and it deserves review on its own terms.

# Changes

- `mapSolInstructionViews` reduces a transaction's instructions, both its own and the ones a simulation reports it would make inside them, to the effects that change what the signer holds or controls. Everything else is dropped.
- Three rules carry most of the readability:
  - An associated token account creation collapses from four instructions into one row carrying the rent it costs the user. On the common case of sending an SPL token to someone who has never held it, the account is the recipient's but the rent is the sender's, and it is the rent that makes it worth showing.
  - A System transfer into a wrapped SOL account is wrapping, and closing that account is unwrapping. Neither has an instruction that says so, so both are recognised by their destination.
  - Consecutive legs of one routed swap hang under the route that produced them, instead of reading as several unrelated transfers. A route with a single leg is not a route.
- The derivation learns which accounts belong to the user rather than trusting the caller alone. A wrapped SOL account is opened and closed inside the same message, so it appears in no balance and no caller can name it; without this, the wrapping, every leg paid from it and the unwrapping all read as somebody else's.
- The result is free of copy and keeps amounts as `bigint` base units. The derivation says what happened, the component says it in the user's language.
- The input is the `jsonParsed` shape, which is what `simulateTransaction` reports for inner instructions and what `getTransaction` reports throughout, so one derivation serves both the review and the activity views.

Nothing renders it yet. Wiring it into the modal is the next change, kept separate so this one can be judged on whether its output is right.

Known limitation, stated rather than hidden: top-level instructions of an unsigned message reach the review as `@solana/kit` objects rather than as `jsonParsed`, so for a message that has not been simulated the top-level half is not yet classified. Every WalletConnect request is simulated, and the simulation supplies the parsed form, so the review is covered; the adapter for the kit representation belongs with the change that needs it.

# Tests

- 20 cases in `sol-instruction-view.utils.spec.ts`, most of them over fixtures captured from mainnet with `getTransaction/jsonParsed` and trimmed to the fields the derivation reads: a DFlow swap, an Orca swap split across three pools, an SPL send that opens the recipient an account, and a transaction the user has no part in.
- The DFlow fixture pins the reduction itself: 24 instructions in, fewer than half that many rows out.
- The Orca fixture pins that three pools stay three routes, since merging them would claim a single route the transaction never took.
- The third-party fixture yields nothing at all, which is the case a filter is most likely to get wrong.
- Unit cases cover the authority rule for deciding whose transfer it is, marking a counterparty that is one of the user's own accounts, approvals and authority handovers, and accounts opened mid-transaction for the user and for a stranger.
- `npm run check` and `npm run check:tests` are both clean at 0 errors and 0 warnings, lint passes with `--max-warnings 0`, and the full Solana suite passes 1800 tests.

author: ajmalpshaik
body:
Found by the daily status check (2026-08-27, container run).

## What was wrong

`CLAUDE.md` described `tools/verify-consistency.ps1` as trailing the Node checker because **"check 9 has not been ported to PowerShell."**

Check 9 *was* ported — 2026-08-22, PR #31 — and the `.ps1` has printed nine numbered section headers ever since. So the sentence was already wrong that day. It then sat still while the Node checker grew checks 10, 11, 12 and 13, which means by today it named **the one gap that had closed and none of the four that had opened** — understating the real gap by a factor of four.

A session reading that line would think porting check 9 was still owed work (it isn't) and that the PowerShell fallback was one check behind (it's four).

## How it was verified

Not from prose — from the two files' own numbered section headers:

| | Sections printed |
|---|---|
| `tools/verify-consistency.ps1` | 1–9 |
| `tools/verify-consistency.mjs` | 1–13 |

## What changed

- **`CLAUDE.md`** — corrected to "thirteen against nine, checks 10–13 never ported", with the wrong version quoted in place so nobody re-derives it, and a pointer to grep the headers rather than trust any prose count.
- **`knowledge/brain-log.md`** — dated entry recording the finding and the blind spot behind it.

## Why no check caught it

Check 9 verifies *live counts* — fragments, skills, native tools. A claim about how many checks a sibling script has is not one of those. Every check in the suite reads content for one specific claim; the count of the checks themselves is the one thing none of them asks about.

The cheap habit that does catch it, now written down: both files print their own numbered section headers, so `grep` them and compare.

author: ruhex
body:
Closes #263

## The problem, verified

Every collaborator on the outbound path was a nullable-optional constructor argument threaded `BgpServer` → `BgpSession` → `RouteAssembler`, and each layer supplied a silent fallback for the one below:

```csharp
_prefixAggregator = prefixAggregator ?? new ExactUnionPrefixAggregator();
_communityResolver = communityResolver ?? NullCommunityResolver.Instance;
if (_peerStore is not null && _prefixService is not null && _appConfig is not null) { ... }
```

Dropping one DI registration produced no error at all. Sessions still established; peers just received the shared route table's **seeded** routes instead of the prefixes their operator selected in the UI. That is a wrong route set, not a disabled feature, and #307 could only make it log a warning after the fact.

Worth noting what the old wiring already got wrong without anyone failing: `Program.cs` never passed `prefixAggregator`, so the `?? new ExactUnionPrefixAggregator()` fallback *was* production. The summarization policy for everything on the wire was reachable only as a default argument.

## What changed

**`RouteAssembler`** requires `IPrefixService`, `IPeerStore` and `AppConfig`. The tri-null guard and the shared-table branch under it are gone, along with the `_routeTable` field only that branch used and the null-forgiveness dance around `_appConfig`. It no longer carries a per-session peer label (that is a method parameter now), so it is a plain singleton.

**`SharedTableRouteAssembler`** is the degraded behavior, kept as a named `IRouteAssembler` a caller chooses on purpose. It preserves #289's owner check — the shared table also holds every NLRI peers announced inbound, and serving those to a different peer leaks one tenant's routes — and announces its activation **once** instead of on every refresh.

**`BgpSessionFactory`** owns the session composition. The accept loop needed none of those dependencies for itself, it only forwarded them: `BgpServer` loses five constructor parameters and four fields, and `new BgpSession(…12 args…)` becomes `_sessionFactory.Create(connection, peerConfig)`. The peer-identity callback that `Program.cs` hand-wired as `(ip, asn) => store.UpsertPeer(ip, asn)` is now just `IPeerStore.UpsertPeer` inside the factory.

`BgpSession` drops `_prefixService`, `_appConfig` and `_communityResolver` entirely — it held all three only to hand them to the assembler it built.

**`ManagementApi`** (`IPrefixService`, `IPrefixSourceService`, `ISessionManager`) and **`PrefixService`** (`RipeStatProvider`, `HttpPrefixProvider`) are required too. A null session manager meant a peer edited in the UI was persisted and never pushed to its live session — six `if (_sessionManager is not null)` guards around exactly that. A null http provider meant `GetUserSourcePrefixesAsync` returned `[]`, so a user's URL source silently produced nothing.

**`Program.cs`** registers `IPeerStore`, `IPrefixAggregator`, `IRouteAssembler`, `IBgpSessionFactory` and `TimeProvider` explicitly, and builds the container with `ValidateOnBuild`.

## Acceptance, checked against a running host

> Removing any single DI registration fails loudly at startup

Deleted the `IPrefixAggregator` registration and started the app:

```
Unhandled exception. System.AggregateException: Some services are not able to be constructed
(Error while validating the service descriptor 'ServiceType: BGPLite.Server.IBgpSessionFactory
 Lifetime: Singleton ImplementationType: BGPLite.Server.BgpSessionFactory':
 Unable to resolve service for type 'BGPLite.Routing.IPrefixAggregator'
 while attempting to activate 'BGPLite.Server.BgpSessionFactory'.)
```

Restored, the host starts clean through to `Application started`.

`ValidateScopes` is deliberately **off**, and this is not a judgment call I made blind — with it on the host dies before reaching any of this project's code:

```
Cannot resolve scoped service
'IEnumerable<IDbContextOptionsConfiguration<BgpDbContext>>' from root provider.
   at EntityFrameworkServiceCollectionExtensions.CreateDbContextOptions<TContext>
```

That is EF's own `AddDbContext` plumbing resolving a scoped option-configuration service while constructing the singleton `DbContextOptions`. The app's own singletons already take `IDbContextFactory` rather than a scoped `DbContext`.

> `BgpServer`/`BgpSession` no longer `new` up their collaborators

`BgpServer` still constructs `new SocketBgpConnection(socket)` — that is the transport adapter for the socket it just accepted, has no configuration of its own, and passing a `Socket` into the factory would only couple the seam to `System.Net.Sockets`.

## Tests

`CompositionContractTests` — 17 new tests, 710 total.

- `ProductionDependency_IsRequired` — a `[Theory]` naming each dependency #263 listed (`RouteAssembler.peerStore`, `ManagementApi.sessionManager`, `PrefixService.httpProvider`, …) and asserting it has no default value and `NullabilityState.NotNull`. Re-adding `= null` to any of them fails here rather than silently at the next route send.
- `BgpServer_DoesNotCarryTheSessionsDependencies` — the second acceptance bullet, as a compile-independent assertion.
- Three `SharedTableRouteAssembler` behavior tests: serves the seed but not a route owned by another peer, applies the outgoing filter, warns exactly once across three calls.
- Two factory tests that establish a real session over the `IBgpConnection` seam and assert it asked the **injected** assembler, and that OPEN upserted the peer.

Verified they fail without the fix. Neutering four things independently — `EnumerateUnowned()` → `Enumerate()`, the once-guard, the factory's `routeAssembler:` argument, and `IPeerStore` back to nullable — produces exactly 4 failures out of 17.

`ScriptedConnection` moved out of `BgpSessionRouteOwnershipTests` into a shared fixture so the factory tests can establish a session without a real socket; `ConfigHotReloadTests` gained three inert stubs now that `ManagementApi` cannot be half-wired.

## Not in scope

`PrefixService`'s optional `ILogger`/`TimeSpan?`/`TimeProvider?` parameters are left alone — those are test seams and tuning knobs, not services whose absence changes what a peer receives.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Added per-peer route assembly for more targeted outbound route announcements.
  * Added a fallback mode that shares only seeded routes while preventing peer-owned routes from being exposed to others.
  * Improved session creation and peer registration consistency.

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Outgoing routes now consistently honor peer-specific filtering.
  * Application startup now detects incomplete configuration immediately instead of failing later.

* **Tests**
  * Added coverage for route isolation, filtering, session setup, and startup composition.

author: natashasusanto10-glitch
body:
## Kenapa sekarang

Project Google baru **tidak bisa** memakai Places API lama. Dibuktikan di produksi setelah kunci baru dipasang — pesan Google berubah:

```
sebelumnya : "You must enable Billing on the Google Cloud Project"
sekarang   : "You're calling a legacy API, which is not enabled for your project."
```

Billing sudah beres; yang tersisa versi API-nya. Google berhenti membuka Places API lama untuk pelanggan baru sejak Maret 2025.

## Bentuk keluaran sengaja TIDAK diubah

Klien Flutter yang sudah terpasang di HP pelanggan membaca `predictions[]` dan `result` bergaya lama. Mengubah kontrak akan merusak **semua versi lama** sampai semua orang memperbarui — bisa berminggu-minggu.

Rute tetap mengeluarkan bentuk lama; hanya jalur ke Google yang pindah. **Nol perubahan di sisi Flutter**, dan begitu deploy, autocomplete pulih di semua versi app tanpa rilis apa pun.

`lib/places/places-new-adapter.ts` menerjemahkan:

| lama (dikeluarkan rute) | baru (dari Google) |
|---|---|
| `predictions[]` | `suggestions[].placePrediction` |
| `place_id` | `placeId` (detail: `id`) |
| `description` | `text.text` |
| `structured_formatting` | `structuredFormat` (`.mainText`/`.secondaryText.text`) |
| `address_components` | `addressComponents` (`.longText`/`.shortText`) |
| `geometry.location{lat,lng}` | `location{latitude,longitude}` |

## Perbedaan protokol yang ditangani

- Host `places.googleapis.com`, bukan `maps.googleapis.com`
- Kunci lewat header `X-Goog-Api-Key`, **bukan** query param `key`
- **`X-Goog-FieldMask` wajib** — tanpa itu Google menolak 400
- HTTP status sungguhan, bukan selalu-200-dengan-field-`status`
- `autocomplete` jadi POST+JSON; `details` jadi `GET /v1/places/{id}`
- `location`+`radius` lama → `locationBias.circle` (radius di-clamp 50 km)

FieldMask sengaja minimal — **tiap field tambahan menaikkan tier penagihan Google**. Dijaga test supaya tidak diam-diam melebar.

`queryPrediction` dari API baru dibuang: tidak punya `placeId`, jadi kalau diloloskan pengguna menekannya dan tidak terjadi apa-apa.

`reverse-geocode` **tidak diubah** — Geocoding API terpisah, tidak ikut deprecated, tetap memakai `interpretGoogleStatus` dari #318.

## Verifikasi

`tsc` 0 error · `eslint` bersih · **706 test lolos** (dari 699)

7 test menguji adapter — termasuk asersi terpenting: hasil adaptasi **lolos `mapGoogleAddress` yang tidak diubah sama sekali**.

**Belum diverifikasi ke Google sungguhan:** kunci hanya ada di Vercel, tidak di mesin lokal. Bentuk request/response mengikuti dokumentasi; pembuktian lewat endpoint produksi setelah deploy.

author: ivomsantiago
body:
Continuação do #43, que já foi mergeado com os dois primeiros commits (arranque sob demanda + engine Go). Estes cinco são o trabalho que veio depois, rebaseado sobre o `Master` atual.

Todos medidos antes e depois, e nenhum promete mais do que entrega.

---

## 1. `perf:` medir as tags que podem vencer — **o maior ganho daqui**

`recommend node` descobria até 100 tags e media **todas** para mostrar cinco. Dois a quatro minutos de relógio, com 95 scans existindo só para serem descartados no ranqueamento. Era, de longe, o maior custo do projeto — maior que tudo que o arranque sob demanda e a engine Go economizaram somados.

Havia dois jeitos de cortar, e só um é honesto aqui: baixar `max_tags` faria uma tag boa fora da janela simplesmente não existir, sem nada dizendo que ela existiu. O outro — escolher quem medir **e declarar quem ficou de fora** — é o que `domain/value_objects/scan_plan.py` faz.

**Uma tag adiada não é uma tag pior. É uma tag não medida**, e o resultado a carrega com o motivo. `deferred` é deliberadamente separado de `unverified`: ali estão medições que falharam, aqui medições que nunca foram tentadas — e a segunda é uma escolha desta ferramenta, não um acidente.

A seleção é uma função pura (sem rede, disco ou scanner) e deliberadamente conservadora:

- majors diferentes nunca competem: `20-alpine` segue sendo resposta legítima ao lado de `22-alpine`, e frequentemente é a certa (LTS);
- variantes diferentes nunca competem (`alpine3.20` ≠ `alpine3.21`);
- um apelido móvel (`22-alpine`) nunca é colapsado num patch fixo (`22.14-alpine`): são perguntas diferentes;
- uma tag sem versão numérica (`latest`, `lts-alpine`) nunca perde para uma versão;
- havendo folga no orçamento, **nada** é cortado.

Medido em 44 tags típicas de `node`: **44 descobertas, 6 medidas**, 38 adiadas — todas por "existe uma tag mais nova da mesma linha". As duas majors, o `latest` e o `lts-alpine` sobreviveram. Nenhuma resposta distinta se perdeu.

Novo: `scan_budget` (padrão 25, `0` mede todas) e a flag `--budget/-b`. O help do `--limit` passou a dizer "discover" em vez de "scan", que é o que ele sempre governou. O bloco `Not Measured` diz quantas, por quê e como desfazer; o `--format json` carrega todas.

**22 testes sobre a função pura**, incluindo a invariante de que toda tag descoberta ou foi medida ou foi nomeada — e um que **recusa as palavras** "vulnerable", "unsafe", "worse", "risk" e "cve" no texto de um adiamento.

## 2–3. `i18n:` a saída ao usuário é inteiramente inglesa

As **278 strings** em português que sobravam foram traduzidas, e com elas os cinco comandos que ainda respondiam em português (`build`, `base-image`, `provenance`, `verify`, `registry-audit`) saíram da lista de isenção.

Convenção mantida: comentário e docstring de *implementação* seguem em português. As docstrings dos comandos não são implementação — elas **são** o `--help`.

O que mudou de verdade no guard, e é a parte que importa: `_NOT_YET_TRANSLATED` estava vazio de efeito, porque **não havia teste** exercendo aqueles cinco comandos. A isenção era documental — o guard nunca os tinha visto. Agora a lista de comandos conferidos sai de `app.COMMANDS` em vez de ser escrita à mão (era por ser escrita à mão que cinco ficaram de fora), há exercícios de saída real dos cinco, e um teste exige que a lista de isenção continue vazia.

As asserções dos testes foram movidas junto, nunca afrouxadas: cada uma continua exigindo a mesma frase, agora na língua em que ela é publicada.

## 4. `feat(doctor):` assinatura cosign na instalação

O gancho `verify_blob` existia desde o início e nada o implementava. Agora a assinatura do `checksums.txt` é conferida quando o projeto publica uma e o cosign está instalado.

A cadeia tem dois elos e nenhum a mais: a assinatura prova que o `checksums.txt` é o que o projeto publicou, e o SHA-256 do arquivo contra a linha correspondente prova que o arquivo é o que aquele `checksums.txt` descreve.

**A ordem inverteu, e isso é correção, não estilo:** a assinatura vem **antes** do digest. Conferir o digest primeiro compararia o arquivo com uma lista que ainda não se sabe de quem é — e uma lista adulterada aprova um arquivo adulterado. Há teste com checksum propositalmente errado que falha *por assinatura*, exatamente para travar a ordem.

A identidade é restrita ao repositório do próprio projeto (`^https://github\.com/anchore/grype/`) e o emissor ao OIDC do GitHub Actions. Sem isso o cosign responde "alguém assinou", que é outra pergunta.

Tristate, como no resto do projeto: `False` é a única afirmação e aborta a instalação; `None` cobre três situações que **não** são "não assinado" — projeto sem assinatura conhecida, cosign ausente, cosign inconclusivo — e nenhuma impede a instalação.

`signs_checksums` do Trivy fica `False` e o comentário diz por quê: o release dele não pôde ser inspecionado deste ambiente, e afirmar que ele assina (ou que não assina) seria inventar.

## 5. `feat(engine):` Grype na engine, e as decisões que ficaram abertas

Os dois scanners entram pelo mesmo lugar; o que difere fica inteiramente no Go — argv próprio, parser próprio, e o fato de que o Grype **não** é serializado por falta de diretórios de cache. O lock BoltDB é do Trivy; aplicar o remédio a quem não tem a doença transformaria `--workers 8` em 1 sem dizer nada.

Uma coisa que a fronteira nova quase deixou passar: `_scan_env()` do Grype devolve `os.environ.copy()` inteiro, e mandá-lo pela fronteira escreveria `DOCKERHUB_TOKEN` e companhia dentro de um documento JSON. Só o par do Grype atravessa, e há teste.

`ecosystem_insights` segue o alvo do plano (a imagem que o usuário nomeia), não a raiz do documento — a alternativa reproduzia o P1 do Remediation Plan: conselho sobre Debian ao lado de uma recomendação Alpine. Agora com teste, que também exige o campo `ecosystem_insights.for`.

---

## Gate

| verificação | resultado |
|---|---|
| pytest | **3317 passam**, 3 skip |
| cobertura Python | 90,65% (mínimo 80%) |
| `go test -race` | verde; 93,2% em `internal/scan` |
| ruff / ruff format / mypy --strict / bandit | limpos |

Rodado depois do rebase sobre o `Master` já

author: mrrodbh
mattadurham
body:
## Goal

A visitor who clicks into this repo should be able to read its history the way they would any well-run project: a changelog at the root, and a write-up behind every change. Until today the repo had neither - 219 merges since the public flip with no pull requests and no changelog.

## What shipped

- **`CHANGELOG.md`** in [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/) style: date sections (Vira ships continuously from `main`, so merge dates stand in for release versions), newest first, Added / Changed / Fixed / Removed groupings. 219 entries across 22 merge dates, back to the public-flip root.
- Entries since 2026-08-27 link their **pull request**; every earlier entry links its `--no-ff` merge commit, and each of those commits now carries a **backfilled PR-style write-up as a commit comment** - the record a PR would have held, posted retroactively.

## Design decisions

- Backfilled bodies and changelog lines are composed from **already-public material only** - the branches' own commit messages and diffstats. Nothing private was read, and every generated file passed the full-strength PII scan (generic patterns plus instance identifiers) before posting.
- No retroactive "Merged" badges are faked: GitHub cannot open a PR for an already-merged branch, and a closed-unmerged stand-in would misread as rejected work. The commit comment is the honest equivalent.
- Category classification is keyword-based from commit subjects; ambiguous entries land in Changed, the honest default.

## Verification

- Full-strength PII scan: 0 hits across all 219 comment bodies and the changelog, run on two regex engines.
- Every link target verified to exist by construction (shas resolved from `git log` on main).

author: arthurrump
body:
This PR aims to improve the handling of citations in LaTeX, both for standard natbib and for biblatex. I based the testcases on the list provided in #858, so it now correctly handles narrative and parenthetical citations, with partial citations where supported and prefixes and suffixes for all configurations.

I included a few cases that are representable in the AST, but for which I could not find a valid syntax. This includes multiple narrative citations (`\citet{jon90, jam91}`), partial author citations and partial year citations in narrative form. These cases are marked with `# myst: ??` in the testcases.

I decided to move all logic to the `cite` handler and let `citeGroup` be a simple pass-through to all children, to avoid a duplication of logic in both. The downside is that the `cite` node changes behaviour not only based on its parent (which was already the case), but also based on its siblings. Overall I think I prefer this over extracting some of the logic and then using that in both the `citeGroup` and in `cite`. An alternative could be to enforce that `cite`s are always in a `citeGroup`, but given that most of the relevant properties are on `cite`, I don't think that option makes much sense.

author: dean-rough
body:
## Summary

`apps/control/api/index.ts` — the real deployed control-plane entrypoint — never wired the config added by [SHO-84](/SHO/issues/SHO-84) (ADR 0004) and [SHO-96](/SHO/issues/SHO-96) (ADR 0005). Both ADRs flag this explicitly: "needs production wiring... before this is reachable outside tests." This PR wires it, with the same off-by-default safety posture already used for `previewDeletionAuthorized`.

- `MADETHIS_PROMOTION_ADAPTER_TOKEN` → `madeThisPromotionAdapterToken` (scoped bearer for `/v1/promotions/*`, distinct from the outreach token)
- promotion store (Postgres-backed, via the existing `createProductionPromotionStore`)
- `LIVE_PROMOTION_AUTHORIZED` → `livePromotionAuthorized` — **defaults `false`**. Not flipped to `true` anywhere in this PR; that stays a separate, later both-leads decision per COLLABORATION.md.
- `SITE_CONTENT_BUILD_TOKEN` → `siteContentBuildToken` + site-content store, guarding `/v1/site-content/*`

Beyond the four config atoms named in the ticket, this PR also wires `runPromotionProvisioning`/`runPromotionRecheck` (the `/internal/jobs/promotion-*` job runners) — ADR 0004 bundles the provisioning trigger into the same "needs production wiring" sentence, and a wired flag with no runner behind it would be inert (both job routes would 503 regardless of the flag's value).

## Safety-guard additions (found during self-review)

- Added `promotionMisconfigured`, mirroring the existing `deletionMisconfigured` guard: if `LIVE_PROMOTION_AUTHORIZED=true` and `VERCEL_API_TOKEN` is set but `VERCEL_TEAM_ID` is missing, this degrades to unauthorized (with a `console.error`) instead of silently provisioning a customer's isolated project into the token owner's *personal* Vercel scope. Covered by a new regression test.
- The exposed `livePromotionAuthorized` is now ANDed with capability (`Boolean(promotionDeploymentService)`), mirroring how `previewDeletionAuthorized` is exposed — it can never read `true` while the job runners are actually unwired.
- Added minimum-length validation (16 chars, matching `CONTROL_SERVICE_TOKEN`) for the two new bearer tokens, since they guard higher-privilege surfaces (real production provisioning, cross-tenant content reads) than the existing unvalidated `MADETHIS_ADAPTER_TOKEN`.
- Fixed a trim inconsistency: `madeThisAdapterToken` is now trimmed the same way the two new tokens are, closing a latent whitespace-only-token auth-bypass shape (not reachable via `api/index.ts` today, since it trims at the env-var read, but the wiring layer itself should not depend on that).
- `apps/control/.env.example` documents the two new vars.

## Deliberately not in scope (see follow-up)

- **Concurrency/claim-lease gap**: `PromotionStore.findPending()` has no claim step (unlike `PreviewTeardownStore.claimExpiryRecords`), so a double-fired `/internal/jobs/promotion-provisioning` can clobber a successful `domain_pending` promotion into `failed`. This is pre-existing `promotion-adapter.ts`/`promotion-store.ts` behavior from SHO-84, out of scope for a wiring-only ticket, but it's a real blocker before `LIVE_PROMOTION_AUTHORIZED` is ever flipped `true`. Tracked as a follow-up.
- No cron configured yet for `/internal/jobs/promotion-recheck` (ADR 0005 §7) — without it, a provisioned promotion can reach `domain_pending` and never automatically advance to `live`.
- The `/internal/jobs/promotion-provisioning` and `-recheck` routes return `200` with a zero-count report when unauthorized, rather than `403` the way `/internal/jobs/preview-teardown` does for unauthorized deletion — an existing `app.ts`/SHO-96 design choice, not part of this diff, flagged for discussion rather than changed here.

## Test plan

- `pnpm --filter @shopface/control typecheck` → exit 0
- `pnpm --filter @shopface/control test` → **164/164 passing** (14 test files), including 9 new tests covering: promotion adapter wiring (unwired vs wired vs closed), site-content store wiring (unwired vs wired vs closed), promotion-provisioning/-recheck job wiring (unwired without a Vercel token, asymmetric gating on `siteContentBuildToken`, safe-by-default zero-report when unauthorized, full end-to-end wiring through to the Vercel-backed service when authorized, and the new misconfiguration-guard regression)
- Not exercised against a live database or live Vercel API — same caveat ADR 0004/0005 already carry for the rest of this integration.
