author: manoldonev
body:
## What

`figma-faithful` step 7 emitted a **translation plan** — the completed token table, the placement decision, the resolved-component list, the analog, the file list — and called it "the cheapest place to catch a wrong token row". Nothing on the lean lane ever read it. It was prose a build session emitted and then implemented against, so both checks written to grade it reached nothing:

- **per-node sizing** is required unconditionally by step 3b, but the plan reviewer's only sizing finding was scoped to a "repeating / wrapping group" — a screen of individually sized controls is not one, so a plan carrying no control dimensions at all drew zero findings, and the design-blind code reviewer then had no recorded number to compare against either;
- **component-resolution suitability** was deferred to `figma-faithful-spec-reviewer`, which returns `N/A` on any input without Copy Index / Components / Screens sections — i.e. on every lean-lane spec. Both deferred checks landed nowhere.

Milestone 3 now refuses an armed ticket, **before the render pass**, unless a committed translation plan exists at `<plansDir>/<key>-lean-plan.md` carrying:

```
planned_from: <the gate stamps this>

| node | repo component | why this component |
| ---- | -------------- | ------------------ |
| Filter panel | @acme/ui Drawer | the frame draws a right-edge sheet over a scrim |

| node | dimensions | overflow |
| ---- | ---------- | -------- |
| Filter panel | fixed 320px wide, hug height | none |
```

Anchored on the **columns**, not on heading names: what is load-bearing is the cell. Every declared cell must be non-empty and no row may be shorter than its header — deleting the trailing cell is not an escape from the empty-cell rule. The arm rides the render lane's own `design_state()` predicate and the same `design_was_armed` state lock, which the plan pass now holds because it is the design pass that runs first.

The two dead reviewer checks are made live against it: `figma-faithful-plan-reviewer` takes ownership of component-resolution suitability, and its sizing check is **inverted** to fire on the silent case (a control-bearing screen with no dimension row at all) rather than only on the loud one.

## The contract was the operator's, not this session's

OR-1 and OR-2 were `pause-and-ask` regions, and every decision below was answered on the issue ([comment](https://github.com/manoldonev/second-shift/issues/694#issuecomment-5440267225)) before any code was written: path, required cells, asserting milestone and ordering, arming predicate, disarm state-lock, patch binding, re-entry. OR-2 was decided **figma-only** — the non-figma `design-faithful` family has no translation-plan step and no plan-reviewer agent, so mirroring is net-new surface and belongs in its own ticket.

The lane did not stop this run: `pause_and_ask_ids` parses `## Open regions` with `awk -F'|'` and reads the id from `$2`, so a **bullet**-form regions section extracts zero ids and milestone 1 passes vacuously. That fail-open is a lane defect independent of this ticket and is worth its own item.

## Honest scope

**The `planned_from` stamp is tamper-evidence, not proof the plan was re-read.** On a stale binding the gate re-stamps and reds; nothing can verify the author reconsidered the token table against the code that moved, and the refusal says so in as many words. What the artifact buys is that the plan exists, is committed, has both tables fully populated, and is dated against a specific patch — so an omission reads as an **empty cell** rather than an absent thought, and a reviewer can see which code the plan was current for. Same bargain #693 struck for the fidelity evidence table.

**No gate reads the plan for correctness, and none is added.** Whether a resolved component draws what the frame draws, and whether a recorded dimension is the design's, are questions the plan reviewer asks and the design-sighted review session answers. The gate parses tables.

## Design decisions worth reading

- **A third patch identity, `plan_patch_id()`** — the branch diff less the verdict record, the render receipt **and the plan itself**. Each exclusion is forced by a different livelock: itself, because the gate stamps into it; the receipt, because the render pass rewrites it on every code change and a fresh screenshot is not a reason to re-assert the plan.
- **`render_patch_id()` deliberately does NOT gain the symmetric exclusion.** It is mirrored at the merge boundary by a reader that cannot see the gate, so a consumer pinned to an older boundary ref would red every armed PR carrying a plan — the #436 shape, invisible from either side. It is also unnecessary **in the direction the exclusion would serve**: the plan is committed before a receipt exists to restale. The other direction is real and is the price of the lockstep — a plan-only commit does move the render id and restale the receipt, forcing a re-render nothing asked for. It converges in one pass rather than looping, and the boundary skew carries the decision on its own. Both directions are now recorded in `docs/testing.md`'s *Couplings considered and declined*.
- **The budget split.** Absence, a missing `planned_from:` line and a stale stamp are `block_milestone` — #642's own criterion, a red naming something the run was going to do anyway. A malformed table is `fail_milestone`. Without the split an armed run spends two of its three milestone-3 attempts reaching its first screenshot.
- **The gate stamps `planned_from`; it never inserts it.** An author cannot stamp it themselves — the value is only knowable after their last commit — so the gate must write it, but the body is design reasoning and not derivable state. It rewrites a line the author declared (`planned_from: pending`) and refuses when that line is absent, naming it.
- **Fenced blocks are skipped.** Step-7 prose invites a plan to quote the required shape; parsing its placeholder cells as violations would refuse an artifact the gate had just told the author to write.
- **No merge-boundary arm.** The boundary re-asserts the verdict chain, and `fidelity: pass` binds to the render receipt, not to the plan. A new boundary arm also owes a capability stamp, an inert path and a pre-stamp fixture — surface no AC asks for.
- **Every deferral in the reviewer family now names a reachable owner, or says none exists.** "The deferred pixel-diff gate" named a thing that does not exist and now names the design-sighted `review-lean` session — **bare, not namespaced**: `docs/namespaces.md` rule 3(a) forbids the `dev-pipeline:` token anywhere in the four toolkits, and round 1's rewrite introduced it at four sites and red CI. Round 2 also grepped the *construct* rather than the file list, which found three more: `figma-faithful-reviewer` (the third agent of the family), and the `figma-faithful` / `figma-faithful-spec` skills. All of them now deny the gate exists instead of deferring to it; component identity is marked interactive-lane-only with its suitability half taken here; copy *capture* is stated to have **no** lean-lane owner rather than being handed to an agent that would `N/A` it. The plan reviewer's own input recognizer was widened to accept the lean-lane artifact — a recognizer narrower than the artifact is the same dropped check one level down.

## Verification

- `lean-gate-selftest.sh` gains **12 `(dp*)` case ids carrying 14 assertions** (`dp0`–`dp11`): the AND half of arming, absence charged to the absent budget, **each of the five malformed table shapes** `plan_violations()` emits — no column declared, an empty cell, a short row, a table carrying no data row, and no delimiter row under the header — the missing `planned_from:` header line, the fenced-example false-red, the stamp-and-commit cycle proving no harness call happens first, staleness converging rather than looping, and the disarm state-lock held by the plan pass.
- Every existing armed case now carries a conforming plan through `dplan_s

author: machadevelopment
body:
Backend del pedido de Keneth: *"si un user carga sus archivos en Q, pero quiere visualizarlo convertido a USD, que le pida configurar el TC y tenga un botón para ver su data en las 2 monedas."*

**Va primero que el PR del frontend** (`macha-frontend#feat/moneda-de-vista`), aunque el frontend degrada solo si este no está: sin el endpoint, el control no se pinta y las cifras se quedan en la moneda base.

## Contradice una decisión escrita, y hay que decir por qué

CU-868kj3gnv descartó el toggle de moneda con este argumento, que sigue vivo en `metrics/currencies.ts`:

> una fila que entró en quetzales tiene `fx_rate = 1`, o sea que NO existe una tasa congelada que la exprese en dólares. Mostrar el dashboard entero en USD obligaría a inventarle una tasa a esas filas.

Acierta en el peligro y se queda corto en las opciones: trata "inventar la tasa" como la única alternativa a las congeladas. Hay una tercera, y es la que pide el flujo — **preguntarle al dueño**. Una tasa que el cliente configuró no es inventada: es la misma que ya mantiene para la ingesta desde el 2026-08-25.

Lo que se conserva intacto es la distinción que esa nota protege:

| | qué es | cuándo se escribe |
|---|---|---|
| `amount_base` | **contabilidad** — auditable, no cambia nunca | una vez, al promover, con la tasa congelada de la fila |
| esto | **una lente** — una sola tasa, rotulada | nunca; en tiempo de lectura |

Ni la ingesta, ni la promoción, ni un solo `fx_rate` congelado se tocan.

## `GET /fx-rate/display?on=`

Resuelve con `resolveFromCatalog`, la **misma** función que decide si una fila se marca durante la ingesta — incluida su caída a la tasa más antigua. El frontend ya recibe el historial y podría elegirla él; sería una tercera implementación de una regla que `lib/fx.ts` ya declara que *"tiene que coincidir o el producto se contradice consigo mismo"*, y una copia en otro repo no se mantiene sincronizada.

La tasa es la del **cierre del período que se mira** y no "la última registrada" (decisión de Keneth). Con la última, la cifra en dólares de marzo cambia cada vez que alguien ajusta el TC aunque en marzo no haya pasado nada: un número histórico que se mueve solo.

`rate: null` con 200 no es un error — es "esta empresa todavía no configuró su TC", el estado que dispara la otra mitad del pedido.

## Y un defecto latente que apareció al mirar esto

**Las dos rutas que escriben en `fx_rates` aceptaban una tasa de 0.** Validaban con `t.Number()` a secas, y el daño no deja rastro: la ingesta hace `amount_base = originalAmount * fxRate`, así que con 0 **toda fila en la otra moneda se promueve con importe cero**, sin marcarse y sin error. Una negativa invierte el signo del movimiento. Y la lente nueva divide por la tasa, o sea que un 0 es una división por cero en la pantalla principal.

`ESQUEMA_TASA` (`exclusiveMinimum: 0`) vive en `lib/fx.ts` y lo importan las dos rutas — dos copias de la regla en dos módulos es exactamente cómo quedaron desalineadas la primera vez. Se valida con `Value.Check` contra el esquema **real**, no leyéndole la propiedad: lo segundo comprueba que alguien escribió `exclusiveMinimum`, esto comprueba que TypeBox rechaza el valor.

El test de "un solo esquema" hubo que acotarlo al `body:` — la primera versión buscaba `rate: t.Number(` en el archivo entero y se disparaba con el esquema de **respuesta** del endpoint nuevo, donde un número suelto es correcto porque ahí la tasa se devuelve, no se acepta.

## Verificación

960 unitarios y 358 de integración en verde, más typecheck, lint y prettier.

author: fcostaoliveira
body:
## Summary

Adds `workloads/workload_feature_store`, modeling the entity-major online-serving layout used by feature stores (Feast, Featureform, Tecton-style systems): one record per entity holding many named feature fields, a whole-entity read/write access pattern, and a read-heavy, Zipfian-skewed request mix - based on the [redis-benchmarks-specification's feature-store playbook](https://github.com/redis/redis-benchmarks-specification/blob/main/redis_benchmarks_specification/test-suites/memtier_benchmark-playbook-feature-store-hash-10M-entities-50-features-template.yml).

Two things the existing core workload couldn't express, both added as generic properties usable by any workload file, not just this one:

- **Field naming**: `fieldnameprefix`/`fieldnamestartindex`/`lastfieldname`, so generated field names can look like `feature_1`..`feature_50` plus a trailing `event_ts`, instead of always `field0`..`fieldN`.
- **Field value CONTENT, not just size**: `fieldvaluetype=numeric/integer/float/boolean/timestamp` (plus `lastfieldvaluetype`, and min/max/precision knobs) generates realistic typed scalars - matching how a feature store actually represents a feature (Feast: `INT32`/`INT64`/`FLOAT32`/`FLOAT64`/`BOOL`/`UNIX_TIMESTAMP`) - instead of opaque random bytes. `fieldvaluetype=random` (the default) is unchanged/backward compatible - existing workload files are unaffected.

Also gives `db/redis/db.go`'s `Read` a whole-entity `HGETALL` fast path (when reading all fields of a hash, matching this workload's access pattern) instead of always enumerating every field name via `HMGET`.


## Test plan

- [x] `go build ./...`
- [x] Verified against a real Redis: `load` + `run` pass, and the underlying generated data reads back correctly (typed values, custom field names, and the new `HGETALL` fast path) via a manual smoke test.
- [x] `go test ./pkg/workload/...` (pre-existing `open workloads/workloadc` test failure is unrelated - reproduces identically on unmodified `master`)

author: demac-aruba
body:
## Objective
Correct the Employees workspace so automatic attendance and payroll calculations respect each employee's employment lifecycle dates, and restore the payroll/timesheet PDF export in Quick Actions.

## Root cause
- `employmentStartedAt` was saved on the canonical staff profile, but `resolveEmployeeSchedule()` ignored it. Because normal attendance is derived automatically from the schedule, dates before the employee's start date were incorrectly projected as scheduled/regular days.
- The current ERP Next employee workspace retained the accounting CSV export but no longer exposed the previously developed payroll summary PDF workflow.

## Changes
- Treat dates before `employmentStartedAt` (and after `employmentEndedAt`, when present) as outside the employment period with 0 scheduled and 0 paid-free minutes.
- Keep the start date inclusive: normal schedule begins on the actual employment start date.
- Add acceptance coverage proving a new hire starting 2026-08-11 has no automatic schedule on 2026-08-10 and receives the normal schedule on 2026-08-11.
- Restore `Export payroll summary PDF` under Employees → Quick actions.
- Generate a browser-native PDF with no new third-party dependency. It includes the selected payroll period and per-employee scheduled, regular, OT, AO, vacation, NWNP, paid-free, salary advances, late minutes, exceptions, and manual-record totals.

## Safety / scope
- No production deployment.
- No data migration or mutation.
- No changes to payroll permissions: PDF export uses the same payroll-sensitive permission gate as accounting CSV.
- Existing accounting CSV remains unchanged.

## Validation requested
- `npm run typecheck` in `apps/erp-next`
- `npm run test:employee-schedule` in `apps/erp-next`
- UI check: employee with start date 2026-08-11 must show no automatic Regular/Scheduled status before Aug 11.
- UI check: Quick actions → Export payroll summary PDF downloads the selected payroll period PDF.

author: myia-ai-01
body:
## Ce que ça corrige

#3014 a ajouté `is_leader` / `leader_pid` / `leader_lock_age_ms` à la sortie de `roosync_indexing(status)` pour qu'un follower sain (file plate = normal, le drain est porté par le leader ailleurs sur la machine) soit distinguable d'un leader bloqué.

**La fonctionnalité était morte en production depuis le jour de sa livraison, sur les 6 machines.**

### Mesure — ai-01, 2026-08-27 17:00Z

| observation | valeur |
|---|---|
| verrou | `roosync-indexer-leader-myia-ai-01.lock` |
| détenteur | PID **38276**, `node.exe` vivant, uptime **38,5 h** |
| renouvelé | **1,3 min** avant la lecture |
| `roosync_indexing(status)` | `is_leader:false` · `leader_pid:null` · `leader_lock_age_ms:null` · **aucun hint** |

Un leader vivant et frais, rendu **exactement** comme « aucun leader du tout ».

po-2025 a lu cette même sortie 20 minutes plus tard et rapporté « ce process est follower » ([#3279 comment](https://github.com/jsboige/roo-extensions/issues/3279#issuecomment-5440927472)). **Cette lecture n'était pas disponible dans la donnée** — le champ vaut `false` partout, leader compris.

## Cause, lue au site d'appel

#3014 atteignait les deux valeurs par **casts** :

```ts
const leaderMachineId = (state as { machineId?: string }).machineId;
const isLeader = (state as { isIndexLeader?: boolean }).isIndexLeader === true;
```

Un cast **affirme** une forme, il ne la **vérifie** pas. L'interface `IndexingState` du tool ne déclarait ni l'un ni l'autre — donc `registry.ts` **ne pouvait pas** les transmettre, même en le voulant : ajouter `machineId` à ce littéral est une erreur **TS2353** (excess property) tant que l'interface l'omet. Vérifié en construisant le fix : le compilateur rejette la bonne donnée et accepte l'omission qui produit la fonctionnalité morte.

Effets, constants sur toute machine :

- `is_leader` = `undefined === true` → **`false` constant**
- `leader_pid` / `leader_lock_age_ms` → **`null` constants** (la lecture court-circuite sur `machineId` falsy)
- le hint « ce process n'est PAS le leader, le drain est porté par PID … » **ne se déclenche jamais** (même garde)

## Pourquoi la CI n'a rien vu — le point central

Les tests #3014 (`roosync-indexing.tool.test.ts` l.492, 518, 547, 553, 574) **fournissent eux-mêmes `machineId` et `isIndexLeader`** dans leur propre littéral d'état. Ils prouvent que l'outil **rend** ce qu'on lui donne ; rien ne prouve que le câblage **le lui donne**. Verts pendant toute la durée du défaut.

Un test qui appelle le handler avec un littéral **ne peut pas, par construction**, attraper un site d'appel qui omet un champ.

## Le correctif

Symétrique de ce que **#2766** avait déjà fait correctement pour les champs dead-letter, à un champ de distance dans la même interface :

- `IndexingState` gagne `machineId?` / `isIndexLeader?` — optionnels pour la même raison que la paire dead-letter (« callers that build IndexingState manually »), et les lectures dégradent vers « inconnu » au lieu de mentir
- les casts deviennent des lectures de champ déclaré
- `registry.ts` transmet `state.machineId` et `state.isIndexLeader`

## La garde

`roosync-indexing.wiring.test.ts` (nouveau) asserte **le littéral du site d'appel**, à la manière des harnais de `scripts/testing/harness/` qui lisent des scripts de production qu'ils ne peuvent pas exécuter. Il teste **ce qui était cassé** (le câblage), pas ce qui marchait déjà (le rendu) — sinon il retombe dans le même angle mort.

**Contre-épreuve exécutée** : retrait des 2 champs → **3/3** assertions de câblage rouges ; la paire `ServerState` reste verte (elle mesure autre chose). La mutation assertait qu'elle avait mordu avant de conclure.

## Validation

- `npm run build` — PASS
- `npx vitest run --config vitest.config.ci.ts` — **13134 passed / 0 failed** / 666 fichiers
- scan secrets + `git diff --check` — PASS

## Portée

**Ce n'est pas #2922.** L'élection de leader **inter-machines** reste user-gated et intouchée. Le leader **machine-local** fonctionne déjà (verrou vivant, vol des verrous stale) — seule son **observabilité** était débranchée. La case 3 de #3279 redevient donc atteignable sans toucher à #2922.

Aucun changement de comportement d'indexation : uniquement ce que le status **rapporte**.

## Reste à faire après merge

Le process MCP en cours charge encore l'ancien build : **mergé ≠ livré ≠ exécuté ≠ observé**. La vérification live (`is_leader:true` + PID sur le process leader) demandera un redémarrage de session — non bloquant, et à faire au fil de l'eau.

Refs #3279 (case 3 de la checklist).

author: babissimo
body:
Closes ClickUp [86cb9br6k](https://app.clickup.com/t/86cb9br6k). Branch `fix/adsb-capture-timestamps`.

## What this fixes

Three places stamped an ADS-B position's freshness with the time it was *handled* rather than the time it was *captured*, and one fabricated the timestamp outright for external-cache entries that carried none. Every 60 s staleness gate keys off that stamp, so the defences switched off exactly when the data was stalest.

The sharpest case was calibration: `record_adsb_calibration` refuses a fix older than `CAL_MAX_ADSB_AGE_S` (10 s), but with `fresh_adsb` reporting `now` the age was always zero, so a fix up to a poll interval old (120 s, or 420 s behind a rate-limit backoff) entered the learned FOV as if it were current. That is 30 km at 250 m/s, feeding the polygon that judges solves.

## Commits

| | |
|---|---|
| `7cc9e22` | Capture timestamps on both ingest paths and the external cache, plus expiry at both cache layers |
| `42c806a` | adsb.lol ground speed stored in m/s, not knots — its own commit, as the ticket asks |
| `b226719` | Fixes from review of the first two |
| `b3c1b85` | Merge `main` (see below) |

`main` is merged in rather than rebased, so the three commits above stay reviewable in isolation. It was not housekeeping: the branch was 17 commits behind and still carried the pre-fix `deploy/tower-contract.sh`, so its `tower-service-contract` check failed on an open-meteo rate limit that `b459167` and `8e84750` had already fixed on `main`. CI runs that script from the PR's own branch, so a bare re-run could not have passed.

The units defect is isolated in its own commit: it is a separate bug that merely shares a location, and it was ~1.94x high on every external truth entry, since OpenSky 429s anonymous access and adsb.lol is the only path that runs in production.

## Notes for review

**`b226719` is the interesting one.** A review of the first two commits found that making freshness honest broke two things that had been quietly relying on every ADS-B stamp coming off the server clock:

- **Calibration stopped entirely for any node more than 2 s out.** `CAL_FIX_DETECTION_SKEW_S` bounds a fix against the node's last detection, and that detection stamp is server wall clock — so comparing it against a node-clock capture stamp turned a co-timing rule into an NTP test. Records now carry `recv_ms` (server clock) alongside `last_seen_ms` (capture); the skew rule uses one, the age gates the other.
- **An adsb.lol outage made stale data look *fresher* than before.** `seen_pos` is an age relative to the fetch that produced the row, and the client serves last-good rows again on a later failed fetch, so resolving it against the current poll re-stamped a frozen snapshot as seconds old every cycle. `AdsbLolClient` now publishes an absolute `captured_at`, resolved at fetch time.
- **`last_seen_ms` could go backwards**, because `adsb_aircraft` is keyed by hex alone and written from two paths for the same frame. A queued replay walked the stamp back by the queue latency and `feed_gc` evicted aircraft being reported at 50 Hz. Writes are guarded now.

Cross-validation's sample watermark is **deleted** rather than patched — it caused four separate defects (a future-dated `timestamp_ms` bought a node permanent immunity; an omitted one skipped every sample; samples sharing a frame's millisecond collapsed to one judgement; deferred samples were never re-judged). The guarantee it reached for already holds: the admission window is far shorter than the interval between cycles, and there is now a test pinning that coupling.

## Deliberately not done

- **The 60–300 s skew band.** A node 90 s backlogged and a node 90 s slow are indistinguishable from a single frame; the former is reported honestly and correctly dropped by the 60 s gates, the latter is fresh data we discard. Narrowing the bound would re-stamp genuine deep backlog as fresh, which is the original defect. Distinguishing them needs arrival time tracked separately from capture time.
- **`/api/v1/ground-truth/real`'s `source` field** still says `opensky_network` whatever fed it. It is a published field and the per-entry provenance it wants belongs to 86cb9btw9. It does gain an additive per-entry `captured_at`, since its docstring invites callers to measure solver accuracy against those positions.
- **Cross-validation only fires on samples captured near a poll.** Gating both sides at 15 s is what a 10 km bar can honestly support, but the cache refreshes every 120 s. Widening its reach means dead-reckoning the entry to the sample's time, not a bigger budget — raised as [86cbaxf1n](https://app.clickup.com/t/86cbaxf1n) and linked.

## Sequencing

Site 1 of [86cb5p1jy](https://app.clickup.com/t/86cb5p1jy) holds behind this, per the decision recorded on the ticket: it rewrites the same `external_adsb_cache` write sites, so this one owns the entry schema outright. It will add a `source` field to the same dict, which should merge cleanly alongside `last_seen_ms` and `recv_ms`.

## Verification

Full backend suite green (exit 0, zero failures, coverage 83.15% against a 55% gate) and `pre-commit run --all-files` clean. 51 new tests across four files, including a regression file with one test per review finding. Re-run after merging `main`: still exit 0.

Not yet verified on a live map. Green tests do not cover the compose/env/frontend seams, so this wants a look at `testmap.retina.fm` once it is deployed.

Worth a baseline either side, because two numbers people watch will move by design: `/api/test/solver-stats` and `/api/test/mlat-accuracy`. External ADS-B fixes stop feeding calibration, which is the point of the change, and adsb.lol-sourced velocities drop by 1.94x.

author: jetsadawijit
body:
# Overview

This is task 3 of 4 in the https-enforcement work, and the part of it that lands here. The `jwz` package now guards the transport on its ten GitHub and GitLab modules, and every page under `docs/github/` and `docs/gitlab/` quotes that module's source in its `Code` section. Without this change the site publishes code that no longer matches the package.

`.agents/docs/content-standards.md` treats a page that disagrees with the source as a defect rather than a style issue, which is why this is a `fix` and not a `docs` change.

# Modified

- `docs/github/{build,delete,invite,release,remove}/index.html` and `docs/gitlab/{build,delete,invite,release,remove}/index.html` — each `Code` block now shows the `../essential` import with the new helpers, the `requireHttpsUrl(config.KEY, 'KEY')` line beside the existing key-exists guard, and the request URL resolved through `resolveSecureUrl`. Each page's `Logic` list gains a matching bullet so the prose and the code agree.
- `docs/github/invite/index.html` — additionally corrects the `Authorization` line, where escaped backticks around the template literal published JavaScript a reader could not copy. This predates the task and every sibling page writes the line correctly; it sat inside a `Code` block already being rewritten, so it was fixed rather than left as a known-wrong page.
- `.agents/memory/` — this repository's own record of the task, its index row, and the repository-state entry.

# Summary

Content-only. No stylesheet, script, partial, or page structure changed, so the Silver Glass rendering is untouched and there is nothing to rebuild — GitHub Pages serves `docs/` directly.

**How it was checked.** Every page's `Code` block was extracted, HTML-unescaped, stripped of comments and compared line by line against the real module in the `jwz` working tree: ten of ten match. Tag balance was then verified across every page under `docs/`.

**Two `http://` strings are deliberately untouched.** `docs/js/site.js` carries the SVG namespace declaration `xmlns`, which is an XML namespace name — a constant identifier that is never dereferenced, and rewriting it to `https` breaks SVG rendering in the inline favicon. `wiki/environments/setup.md` carries `http://localhost:8000/`, the loopback address of `python3 -m http.server`, which does not speak TLS. Neither is a transport and both are false positives for a scheme rewrite.

**One instruction left stale on purpose.** `.agents/knowledge/jwz-package-surface.md` says the platform operations "resolve rather than throw", which does not account for the configuration-time throws. That file states outright that correcting it is a discovery finding rather than a self-applied edit, so it is reported for selection instead of being changed here.

Merge order: 3 of 4 — merges after JetsadaWijit/jwz#15, since the pages quote the source that pull request introduces.

## Summary
This PR introduces the Free-To-Revert (FTR) resume navigation method for ASAS (Airborne Separation Assurance System), along with supporting infrastructure improvements and bug fixes.

## Key Changes

### New FTR Resume Navigation Method
- **New file**: `bluesky/traffic/asas/ftr.py` - Implements the FTR criterion based on Wouter Schaberg's thesis
  - Determines when aircraft can safely revert to autopilot velocity by checking if the closest point of approach (CPA) remains beyond the protected zone
  - Supports two criteria: one based on intruder's current velocity, another on intruder's desired velocity
  - Three intent modes: `OFF` (skip second criterion), `ASSUMED` (use velocity at conflict detection), `DECLARED` (use autopilot data)
  - Includes `FTRINTENT` command to configure the intent method
  - Properly handles wind effects and track-making calculations

### ASAS Infrastructure Updates
- **Modified**: `bluesky/traffic/asas/__init__.py` - Registers the new FTR class
- **Modified**: `bluesky/traffic/asas/resumenav.py` - Enhanced to display method-specific messages via optional `selectedmsg()` callback

### Test Scenario
- **New file**: `scenario/ASAS/RESNAV-FTR-2DEG.scn` - Test scenario for FTR with shallow-angle (2°) conflict geometry

### Performance Envelope Optimization
- **Modified**: `bluesky/traffic/performance/openap/perfoap.py` - Refactored speed limit construction using `np.select()` for cleaner, more maintainable code
- **Modified**: `bluesky/traffic/performance/openap/coeff.py` - Reordered descent vertical speed minimums for consistency

### UI Enhancement
- **Modified**: `bluesky/ui/qtgl/console.py` - Added Cmd/Ctrl+V paste support in the command console for improved usability

## Implementation Details
- FTR uses flat-earth approximation for distance calculations
- Handles edge cases like crosswind exceeding airspeed by falling back to current ground velocity
- Properly manages conflict pair lifecycle, including cleanup of assumed intents
- Supports waypoint recovery after conflict resolution

author: madlp24
body:
Closes #78

Mesa knows what every product costs. This turns that into the one number you want
before sending an event proposal: what the event leaves you.

## What is here

**`MenuItem`, the client-facing layer over `catalog.Product`.** The POS calls a dish
`CROQUETAS DE LOMO AHUMADO *4U`; a proposal cannot. A menu item carries the name,
description and quoted price, and its `product` link is the only source of cost.
`product_units` bridges a unit mismatch — a kilo of picanha is 1000/420 of a 420 g
portion.

**Composing from a budget.** Give it a price per guest, a headcount and an event type
and it builds the menu that fits. It reasons in cost per guest — price divided by how
many guests one unit serves — because that is the only way a 300.000 station and a
30.000 dessert compare against the same budget. Quantities round up (two stations for
30 guests are paid whole), and when a budget cannot cover the event it says so and
reports the floor instead of quietly overshooting.

**Cost, profit and margin** on every quote, judged against a 60% target taken from
events this restaurant has already billed.

**A PDF for the client.** Prices only. Cost, profit and margin never appear in it —
there is a test that asserts exactly that.

## Two things worth a second look

**Tax was being added twice.** Menu prices already contain the impuesto al consumo.
The spreadsheet this replaces extracted the contained 8% and then added it back to the
total, overcharging by 6.8% on every quote (verified against two real ones). Here the
contained tax is shown and not re-added; the tip applies to the pre-tax base.

**A product with no cost is unknown, not free.** Counting it as zero silently inflated
a real quote's margin to 76.3%. Now such a quote reports no margin at all and names the
line that is missing its mapping. That is `5376e85`, and it is the reason the margin
card can be trusted.

## Notes for review

- `reportlab` moves from `requirements-dev.txt` to `requirements.txt`. It was already
  in the project for PDF test fixtures; it now renders the quote PDF at runtime.
- `python manage.py seed_menu --restaurant <id>` builds the menu from the catalog and
  maps every item to its product. Cuts sold by the gram become one-kilo items, since
  quoting 20 units of a per-gram product means 20 grams of wagyu.
- Everything is tenant-scoped, with tests for cross-tenant reads on quotes, the PDF
  and product mapping.
- 43 new tests; the suite is at 201. PDF assertions read the document back with
  `pdfplumber` rather than grepping the file, because reportlab compresses page
  streams and a raw-bytes assertion passes whether or not the string is on the page.

author: lathif21
body:
One commit on top of `master`, now that #9 has merged.

**These four pages are generated. All of it is in `build.py`** — `index`, `hoe-werkt-het`, `realisaties` and `tutorials` are build output, and editing the HTML directly is lost on the next run. That happened during this work: hand edits removing the SETT mark and the SETT name from the display copy were reverted by a rebuild. This commit puts them where they survive.

## Overzicht's Realisaties is the book's photography grid

04.01 and 04.02 both lay their images out the same way, and it is not a masonry: four columns, **no gutter**, cells spanning one or two columns and one or two rows, so the plates butt into a single wall. The nine run as two uprights beside a split column, then a double-width plate beside two uprights, then the closing pair — 04.02's own two blocks.

- Square-cornered, unlike the cards elsewhere in `pages.css`. Two rounded corners meeting leave a notch of background between them, which is the one thing a shared edge must not do.
- At two columns the **column** spans drop and only the row spans carry the rhythm: at four columns a double-width cell is half the wall, but at two it is the whole measure, and one row of height across the whole measure crops the photograph to a 4:1 sliver. Below 560 it is a single stack of 4:3 plates, still butted.
- `masonry()` is gone; nothing called it. `realisaties.html` keeps the nine as separate cards on the dark field — two galleries in two registers, which is the book's own habit.

## The brand name in the display copy is Atelier DIY's, not SETT's

- `DIY ATELIER IS NOT JUST A PRODUCT…` on Overzicht, as **one** spread unit. Split in two, 01.05's justification pushes "DIY" and "ATELIER" to opposite ends of the measure and the company reads as two companies.
- `SET THE TABLE FOR UNFORGETTABLE MOMENTS.` on Realisaties and `READY SET GO!` on Tutorials — the book can write SETT there because its name doubles as the verb; here the pun has no owner.
- Same sweep over the catalogue's poster block and its vertical rail in `webshop.html`.

## The header lockup drops the logo-icoon

On all six pages. 01.03 allows the mark beside the wordmark and `header()` used to emit it, but the bean is SETT's mark and this is Atelier DIY's site — the brandbook is the design system here, not the brand. `webshop.html` and `product.html` change only through `sync_chrome()`.

### One line to confirm

Realisaties reads `SET THE TABLE FOR UNFORGETTABLE MOMENTS.` The hand edit it came from read `DIY ATELIER THE TABLE…`, which isn't a sentence. Easy to change if the company name was wanted in that line.

### Verified

Headless renders at 390 / 700 / 1024 / 1440: no horizontal overflow at any width, no justified line overflowing its own box, and the mosaic holding all nine cells at each breakpoint.

author: aterga
body:
Reduces the served tool surface to the app/canister tools, and drops every mention of tooling outside the current scope from the docs, landing page, policy, and server instructions (maintainer review: describe what we ship today, nothing else). Builds on the `IcCanisterTools` / `IcProtocolTools` split from #157 (now merged — this PR targets `main`).

## What the server serves

`IcTools` composes only `IcCanisterTools`: **11 tools** — the app/canister-scoped tools (`get_canister_candid`, `get_canister_oql_schema`, `get_canister_api_doc`, `canister_query`, `canister_update_call`, `get_app_principal`, `list_app_accounts`, `open_app`, `resolve_app`, `discover_app_canisters`) plus **`icp_oql_guide`**, the one `icp_`-named tool on the canister side: it is the dialect guide the canister OQL read flow runs on (`icp_oql_guide` → `get_canister_oql_schema` → `canister_query`). 10 of the 11 carry read-only annotations; `canister_update_call` is the one write. The `skill://` resources (the official IC skills) and the `candid://` / `oql://` references stay served.

## What is no longer served

`IcProtocolTools` — the 15 `icp_` protocol/meta tools (dashboard name/id lookups, the IC skills as tools, canister creation/management) — is not part of the default composition. `tools/call` on one of those names returns the router's standard "tool not found" error (`-32602` invalid params — the same shape any unknown tool name gets, so these are indistinguishable from nonexistent tools). The type remains public, documented, tested library code (`pub fn new`, pub router) so an embedder can dispatch its router from their own `ServerHandler`; that is API documentation on the type itself, not product messaging.

## Changes

body:
## Why `GET /api/feed` is the homepage payload (~360KB) and cannot be used from a Chrome extension new-tab page: OPTIONS returns SPA HTML, GET has no `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`. This adds a slim public read API for third-party clients. The Chrome extension itself lives in a **standalone repo**, not this monorepo. Public GET surfaces (`/api/feed`) are not rate-limited; this endpoint matches that. Failures return `{ "error": "unavailable" }` with no D1/admin detail. ## Public URL `GET https://news.duyet.net/api/public` Local Worker: `http://localhost:3014/api/public` (`pnpm --filter news dev`). No auth. CORS allows `chrome-extension://…`, `http://localhost` / `http://127.0.0.1`, and `https://*.duyet.net`. OPTIONS is intercepted in the Worker fetch entry (same SPA-fallback reason as `/api/subscribe`). Cache: `public, max-age=120, s-maxage=300, stale-while-revalidate=600`. ## JSON shape ```json { "tldr": { "date": "2026-08-27", "bullets_en": [{ "text": "...", "item_ids": ["..."] }], "bullets_vi": [{ "text": "...", "item_ids": ["..."] }] }, "stories": [ { "id": "...", "url": "https://...", "title": "...", "title_vi": "...", "category": "Industry", "image_url": "https://...", "published_at": 1787793175 } ], "updatedAt": 1756300000000 } ``` `tldr` may be `null`. Up to 16 bullets per language and 8 top stories by `rank_score`. Typical payload is a few KB (well under 50KB). `published_at` is epoch seconds. ## Tests - Shape, size cap, thin-snapshot fallback, missing `image_url` column, no-auth, sanitized errors: `apps/news/src/lib/public-queries.test.ts` - CORS preflight for `chrome-extension://` and localhost: `apps/news/worker/__tests__/public-cors.test.ts`
  
## Summary by Sourcery Expose a compact, cached, CORS-enabled public news digest API for third-party clients. New Features: - Add an unauthenticated `/api/public` digest endpoint exposing bilingual TL;DR content and a limited set of top stories for third-party clients. Bug Fixes: - Prevent public API failures from exposing database or administrative error details. - Provide a title-based TL;DR fallback when stored snapshot content is insufficient and support databases without the optional image column. Enhancements: - Add origin-restricted CORS handling for Chrome extensions, local development, and Duyet subdomains, including Worker-level preflight interception. - Keep the public response compact with bounded bullets and stories plus public caching headers. Documentation: - Document the public digest API, response shape, access policy, CORS behavior, and caching guidance. Tests: - Add coverage for the public digest response shape, payload limit, fallbacks, sanitized failures, public access, and CORS preflight behavior. - Extend the smoke checks to validate the public endpoint and Chrome-extension preflight handling. ## Summary by CodeRabbit - **New Features** - Added an unauthenticated public digest API at `GET /api/public`. - Provides bilingual TL;DR bullets and up to eight top stories in a compact JSON response. - Supports browser extension, localhost, and approved site origins through CORS. - Added public caching to improve response speed and reduce load. - **Documentation** - Documented the endpoint, response format, caching, CORS behavior, and payload limits. - **Tests** - Added coverage for API responses, CORS preflight handling, payload limits, fallbacks, and error behavior.

author: stephenwithph
body:
Brings every `uses:` tag in `.github/workflows/` up to the current major, fixes the CI warnings that surfaced as a result, and adds a Dependabot config so this doesn't need doing by hand again.

## 1. Action version bumps

| Action | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `actions/checkout` | `v4` | `v7` |
| `actions/setup-python` | `v5` | `v7` |
| `actions/upload-artifact` | `v4` | `v7` |
| `actions/download-artifact` | `v4` | `v8` |
| `astral-sh/setup-uv` | `v4` | `v10.0.1` |

`setup-uv` is pinned to an exact patch because Astral stopped publishing floating major tags after `v7` — `v8`, `v9`, and `v10` exist only as exact patch tags. `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1` was already on its recommended floating branch ref and is unchanged.

Each tag was verified to resolve upstream and to be the current latest major. Reviewed the release notes for every intervening major; nothing in them bites here:

- Most of the jumps are Node 20 → 24 runtime bumps requiring runner >= 2.327.1. All jobs run on `ubuntu-latest`, which already satisfies that.
- `upload-artifact@v7` direct (unzipped) uploads are opt-in via `archive: false`, so the v7 upload → v8 download pairing in `publish.yml` and `tests.yml` still uses the normal zip path.
- `download-artifact@v8` now **errors** on a digest mismatch instead of warning. Default-safe, and preferable on the publish path — a corrupted transfer fails the run rather than quietly proceeding to PyPI.
- `setup-python@v7` removed the `pip-install` input; `publish.yml` only passes `python-version`.
- `checkout@v7` blocks fork-PR checkout under `pull_request_target` / `workflow_run`. Triggers here are `pull_request` and `release`, so no impact.

## 2. `enable-cache: false` on setup-uv

The bump produced four new CI annotations. `setup-uv` caches by default from v5 on, and its default cache key interpolates the runner's system Python rather than the matrix Python — so all eleven jobs computed one identical key. Three jobs lost the race to save it (`Unable to reserve cache`), and the winner's wheels would be restored into jobs targeting a different interpreter. Separately, `sdist-install-check` has no checkout step, so nothing matched the dependency glob and its key degraded to `-no-dependency-glob`, which as setup-uv warns can never be invalidated.

Disabling restores the pre-bump behavior. Nothing is lost: a cold `uv sync` in these jobs resolves in under a second, so the cache was not buying anything to begin with.

## 3. Dependabot config

New `.github/dependabot.yml` covering `github-actions`, so these bumps arrive as PRs from here on. A multi-ecosystem group collapses updates into a single weekly PR rather than one per ecosystem.

Deliberately scoped to Actions only for now. Adding the `uv` ecosystem later needs a considered `versioning-strategy`: the `>=` floors in `[project.dependencies]` are the contract published to consumers, and `install-check` resolves `--resolution lowest-direct` against them, so a strategy that raises those floors would narrow what consumers can install and hollow out that job.

## Verification

CI is green with **zero annotations** (previously four). The run exercises `checkout@v7`, `setup-uv@v10.0.1`, `upload-artifact@v7`, and `download-artifact@v8` across the full support matrix, so the artifact v7 → v8 pairing is proven.

`publish.yml` only fires on a published release, so `setup-python@v7` and the publish-side artifact download go unexercised until the next release.

author: srid
body:
Two commits that are deliberately *not* one. **The kolu pin advances to current master, and Effect moves to `4.0.0-rc.112`** — but this time the second is not a consequence of the first, which is the interesting part.

### The pin: `53a83d1` → `f9ace75`

#90 had to carry kolu and Effect together, because the pin was three weeks stranded on the last kolu revision that still spoke `effect@4.0.0-beta.103`. Nothing like that is true here. Of the six kolu workspace packages odu hydrates (`nix/overlay.nix` → `scripts/hydrate-kolu-packages.sh`) — `surface`, `surface-mcp`, `surface-remote`, `shell-quote`, `surface-map`, `log` — a full recursive diff across the two revisions turns up **exactly one changed line, and it is a comment**:

```diff
--- packages/surface/src/frameChunking.ts
-  * `rejectionFor` / `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` in `@kolu/padi/upload`; olai's
+  * `rejectionFor` / `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` in `@kolu/padi-client/upload`; olai's
```

No file added, removed, or renamed; all six `package.json` files are byte-identical between the revisions. Everything kolu landed since fell outside the hydration set:

| kolu PR | What it did | Why odu doesn't feel it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [#2205](https://github.com/juspay/kolu/pull/2205) | `@kolu/surface-cli` — any surface projected as CLI verbs | New package; odu doesn't hydrate it |
| [#2216](https://github.com/juspay/kolu/pull/2216) | Carved `@kolu/padi-client` out of the daemon | Renames a package odu never consumed — hence the comment above |
| [#2217](https://github.com/juspay/kolu/pull/2217) | The Dock row as a package, plus its attention feeds | kolu's own UI surface |

### Effect: `4.0.0-rc.110` → `4.0.0-rc.112`

kolu master is still on rc.110 — its last Effect move was [kolu#2180](https://github.com/juspay/kolu/pull/2180), *"Effect leaves beta"*, 2026-08-18. **odu takes rc.112 anyway, and the `//overrides` note now records why that is safe rather than reckless.**

Hydration is `cp -rL`, so bun never resolves the `@kolu/*` packages' own dependency blocks — this repo's root `overrides` is the *sole* authority over which Effect kolu's code compiles against, and there is no second realm for `_tag`-based error narrowing to disagree with. What catches a bad bump is `ci::typecheck`: `skipLibCheck` skips `.d.ts` and kolu ships `.ts`, so **all 65 hydrated kolu source files sit in the tsc program**. A realm those sources can't compile against is a red node, not a runtime surprise. They compile.

It also closes a latent split that predates this PR. `@effect/platform-node@rc.110` depends on `@effect/platform-node-shared` by caret while `overrides` named only `effect` and `@effect/platform-node` — so the lock carried `platform-node-shared@4.0.0-rc.111`, whose `peerDependencies` ask for `effect: ^4.0.0-rc.111` against a pinned rc.110. At rc.112 the closure agrees on its own; **no third override needed**.

`bun.lock` is relocked and `bun.nix` regenerated through `nixpkgs-fmt`, so `ci::bun-nix-fresh` agrees.

> One thing left alone on purpose: the `juspay/kolu/agents#master` APM devDependency in `apm.lock.yaml` also tracks kolu master, but it is maintainer-only agent config regenerated by `just apm` — unrelated to the surface libraries this pin governs, and its own change when it wants one.

### Try it locally

```sh
nix run github:juspay/odu/advance-kolu-f9ace75 -- dump
```

author: mpdecker
body:
Fixes the discoverability problem found while driving the reader by hand during the end-to-end run.

## The problem

iOS shows only the first few selection-toolbar entries and hides the rest behind an overflow arrow. The screen's own actions were appended *after* the platform items, so selecting text gave:

```
Copy | Look Up | Search Web | ›
```

**Both Highlight and Note were behind the ›** — one tap deeper than Search Web, on a screen whose entire purpose is annotating. It also contradicted the hint printed directly below: *"Select text to highlight or add a note."*

## The fix

Order the app's actions first. Verified on device:

| | Toolbar |
|---|---|
| Before | `Copy · Look Up · Search Web · ›` |
| After | **`Highlight · Note`** `· Copy · Look Up · ›` |

Search Web moves to the overflow instead, which is the right trade on this screen. Nothing is removed — everything the platform offered is still reachable.

## Why it's extracted

The invariant is now `annotationMenuItemsFirst`, covered by tests, rather than resting on argument order inside a widget tree. That ordering is precisely the kind of detail a later refactor re-breaks silently, and the original bug was invisible to every existing test — it only showed up by looking at the running app.

Three tests: our items lead, platform items keep their relative order, and nothing annotation-related appears when there's no selection.

## Verification
- `flutter analyze` — 0 errors, 0 warnings
- `flutter test` — **383/383** (+3)
- Confirmed on the iPhone 17 simulator with the same long-press gesture that exposed the original problem; zero runtime errors

author: gaborbernat
body:
Linking to a rendered flag required the `:ref:` role with a hand-assembled anchor such as `` :ref:`tox-run---magic` ``, and a program or flag with a capital letter also needed `:force_refs_lower:`. Sphinx resolves the `:option:` role through its own `progoptions` table, keyed on program and option name, which the directive did not fill; https://github.com/tox-dev/sphinx-argparse-cli/issues/345 asks for this.

Each flag and positional argument now also registers with `StandardDomain.add_program_option`, using the same anchor id the `:ref:` labels already point at. `` :option:`tox run --magic` `` resolves, and so does a bare `` :option:`--magic` `` under a `.. program:: tox run` scope, including the `--magic=value` spelling Sphinx strips before lookup. 🔗

Existing URLs and `:ref:` targets stay as they were. Two limits remain. `progoptions` is keyed by program rather than document, so `sphinx_argparse_cli_prefix_document` does not apply and the first document rendering a program wins. Sphinx only strips `=value` when the program comes from `.. program::`, so `` :option:`tox --magic=1` `` stays unresolved. The README covers both.

author: akarshkushwaha
body:
Fixes: #20225 

### What this PR is about
This fixes a server crash in `trigger_workflow#create` caused by a `"\xE2" from ASCII-8BIT to UTF-8` conversion error when downloading GitHub workflow configurations.

### Why this change was made
When `Workflows::YAMLDownloader` downloads a workflow YAML file from GitHub, `Base64.decode64` returns the content as an `ASCII-8BIT` string. However, Rails configures `Tempfile` to expect `UTF-8` text. If the YAML file contains multi-byte characters (like an em-dash), Ruby attempts to transcode the binary string to UTF-8 during `write`, causing an `UndefinedConversionError`. 

By appending `.force_encoding('UTF-8')` before writing, we simply update the string's encoding label so Ruby safely writes the bytes exactly as they are without attempting a broken transcode.

### How to verify
1. Trigger a GitHub workflow sync using a repository where the YAML configuration file contains multi-byte characters (like an em-dash or smart quotes).
2. Verify that the background job successfully saves the file and proceeds, instead of crashing the action with an encoding error.

body:
## What

The remaining three MVP implementation plans, completing the decomposition begun with the resource registry plan.

Documentation only. No code, no schema, no behaviour change.

| Plan | Tasks | Lines |
|---|---|---|
| K2 — Capability Gate | 12 | 1255 |
| K3 — Memory Store | 11 | 671 |
| A1 + S2 — Obsidian slice and effort tuning | 8 | 403 |

## Positions worth reviewing

**K2:** specificity is resolved before mode, so a global deny does not overrule a deliberate per-task allow — that is what makes narrow grants worth granting. A parity fixture pins the six drop rules the current allow-list accumulated before any caller is switched over.

**K3:** the memory push targets the **user** prompt, not the system prompt. System-prompt content is truncated silently at 10 000 characters, head-first, and custom content is prepended — so a block there would delete the stage instructions and leave a well-formed prompt that no longer says what to do.

**A1:** the SSRF guard is not relaxed to reach Obsidian on loopback. The client carries its own dial policy permitting exactly the configured host, rather than widening a check every outbound call depends on. TLS is a three-way decision defaulting to fingerprint pinning, not a silent `-k`.

## One task removed by verification

The capability-gate spec lists outcome-vocabulary normalization as gap G6. It already shipped separately with the ACP fix, so the plan says so and does not schedule it. Writing from the spec rather than from the tree would have produced a task for finished work.

## Known depth difference

K3 and A1 are lighter than the K1 plan at six spots, where a test is given as a commented stub plus an instruction rather than finished code. Where those spots consume K2 or K3 interfaces the reason is deliberate: spelling out exact code against signatures that do not exist yet is precisely the defect pattern that produced five plan defects and four fix rounds during K1 execution. Both plans carry a warning block requiring the merged signatures to be re-read before those tasks are dispatched.

## Sittings: Results stage (`web/public/sittings.html`)

- **On-device scoring** with the published rubric arithmetic (`v = d×w`, `raw = Σv/Σw_max`, `score = round(5 + raw×3)`, DA/IC/PA confidence seeds, caps 0.85/0.70/0.60, NA −0.10, unscored <2, probe-flip / split-candidate / promotion flags). The scorer module is validated in node against the rubrics' worked examples — personal §6.1/§6.2 and corporate §8.1/§8.2 reproduce exactly — plus NA, flip, split, and promotion cases.
- **Results screen**: per-dimension cards (pole pair, 2–8 scale bar, lean, confidence with the instrument-only *act-but-flag* ceiling shown as the effective band), style/voice rule drafts (marked unapproved), absolutes, follow-up questions, Part F echo.

## Dashboard: constitution viewer

- New auth-gated `GET /api/ethos/constitution` returns the active document + parsed status (deliberately not in `PUBLIC_API_PATHS`).
- The Ethos badge is now a button: clicking opens a modal with the version header (company · version · variant · compiled · DEMO warning) and the full document — anyone using the agent can read the rules it runs under. Vanilla mode gets an explainer with the install one-liner.

author: ricardocerdarojas
body:
## El ítem del backlog no era lo que decía

Pedía *"promover `ExegeticalStrategy` a entidad (~15 puntos de contacto)"*. Al mirarlo, resultó ser **un tipo de dos valores** — `'free' | 'dialectical'` — y lo repartido no era el tipo sino **su política**:

- `?? 'free'` en **cuatro** lugares de la interfaz
- `?? 'dialectical'` al crear el paper **y otra vez** al guardarlo
- `=== 'dialectical'` cada vez que había que decidir si mostrar la cobertura por roles
- y la unión `'free' | 'dialectical'` escrita a mano en **dos props**, en vez del tipo del dominio

Seis sitios con la misma decisión copiada — exactamente el reparto que ya hizo divergir el catálogo de modelos (#489) y la tabla de libros bíblicos (#490) esta semana.

## La asimetría que había que preservar

Ahora está **declarada** en vez de implícita:

| Caso | Modo |
|---|---|
| Paper **nuevo** | `dialectical` — el andamiaje ayuda a quien aprende el método |
| Paper **anterior al campo** | `free` |

No es un descuido. Un paper viejo **no eligió método**, así que leerlo como dialéctico lo llenaría de avisos por no haber balanceado unos roles que nunca se le ofrecieron — reprochándole no seguir una metodología que no existía cuando lo escribió.

Es la misma regla que gobierna la procedencia del borrador y la autoría del sermón: **sin dato no se supone nada en contra del usuario.** Hay un test que falla si alguien unifica las dos constantes.

## `usesRoleCoverage(strategy)`

Nombra la pregunta que cada pantalla venía haciendo por su cuenta. Cambiar qué implica el método dialéctico ya no exige recorrer las pantallas una por una.

## No se promueve a entidad, y es deliberado

Una entidad para un valor de dos opciones **sin identidad ni ciclo de vida propio** sería ceremonia. Lo que faltaba era **un lugar donde vivieran sus reglas**, no una clase.

## Verificación

5 paquetes en verde (**7 tests nuevos**, incluido el del valor corrupto: basura en el documento cae al lado que *no* reprocha) · tipos 567 = baseline · i18n 587 · hooks 37 · build ✓

## Para probar en la UI

**Exégesis → crear un paper nuevo**: debe arrancar en dialéctico y mostrar la tarjeta de cobertura por roles en el corpus. **Abrir un paper viejo** (anterior al campo): debe leerse como libre, *sin* avisos de roles. Cambiar el modo en la configuración debe seguir alternando la tarjeta.

author: braven112
body:
## Summary

The Custom Rankings board is now a two-way My Draft List client for every owner. Pull your list down from MFL, reorder it here, push it back to the list the Live Draft Room actually reads.

- **Pull / Push / Undo** against MFL's `myDraftList`, using the owner's own session cookie — the same credential the roster-move endpoints use.
- **Draftable-player filter**, per league: TheLeague drafts rookies only (237 available), the AFL drafts anyone not rostered *in your conference* (2,525).
- **The filter limits the push** — what you see is what gets written.
- **Opened to every owner.** `/cr` was admin-only while it was an unreleased experiment.

## Why the auth shape is what it is

MFL's `import` never honors an APIKEY — for any endpoint — and `myDraftList` exposes no `FRANCHISE_ID`, so there is no commissioner path and no server-side path. A push only happens while its owner is logged in and clicking. That rules out any cron or background reconciler, and it's documented in `docs/claude/insights/domains/mfl-api.md` (which also corrects two February entries that had the APIKEY half wrong).

## Safety, in the order it matters

- The pre-write read is a **stop**, not a warning: if we can't capture the board we're about to replace, we replace nothing.
- The snapshot is of what MFL holds *at push time*, not what the page saw on load, and it survives being restored.
- `pushDraftList` refuses an empty list — MFL would accept one and erase the board.
- A player id the league's feed can't name **blocks** the push instead of being dropped. There are two Justin Jeffersons in the 2026 feed (`14836` WR MIN, `17634` LB CLE rookie) and 39 duplicate names overall.

## The AFL wrinkle

The Free Agents page defines `rostered` as "held in *every* conference" — unavailable to anybody. A draft board has to ask "held in *mine*": the AFL is a duplicate-player league and 60 of its 108 rostered players sit on two rosters at once, so a player held only in the other conference is fully draftable by you. Same shared math (`afl-conference-rosters.mjs`), deliberately different predicate. Fails closed — an untrustworthy roster payload hides the filter rather than hiding players wrongly.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm test:unit` — 270 files, 6,869 tests
- [x] `pnpm test:types` — baseline holds at 1913
- [x] Rendered both boards with a forged owner session in real Chromium
- [x] Push verified by intercepting the POST payload: TheLeague 561 → 22 filtered, AFL 552 → 470
- [x] Pull and push confirmed against **live MFL** by the author
- [ ] CI passes
- [ ] Manual smoke test on Vercel preview

## Known gap, not addressed here

TheLeague's board seeds from veteran-heavy ranking sources, so it carries **22 draftable rookies out of the 237 that exist**. The filter is honest about it, but a rookie-pool league is a thin place to draft from. Seeding from the draftable pool rather than the composite is the obvious follow-up and is deliberately out of scope.

author: johntarbox
body:
On [#1047](https://github.com/JohnTarbox/takemetothefair-cloudflare/pull/1047) (merged, `3999fa5b`, deployed).

#1047 turned the collision into a clean 409. That closed three of the four acceptance criteria and quietly broke the fourth:

> `error_logs` records the collision as a handled event, not `level='error'` with a raw driver string.

Before the fix, a collision at least left an `error` row — that row is how we found the three affected accounts. After it, the pre-flight path logged **nothing**. A collision that keeps happening would look identical to one that had stopped, and the only evidence this affects real people would be gone.

**The old broken behaviour was the observability.** Replacing it with silence is a regression even though the user-facing outcome improved.

## Now

`level='warn'`, `source='api/auth/register:name-collision'`, carrying entity type, slug, and claimed state. No driver string, and no `error` object that could smuggle one in.

It's also the **demand signal**. Every one of these is a vendor already in the directory trying to sign up — the funnel OPE-59 measured at ~0 conversion (1 of 5,289). How often this fires, and whether a claim follows, is the only way to tell whether the claim link from #1047 is worth anything.

## Mutants

| Mutant | Reddens |
|---|---|
| Remove the log entirely | the new handled-event test |
| Log at `level='error'` | same test — handled ≠ error |

`3874` app green under `TZ=UTC`; tsc and eslint clean.

author: nokuchimbetete
body:
The credo sorting screens have been collected from every student since the feature shipped, stored in full, and **never read by the scoring**. Vibes and allocations came only from the multiple-choice questions. Since those spread 25 points across 25 legacies, top scores land at 2 to 5 points, legacies tie constantly, and every tie was settled **alphabetically**.

## Change

`rankLegacies` now accepts the person's credo positions and uses them to order legacies the questions score equally:

1. question score, highest first (unchanged, and still decisive)
2. credo position, where they ranked that legacy on its screen
3. alphabetical, only when the credo cannot separate them either

The credo can never override a higher question score. It only orders equals.

## Measured on the live 2030 cohort (115 completed)

| | |
|---|---|
| tied pairs separated by credo | **5220 / 6262 (83%)** |
| students tied for their top legacy | 57 (50%) |
| ...of those, credo picks a clear winner | **39 (68%)** |
| ...still tied, same position on their screens | 18 (32%) |
| students whose 1st Choice changes | 26 (23%) |
| allocated students whose "Nth choice" number changes | 41 |

The 32% that remain tied are a structural limit: each credo screen only ranks five legacies against each other, so two tied legacies from different screens are never directly compared.

## Consistency

Threaded through every place ranking happens (allocator, both exports, dashboard, and the vibe) so they cannot disagree. Two different tie-breaks in two code paths was exactly the bug reported last time.

## What does not change

- **Existing vibes.** The write-once guard returns early for anyone already finished.
- **Stored allocations.** Only change if an admin re-runs allocation.
- **Displayed ranks do change** for 41 allocated students, because the ranking is now based on their actual preference rather than the alphabet.

`tied` labels now mean something narrower and more useful: same question score *and* nothing in the credo ranking to separate them.

Build passes; unit **134/134** (5 new); integration **46/46**.

author: alnervik
body:
## Summary
This PR fixes how sprite signatures are generated and compared by properly handling transparent pixels in sprite images. Previously, transparent pixels with black RGB values were causing incorrect color bleeding into signature comparisons. Now sprites are composited over a black background before processing, matching the game's visual appearance and ensuring consistent comparisons.

## Key Changes
- **build_signatures.py**: Modified `to_signature()` to composite RGBA sprites over a black background before downscaling, eliminating alpha channel from final signatures
  - Added detailed docstring explaining the transparency handling issue
  - Removed alpha channel from the signature data (now RGB only instead of RGBA)
  - Uses PIL's `paste()` with alpha mask to properly blend transparent areas with black background

- **index.html**: Updated the canvas-based signature extraction to match the new approach
  - Fills canvas with black background before drawing query images
  - Extracts only RGB values from canvas data (skips alpha channel)
  - Added comments explaining the change and linking to build_signatures.py

- **data/signatures.json**: Regenerated with new signature format (RGB-only, no alpha)

## Implementation Details
The core issue was that PIL's downscaling doesn't use premultiplied alpha, causing transparent pixels (often with RGB 0,0,0 from GIF conversion) to contaminate edge pixels with black noise. Additionally, comparing alpha values directly against query images with solid black backgrounds was skewing distance calculations. By compositing over black first, we ensure:
- Transparent areas become actual black pixels
- Signatures match the visual appearance in-game
- Query and database signatures use the same color space (RGB without alpha)

author: jmrplens
body: libgen-mcp **1.7.2** adds `--trusted-origins` and, with it, answers the CORS preflight itself, echoing the caller's origin. The deployment runs it with `*` — the same decision already taken for gitlab, and for the same reason: there is no ambient authority to steal here (no cookies, no session, and libgen takes no credential at all). ### The vhost had to change in the same breath nginx was adding `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` to **both** MCP locations from a shared snippet. With 1.7.2 that would have left `/libgen` answering with **two** of them — which a browser rejects outright (*"contains multiple values"*) while `curl` keeps reporting 200. The release warns about exactly this. So the CORS block moved to its own snippet, `cors_mcp.conf`, included **only** by `/gitlab`: gitlab-mcp-server 2.7.4 still answers `OPTIONS` with 405 and sends no CORS header of its own, so there nginx remains the only layer that can. Verified against the running container, not assumed. | endpoint | who answers CORS | `ACAO` headers on a cross-origin POST | |---|---|---| | `/libgen` | the server (1.7.2) | 1 — echoes the origin | | `/gitlab` | nginx | 1 — `*` | ### Site side - Server cards refreshed by the updater (libgen 1.7.2, gitlab 2.7.4), and the `servers.ts` fallbacks brought level with them. gitlab's had drifted since 2.7.4 auto-deployed. - **The e2e origin shim is gone.** It existed only because the endpoints refused the cross-origin request Playwright makes from `localhost`; libgen now accepts it, so those specs talk to production with nothing rewritten. Full suite **70/70**, including the eight that used to be skipped for lack of egress. ### Verification The decisive check is a real browser on a foreign origin — the only thing that sees a duplicate header. From a page served at `http://127.0.0.1:4392`: ``` libgen: HTTP 200 — event: message data: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":… gitlab: HTTP 401 — {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":null,"error":{"code":-40100,… ``` A CORS failure would be neither of those: it would be a network error before any status. Already deployed. ## Summary by Sourcery Update the MCP deployments and site metadata to provide reliable cross-origin browser access without duplicate CORS headers. Bug Fixes: - Ensure the libgen and gitlab MCP endpoints expose a single valid CORS response for browser clients. Enhancements: - Update the advertised libgen and gitlab server versions and remove the end-to-end test origin workaround now that production endpoints accept the browser requests directly. Deployment: - Adjust the nginx MCP routing so CORS handling is provided by the appropriate layer for each endpoint without duplicate headers. Tests: - Run browser end-to-end coverage against the real MCP endpoints without rewriting request origin metadata. Chores: - Refresh server card and surface metadata for the updated MCP releases. --- ## Summary by cubic Updates `libgen-mcp` to 1.7.2 and `gitlab-mcp-server` to 2.7.5, both of which now answer CORS preflights themselves by echoing the caller's origin. nginx no longer adds a CORS header to either MCP endpoint, so each responds with exactly one `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` header. **Infrastructure** - The nginx CORS block was removed from `/gitlab` only after 2.7.5 landed; the nginx reload happened before the image swap, so the deployment never sent duplicate headers. **Site and tests** - Server cards and `servers.ts` fallbacks bumped to `libgen-mcp` 1.7.2 and `gitlab-mcp-server` 2.7.5. - Removed the e2e origin shim; the full suite runs against production with nothing rewritten, 70/70. - Refreshed the committed `person.snapshot.json` so the fallback matches the canonical #person document. Written for commit 2469ec41197a362f440af6469f2a59ce414c95fb. Summary will update on new commits.

body:
Author-Lane: skills272-sk272-move-scorer-refs

Implements #272's director decision (Option B) — move the 10
`skills/*/references/` files still carrying scorer-resembling language,
leave results and `docs/` analysis public. Do not relitigate A/B/C/D.

## Which 10, and how they were found

Re-ran the issue's own measurement rather than assuming: `grep -rlEi
'GROUND_TRUTH|scorer|PASS-FAIL' skills/*/references/` on current
`origin/main` (`0ac8be3`) returns exactly 10 files — matching the
director's decision comment's own count — and all 10 are
`eval-result.md` files. (Neither `GROUND_TRUTH` nor `PASS-FAIL` appears
anywhere in `skills/` today; every hit is the word "scorer".)

**Flagging this for review rather than silently picking a reading:**
those 10 files are exactly the `eval-result.md` class the brief's own
"what NOT to move" section says stays public ("retrospective outcome
records, not scoring keys"). Reading their content confirms that — each
"scorer" hit is a narrative aside describing an *automated eval
instrument's own bug* ("An automated scorer initially flagged... the
scorer's own keyword match had misread..."), not a checked-in rubric or
answer key. There is no literal scoring key in any of these 10 files.

## What this PR actually does

Given that content reality, full deletion of these files would (a)
contradict the "eval-result.md stays public" policy stated two
paragraphs above the "10 files move" instruction in the same brief, and
(b) break `scripts/eval_status.py`'s `check()`, which hard-requires each
skill's recorded `evidence` path to exist as a real file in *this* repo
— deleting the file would turn all 10 skills' entries into a genuine
`evidence path ... does not exist` finding, i.e. recreate the exact
broken-pointer failure class #282's lane already found once tonight,
this time as a harder outright check failure instead of a softer
`could_not_measure`.

So: **edited these 10 files in place, not deleted.** For each, the
paragraph containing the scorer-instrument narrative moved verbatim into
the private `jonhill90/agent-evals` repo (companion PR:
jonhill90/agent-evals#26 — do not merge either side alone until both are
ready, see below). What remains in this repo is the verdict line
(scorer-free reword where the word appeared there), a short scorer-free
outcome summary, and the file's pre-existing "evidence lives in
agent-evals, private repo" citation paragraph, **unchanged**.

File **paths** under `skills/*/references/` did not change — only
content. That means every existing pointer keeps resolving without
modification: `docs/eval-status.json`'s 10 `evidence` fields,
`docs/eval-log/<skill>.jsonl`, and the two `docs/` prose citations
(`docs/eval-cost-delta-recount.md` → `mechanize`,
`docs/eval-pass15-remaining-four.md` → `prd`).

## Verification (the acceptance test, not a proxy)

```
$ python3 scripts/validate_repository.py
Validated 41 skill(s): 0 error(s), 0 warning(s)

$ python3 scripts/eval_status.py
clean: 41 skill(s) recorded, record matches skills/

$ python3 scripts/eval_status.py --summary
could_not_measure: 29
drop: 1
improve: 8
keep: 3
rename: 0
unevaluated: 0
```
Byte-identical to the numbers #272's own decision comment recorded
before this move — the verdict record was not touched, only the
scorer-language prose.

```
$ python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
Ran 187 tests in 3.6s
OK
```
(This run also caught two real regressions from an earlier draft of
this PR — a `tests/evals` internal-path leak and a line-wrap that broke
the private-repo "not publicly available" disclosure phrase across two
lines — both fixed before this push;
`tests/test_validate_repository.py::NoDanglingEvalReferenceTests` is
what caught them.)

```
$ npx skills add . --list
```
exits 0, lists all 41 skills including the 10 touched here.

## Coordination with the agent-evals side

Companion PR: jonhill90/agent-evals#26 (private repo, not linkable
here). Because this PR doesn't change any evidence path, there is no
merge-ordering hazard for `eval_status.py` — this side is self-contained
and green with or without the private PR merged first. Merging the
agent-evals side is still worth doing so the full write-ups actually
land somewhere, but it is not a blocking dependency for this PR's own
checks.

## Untouched, per the brief

- `eval-blocked.md`, `eval-case.md` files — not moved, not edited.

## Summary

* add an explicit regression test for a beach with a non-website contact and no approved business claim
* verify `website` remains `NOT_APPLICABLE`
* verify no phantom `MISSING_FIELD` issue is generated for `website`

## Scope

* `fdd9dc7 test(data): cover beach contacts without approved operator`

author: manolbh
body:
## Résumé
- Remplace le classement automatique par titre (`sortChaptersByNaturalTitle`, `revision-chapter-sort.js` — supprimé) par une numérotation manuelle 1..n des chapitres **ouverts** d'une matière, dans le widget « Chapitres » (onglet Révisions).
- Case carrée numérotée (remplace l'icône « tableau ») → clic → panneau de choix (grille de n numéros, numéro actuel désactivé) → déplacement + renumérotation atomique côté SQL via `public.reorder_chapter(p_chapter_id, p_new_position)`.
- Bulle « Chapitre » retirée de la ligne (code mort associé nettoyé dans `renderModePill`).
- Fermeture / suppression d'un chapitre ouvert renumérotent automatiquement les chapitres ouverts restants de la matière (triggers SQL, aucun changement requis côté front sur `closeChapterForProject`).
- Création d'un chapitre : toujours `max(position)+1`, désormais scopé aux seuls chapitres **ouverts** (`computeNextChapterPosition`).

## Décision de conception validée
La numérotation 1..n est scopée aux chapitres **ouverts** d'une matière (option recommandée, confirmée en amont). Un chapitre fermé garde une position gelée, hors de la séquence active — il n'affiche plus de case, seulement l'icône `table-check` existante. L'unicité est portée par une colonne dérivée `open_position` (NULL si fermé) plutôt qu'un index partiel, pour pouvoir la rendre `deferrable initially deferred` (un index partiel ne peut pas l'être).

## Schéma
- Migration `supabase/migrations/202608270001_chapter_manual_position.sql` :
  - backfill de `public.chapters.position` reproduisant l'ordre actuellement affiché (tri naturel par titre, par matière et par statut ouvert/fermé) — aucun mouvement visuel au déploiement ;
  - colonne dérivée `open_position` (generated, NULL si fermé) + contrainte unique déferrable `(matter_id, open_position)` ;
  - fonction `chapters_renumber_open(matter_id)` + triggers `AFTER UPDATE OF closed_at` et `AFTER DELETE` sur `public.chapters` ;
  - RPC `public.reorder_chapter(p_chapter_id uuid, p_new_position integer)`, `security invoker`, borne 1..n, verrou advisory par matière.
- Appliquée automatiquement au merge via `auto-apply-migrations.yml` — rien à lancer en local.

## Tests
23 nouveaux tests (`node --test`) :
- `apps/web/js/views/project-situations/revision-chapter-position.test.mjs` (17) : tri par position, rendu de la case/panneau, ouverture/fermeture (clic case, clic extérieur, Échap — assertions sur le code source des écouteurs), non-propagation du clic, `computeNextChapterPosition` (création = max+1 parmi les ouverts), succès/échec du déplacement (message d'erreur explicite, pas de mise à jour optimiste silencieuse).
- `supabase/functions/chapter-manual-position-migration-source.test.mjs` (6) : structure de la migration (transaction, backfill partitionné, colonne dérivée, contrainte déferrable non partielle, triggers de renumérotation, clamp 1..n de la RPC, `security invoker`).
- Suite complète : 2608/2608 verts (dont les 385 tests déjà en place dans `project-situations` et `project-subjects`, aucune régression).

## À vérifier manuellement après déploiement
- [ ] Après merge + application de la migration, ouvrir l'onglet Révisions sur une matière existante : la liste ne doit **pas** bouger visuellement (backfill reproduit l'ordre actuel).
- [ ] Cliquer une case → le panneau s'ouvre sous la case, numéro actuel grisé/désactivé ; choisir un autre numéro déplace la ligne et renumérote sans trou.
- [ ] Clic en dehors du panneau / touche Échap → fermeture sans changement ; le clic sur la case n'ouvre pas le chapitre.
- [ ] Fermer un chapitre (icône poubelle du swipe) → les chapitres ouverts restants se renumérotent 1..n ; le chapitre fermé garde l'icône `table-check`, sans case.
- [ ] Créer un nouveau chapitre (fichier ou vide) → apparaît en dernière position (n+1) parmi les ouverts.
- [ ] Vérifier que la page Matière (`project-subject-chapters.js`, hors périmètre de ce chantier) n'affiche rien d'anormal pour les chapitres fermés existants (leur `position` reste celle du backfill, non renumérotée par la suite).
