author: antoniolocascio
body:
The ZiSK multi-proof verifier lane on `release/v0.33.0-atomic-interop`. **Supersedes #2419**, which sat on `draft-v31`.

## What the lane does

`MultiProofVerifier` requires BOTH an Airbender proof and a ZiSK proof for each state transition, and accepts only the combined proof type 5. It folds nothing: the batch public inputs reach both sub-verifiers whole. The wrapped ZKsync OS verifier owns the fold the settlement layer defines, and `ZiskVerifier` rebuilds its own chain in `_selfContainedChain`.

The ZiSK public values are **not carried in the proof**. Every range, single batch or many, is one aggregated proof, and `ZiskVerifier` reconstructs the 320-byte public values on-chain from its own pinned VKs plus the batch public inputs. That makes the cross-proof binding inherent: a ZiSK proof attesting to a different transition reconstructs a different SNARK signal and fails the pairing.

The carried-hash slot (`_proof[1]`) and every header bit at or above 8 in `_proof[0]` are reserved and must be zero.

## Testnet fake modes

Testnets preserve the real type-5 path for all three server modes:

- `Real`: real Airbender + real ZiSK.
- `FakeZisk`: real Airbender + a padded, public-input-bound ZiSK mock component.
- `FakeAll`: canonical Airbender and ZiSK mock components inside type 5.

The multiprover deployment composes `MultiProofTestnetVerifier -> MultiProofVerifier -> {ZKsyncOSTestnetVerifier, ZiskTestnetVerifier}`. `ZiskTestnetVerifier` accepts only the canonical 24-word padded mock component `[3, 0, 13, foldedPublicInput, 0...]`; every other proof delegates unchanged to the real ZiSK verifier. Production still wires the strict Airbender and ZiSK verifiers directly.

## The fold

The settlement layer folds a range as one keccak over the **concatenated untruncated** batch public inputs, with `PUBLIC_INPUT_SHIFT` applied once at the end. A single batch short-circuits with no keccak. `ZiskVerifier`, the ZiSK aggregator guest, and both testnet fake-component verifiers apply that same rule.

The guest side is already in: matter-labs/zksync-os-zisk#26 made the cutover and #30 rotated the fixtures.

## Pins

| | |
|---|---|
| inner programVK | `0x8168c5d383a50a9c7a40561b82bf679cc6dfdab0308417b4fea653362d78d080` |
| aggregator programVK | `0xf68b9862e424e377af7b4220a419ce45bc52ce70b0a37aea486a15a5ca38b738` |
| vadcop-final root | `0xcf2a309856f107b143836ada112806da71ae11567fa3f2d2050baba5381c7b7d` |
| `_VK_HASH` | `0x9d04cf648d751264abba6492119b5b141daab63ed501d24813919a939512a999` |

`_VK_HASH` is `keccak256(innerProgramVK || aggregatorProgramVK || rootCVadcopFinal)`. The server derives the ZiSK verification key hash of the protocol version the same way, so a rotation of any pin is visible on both sides.

## ZiSK kill switch

A chain admin can settle without a ZiSK proof through `setZiskVerificationDisabled(bool)` on the Admin facet (`onlyAdmin onlyZKsyncOS`), read back through `IGetters`. `MultiProofVerifier` reads the requirement from its caller, which in production is the chain's diamond, because one verifier serves every chain of a protocol version through `ChainTypeManager.protocolVersionVerifier`.

## Deployment and protocol_ops

`multi_proof_verifier` is absent/off by default. With the flag off, `DeployCTM` uses the original verifier selection and the deployed set is unchanged.

`protocol-ops ecosystem init` and `ctm init` now carry:

- `multi_proof_verifier`
- `zisk_plonk_verifier_addr`
- optional `zisk_range_verifier_addr`

Invalid VM/address combinations fail before Forge runs. The CTM output also exposes the Airbender, ZiSK, ZiSK testnet, and multi-proof verifier addresses when that lane is deployed.

The snarkJS Plonk verifier is GPL-3.0, so it remains generated, deployed standalone, and referenced by address rather than committed as Solidity source. `DeployCTM` refuses an address with no code. A companion zk-deployer change generates/builds and deploys this contract before calling `ecosystem init`, then passes the resulting address through the fields above.

## Verification

- Focused `MultiProofVerifier`, `ZiskTestnetVerifier`, and deployment Foundry suites: **32 passed**.
- `protocol-ops` unit tests: **33 passed**.
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Selector regeneration/check, Foundry build (EVM + ZKsync), Solhint, and Prettier: clean.

`ZiskVerifierRealProofTest` drives real ZiSK proofs through the real pairing when the generated Plonk verifier is present; CI generates it in `check-verifier-generator-l1`.

body:
## Description

PR 4 of the stack described in #31292. Replaces #31180, which GitHub would not let me retarget.

The automations page gains a second tab, Slack workflows, listing what is allowed with the spaces each one reaches, when it was added and a revoke button. Adding one takes the sender name Slack shows on the workflow's messages, which has to match exactly, plus the spaces it may reach; we cannot enumerate workflows from the Slack API, so the name stays manual entry and the dialog says so. The tab carries its own credits card so workflow spend sits next to the triggers one. Admins on legacy plans do not see the tab and keep going through poke.

The spaces dropdown fetches on open and filters client side. No endpoint searches spaces by name today, worth adding if the list gets long.

## Tests

Covered end to end by the endpoint suites in PRs 2 and 3. Checked the tab against a dev workspace seeded with `slack_workflow` consumption and 30 allowed workflows spread over several spaces: search, sorting on name and date, pagination, allow, revoke, and the empty state for a workspace with no Slack bot.

## Risk

An admin on a credit-priced plan can now grant a Slack workflow access to their spaces' agents without us. That is the point, and it stays scoped to spaces the admin already administers. Anyone who can run the workflow in Slack can summon those agents, guests included, which the dialog states.

## Deploy Plan

Deploy front. Nothing to do on connectors: the message the bot posts when it refuses an unknown workflow still points at support.

author: camilohollanda
body:
Espelha para o `iddh-members` o que o `ops/werify-digest-promotion` (#10) já fez para o werify.

## Problema

As Applications `iddh-members-production` e `iddh-members-staging` acompanham as tags imutáveis `main-<sha>` / `staging-<sha>` com `newest-build` — estratégia que escolhe pelo campo `created` interno da imagem e **ignora a tag de ambiente por completo**.

Consequências:

- **Rollback é impossível.** Reposicionar `:main` num artefato anterior é invisível para o reconciliador. Mesmo um override direto na Application é substituído em ~2 min por qualquer `main-<sha>` que tenha sido construído por último.
- O `created` é sensível a cache: com camadas reaproveitadas, a ordem que o `newest-build` infere pode não ser a ordem real dos deploys.

## Mudança

Digest-tracking de `:main` / `:staging` torna a tag de ambiente o ponteiro explícito de promoção. O CI do members publica as tags imutáveis primeiro e só move essa tag depois de um build bem-sucedido, atrás de uma guarda de digest; e o workflow manual "Deploy members app" a move registry-side para promote/rollback.

## Impacto no que está rodando: nenhum

Verificado contra o registry e o cluster antes de abrir:

| tag | digest | rodando |
|---|---|---|
| `:main` | `sha256:f00cc389…` | `main-4b12b58` — mesmo digest |
| `:staging` | `sha256:4ed27eab…` | `staging-19eb2a1` — mesmo digest |

Os dois Deployments já referenciam `:main` / `:staging` nos manifests. A troca não dispara rollout.

## Ordem de merge

Companheiro de iddh-com-br/members#145. Este PR pode ir antes ou junto: sob o workflow atual do members, `:main` e `:staging` continuam sendo publicados a cada build, então o digest-tracking já funciona para deploy normal. Sem ele, a guarda de digest e o rollback manual daquele PR ficam inertes.

## Summary

- The chatbot's burst rate limit (`LIMITE_CONSULTAS = "4/10second;120/hour"`, `chatbot_router.py`) is **deliberately left unchanged**. It is real cost protection once a paid provider is configured, and it now behaves as documented once more (issue #739 switched the free-tier model, and the owner separately confirmed the limit itself is not the bug). Issue #708's finding was that the 429 it produces LIED about why: it read as a generic outage ("no disponible") instead of "you sent several questions in a row, here's when you can try again." This PR fixes only that message — do not raise `LIMITE_CONSULTAS` to work around this; the owner explicitly rejected that.
- `ApiClientError` gains `retryAfterSeconds`, following the exact same pattern PR #723 used for `code`: the BFF's chatbot route now forwards the backend's `Retry-After` header (set by `_manejador_limite_excedido` in `backend/main.py`) instead of dropping it, and the client parses it off the response.
- `ChatWidget` no longer folds a 429 into the generic `mensajeDeError` switch. It has its own path: an honest, non-scolding message — "Hizo varias consultas seguidas. Espere {N} segundos y vuelva a intentarlo." — using the REAL wait from `Retry-After` (falling back to a defensive 10s only if the header is somehow absent), and it locks the composer (input + send + quick replies) for that same wait so a visitor can't type into a field that would just 429 again. The lock lifts itself automatically once the countdown reaches zero — no action needed.

## Why the composer is locked, not just the message

An input that still looks live but silently drops whatever's typed into it during the cooldown would be its own small dishonesty — the same class of problem this PR is fixing. Disabling it for the stated wait, with the alert as the visible reason, keeps what the UI shows in sync with what it will actually do.

## Tests

New/updated, each verified red against current `main` before the fix:
- `frontend/src/app/api/chatbot/__tests__/route.test.ts` — the BFF forwards `Retry-After` on a 429, and invents none on other statuses.
- `frontend/src/services/__tests__/api.test.ts` — `ApiClientError.retryAfterSeconds` carries the parsed wait, and stays `undefined` when absent/non-numeric.
- `frontend/src/components/chatbot/__tests__/ChatWidget.test.tsx` — a 429 shows the real wait (not a hardcoded number), never says "no disponible"/"no se pudo contactar", locks the composer, falls back sanely when `Retry-After` is missing, and re-enables the composer on its own once the wait elapses (real-timer test). A genuine 5xx still renders the connectivity message and does NOT lock the composer, proving the two failure classes don't collapse into one.

```
cd frontend && pnpm run type-check   # clean
cd frontend && pnpm test             # 248 files, 4226 tests, all passing
cd frontend && pnpm run lint         # clean (pre-existing unrelated warning in app/sponsors/page.tsx, same as noted in #723)
```

Backend untouched — no backend changes, so no `uv run pytest` / `ruff check` needed here.

## Verified live (browser, Playwright)

QA stack at `127.0.0.1:3000` (unpatched `main` @ `22a0189`, no chatbot provider configured — degraded/instant-fallback mode, ~6ms replies). Sent 6 messages back-to-back through the real widget; the 5th trips the limit. **Before:** alert reads *"Está preguntando muy seguido. Espere unos segundos y vuelva a intentarlo."* — no real wait, and the composer stays fully interactive (only the transient `enviando` disable applies) so it 429s again on the next keystroke.

Patched build stood up on `127.0.0.1:3011` (production standalone server, same backend). Same 6-message burst. **After:** alert reads *"Hizo varias consultas seguidas. Espere 10 segundos y vuelva a intentarlo."*, matching `retry-after: 10` on the actual 429 response (confirmed via curl on the same server; a burst fired closer to the previous window's edge showed `retry-after: 7` instead — always the real remaining time, not a constant coincidentally reading the same as the 10s fallback). Both the input and the send button were disabled (`disabled: true`) for the full duration; polled again ~11s later and the composer had re-enabled itself and the alert had cleared, with no visitor action.

Closes #708

author: tomaszjanusz
body:
## Summary Hostile page scripts can still reach iframe ownership and Canvas after Preview: they shadow `hasAttribute` / `getAttribute` on the element, poison `String.prototype.trim` and `Set`/`WeakSet` lookups, replace all three Canvas export anchors, or swap in a non-configurable sentinel that we used to treat as a new native baseline. This change captures Element and string primordials for iframe topology, classifies `about:blank`, `javascript:`, `vbscript:`, `srcdoc`, http(s), and opaque `blob:`/`data:`/`filesystem:` destinations, and restores Canvas `getImageData` / `toDataURL` / `toBlob` whenever the prototype identity is unchanged. Non-configurable replacements stay in place instead of becoming the new baseline. Playwright now checks that a real dedicated Worker bootstrap-ack never appears as the first page `message` and that X-Ray does not mark the worker as failed or degraded. The Firefox `main-world-runtime.js` budget gate is kept by leaving destination classification out of the injected hot path instead of raising `FX_MAIN_WORLD_MAX_BYTES`. Parent ownership names `javascript:`, `vbscript:`, and `data:` together; only the first two are parent-owned. ## Validation - [x] `pnpm task lint` - [x] `pnpm task check` - [x] `pnpm task test:unit` - [x] Both targets still build (`pnpm task build:chrome`, `pnpm task build:firefox`) - [x] Worker bundle regenerated if `packages/refract-core` changed (`pnpm task generate:worker-source`) Also passed: `pnpm task check:worker-source`, `pnpm task format:check`, focused canvas Chromium/Firefox tests, iframe ownership tests, `tests/build-contracts/firefox-build.test.ts` (runtime 169127 B ≤ 169216 B), `tests/build-contracts/chromium-build.test.ts`, and `PT_E2E_LANE=core` Playwright `extension-runtime.spec.ts` `-g bootstrap-ack`. ## Changelog - [x] I updated `CHANGELOG.md` in `## [Unreleased]` for user-facing changes. - [ ] This change does not need a changelog entry (internal/test/CI/refactor only).
  
--- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. Autofix is disabled. > [!NOTE] > ### Harden iframe ownership and canvas integrity against prototype tampering > - Canvas: when page code replaces `getImageData`/`toDataURL`/`toBlob` without changing prototype identity, [syncCanvasInstall](https://github.com/Privacy-Thing/browser-extension/pull/19/files#diff-98ef731c95aeed08c52ecea79b16ed4f4cdcd932269c4d5b147b17bebf7f805b) now treats this as tampering and restores all three wrappers via `restoreCanvasAnchor` instead of dropping the cached installation; added `resetCanvasInstall` to clear the per-global cache. > - Iframe ownership: [iframe-realm-ownership.ts](https://github.com/Privacy-Thing/browser-extension/pull/19/files#diff-fc5aa3479881a0f416ed4319e7b866de99850d85882287abd0689af144e7083b) captures `Element.prototype.hasAttribute`/`getAttribute` and `String.prototype.trim` at module load and routes all attribute reads and trimming through these captured intrinsics, so instance shadowing or later prototype poisoning cannot alter ownership decisions. > - Added `classifyIframeDest` and reworked `shouldParentOwnFrame`: `about:blank`, `javascript:`, and `vbscript:` are parent-owned; `data:` is destination-owned; all other non-about schemes are not parent-owned. > - Iframe installers in [iframe-patch.ts](https://github.com/Privacy-Thing/browser-extension/pull/19/files#diff-727f21c7a38d29ca5f7f5bffabde185fd431e84d03eb3c8b0cc3abe25ce010d5) and [iframe-realm-installer.ts](https://github.com/Privacy-Thing/browser-extension/pull/19/files#diff-5e52eb888bb158c98c8fbabc9faae1c546a19aa38ceea01d61a0faf536077781) now use `privateWeakSetHas`/`privateWeakSetAdd` and `iframeHasSrcdoc` instead of direct `WeakSet`/element methods. > - Behavioral Change: `shouldParentOwnFrame` now classifies `data:` iframes as destination-owned (previously could be parent-owned) and relies on captured intrinsics for `hasAttribute`/`getAttribute`/`trim`; reviewers should verify the decision matrix in [shouldParentOwnFrame](https://github.com/Privacy-Thing/browser-extension/pull/19/files#diff-fc5aa3479881a0f416ed4319e7b866de99850d85882287abd0689af144e7083b) matches expected ownership semantics for `data:` and `srcdoc` cases. > > > > Macroscope summarized a2f2090. > > ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Improved Canvas protection by detecting and recovering from tampering with image and export methods. * Improved iframe handling across destinations such as blank, inline, web, blob, data, and JavaScript URLs. * Increased resilience when page scripts override browser methods. * Fixed navigation seed handling when input contains surrounding whitespace. * **Tests** * Added coverage for Canvas recovery, iframe ownership, and dedicated worker runtime behavior.

author: roseoutllc
body:
## Why
After #1971, a clean production run of `lobster ravioli in Queens` completed in ~2.07s but still ranked Nikko Hibachi #1 using only the inferred `seafood` parent. A lower-ranked Kyuramen had actual lobster evidence.

The scorer also allowed a single canonical token such as `lobster` to count as matching the full multiword phrase `lobster ravioli`, which made fallback evidence look stronger than it really was.

## Change
- Add strict dish-evidence matching: multiword dish phrases require the full phrase; single-word dish components may use canonical evidence.
- Give dish-specific fallback coverage higher intent strength than broad inferred cuisine-only matches.
- Apply a small bounded penalty to broad restaurant fallbacks that have no dish-specific evidence.
- Preserve the existing exact single-menu-item match and +8 exact-menu boost as the strongest evidence.
- Do not change candidate pool sizes.

## Regression coverage
- Exact `farfalle cacio e pepe` still wins.
- Split `lobster` + `ravioli` evidence ranks above weaker fallback but is never labeled exact.
- A 2.6-mile lobster-evidence candidate must outrank a 0.3-mile seafood-only candidate.

## Production baseline before this PR
- exact dish: 3.33s total / 3.12s retrieval / 2.1ms ranking, American Brass #1
- fallback: 2.07s total / 2.04s retrieval / 7.2ms ranking, relevance still wrong

author: claude[bot]
body:
⚠️ **RUTA SENSIBLE (LÍMITE 1): ESTE PR MODIFICA `.harness/harness.mjs`**, el motor que es toda la cadena de verificación del arnés. En un PR la CI corre la versión de esta rama, así que el cambio se auto-valida: revísalo con ese cuidado. No toca `permissions:`, secrets, CODEOWNERS ni ningún workflow.

## Tarea elegida y por qué esa

**Nivel 3 — Motor y agentes → robustez en `.harness/harness.mjs`**: siguiente punto de fricción **real** (con evidencia), en la línea de los ~14 guardianes de "falso verde" ya fusionados (#12–#32).

Elegí ésta y no otra porque los niveles 1 y 2 del backlog están **agotados** (adaptadores Go/Rust/Java, coherencia de docs, ejemplos go/rust — todos MERGED #2–#9) y no hay ramas `autonomous/*` huérfanas sin PR (las remotas que existen corresponden a PRs ya fusionados). Dentro del nivel 3 preferí la robustez del motor con evidencia reproducible antes que reescribir prompts de agentes (que exige un desvío *observable* que no tengo).

**El bug (evidencia reproducible):** `name` valida su tipo desde #24, pero `id` —el **otro** campo-clave, que la unicidad de #22 normaliza con `String(f.id)`— quedó **sin guardar**. Un `id` no-escalar se coacciona en silencio y rompe la identidad de dos formas simétricas:

- **FALSO ROJO:** `String([1]) === String(1) === "1"`, así que `id:[1]` e `id:1` se reportan como `id duplicado en features: 1` sin serlo realmente.
- **FALSO VERDE (el peor, límite 2):** dos ids no-escalares **distintos** (`{}` y `[]`) coaccionan a `"[object Object]"` y `""`, no colisionan, y la lista pasa como `feature_list.json válido (2 features)` en verde con dos features de identidad rota. `status`, además, las pinta como `#[object Object]`.

**El arreglo:** un `id` PRESENTE debe ser `string` o `number`; `null`/ausente siguen siendo "sin id" (el id es opcional, igual que ya asumía el filtro de unicidad). La unicidad ahora solo coacciona ids escalares, así que un id malformado produce **un** `[FAIL]` claro que nombra la causa, no un "id duplicado" confuso. Misma familia y forma que el string-leaf de paths/commands (#15) y el guardián de `name` (#24).

Diff: +30 líneas en `.harness/harness.mjs` (guardián + ajuste del filtro de unicidad) y +6 tests de regresión en `.harness/test/engine.test.mjs`.

## Verificación real ejecutada

Comandos y su resultado (no "debería pasar"):

- **Reproducción del bug ANTES del arreglo** (en un tmpdir, sobre el motor sin parchear):
  - `id:[1]` + `id:1` → `[FAIL] id duplicado en features: 1` (falso rojo). ✅ reproducido
  - `id:{}` + `id:[]` → `[OK] feature_list.json válido (2 features)`, `status` exit 0 (falso verde). ✅ reproducido
  - `id:{}` en `status` → `#[object Object]`. ✅ reproducido
- **Suite del motor** (la red de regresión de #20): `node --test .harness/test/engine.test.mjs`
  → **`# tests 67  # pass 67  # fail 0`** (61 previos + 6 nuevos). ✅
- **Árbol raíz verde:** `node .harness/harness.mjs init` → **exit 0** (con el WARN de diseño de `commands.test` vacío, esperado por el límite 4/5). ✅
- Comprobado a mano tras el arreglo: `id:[1]`/`id:1` ya NO dan "id duplicado" sino el `[FAIL]` de id no-escalar; `id:{}`/`id:[]` ya NO pasan como "válido".

No toqué los ejemplos ni comandos de mutación, así que no corresponde correr sus suites/mutación para este cambio (el gate del motor es la suite de arriba).

## Qué NO cubrí y por qué

- **No wireé el job `engine-tests` en `.github/workflows/harness-ci.yml`.** `docs/verification.md` (líneas 92–100) lo documenta, pero el workflow **no** lo tiene: la suite del motor hoy solo corre en local, no en CI. Es una inconsistencia **preexistente** (anterior a este PR) y de otra tarea; añadirla tocaría un segundo fichero sensible (límite 1) y rompería "una sola tarea por ejecución". La dejo señalada aquí para que un humano decida wirearlo — mientras tanto, verifiqué los 6 tests nuevos en local (salida arriba).
- **No añadí guardián de `id` como CAMPO OBLIGATORIO.** El `id` sigue siendo opcional (varios fixtures lo omiten); solo valido su forma cuando está presente, para no cambiar un contrato establecido.

author: joao-araujoo
artur-
body:
copyFilesFromJar_doNotUpdateFileIfContentIsTheSame asserted that the copied file was older than System.currentTimeMillis() read right after the copy. That comparison truncates the reference time to whole milliseconds while the file modification time carries sub-millisecond precision, so it only holds when a millisecond boundary happens to fall between writing the file and reading the clock. On fast machines it usually does not, and the test fails.

Record the file's own modification time before the second copy and assert it is unchanged afterwards, which is what the test is actually about.

Backport of ce57f79c798d44520740b4bec0ed254d70914699, already on 24.8 and later.

Makes the 4 React hooks in `src/hooks/` actually reachable, and fixes the missing `react` dependency declaration:

author: cole-zoom
body:
Editing `scene.json` updates an open Blender viewport in **~36ms**, instead of costing a render to look at anything.

```bash
blended watch projects/lancedb/scene.json
# then install addon/blended_live.py, press N ▸ blended tab
```

### The architecture already allowed this

`blended_backend` has been restricted to stdlib + `bpy` since Phase 0, purely to keep the host/guest boundary honest. That restriction is exactly what lets the **same build code** run inside the GUI — the add-on imports `build()` directly. No subprocess, no second implementation.

### `clear()` not `reset()`

`reset()` calls `read_factory_settings`, which is right for a background render and would **throw away your open file** in the GUI. `clear()` removes built content only, so viewport angle, selection and timeline position survive a rebuild. Verified: a scene property set before rebuilding is still there after two rebuilds, with no duplicate objects and no orphaned meshes.

```
REBUILD 1: 65ms  480 frames
REBUILD 2: 36ms  480 frames
REBUILD 3: 37ms  480 frames
```

### Modal timer, not a thread

`bpy` is not thread-safe — touching scene data off the main thread crashes Blender rather than misbehaving. A test asserts `threading` never appears in the add-on.

### Cleanup

Eight scene variants, 16 `.blend` files, 9 videos, 12 stills — **102 MB** — replaced by a single `projects/lancedb/scene.json` carrying the settings the work converged on.

**That deletion silently disabled 4 tests**, which skipped on a missing path rather than failing. They now point at the live project and assert what it actually is: a spot lamp rather than a sun, ripples off, relief damped where wet.

**121 passing, none skipped.**

author: rbstp
body:
## What exists, and what changed

The streak was drill-only: `drill.js record()` kept a running counter in `cnpe:v2`'s `drillmeta` (day, n, earned, streak, best), shown on the drill page tiles and the dashboard's Drill button. Verifying an exercise, completing a section or scoring a mock exam task was invisible to it.

Now there is ONE console-wide streak, and it speaks the audience's language: **Study uptime**. Every positive action records into a new store key `days` (local `"YYYY-MM-DD"` -> `{c, x, s, e}`: cards answered, exercises verified, sections completed, exam tasks scored), bumped on the same code paths that already save those actions. Un-ticking is not an action and never counts. The streak and its record are **derived from the map at render time**, never stored as counters, so merged or imported history recomputes instead of fighting a stored total. Alive if today or yesterday qualifies, local dates, the drill's own day key.

UI, in the console's existing idiom:
- Dashboard stats row: a **Study uptime** tile (`N days · record R`) with an eight-week heartbeat strip: one cell per day, newest bottom right, existing `--moss`/`--surface-3` tokens via classes, per-cell tooltips with the day's heartbeat count. The static "Domains: 5" filler tile retired to keep the row at five tiles (the article is 940px; a sixth tile wraps the row). The strip sits in the stats row, which the existing print stylesheet hides like every stat tile; the cells carry `print-color-adjust` so they read anywhere they do print.
- The Drill button now says `Drill 10 · up N days`; the drill page tile and session summary carry the unified number, while the drill keeps its own ten-cards daily-goal line untouched.
- Prose updated on drill.html ("the streak is console-wide, and it reads like uptime... a day with none takes the streak down, and unlike your workloads it does not self-heal"), index.html and the curriculum README.

## Seeding and migration

Nobody's current streak resets the day this ships: on first run (and again after an import merges a `drillmeta`), an alive legacy streak of N ending on `earned` backfills the N days ending there; a dead one only carries its best forward as the record. Export/Import merges `days` as a per-day, per-counter max (union of days, never lowering a count), through the existing `mergeProgress` choke point; Reset clears it; the store initializer tolerates junk in the new key like the existing buckets. `drillmeta` stays maintained so an export read by an older console still shows a sane streak.

## CI: the browser pass becomes a gate

There was no Playwright check in the workflows; the `site` job only asserts the staged files exist. `curriculum/tools/streak-check.js` (new) drives the staged site over `file://` in headless Chromium, and runs both at PR time (new `browser` job in ci.yml) and in the deploy workflow, keeping the repo's stated invariant that the deploy gate and the merge gate cannot drift apart. Playwright is a pinned (`1.56.1`), CI-only `npm --no-save` install: no manifest or lockfile is written and the console itself stays dependency-free. `make streak` gives it a local entry point next to `make site` and `make grade`.

## Verification

- `node --check` on every touched JS; `python3 tools/extract-drill.py --check` green (drill-data.js untouched); `python3 tools/bundle.py`; `tools/check-site.sh` (35 html files).
- **44/44 Playwright assertions** against the staged site, run through the committed script exactly as CI invokes it (Playwright-managed headless Chromium, no CHROMIUM_BIN): each action type (drill answer, exercise verify, section complete, exam dot) heartbeats the day once; un-tick never increments; seeded multi-day history renders the right streak, record and heat strip (56 cells, correct lit count); a gap day breaks the streak; drillmeta seeding preserves an alive legacy streak (earned today and earned yesterday) and a dead one keeps only its record; export -> import into a fresh profile carries history and the merge never lowers a count; the bundle behaves across `#index` and `#DR` hash routes with repeated `boot()` re-runs; junk stores boot clean; zero console errors throughout, both themes.
- Heat strip eyeballed in light and dark (screenshots via the script's `STREAK_SHOTS` mode).

body:
## What

`build_handlers` registered 3 of 13 enqueued outbox job types. Ten fell to
`unroutable`. Five of those ten are the notices the paying traveller is supposed to
receive; this PR routes them, plus the practice-received notice:

| job type | state guard | what the traveller gets |
|---|---|---|
| `checkout_ready_email` | `awaiting_payment` | the payment link |
| `payment_failed_email` | `failed` | why it failed, what to do |
| `payment_expired_email` | `expired` | the link expired, how to restart |
| `refund_email` | `refunded` | refund confirmed |
| `practice_received_email` | `paid` | practice received, D-7 checkpoint |
| `portal_invite` | — | passwordless portal link |

`payment_paid_email` was already handled — this is the SECOND notice, not the first.

## Boundaries held

- **One figure, never a breakdown**: `f"IDR {facts.price_idr:,}"` at 4 sites, no
  arithmetic, no fee/PNBP split (the split is internal by ruling).
- **Only the published D-7 checkpoint** appears in customer copy.
- **No PII in logs** — and that is now a tripwire, not an inspection:
  `test_no_handler_writes_applicant_pii_into_a_log_line` parametrizes all six
  handlers, seeds a unique marker email per order, and asserts the log lines carry
  the `order_id` and none of email / name / passport / phone.
- Sender is `zantara@balizero.com` via Brevo, key read from env.
- No emoji.

## Proof the tests can go red

Three mutations, each restored afterwards:

1. Widened the refund state guard → 1 red.
2. Turned the five `raise EmailSendFailed` into `return` → 5 red.
3. Added `facts.email` to the `checkout_ready_email` log line
   (`outbox_handlers.py:282`) → the PII tripwire goes red (1 failed, 4 passed).

Baseline: 169 passed on the handler suite; 22 passed on this file.

## What this does NOT close

Four of the ten unhandled job types remain unrouted. The scoped `unroutable > 0`
alarm is deliberately a separate PR — an unscoped one would fire forever for the
known-unhandled types. Tracked in `PENDING-ARMS.md`.

author: rudrashettyrajkumar
body:
## Why

The deployed Render instance has an empty Postgres, so once the SPA loads it shows no data.

## What

Re-enables the demo seed that `docker-entrypoint.sh` already supports, and fixes its idempotency check for managed Postgres.

- **`render.yaml`**: `SEED_DEMO` → `true`.
- **`docker-entrypoint.sh`**: normalize the `DATABASE_URL` scheme (via the app's `_normalize_pg_url`) before the `count(*)` check.
  The old check did `create_engine("postgres://...")`, which SQLAlchemy 2.0 rejects → it always fell into the `except` branch and **re-seeded on every boot**. Since `app.demo` runs `drop_all()`, that would wipe any real runs on restart.
  Now: first boot → no `runs` table → seed once; afterwards → `count > 0` → skip.

Seeds a full fake-LLM run: 5 competitors, ~72 posts, campaign detection, strategy pillars/opportunities, 30-day calendar.

## Verification

Local, against a scratch DB:
- empty DB → check exits 7 → `app.demo` seeds → 1 run
- seeded DB → check exits 0 → skips

`postgres://…` and `postgresql://…` both normalize to `postgresql+psycopg2://…`.

## After merge

Render → **Manual Deploy → Clear build cache & deploy**. First boot logs `[entrypoint] seeding demo run...`; the dashboard then shows the demo run. To later replace it with real data, start a run from the UI (the seed won't re-run).

author: hanthor
body:
Bringup leg [33045828544](https://github.com/tuna-os/tunaos-packages/actions/runs/33045828544) was the first leg that ever **published**: 441 built, **580/673 sources now served** (baseline 509), every '+'/'^' filename repaired (0 remain in the index). Its 25 failures put the GNOME 51 core behind exactly two causes, both fixed here.

## 1. The pango wall (blocks gtk4, libadwaita, mutter → gnome-shell → gdm)

- gtk4 4.23.3 requires pango ≥ 1.58; served pango is 1.57 → gtk4/libadwaita vendor pango as a meson subproject (the `libpangoft2-1.0.so.0.5800.0` in the build log is the tell) and die on `-Werror=unused-but-set-variable` at `pangofc-fontmap.c:2341/3132`.
- Standalone `src/deps/pango` 1.57 separately FTBFS: `pangofc-fontmap.c:4015: implicit declaration of 'FcFreeTypeQueryAll'` — 1.57.0 never includes `fontconfig/fcfreetype.h`.

**1.58.2 fixes both**: it adds exactly that include (line 50 of the same file, verified against the upstream tarball) and satisfies gtk4's floor so the vendored subproject path dissolves. Version bump + `sources` SHA512 updated from the downloaded tarball.

## 2. The changelog wall (killed gnome-desktop3; 11 more waiting to die the same way)

`%changelog not in descending chronological order`: a hand-written entry sits above `%autochangelog`, whose git-derived entries are newer — rpm sees ascending order and errors. Twelve gnome-51 specs share the pattern, including **gdm, gnome-shell, gnome-session** — undetected only because the leg deferred before reaching them. All twelve changelog sections reset to bare `%autochangelog` (the history lives in git, which is what autochangelog reads; verified no non-changelog line was touched).

## Sequencing

src/ edits re-key the cells — post-#563 that's the normal cost of a fix, not a loss: accumulation rides the **published index**, and the 441 served packages skip regardless of key. Plan: merge this + #565, then one hosted leg builds the 232 deferred plus the un-walled GNOME core.

author: dpeterka
body:
First slice of **Phase 3**. A non-LLM engine the deep review can be adjudicated against — the third leg of the anti-anchoring design, alongside the cross-family Challenger and the ledger-blind panel.

I started here because Phase 3's acceptance criterion leans on the divergence-adjudication path, which is the machinery this session has spent the day hardening. The criteria scorers are pure deterministic code with no external dependency, so they can land and be tested before LIRICAL/Monarch bring their data requirements.

## Three decisions that matter more than the arithmetic

**Three states, never two.** Every item is `met` / `not_met` / `not_assessed`. These sets mix laboratory items with clinical ones — fever, arthritis, oral ulcers, renal biopsy classes — that no lab row can answer. A scorer that recorded an unseen item as `not_met` would report a confident low total that is really an artifact of missing input. That is the failure most likely to talk a reader out of a real diagnosis. Totals are documented everywhere as a **floor**, and `points_not_assessed` states the headroom — 43 points of it on this patient's real data.

**Domain maxima.** These criteria are additive *across* domains but take only the single highest-weighted met item *within* one. Summing every met item would inflate a patient whose one affected organ system happens to have several graded entries. Both complement items met scores 4, never 3 + 4.

**Every met item is cited**, with the `labs:<slug>:<date>` ref it was decided from — so a criteria result is checkable by the same machinery as any model claim (ADR 0028).

## The alias list lasted about four minutes

I first matched analytes by a hand-written list of spellings. Against the real corpus it immediately missed two:

| stored name | why the alias list failed |
|---|---|
| `Complement C4c` | not `C4`, not `Complement C4` |
| `Smith (Sm) Antibody` | not `anti-Smith`, not `Sm Antibody` |

A criteria scorer that reports `not_assessed` for an analyte the patient actually had measured is worse than one that errors — it looks like an answer. Lookup is now regex over normalized names, and both spellings are regression tests.

`Cardiolipin Antibody IgA` is deliberately **not** matched: the 2019 set names IgG and IgM only, and this patient has a stored IgA that would otherwise score a point the published criteria do not award. Also pinned.

## Verified against the real corpus

```
entry_met=False  points=0/10  headroom=43
  not_met  3pt  Leukopenia (<4.0 ×10⁹/L)                      [1 ref]
  not_met  4pt  Thrombocytopenia (<100 ×10⁹/L)                [1 ref]
  not_met  2pt  Anti-cardiolipin, anti-β2GP1, or lupus antico [2 ref]
  not_met  3pt  Low C3 or low C4                              [1 ref]
  not_met  6pt  Anti-dsDNA or anti-Smith                      [2 ref]
  not assessable: 16/21
```

ANA is negative, so the entry criterion correctly rules the set out — a clinically meaningful, honest result, with every lab-answerable item resolving to a real row.

## Scope

`SCORERS` is a registry; the framework (three states, domain maxima, cited items, floor totals, entry criteria) is shared by all ~10 sets PLAN.md calls for. This PR lands the framework plus SLE 2019. **Not yet wired into the review DAG or the UI** — that is the next step, and I have not claimed the phase's acceptance criteria are met.

1559 pass, coverage 93.62%. PLAN.md marks Phase 3 in progress.

author: sinity
body:
## Summary

The `require-devtools` PreToolUse hook denied bare pytest in every repository,
not just this one.

## Problem

The hook inspects the command but never the working directory, so running
`pytest` in `/realm/project/sinnix` — which has no `devtools` — was refused with
advice to use a command that does not exist there. The guard blocked work it has
no authority over, leaving the opt-out variable as the only route.

## Solution

Resolve the command's `cwd` against `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` and allow anything
outside this checkout. Also dropped 20 lines of narrated correction history from
the header, which this repository's writing rules forbid in durable text.

## Verification

    cwd=/realm/project/polylogue  pytest tests/                  -> exit 2 (deny)
    cwd=/realm/project/sinnix     pytest test_admission.py       -> exit 0 (allow)
    cwd=/realm/project/polylogue  devtools test tests/           -> exit 0 (allow)
    cwd=/realm/project/polylogue  git commit -m "...pytest..."   -> exit 0 (allow)

Residual risk: a command whose `cwd` is this checkout but which operates on
another repository via `git -C` is still denied. That is existing behaviour and
is not made worse here.

author: myersben9
body:
Copilot follow-up on #18, plus the version-bump automation Ben asked for.

**Script fix:** `_publish_pypi.sh` still hardcoded the `0.7.6` artifact glob (note: the actual 0.7.7 upload was done with an explicit glob, so PyPI is correct — the script was just stale) and its interpreter handling was Windows-only and unquoted. It now derives the version from `pyproject.toml`, rebuilds dist for exactly that version, quotes the interpreter, and recognizes both venv layouts. Demoted to a manual fallback.

**Automation:** new `.github/workflows/publish.yml` — pushing a `vX.Y.Z` tag builds sdist+wheel, **verifies the tag matches the pyproject version** (a stale tag can never publish the wrong code), and uploads via **PyPI Trusted Publishing (OIDC)**, so no API token is stored in GitHub or anywhere else. One-time PyPI-side publisher registration documented in the workflow header.

Release flow after this: bump version -> merge -> `git tag vX.Y.Z && git push origin vX.Y.Z` -> PyPI updates itself.

author: gabebatista
body:
## Summary
The Linux Horde agent Ansible playbook (`modules/unreal/horde/config/agent/horde-agent.ansible.yml`) runs dpkg-based i386/multiarch/apt tasks that are Debian/Ubuntu-only. On Amazon Linux 2023 (and any non-Debian distro), `dpkg --add-architecture i386` fails with `dpkg: No such file or directory`, aborting the whole play **before** the Download/Configure/CreateService/EnableService tasks — so the agent is never installed or enrolled. The sibling Wine/DotNet-backport tasks already carry a `when: ansible_distribution == "Ubuntu"` guard; the i386/multiarch/apt tasks were missing it.

## Change
- Add `when: ansible_distribution == "Ubuntu"` to `Check if i386 enabled`.
- Combine to `ansible_distribution == "Ubuntu" and result_i386_check.rc == 1` on `Enable Multiarch` and `Update Cache` (the register short-circuits safely on non-Ubuntu).

+3/-2, one file.

## Testing / validation
Validated live on an Amazon Linux 2023 Horde sync agent (SSM `AWS-ApplyAnsiblePlaybooks`).
- **Before:** play FAILED at `Enable Multiarch` (dpkg missing).
- **After:** `PLAY RECAP ok=13 changed=6 skipped=5 failed=0` — the 5 Ubuntu/dpkg tasks correctly SKIPPED; play reached Download/Configure/CreateService/EnableService; `horde-agent.service` active (running); agent connected to the Horde server and pending approval.
- YAML syntax validated (`yaml.safe_load` OK).

## Blast radius
Ubuntu agents unaffected (guard matches prior behavior when distro==Ubuntu); only changes behavior on non-Ubuntu (now correctly skips Debian-only steps). No API/interface change.

supported that. It does not, and it should be closed rather than rebased.

merged and did the same job independently and more thoroughly. Three commits have

closing comment and no human review on it, only an automated Codex one. That it

[Ruled, Sebastian 2026-08-27]. Only English carries `managedText1`; the other 37

| --- | --- |
| `setTitle.ts` -- the browser tab title | **Yes.** `ShowTasks.vue:318` calls it on every render of the upcoming-tasks screen. `useTitle.ts` was corrected by BRA-1444; this second helper was missed. |
| The header logo, which draws the words "Brazn Tasks" | **Yes.** `Navigation.vue` and `AppHeader.vue` render it on every screen behind sign-in; `ContentLinkShare.vue` renders it to anonymous link visitors. |
| The logo's accessible name | **Yes.** `alt` is not a valid attribute on `<svg>`, so for these `role="img"` assets the accessible name comes from `<title>`. Fixing only `alt` would have left a screen reader still saying "Brazn Tasks". Both are fixed. |
| The web app manifest | **Yes.** It is the label a customer gets on their home screen or desktop when they install the app. |
| The Safari pinned-tab title, and the token-refresh console warning | Yes, though both are marginal. |
| `migrators.ts` -- the import wizard label | **No.** `migratorName()` prefers `nameKey`, and `vikunja-file` has one that already reads "ONE / Vikunja export". The literal is a dead fallback. Corrected anyway, because a dead fallback naming the wrong product is what gets read the day the key is removed. |

The brief I was given said only the logo was assessed as reachable. That is wrong
for the tab title, which is reachable, and the two extra items -- the manifest and
the visible wordmark -- were not in the brief at all.

**The guards.** `fork-guards.yml` already refused a catalogue value naming
Vikunja. It now refuses Brazn Tasks and Percy as well, across all three catalogue
directories, and the unit test over the ONE pages' catalogues is extended to
match so the failure arrives in `frontend-unit` in seconds rather than only in
`fork-guards`. This lands in a second commit, after the fix, because the same
guard reads `pkg/i18n/lang` and extending it first would have turned every build
red.

The pattern is `brazn tasks` with a space, never `brazn`: the repository address
uses a hyphen and the product's own address is `brazn.one`, so both survive.
Percy is refused deliberately even though Percy is a live name for the assistant
-- no catalogue value carries it today, no regex can tell the assistant from the
old product name, and when attribution copy lands it goes on an allowlist the way
"Vikunja export" did. The `percy-service-*.ts` and `percy-http-*.ts` citations
under `frontend/public/one` are deliberately out of scope: 123 of them are
provenance for a reverse-engineered contract, so only that directory's catalogues
are scanned and not its code.

## A test expectation was edited

One, and it is a fixture rather than an assertion.
`frontend/src/brazn/one/api.commercial.test.ts:57` builds a canned SPA index page
whose `<title>` said "Brazn Tasks"; it is fed to the commercial API client as an
HTML response body to prove the client rejects HTML where it expects JSON. The
title is never asserted on. It now says "ONE" so the fixture matches the real
`frontend/index.html`, which has said "ONE" since before this change. No
assertion was loosened anywhere: the guard patterns match one exact name each,
and nothing was widened to accept either name.

## How it was checked

- `pnpm test:unit` -- 73 files, 1366 tests pass. Same counts as #85 reported.
- `pnpm build` -- succeeds. The built manifest reads `"name":"ONE"`.
- ESLint on every changed file -- 0 errors. The 4 warnings are the pre-existing
  axios-dependency notices in `fetcher.ts` and two test-file ignore notices.
- **The guards were checked by making them fail.** Reintroducing
  "Save to Brazn Tasks" and "Ask Percy" into `frontend/public/one/i18n/en.json`
  turns the unit test red on each name independently; the same substitutions in
  `pkg/i18n/lang` and `frontend/src/i18n/lang` make the workflow grep report
  them. With the tree as it stands all three directories are silent, with the 16
  repository-address values in place.
- **That mutation testing found a hole in my own guard, and the third commit
  fixes it.** The first version put all three names in one grep and then filtered
  the result through the "Vikunja export" allowance. That allowance exists for a
  single value -- the import picker's, which reads "ONE / Vikunja export" -- so a

  filter and the guard reported nothing. I only found it by mutating that exact

author: danfuzz
body: From: Agent working on behalf of @danfuzz (Claude Opus 5) Three findings a review of the IPC envelope work (#6323) turned up, each of which is true on `main` today and independent of that work. Landing them here keeps them out of a larger change — and keeps them landed if that change ever has to be reverted. ## `postToClient()` had no guard It is the whole of the worker's outbound side, and `postMessage` refuses part of the value domain the protocol types admit. An interned `symbol` is a `FabricValue`, and structured cloning throws on one, nested or not: ``` clone THROWS:: interned symbol -> DOMException clone THROWS:: record holding an interned symbol -> DOMException ``` Replies survive that today — the message listener's `catch` turns the throw into an error reply. The notification paths do not: they post from a `queueMicrotask` callback, outside any caller's `try`, where the throw is an uncaught error instead. A refused post now substitutes a strings-only stand-in naming what could not go, and reports that by returning `false`. **The return is not decoration, and an existing test proved it.** Guarding without reporting the outcome counts a substituted reply as `responded` rather than `responded-error`, silently corrupting the request ledger — which `web-worker-console-bridge.test.ts` caught immediately. Its claims about the ledger are unchanged. What changed is the reply's text, which now names the message as well as the reason, so its assertion asks for that rather than for an exact rendering. The new `post-to-client.test.ts` drives the three refusal paths and one ordinary message. Its fake `postMessage` calls `structuredClone` so it refuses exactly what a real one refuses, rather than guessing which values those are. Ablated: with the guard rethrowing, the three refusal tests fail and the ordinary-message control still passes. ## `JSON.stringify()` destroyed the report that used it The invalid-request report renders the message it is refusing. Structured cloning delivers a `bigint` intact, and `JSON.stringify()` throws on one: ``` structured clone carries bigint: bigint 42n JSON.stringify THROWS: TypeError: Do not know how to serialize a BigInt ``` So the one report whose whole job is to say which message was wrong could instead say "Do not know how to serialize a BigInt". It renders through `value-debug` now, bounded, as the other reports here already do. ## Decoded payload arrays say `readonly` Nineteen protocol payload fields, and the four `RuntimeClient` trace accessors that return them. Every consumer the type checker then flagged wanted an honest declaration and never a copy: three `runner` parameters that read their argument and never write it, a `shell` cached field and its accessor, an `html` op array, and two test annotations. The console arguments become a `FabricArray`, that being the data model's own name for the readonly array of `FabricValue` they are. Nothing changes at run time. What changes is that the declarations stop promising more than the values give — and the type checker is what proved that none of the promises were being used: had any of those functions actually mutated its argument, the widening would not compile. ## Checks `deno task check`, `deno fmt --check`, `deno lint`, `deno task check-docs`, and `deno task cfcheck` (422 pattern files) all pass, as do the `runtime-client` (16 tests), `html` (25 tests), and full `runner` (1303 tests) suites.

author: hplovecraft208[bot]
body:
### 🎯 What does this PR do?
The nightly failure reporter is the only thing that turns a red scheduled run into a visible issue, and it died before the issue write on every scheduled run from 2026-08-23 through 2026-08-26: the gh build on runner image ubuntu24/20260816.277 consulted local git eagerly even though every invocation passes --repo, and the job ran with no checkout, so gh crashed with fatal: not a git repository and four red nightlies produced no signal. Review of the first attempt (a GH_REPO env pin) proved with a live gh binary that the env is never read when --repo is present, so no flag or env combination controls an eager git consult. The robust insulation is to make the job a repository: this adds a pinned sparse checkout (persist-credentials false, sparse-checkout .github, because the full tree carries ~971 MiB of samples this job never reads), keeps the --repo flags, and pins the checkout's existence, ref, credential hygiene, and sparseness in the infra test with a named failure each.

### 🧪 How to test
Delete the nightly-report checkout step, its persist-credentials line, or its sparse-checkout line and run pnpm test:health-gates: each produces its own named failure; restored, the check passes. On the next scheduled run that fails, confirm the reporter files or updates the nightly issue rather than dying before the write.

### 🖼️ Screenshots
None.

### 📌 Related tickets & additional notes
Closes #2933

author: claude[bot]
body:
<!-- ccr-slack-attribution -->
_Requested by **John Kleinschmidt** · [Slack thread](https://electronhq.slack.com/archives/C039043TJEB/p1787851462569749?thread_ts=1787851462.569749&cid=C039043TJEB)_

#### Description of Change

**Before:** Rerunning failed jobs on a Windows build could die at "Restore src cache via AZCopy" with `SAS Token not found; exiting src cache download early...`. The checkout job saves the SAS token under `sas-key-<platform>-<run_number>-<run_attempt>`, but `restore-cache-azcopy` probes only two exact keys: attempt 1's and the current attempt's. On a rerun-failed-jobs attempt the checkout job is skipped, so no current-attempt key exists — and if attempt 1 ran no jobs (e.g. it only hit the fork-approval gate), no attempt-1 key exists either. Restore then finds nothing and the build fails, even though a valid key from an intermediate attempt (e.g. `-2`) is sitting in the cache. Concrete example: run [32992122493](https://github.com/electron/electron/actions/runs/32992122493) attempt 3 on #53101.

**After:** The restore step falls back to the newest saved `sas-key-<platform>-<run_number>-` cache entry for the run, so reruns reuse the token saved by whichever earlier attempt actually ran checkout, instead of failing outright.

**How:** Adds a `restore-keys` prefix fallback (`sas-key-${{ inputs.target-platform }}-${{ github.run_number }}-`) to the second "Obtain SAS Key" restore step. `actions/cache` restore-keys matching returns the most recently created cache entry with that prefix, so the newest saved token wins. The two existing exact-key probes are unchanged.

One thing to note on token lifetime: the SAS token is minted by the `sas` sidecar over `/var/run/sas/sas.sock`, whose configuration (and therefore the token TTL) is not in this repo, so I can't confirm from here how long an earlier attempt's token stays valid. If the TTL is generous relative to how stale a rerun can be, this is a strict improvement; if it can expire, the fallback still only converts a guaranteed failure into an azcopy auth error at worst. Worth a sanity check from someone who knows the Azure/sidecar config.

- [ ] [I have reviewed and verified the changes](https://github.com/electron/governance/blob/main/policy/ai.md)

author: novai42
body:
## Summary

Fixes #6587 — a client-supplied header (e.g. `user-agent`) overwrites the provider's `network_config.extra_headers` on the upstream request. Gateway configuration should be authoritative for the headers it pins: `extra_headers` now wins over headers organically forwarded from the client.

**Root cause:** in the Anthropic OAuth passthrough flow (client authenticates the Anthropic-compatible route with its own `Authorization: Bearer ...` token), the integration captures the caller's raw headers and `setPassthroughHeaders` (`core/providers/utils/utils.go`) applies them with an unconditional `Set()` *after* `SetExtraHeaders` has applied the provider's `network_config.extra_headers` — so the caller's value for the same header always clobbers the configured one.

## Changes

- `core/providers/utils/utils.go`: `setPassthroughHeaders` never overwrites a header that is already on the request. Every call site (`completeRequest` and both streaming handlers in `core/providers/anthropic/anthropic.go`) applies `SetExtraHeaders` first, so configured `network_config.extra_headers` keep precedence over the caller's copy of the same header — no exported signature change, no call-site churn. Caller headers without a configured counterpart (the OAuth `authorization` credential, `x-stainless-*` telemetry, ...) are forwarded exactly as before, including the `accept-encoding` codec filtering.
- `core/providers/anthropic/passthroughheaders_test.go`: new regression test `TestSetPassthroughHeaders_ConfiguredExtraHeadersWin` — the caller sends `user-agent` / `x-app` / `accept-encoding`, the operator configures the same keys, and the configured values must reach the upstream request on both the buffered and streaming paths while the caller's `authorization` still passes through.

Design notes:
- Header precedence is now a property of call order and reads: explicit per-request override (`x-bf-eh-*` → `BifrostContextKeyExtraHeaders`, applied inside `SetExtraHeaders` with documented priority) > configured `network_config.extra_headers` > organic caller passthrough headers.
- The check is `req.Header.Peek(k)` — fasthttp normalizes header-name case on Set/Peek, so `User-Agent` in config matches `user-agent` from the client without manual canonicalization.
- Caller auth/version headers applied last by `completeRequest` are untouched, as is the forced JSON content type.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Chore/CI

## Affected areas

- [x] Core (Go)
- [ ] Transports (HTTP)
- [ ] Providers/Integrations
- [ ] Plugins
- [ ] UI (React)
- [ ] Docs

## How to test

```sh
cd core
go build ./...
go test ./providers/anthropic/ -run 'TestSetPassthroughHeaders' -v
go test ./providers/anthropic/ ./providers/utils/
```

Red-before-green: `TestSetPassthroughHeaders_ConfiguredExtraHeadersWin` fails on `dev` with the caller's values winning (`configured extra header "User-Agent" must win over the caller's copy: got "claude-cli/2.0.8 (external, cli)", want "gateway-agent/1.0"`) and passes with this change.

Manual validation matching the issue repro: configure `user-agent` in the provider's `network_config.extra_headers`, call the Anthropic-compatible endpoint with a Bearer (OAuth) credential and a `user-agent: client_header` request header — the upstream request now carries the configured value.

## Screenshots/Recordings

N/A (no UI changes).

## Breaking changes

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

Behavioral note: callers in the OAuth passthrough flow can no longer override a header the gateway operator has explicitly pinned in `network_config.extra_headers` (that is the bug being fixed); the `x-bf-eh-*` header channel remains the supported per-request override. All other caller headers are forwarded as before.

## Related issues

Closes #6587

## Security considerations

Strengthens operator control: gateway-configured headers can no longer be silently replaced by client-supplied values on upstream requests. No secrets, auth flows, or PII handling changed; `x-bf-*` internals remain stripped, hop-by-hop headers remain dropped.

Provider-harness exemption: this change is not client-observable on the wire (it alters headers sent upstream in the Anthropic OAuth passthrough flow, which needs a live OAuth credential and per-case provider `network_config` that the harness does not model); regression coverage is the Go unit test above. `tests/e2e/api/collections/provider-harness.json` was checked: it has no case asserting upstream header precedence for `extra_headers` (its section 9 "Passthrough (catch-all forwarding)" covers the unrelated catch-all routes where Bifrost injects its own key), and it already delegates behavior it cannot provoke to Go unit tests (see the harness note referencing `core/providers/anthropic/serversidefallback_test.go`), which this PR follows.

author: craigvc
body:
`FileSaveBackend` passed `true` to `store_var` and `get_var`. That is Godot's `allow_objects` flag, and the engine's own documentation is blunt about what it means: **a deserialised object can carry a script, and that script runs.**

```
109 suite(s), 2528 test(s), 2528 passed, 0 failed, 10556 assertions
RESULT: PASS
```

Reported by @craigvc, and correct on all four counts.

## Why it matters

A save file lives in a directory the player can write, gets synced between machines by Steam or a console's cloud, and gets passed around in forum threads when someone wants help with a broken run. Any of those is a path from an edited file to code execution inside the game. "The file is trusted" was never true of `user://`.

**Nothing was gained by it.** The file's own doc comment justified binary serialisation by pointing at `Transform3D` and `Vector3` — but those are *Variant* types, not objects, and they round-trip perfectly well with the flag off. Plan 26 already forbids saving nodes, so a save that genuinely needed object decoding would be one that had already broken that rule. The whole suite passes with the flag off, which is the evidence.

## What else changed

Three protections against a save that is damaged rather than hostile — losing a hundred-hour run to a power cut is its own kind of failure:

- **Atomic write.** The save lands on a `.tmp` and is renamed into place. A rename is the cheapest thing a filesystem offers that is either done or not done; writing into the real file means a crash leaves the player with neither the old save nor the new one.
- **Backup.** The previous save moves aside rather than being overwritten, and is read when the current one will not load. Erasing a slot takes its backup with it — a deleted game that comes back as its own backup is worse than a deleted game.
- **Checksum.** A truncated or edited file is refused rather than half-loaded. Half a save is not a save: restoring one leaves a world where some entities know about a quest and others do not.

**The checksum is not a security control, and is documented as not being one.** Anyone who can edit a save can recompute it, and there is no key here to stop them. It catches corruption and casual tampering; the object flag is what stops a hostile save from running code. A project needing genuinely tamper-proof saves wants a signature and a secret this framework has nowhere to keep.

## Why 2,519 tests missed it

Worth stating precisely, because "the default backend is in-memory" isn't quite it — `FileSaveBackend` *was* covered, for round-trip, listing, erasure and path traversal.

The real reason: **every persistence test writes with the same backend it reads with.** That makes them round-trip tests, and a round-trip test cannot fail on a hostile file because it never produces one. No test had ever written a save file by hand.

`test_save_security.gd` does exactly that — writes the bytes the way anyone with a text editor and the save directory open can, then asks the backend to load them. Its first assertion is that the fixture genuinely decodes to a live `Object` under `bytes_to_var_with_objects`, so that refusing it proves something rather than passing because the bytes turned out inert.

Both attack shapes are covered: an enveloped file with a **correctly recomputed checksum** (the realistic one, since the checksum is not a defence), and a bare legacy-format object file (so the envelope is not something an attacker can simply opt out of).

## Guards verified by breaking them

| Break | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `bytes_to_var` → `bytes_to_var_with_objects` (the original hole) | red — the object test alone |
| Stop comparing the checksum | red — the tamper test |
| Stop keeping the previous save | red — 2 tests |
| Write straight to the real file, no temporary | red — 8 tests, including pre-existing ones |

## One breaking change

**Saves written before this cannot be loaded, and there is deliberately no migration** — reading an old save means decoding it the old way, which *is* the vulnerability. A file with no envelope reads as damaged, because there is no way to tell it apart from one that is. Noted in `docs/migration-guide.md`. It is a container change, not a content change, so `SAVE_SCHEMA` does not move and no `SaveMigration` is involved.

author: juwan-hwang
body:
## Problem
When validating paths for new files that have not yet been created, `validatePathWithinRepo` fell back to calling `realpath(parentDir)` on the immediate parent directory.

If a new file is being created inside nested directories that do not yet exist (for example `src/components/button/index.tsx` where neither `components/` nor `button/` has been created yet), `realpath(parentDir)` threw `ENOENT`, which was caught and caused the function to incorrectly reject the valid path with `Path '...' resolves outside the repository root`.

## Solution
Update `validatePathWithinRepo` to walk up the directory tree to find the closest existing ancestor directory:
- Recursively inspect parent directories until an existing ancestor directory is found.
- Verify that the resolved ancestor directory resides within `resolvedRoot`.
- Return `initialPath` for the non-existent target path once the ancestor is validated.

## Testing
- Added unit tests for new files in nested non-existent directories under existing directories (`src/components/button/index.tsx`).
- Added unit tests for new files in deeply nested non-existent directories from repo root (`deeply/nested/non/existent/dir/file.txt`).
- Verified path traversal attacks (`../outside/...`) and escaping symlinks continue to be correctly rejected for non-existent nested paths.
- Verified valid internal symlinks to directories continue to accept nested new files.
- All path validation unit tests pass (`27 pass, 0 fail`).
- All format and TypeScript checks pass (`bun run format:check`, `bun run typecheck`).

author: khajavi
body:
## Motivation

`notify-docs-release` pings `zio/zio`'s `repository_dispatch` after a docs publish, using `secrets.PAT_TOKEN` - a static personal access token that has to be manually provisioned per consuming repo before this job can work at all. `zio/zio-cli` hit exactly this: after adopting `zio-sbt-ci`, its docs pipeline is otherwise fully working (OIDC npm trusted publishing, the `update-readme` fix from #757/#758), but this one job is still blocked on a `PAT_TOKEN` secret nobody's set up for it.

## Change

Same pattern already established for `auto-merge.yml`'s own token problem: mint a short-lived GitHub App installation token via the existing `zio/generate-github-app-token` action and `APP_ID`/`APP_PRIVATE_KEY` secrets, gated on `secrets.APP_ID != ''` so repos without the app configured skip cleanly. `PAT_TOKEN` stays as the fallback (`steps.generate-token.outputs.token || secrets.PAT_TOKEN`), so nothing already relying on it breaks.

One real difference from the `auto-merge.yml` case worth calling out: there's no `GITHUB_TOKEN` fallback here, because the dispatch targets `zio/zio` - a *different* repository - and `GITHUB_TOKEN` is scoped only to the repo the workflow runs in. The minted app token only helps if that app is actually installed on `zio/zio` too; if not, this fails the same way a missing `PAT_TOKEN` does today, no worse off.

## Test plan

- [x] `sbt ciGenerateGithubWorkflow` produces exactly the expected diff in this repo's own `ci.yml` (Generate Token step + env-based Authorization header)

## Resumo

F3 etapa 5 do roadmap, implementando o [ADR-0023](docs/adr/0023-editor-de-grupo.md) por inteiro:

- **Menu de contexto de grupo** (RF-2.22) -- abre com clique direito na pílula.
- **Editor de grupo** (ADR-0023), o quinto widget de chrome -- popover com três regiões navegáveis (campo de nome, faixa de seis swatches, lista de ações), aberto por `group.rename`/`group.set_color` (a partir do menu) ou duplo clique na pílula.
- **Popover de destino do `tab.move_to_group`** (RF-2.20) -- "Mover para grupo" no menu de aba sai do estado esmaecido; lista os grupos explícitos + "Novo grupo", primeira lista rolável do chrome.

## Decisões de implementação

- `group_menu.rs` é a definição única de ações (RF-10.21): seis `GroupAction`, lidas tanto pelo menu (as seis) quanto pelo editor (as três que não são campo/faixa) -- os dois caem em `WindowState::run_group_action`.
- Edição de nome ao vivo sem tocar o `Workspace` até `Enter` -- mesmo truque do rename de aba da F2 (buffer preferido ao modelo na hora de pintar). `Esc` só descarta o estado.
- Cor e ações do editor **não** são ao vivo: mover o realce não aplica nada, só `Enter`/clique -- mesma regra "hover e foco são o mesmo realce" do menu de contexto.
- `Workspace::move_tab_to_group` (novo em `porecatu-core`) cruza fronteira de grupo, diferente de `move_tab` (só reordena dentro do mesmo).
- `group.close_all` sempre confirma (RF-2.23): `DialogAction::CloseGroup` novo, corpo com a contagem.
- Os três widgets nunca coexistem entre si nem com o menu de aba (`close_all_popovers`, um ponto só do código).

## Fora do escopo

- `group.create` continua sem gesto que crie grupo explícito (mesmo padrão "core à frente da UI" das etapas 2-4) -- os três widgets são testáveis via `Workspace` direto.
- `group.next`/`group.prev` (RF-2.21) -- fora do título desta etapa.
- Atalho de teclado para as ações de grupo -- sem parser de `[keybindings]` até a F4.
- Rolagem por roda do mouse no popover de destino -- só realce por teclado/clique arrasta a janela visível.
- Entrada de cor por hexadecimal (RF-2.10) -- diferida pelo próprio ADR-0023.

author: synexsolucoes-debug
body:
## O que muda

Fecha **de ponta a ponta** o bloco de regras de processo: o motor aplica, o servidor grava e o modelador configura.

### Motor (§23, §25)

- **Regra de saída e regra de entrada** — a de saída pergunta *"esta etapa já pode ser deixada"*, a de entrada *"aquela etapa já pode receber"*. Códigos de bloqueio distintos, porque quem foi barrado precisa saber qual das duas o barrou; a de entrada nomeia a etapa de destino.
- **Bloqueio por erro de integração** — a etapa declara de quais canais depende. Travar por um canal não declarado transformaria uma falha do Teams em parada do DP inteiro; há teste cobrando.

Os canais em erro são carregados junto da instância, como os fatos: uma regra que depende de um argumento que o chamador pode esquecer é uma regra que às vezes não vale.

### O bug que a UI revelou

`sanitizeProcessStepConfigs` monta o objeto `settings` **campo a campo**, e as quatro chaves novas não existiam lá. A condição configurada **sumia no caminho até o banco, sem erro nenhum** — o motor executaria um processo sem a regra que alguém acabou de escrever.

O saneador passa a aceitá-las usando **o mesmo parser do motor**: o que a execução descartaria também não é gravado. Isso significa que as condições do #99 eram, na prática, inconfiguráveis pela API padrão.

### UI no modelador (§23, §25)

Três blocos novos no painel de propriedades: *Regras da etapa*, *Condição de cada saída*, *Dependência de integração*.

- A linha lê como uma frase — **campo → operador → valor** — porque quem configura processo não é programador.
- Operador sem valor **esconde** o campo em vez de desabilitá-lo: um campo cinza ao lado de "está vazio" só faz perguntar o que vai ali.
- A lista de operadores é **importada** de `process-conditions`, não recopiada. Uma tela que oferecesse um operador a mais entregaria ao usuário uma regra que o servidor descarta em silêncio — há teste cobrando a paridade.
- O campo é livre com sugestões em `datalist`; `custom:` alcança qualquer campo personalizado, inclusive o criado depois.

**Limitação documentada:** as setas vêm do XML da versão, então uma seta recém-desenhada só aparece depois de salvar o diagrama.

### Retrocompatibilidade (§48, §108)

4 testes de **comportamento** com um `d1` de mentira: demanda sem versão recusa com motivo próprio, demanda com versão e sem área carrega, condição sobre área vazia falha em vez de liberar, e 404 preservado.

## Sobre a §88

Fui mexer na paleta e **não mexi** — os dois valores "ausentes" foram substituídos de propósito e o código está mais certo que o briefing:

- Azul e marinho vêm dos **pixels do símbolo oficial**, não de estimativa.
- O cinza `#64748B` do briefing rende **4,48:1** sobre o fundo — **reprova** WCAG 2.2 AA. O adotado rende 5,78:1. Recalculei.

Adotá-lo criaria a violação que o próprio `a11y-check` reprovaria no PR seguinte.

## Verificação

| Verificação | Resultado |
|---|---|
| `npm run ci` | **1236 testes** (1221 antes, 15 novos), lint, typecheck, db:check, build |
| `npm run verify:sql` | 1281 consultas, **0 falhas** |
| `npm run a11y-check` | 74 telas, **0 violações** WCAG 2.2 AA |
| `npm run browser-check` | **102/102** |

Os dois últimos contra o produto de pé com PostgreSQL 16 local e as 72 migrations — como o job `interface` faz.

## O que continua faltando

§31 (abas dentro de um processo) e §26 (documento como marcação, não anexo verificado — depende da resposta do DP).

body:
## `/challenge` dostępne dla każdego gracza

- zdjęte `setDefaultMemberPermissions(Administrator)` z rejestracji komendy
- zdjęta bramka `_isHeadAdmin` w `handleChallengeCommand`
- komenda przeniesiona z własnej ścieżki routingu (przed sprawdzeniem kanału) do zwykłego `switch`, więc podlega tej samej zasadzie co `/update`, `/ranking` i `/profile`: **wymaga skonfigurowanego serwera i kanału bota**. Wcześniej działała na dowolnym kanale, bo dotyczyła wyłącznie head admina

Select menu `chal_*` nadal routowane są przed `isAllowedChannel` — wizard jest efemeryczny i żyje w wiadomości, która powstała już na dozwolonym kanale.

## Zaproszenie wygasa po 24 h zamiast 48 h

`INVITE_TTL_MS` = 24 h. Zaktualizowane komunikaty w obu językach (`challengeSent`, `challengeDmInviteExpiredNotice`) oraz komentarze i dokumentacja.

## Po upływie 72 h wygrywa wyższa suma

Dotąd każde wyzwanie bez kompletu wyników po obu stronach kończyło się jako `unresolved` — gracz, który dowiózł swoje trzy wyniki, nie dostawał nic za bezczynność przeciwnika.

`sweep()` rozstrzyga teraz po sumach, gdy komplet zebrała **przynajmniej jedna** strona (`_finalize`, ten sam kod co przy naturalnym końcu). `unresolved` zostaje wyłącznie na sytuację, w której kompletu nie ma **nikt**.

- ⚠️ **Sam komplet nie przesądza o wygranej — decyduje suma.** Trzy słabsze wyniki przegrają z jednym lepszym; komplet jest warunkiem *rozstrzygnięcia*, nie *zwycięstwa*
- pojedynki domknięte czasem idą **tą samą drogą co naturalny koniec** — `sweep()` oddaje je w `finished`, a `_handleChallengeSweep` woła `_finishChallenges`: osiągnięcia, DM z werdyktem i jednorazowy przycisk „pochwal się"
- `_handleChallengeSweep` destrukturyzuje zdarzenia z domyślnymi `[]` — drugi wywołujący (ręczne zamknięcie z Centrum Dowodzenia) nie przekazuje nowego klucza
- `forceFinish` (ręczne zamknięcie przez admina) **celowo zachowuje niższy próg**: wystarczy jeden wynik po dowolnej stronie. To wyraźna decyzja człowieka, a nie automat działający pod nieobecność ludzi — różnica opisana w komentarzu przy metodzie
- `challengeDmUnresolvedDesc` (pol + eng) mówi teraz wprost, że kompletu nie zebrała żadna ze stron

## Osiągnięcie za remis

Nowe `chal_draw_1` — **Godny Przeciwnik / Worthy Opponent** 🤝 (rare, ukryte), warunek `challengesDraws >= 1`.

- nowy licznik `progress.challengesDraws` + `achievementService.trackChallengeDraw()`
- `_applyChallengeAchievements` obsługuje teraz `finished` **bez zwycięzcy** → nalicza remis **obu stronom**. `unresolved` nadal nie nalicza niczego — pojedynek się nie odbył
- **cofanie działa symetrycznie:** remis to `finished` z `winner === null`, więc same `winnerSide`/`loserSide` by go nie wykryły — `removeScore` oddaje w `reopened` dodatkową flagę `wasDraw`, a `_undoChallengeResolution` woła `revertChallengeOutcome(..., 'challengesDraws')` dla obu stron
- `revertChallengeOutcome` przyjmuje trzecie pole; odbieranie osiągnięć nadal ograniczone do ID `chal_*`

## Dokumentacja

`EndersEcho/CLAUDE.md`: uprawnienia i routing `/challenge`, TTL zaproszenia, obie ścieżki rozstrzygnięcia wraz z ostrzeżeniem „komplet ≠ zwycięstwo", rozbita tabela sweepa, licznik `challengesDraws`, opis naliczania i cofania remisu, wiersz w tabeli osiągnięć. Poprawione zweryfikowane liczby osiągnięć (kategoria `explorer` 64, w tym 23 za wyzwania).

`Muteusz/config/all_commands.json`: `/challenge` → `requiredPermission: "public"`.

author: stevenlshafer
body:
**Steve:** *"What is worth avoiding is having 'refinements' in the parser cause significant deterioration in the ability to parse earlier corpora."*

That's a different problem from the holdout, and nothing here measured it. A holdout answers *does this generalize*. It says nothing about whether a fix **broke articles that used to work**.

## The aggregate actively hides it

Parse rate can't distinguish these:

| | |
|---|---|
| 84.9% → 85.1% | 4 more files parse, nothing broke |
| 84.9% → 85.1% | **40 fixed and 36 broken** |

Very different pieces of work — the second is churn wearing the costume of progress — and every parse rate this repository has quoted could have been either.

## Verified by fabricating exactly that case

40 fixed, 36 broken, net +4. The aggregate reads 84.9% → 85.1%, indistinguishable from four clean wins. The report says:

```
FIXED  40   BROKEN 36   net +4
churn: 76 file(s) changed outcome to move the net by 4
(a net gain that costs 36 working file(s) is a trade, not a free win)
```

…then names every broken file and groups them by source — breakage clustered in one journal means a **layout assumption changed**, scattered breakage means **something more general moved**. Different bugs; the grouping is free.

## Not a hard threshold by default

"Significant deterioration" is a judgment: breaking two files to repair forty may be right; breaking one flagship journal's layout may not be, even at a smaller count. So it reports by default, with `--max-broken` for automation. A number nobody chose is not a standard.

**Exit codes verified directly rather than through a pipe** — the first check showed `exit 0` on a *failed* gate because `tail` was masking Rscript's status. A gate that reports failure while exiting 0 is useless in automation.

Works on any corpus — it discovers the key and outcome columns, so the same script serves ParseOutcomes, the A&A run, medRxiv, and the PubTables mining outcomes.

The baseline is committed so it's stable and inspectable; `--snapshot` moves it only deliberately, since a baseline that drifts with the code makes every comparison look clean.
