author: joshuafolkken
body:
closes #991

## 何を直したか

CI が E2E を回すかどうかを決める `e2e-detect` の条件を、ローカルガード（`scripts/test-e2e-guard.ts`）と同じ「`node_modules` の外に `*.e2e.{ts,js}` が 1 つでもあるか」に揃えた。config のファイル名（`playwright.config.ts`）は見なくなった。

旧条件は「`playwright.config.ts` が存在し、かつ `find tests src/routes` で spec が見つかる」だったため、`src/lib/foo.e2e.ts` のような配置や `playwright.config.js` を使う構成では `enabled=false` になり、`e2e` ジョブが skip され、skip は pass として数えられ、**E2E を 1 度も走らせないままマージされていた**。#902 で完了ゲートから人手の E2E 実行が外れたことで、この検出ずれを補償するものが無くなっていた。

## 変更点

- `templates/workflows/ci.yml` / `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: `e2e-detect` の検出を書き換え。パイプではなくコマンド置換 + `-print -quit` を使い、`bash -eo pipefail` でも SIGPIPE 由来の誤判定が起きないようにした。
- `scripts/ci-yml-e2e-detect.test.ts`（新規）: workflow から `run:` ブロックを取り出して bash（`-e` と `-eo pipefail` の両方）で実行し、同じ fixture に対する `test_e2e_guard.has_e2e_tests` の答えと突き合わせる。prose ではなく実行で一致を固定する。
- `scripts/ci-yml-fixture.ts`: `find_step_by_id` / `step_run` を共有化（3 つの ci.yml スイートが同じ探索を書いていた）。
- `scripts/git/git-pr-checks-e2e-gate.test.ts`: `E2E` を必須チェックに加えない決定と、その受け入れコストを固定。
- `prompts/testing-guide.md` § 6: 「前提条件」の記述を実装後の状態に更新。

## `E2E` を必須チェックに加えない（Tier A）

必須チェックは *skipped* なジョブで満たされる（rollup パーサが `SKIPPED` を `pass` に写す）ため、`E2E` を必須にしても今回の欠陥は素通りする。赤い E2E は #990 以降すでに待ちを即終了させマージを止める。一方、この workflow を使っていないリポジトリでは `E2E` が `missing` になり、評価が `pending` のまま 32 分の待ちを使い切る。詳細な根拠は #991 のコメントに記録。

## 配布時の影響範囲

`*.e2e.{ts,js}` を持ちながら Playwright を実行できない構成は、skip（緑）から E2E 赤に変わる（意図した挙動）。`notify-auto-tag` は `e2e` の `success` / `skipped` を要求するため、その構成では auto-tag も止まる。kit 自身は spec を持たないため影響なし。

## ルール遵守測定（`josh eval`）

`pnpm josh eval:scope` は **`required`**（`prompts/testing-guide.md` が対象）と回答した。`pnpm josh eval` を 2 回実行したが、いずれも判定行に到達する前に kill され、**verdict を 1 度も出していない**。よって結果は `held` でも `unmeasured` でもなく **測定不能**である。測定が取れなかったことは変更が安全であることの根拠ではない。eval 自体の劣化は joshuafolkken/kit#1001 で追跡中。

## 検証

- `pnpm josh gate`: lint / type check / cspell / unit すべて green
- `/code-review medium` 2 ラウンド。1 ラウンド目の High/Medium（`pipefail` 下で `find | grep -q` が誤判定する件、ハーネスが片方のシェルしか試していない件）を修正済み。2 ラウンド目は Low のみで、うち事実誤りの 2 件を修正。

author: keyurgolani
body:
## What changed

The task detail panel's **exit-criteria bar had no `role`, no name and no `aria-valuenow`** — a bare
`<div>` with a percentage width sitting under a heading that read `Exit criteria · 2/3`. It now goes
through `ui/Meter`.

This is the follow-up the `ui/Meter` adoption pass (#2145) named. That pass took seven of eleven
hand-rolled determinate bars and deferred four, and its own comment recorded that the reason was
**false** for this one:

> `pages/tasks/TaskDetail.tsx` — 6px track that IS byte-equivalent to Meter's default. Held back only
> because the brief scoped it out; it is a one-line follow-up.

`mb-2 h-1.5 rounded-pill bg-surface-high overflow-hidden` is `Meter`'s default track exactly, and
`mb-2` rides the `className` that same pass added — which is what that prop was for.

## Change class

**R** (refinement). One call site, plus the rail's own ratchet.

## What I validated as a user

Own gateway on `:10860`, isolated home, `PYTHONPATH=$PWD/src`, served `assets/index-C-AJY0OD.js`
verified equal to my build's. Seeded with `demo-home`, opened `#/tasks?open=t-1a4c7e02` (a task with 3
exit criteria, 2 done) at 1440×900, and read the track and the a11y node off both builds:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| track box | **388×6 @ y406.1** | **388×6 @ y406.1** |
| track background | `rgb(40, 42, 44)` | `rgb(40, 42, 44)` |
| border radius | `9999px` | `9999px` |
| `role="progressbar"` | **absent** | **present** |
| `aria-valuenow` | — | **67** (2 of 3) |
| accessible name | — | **"Exit criteria"** |

**Byte-identical geometry, background and radius** — the adoption is pixel-neutral, which is why it was
the one deferred site worth taking. The section heading beside it already says `Exit criteria · 2/3`, so
a screen-reader user now gets the same fact from the bar instead of nothing.

Not verified: screen-reader pass, real-device touch.

## The rail ratchets 4 → 3, which is the move it calls the intended one

`meterAdoption.test.ts`'s own header says *"The rail's job is that this list does not GROW. Adding an
entry to it is the forbidden move; deleting one by adopting Meter is the intended one."* So `DEFERRED`
loses `TaskDetail.tsx` and the pin moves `toBe(4)` → `toBe(3)` **in this commit**.

The three that remain are genuinely deferred, not procedurally:

- `ModelsPanel.tsx` — 6px track on `bg-surface-container`, so adopting `Meter` retints it.
- `ui/genui/components.tsx` — 8px track; `Meter` has no 8px rung and inventing one for a single
  model-authored widget is speculative API.
- `loops/RunProgress.tsx` — square corners, and its only conveyance of progress is fill width plus a
  `title` on a **non-interactive div**, which is not an accessible name at all. It needs a shape
  decision, not an adoption.

**3 mutations, all killed** (baseline green after each, restored from `cp` backups):

| # | mutation | result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | revert the adoption — hand-rolled bar returns while off `DEFERRED` | 1 failed |
| 2 | put `TaskDetail.tsx` **back** on `DEFERRED` (the forbidden move) | 1 failed |
| 3 | leave the pin at `4` after removing an entry (a stale pin) | 1 failed |

## One rail needed renumbering, and it is worth flagging

`disabledReasonCensus.test.ts` excuses four `TaskDetail.tsx` controls **by line number**, so the twelve
lines of comment added here shifted all four: `197/208/226/254 → 210/221/239/267`, plus the `at(…, 254)`
anchor → `267`. I read each new line to confirm it is the same control (`disabled={readOnly}` ×2,
`disabled={!dep || !onOpenTask}`, `disabled={!onOpenTask}`) — **nothing about those controls changed**.

Renumbered with a note in the rail: a census keyed on `path:line` is exact about *which* site it
excuses, which is its strength, but it makes an unrelated insertion look like a new offender. Worth
re-keying on the control's own text if it bites a third time.

## Gate

- `npm run typecheck:web` — clean
- `npm run test:web` — **523 files / 5614 tests passed, exit 0** (full run). The first run failed only
  on the `disabledReasonCensus` line numbers above; green after renumbering.
- `npm run build` — ✓, ui-docs 102 components
- `npm run smoke:render` — **PASS, 5/5 routes**
- `make lint` / `make test` not run: **zero Python changed**

No visual baseline moved (the track is byte-identical). `docs/design/consistency-audit.json` was
rewritten by vitest and **not staged**. `tests/test_structural_baseline.py` is already red on `main` and
was left alone.

## Docs touched

None — the reasoning lives in the call site's comment and in the rail's ratchet note.

author: jarvis1openclaw
body:
Opened by an estate-wide sweep on 2026-08-27. **Nothing here was merged or changed**; this makes existing work visible.

This branch is **1 commit(s) ahead of `main`** and had no pull request, so its work existed only as a branch nobody was reviewing. On the same sweep, 85 checkouts across five hosts held commits that existed on **one machine only** and would have been destroyed by a pull, a checkout, or a worktree prune.

| | |
|---|---|
| branch | `pi/b65d0215-liveness` |
| commits ahead | 1 |
| last commit | 2026-08-26 |
| latest subject | chore: reconstruct frozen f4ffb2be parent |

## This needs triage, not automatic merging

The sweep could not tell finished work from an abandoned experiment, so it assumed nothing. One of three things is true here, and someone who knows the work should say which:

- **still wanted** — bring it up to date with `main`, get CI green, review and merge
- **superseded** — close it, and record what replaced it so the next sweep does not resurface it
- **abandoned** — close it; the commits stay reachable on the branch for audit

The rule this restores is already in the worker brief: branch first, commit early, push, open a PR, put the URL in the verdict. Work that only ever lived in a local worktree skipped that, which is why a sweep was needed at all.

author: nozerorma
body:
Supersedes #2 (closed). That branch had drifted too far from `main` to rebase cleanly, so this is the same work rebuilt on top of current `main` (28f054b): the modules were first extracted as small single-purpose branches, each `assembleDebug`-checked, then merged and localized. `git merge-base` with `main` is 28f054b, so it applies as a fast-forward.

72 files, ~+10.4k lines. Debug build tested on a KEY2 (LineageOS 22.2 / Android 15, 4.19 kernel); the signed release build is not device-tested.

## New modules (11)

**Keyboard**
- **Calculator Keys** – physical keys → AOSP/Google Calculator buttons (accessibility service, no root)
- **IME Suggestion Shortcuts** – Ctrl+W/E/R pick candidate 1/2/3 from the physical-keyboard candidate strip; only fires while a suggestion is showing; needs a key remapped to Ctrl
- **Chat Enter-to-Send** – Enter sends, Alt+Enter / Shift+Enter newline, in ~15 messaging apps
- **Call Shortcuts** – on the Google Phone call screen: M mutes, Currency/Ctrl toggles speaker, Q W E R / S D F / Z X C send DTMF; per-locale button-label matching
- **Auto-Focus** – in selected apps, focus + type into the first text field on the first printable keypress

**Display**
- **Extra Dim** – dim below the system minimum brightness, optional boot-persisted night schedule

**System**
- **Ticker Notifications** – scrolling status-bar banner instead of heads-up popups, and turns heads-up off system-wide while enabled. `NotificationListenerService` + a `TYPE_ACCESSIBILITY_OVERLAY` window; per-app / per-category blocklist; fixed / app-icon / Monet colour modes. Adds an `androidx.palette` dependency.

**Network**
- **Auto-disable Bluetooth** – turn Bluetooth off after a configurable idle period with nothing connected. Root daemon from service.d; multi-signal connection detection (adapter ACL state, A2DP/HFP active device, playback, AVRCP); wall-clock deadline so suspended time counts
- **Auto-disable Location** – same design, for Location; passive low-power Play-services location checks don't reset the timer
- **Global Telemetry Block** – disable Firebase Crashlytics system-wide (root, boot-persisted)

**Info**
- **Battery Usage** – per-app battery estimate from the platform's native power model

## Changed

- **Navigation**: bottom bar split into Keyboard / Display / System / Network tabs (plus Info and Settings) instead of one flat list
- **ZRAM screen**: seeds its controls from the live device state and marks which values come from ROM defaults
- **Status bar**: icon/background colour set explicitly per light/dark scheme

## Localization

- Every user-facing string (~499) moved from Kotlin literals into resources. `Screen` titles/subtitles, `AppTab` labels and `AccessType` labels are now `@StringRes`; `SettingsBackup.BackupModule` labels are string resources.
- Translations for **Catalan, German, Spanish, French, Italian, Dutch, Portuguese**. The 326 previously-translated strings for the older overlapping modules are carried over verbatim; ~173 new strings per language cover the new modules and Ticker. Key parity and printf-specifier parity with the English source verified for all 7 files.

## Fixed

- **Home menu**: the per-module access badges (`[root]` / `[accessibility]` / `[notification]`) shared an unweighted row with the subtitle, so a long subtitle squeezed them to near-zero width and each badge wrapped one character per line (surfaced by the longer translated subtitles). The subtitle now yields space and wraps itself; badges stay on one line.
- **5GHz Hotspot Workaround**: the boot script broke out of its retry loop on the first successful `force-country-code` call, so the telephony stack's SIM-country detection (~30–60 s into boot) silently reverted it. It now re-applies every 3 s for ~4 minutes after boot, then runs a 60 s drift watchdog, and stops as soon as the feature is toggled off.

## Notes for review

- `Screen.kt`, `HomeScreen.kt` and `Key2AccessibilityService.kt` were merged by hand (the repo's `merge=union` driver mangles adjacent inserts there). `onKeyEvent` dispatch order: IME-suggestions → nav-gesture → in-call → auto-focus → chat-composer → calculator → PIN.
- Auto-Focus and Call Shortcuts were device-tested (including a real call). The idle daemons are ports of hardened versions from the sibling q25toolbox project.
- `app/build.gradle.kts` now reads `keystore.properties` (repo root, gitignored) for release signing and falls back to an unsigned release when it's absent, replacing the commented-out placeholder block.
- Happy to split this into per-area PRs (the `feat/*` branches still exist and rebase cleanly) if you'd rather review it in pieces.
- versionCode 1 → 31, versionName → `5.0`; CHANGELOG.md and README.md updated.

author: frankd412
body:
## The problem

`effective_latency` is the only latency metric in AIPerf that includes failed requests.

It isn't computed through the metric registry, so it never passes the `record.valid` gate in `MetricRecordProcessor.process_record` that makes `request_latency`, TTFT, ITL and everything else success-only. It's derived at summarize-time from the column store's `end_ns` / `credit_issued_ns` columns, and `MetricsAccumulator.process_record` ingests those for **every** record, errors included.

The result today is a metric that is quietly *understated*. An errored record's `end_perf_ns` is unset, so `_create_metric_record_metadata` falls back to `start_perf_ns` and the failure enters the distribution as a queue-wait-only sample of a fraction of a millisecond. On a 100-request run at 34% errors:

| | `request_latency` | `effective_latency` | samples |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| main today | 747.6 ms (n=66) | **494.1 ms** | 100 |
| main + this PR | 771.8 ms (n=64) | **772.5 ms** | 64 |

`effective_latency` reads 34% below the true success-side latency, purely because 34 near-zero samples are averaged in. The `count=100` against `request_latency`'s `n=66` is the tell.

This gets worse, not better, once errored records carry an honest end timestamp. With #1333 applied — which correctly stamps `end_perf_ns` on non-2xx responses — the same workload with a 2 s time-to-error swings the metric the other way, to **1214 ms**, because each failure now contributes its full duration to the success distribution. Either way the number is wrong; this PR makes it right in both worlds, and is independent of #1333.

## The change

**`effective_latency` is masked on `has_error`.** `RequestRecord.valid` is `not has_error and …`, so this gives the metric exactly the same population as every other latency metric — including cancellations, which carry `ErrorDetails(code=499)` and are already absent from `request_latency`. The mask composes with the existing export-context (phase/window) mask.

**New `adj_effective_latency`.** A coordinated-omission metric with no failure-aware companion would be the one gap that reporting the success-only view opens, so this adds the treatment `PERCENTILE_INCLUDES_FAILED_REQUESTS` gives the registry latency metrics: the success-only distribution plus one `+inf` sample per errored record, rendered as `Effective Latency (CO-aware) (error-adjusted)` in the Effective console table. `avg` / `sum` / upper percentiles become `inf` (serialized as `null`, matching `adj_request_latency`); `std` is `None` because variance is undefined over a distribution containing `inf`. Omitted on a clean run (nothing to inflate) and on a total-failure run (no distribution to inflate).

`effective_latency` is not a registry metric, so it cannot carry the flag — the `+inf` builder is refactored so both paths share one implementation instead of duplicating the percentile logic.

## Deliberately unchanged: `effective_concurrency`

The sweep-line curves keep counting failed requests. A request that hung before returning 5xx genuinely occupied a slot for that whole time, and dropping it would under-report the load the server actually carried. The asymmetry between the per-record Effective metric and the sweep-line Effective metrics is now stated in the docs rather than left implicit.

Token-weighted and decode-phase curves are unaffected either way: an errored record has no `input_sequence_length` / `output_sequence_length` to weight by, and never reached first-token, so its `generation_start_ns` is NaN.

## Verification

- `tests/unit/` green
- 8 new tests in `tests/unit/metrics/test_derived_latency.py`: the error mask, mask composition with an export-context window, `+inf` inflation, the p50 failover at a 50% error rate, and both empty-population cases
- `pre-commit run` — all hooks pass
- End-to-end runs above reproduced against the in-repo mock server (`--error-rate 30`, with a 2 s delay injected before the 500 for the #1333 comparison, since instant errors make that delta invisible)

## Docs

`docs/reference/effective-vs-active-metrics.md` gains a "Failed requests" section covering both behaviors, plus two rows in the metric-selection table.

## Relationship to #1333

Independent — this branch is based on `main` and contains none of #1333's commits. The two interact but neither blocks the other: #1333 makes errored records carry a real end timestamp, which changes the magnitude and sign of the error this PR fixes. Context in https://github.com/ai-dynamo/aiperf/pull/1333#issuecomment-5432868297.

author: gokhan
body:
## Summary

Adds Grok (the xAI coding CLI) to the request-logger catalogue, in the same shape as Copilot: one provider, one env override, no config file.

- Grok builds the system prompt on the machine and sends it over HTTP to `cli-chat-proxy.grok.com`, so it can be logged. A grok.com login and an `XAI_API_KEY` both talk to that host; the API key is a credential fallback, not a different route.
- The printed command is `GROK_CLI_CHAT_PROXY_BASE_URL=http://localhost:PORT/v1 grok`. The `/v1` suffix is required: Grok appends `/responses` (and `/models`) to the default `https://cli-chat-proxy.grok.com/v1`.
- The existing OpenAI renderer already reads the Responses API shape Grok uses by default.
- `GROK_MODELS_BASE_URL` is a different override (it switches the CLI onto API-key auth against a custom `/v1/models` endpoint). The command never sets it; a warning tells the student to unset it if it is already in the environment, or the logs folder stays empty.
- Grok also makes a second model call to title the session, so one turn can write two captures — the same fan-out as OpenCode. Documented in the README next to that note.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest run request-logger` — 296 tests pass, including new Grok coverage: catalogue order, `needsProvider`, host, `/v1` suffix, OpenAI renderer, POSIX and PowerShell commands, `GROK_MODELS_BASE_URL` not set, custom-target template reuse, `customTargetNeedsModel` false
- [x] `npx prettier --check` on changed files
- [x] Live `grok -p` turn through the proxy: `POST /v1/responses` returned 200, capture has tools + prompt + reply; GETs (`/v1/models`, `/v1/settings`) were forwarded and not logged

author: chmoses98
body:
## Summary

Real results for MLB-RSCH-0005 (Multi-Season Team Offense Recency/Form
Backtest): does a team's recent offensive performance, relative to its own
point-in-time season baseline, predict next-game scoring beyond PIT-safe
season/opponent baselines — or is it mostly noise/mean reversion?

**No new fetch was needed.** Every schedule payload already committed by
MLB-RSCH-0003 carries both teams' final scores per game, so this experiment
ran entirely **locally** against the existing cache — no GitHub Actions
dispatch, no network access. Full write-up in
`docs/EDGELAB_MLB_RSCH_0005_TEAM_OFFENSE_RECENCY.md`.

**No production code, config, staking, risk-gate, or settlement logic is
touched. `productionBehaviorChanged: false` in the machine-readable result.**

### Headline finding: NO_USEFUL_SIGNAL

- **H1/H2/H3 (5/10/20-game recent-form deviation persistence)**: all nine
  correlation CIs (3 windows × 3 periods) cross zero — no statistically
  confident relationship between recent form and next-game scoring in any
  period.
- **H4 (frozen control-vs-candidate regression)**: adding recent-form
  deviations to a season+opponent-baseline regression improves development
  MAE by only 0.03% and shows no consistent improvement out-of-sample
  (slightly worse in validation, slightly better in holdout — both
  differences under 0.002 MAE).
- **H5 (extreme hot/cold groups)**: teams on an extreme hot or cold streak
  (development-frozen 10th/90th percentile cutoffs) regress **88–100% of the
  way back to their own season baseline by the very next game**, in every
  period, both directions — a strong, consistent, out-of-sample-replicated
  descriptive finding.
- Recent offensive form is **mostly noise/mean reversion**, not a repeatable
  predictive signal, across 20,478 real team-games (2022–2026, well above
  the 10,000-team-game minimum).

### What this PR adds
- `lib/edgelab/backtest/team_offense_recency_reconstruction.py` — PIT
  season/opponent baselines, fixed 5/10/20-game recent-form windows and
  deviations, 20-prior-game eligibility floor, outcome extraction. Reuses
  `is_strictly_before()` unchanged.
- `lib/edgelab/backtest/team_offense_recency_stats.py` — dependency-free
  (no numpy) closed-form OLS for the frozen control-vs-candidate comparison,
  percentile cutoffs and persistence-vs-regression summary for extreme
  groups.
- `lib/edgelab/backtest/bullpen_backtest_reconstruction.py` — additive,
  backward-compatible extension of `extract_team_games_from_schedule()`
  with `runsScored`/`runsAllowed`/`opponentTeamId` (that module's own
  30-test suite still passes unchanged).
- `scripts/edgelab/run_multiseason_team_offense_recency_experiment.py` —
  preregisters MLB-RSCH-0005 before any outcome analysis, builds team-game
  rows across development(2022-2024)/validation(2025)/holdout(2026) with
  team-clustered bootstrap CIs for H1-H3, a development-fit-and-frozen
  regression comparison for H4, and development-fit-and-frozen extreme-group
  cutoffs for H5.
- `data/edgelab/experiments/MLB-RSCH-0005.json`,
  `data/edgelab/experiment_reports/MLB-RSCH-0005/RPT-054001d7be17503c.json`,
  `data/edgelab/analytics/latest_mlb_rsch_0005_team_offense_recency_backtest.json`
  — the real preregistration record and machine-readable results.
- `docs/EDGELAB_MLB_RSCH_0005_TEAM_OFFENSE_RECENCY.md` — full write-up.
- 106 new tests: PIT feature reconstruction, leakage guards, eligibility,
  OLS/percentile/persistence statistics, preregistration ordering, holdout
  isolation, frozen-candidate/cutoff reuse (proven by object identity, not
  just equal values), end-to-end synthetic-cache backtest, signal
  classification.

### Verification
- Data integrity hand-verified against a real 2023 row (SD, 2023-04-25).
- Focused MLB-RSCH-0005 test suite: 106/106 passed.
- Full CI-equivalent suite (`pytest tests/ -q`): 7061 passed, 7 skipped, 4

body:
## v1.8 — tes données peuvent sortir du navigateur

Un bouton sur ton profil télécharge tes favoris, ta liste de suivi et ton historique dans un fichier. Un autre les restaure — sur un autre appareil, ou après un nettoyage de navigateur.

Jusqu'ici, un « effacer les données du site » les emportait **sans aucun recours**. C'est le filet qui manquait sous tout ce qui a été protégé ces derniers jours.

## Ce qui ne peut pas mal tourner

**Une restauration complète, elle ne remplace jamais.** Importer une vieille sauvegarde ne peut pas faire reculer une progression : une série suivie jusqu'à l'épisode 12 le reste, même si le fichier la connaît à l'épisode 3.

**Le fichier n'emporte pas ton consentement aux cookies.** Le restaurer reviendrait à te faire dire oui à ta place ; il te sera redemandé, comme à la première visite.

**Un fichier abîmé est refusé en entier**, sans rien écrire. Une restauration à moitié laisserait un état dont personne ne saurait d'où il vient.

## Vérifié

178 tests, 12 parcours, 34 passes d'accessibilité. Le téléchargement est contrôlé sur le build — il pouvait buter silencieusement sur la politique de sécurité de contenu — et le fichier produit ne contient pas le consentement.

#### What type of PR is this?
/kind enhancement
/sig storage

#### What this PR does / why we need it:
`ValidateKey` in `pkg/yurthub/storage/utils/validate.go` currently only checks
that a `storage.Key` is non-nil/non-empty and has the expected concrete Go
type (via `reflect.TypeOf`). It does not validate the internal format of the
key's path, as noted by an existing TODO comment:

```go
// TODO: should also valid the key format
```

This means a key with the correct type but a malformed internal path (e.g.
missing segments, invalid resource/version/group format) passes validation
silently, and only fails later when it is actually parsed/used (e.g. by
`disk.ExtractKeyBuildInfo`).

This PR completes the TODO by:
- Adding an optional `KeyFormatValidator` interface (`Validate() error`) in
  `pkg/yurthub/storage`, kept separate from the existing minimal `Key`
  interface so it stays backward compatible for key types that don't need
  format validation (e.g. `ClusterInfoKey`).
- Implementing `Validate()` on `disk.storageKey`, reusing the same parsing
  rules already used by `ExtractKeyBuildInfo`.
- Updating `ValidateKey` in `utils/validate.go` to call `Validate()` via a
  type assertion, only when the key implements it.
- Adding unit tests covering both `disk.storageKey.Validate()` and the
  updated `utils.ValidateKey`.

body:
## BUG-530 — the ＋ sheet says what the press does

The ＋ sheet's top option read **"☰ Play Next"** on all six track sheets, and the
series/boxset ＋ Queue confirmed **"Queued to Play Next"** — long after TASK-504
and TASK-505 had put the last media type on the append. Every press lands at the
end of the Queue, so the sheet promised the front of it and the toast that
followed confirmed the end. On the companion's own series list the two toasts had
already drifted apart from each other.

The option is now **"☰ Add to Queue"**, and the last hand-written toast reads its
wording from `queueAddStatus` like the other twelve ＋ producers do.

### Verified against fresh `origin/main`, per site

The spec asked for this before rewording anything: **no site still front-inserts.**
Every ＋ press already routes through `queueAdd`, so this PR is wording only — no
behaviour change, no engine change.

The spec's list was written on a checkout predating both cutovers, so the re-count
differs: `screen-detail-page.js` was the **only** remaining hardcoded
`showStatus('Queued to Play Next')` — `companion-detail.js` and `companion-audio.js`
had already moved onto the config. The six sheet labels were all still stale.

### Where the wording lives

`core/queue-shell-config.js` already owned `"Added to Queue"`. The sheet label now
sits beside it as `QUEUE_ADD_LABEL`, so the option and the confirmation it produces
can't drift apart again.

**Plumbing call:** one exported constant, not a per-type `add.label` field. Every
type appends, so the option says the same thing everywhere — a per-type field
would need `mediaType` threaded through six screens' `addState` to render a label
that never varies, and a type wanting its own word here is exactly the difference
that file's ⛔ says to fix rather than codify.

### Changed

- `core/queue-shell-config.js` — `QUEUE_ADD_LABEL`, beside `APPEND`'s status.
- Six sheet sites, TV and companion mirrored per FEAT-017/028 — album detail,
  artist, playlist detail on both surfaces.
- `screen-detail-page.js` — `queueVideo` toasts via `queueAddStatus`.
- Comments describing the option as "Play Next" across `screen-detail.js`,
  `screen-video-page.js`, `components/tile.js` and the six sheets.
- `docs/VERIFY-STORIES.md` — the C13/C14/T13 flow steps naming the old label.

### Tests

Red first, then fixed: the eight e2e label assertions and the config unit test
failed on the unfixed code, then passed. Toast assertion in `video-queue.test.js`
moved to `"Added to Queue"`.

- Touched e2e suites: **82 passed**.
- `checks-local`: **28/28 green**, cyclomatic cap included.
- Scoped mutation sweep on the one changed `core/` file: **100%, 0 survivors**
  (56 mutants). It entered at 94.64% with three survivors in `queueAdd`'s error
  strings — inherited, not from this diff, and killed here by asserting the actual
  messages rather than only that the press rejects.

### Out of scope

`docs/QUEUE.md` is stale the same way — TASK-529. What ＋ *does* is settled
FEAT-497 behaviour and untouched.

### Run it

```bash
python3 /Users/dan/dan-grew-repos/grew-tv/media-manager/core/media-manager.py \
  --app-dir         /Users/dan/dan-grew-repos/grew-tv-app-BUG-530 \
  --manifest-dir    ~/dan-grew-repos/grew-tv-state/manifests \
  --content-root    ~/rips \
  --state-repo-dir  /tmp/grew-state
```

press ＋ on a track.

body:
## Почему такой замер **Первый отказ нарисован в самом курсе.** Итоговая схема Л10 состоит из двух столбцов: слева философия *как знание* — запомнить имена и учения, спорить о терминах, блеснуть эрудицией, философия остаётся в голове; справа философия *как образ жизни* — проверять свои убеждения, жить по своим ценностям. Мерить себя выученным значило бы считать очки по левому столбцу схемы, которая нарисована ради правого. **Второй отказ** — от числа вопросов, на которые слушатель наконец определился. Л1 отдельным разделом говорит: философия даёт не ответы, а вопросы получше; Л10 — что жить с открытыми вопросами это умение, а не промежуточное состояние. Мерятся два действия, оба из правого столбца: 1. **Сократический ход** — сколько раз за неделю человек попросил определение («что именно вы называете справедливым, нормальным, успешным») вместо того, чтобы спорить дальше. 2. **Дихотомия контроля** из Л7, которую Эпиктет называл началом мудрости — сколько раз в конкретной тревоге он разделил, что в его власти, а что нет, и снял усилие оттуда, где не в его. ## Задания Практикумов в курсе **не было ни одного**, поэтому все двадцать заданий новые: по два на лекцию, плюс сверка-возврат в Л2–Л10. ## Экзамен Про выпускника такого же курса, который живёт целиком в левом столбце. Он свободно объясняет разницу рационализма и эмпиризма и вставляет в спор, что «это, собственно, платоновский вопрос». При этом: - за месяц трижды поссорился, доказывая свою справедливость — и ни разу не спросил, что собеседник называет справедливым; - полночи не спит от новостей — дихотомия контроля лежит нетронутой; - полгода не решается на разговор с начальником, объясняя это тем, что «свобода воли — вообще спорная штука». Последнее разобрано отдельно: философское затруднение употреблено во вред себе — неопределённость в теории превращена в отказ от действия, хотя все три позиции курса ведут к одному практическому выводу. Итог: ему не нужно читать больше, ему нужно один раз применить. ## Хронометраж Лекции 16,7–18,7, финал 19,4 (было 13,3–15,8), курс 176 мин. ## Проверки - `check_site.py` — 1773 страницы, 0 ошибок - `check_blog.py` — 0 ошибок, 0 предупреждений - алфавит, markdown, баланс `

`, дубли `id`, посторонние символы — чисто - рендер Playwright на 960 px: Л1 и Л10 — без горизонтальной прокрутки и JS-ошибок В журнале `KURSY-STATUS.md` строка курса переведена из 🔧 в ✅ — готово 69 курсов из 102. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_01M9AJ1rzB1GeEahyQGXb655 --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code/session_01M9AJ1rzB1GeEahyQGXb655)_

author: halorgium
body:
## Problem

The extended `ps -x` output rendered a wide **14-column** `hux.table`. On any terminal narrower than the full table width — which is nearly always, given it packs dyno UUIDs, timestamps, IPs, routes, and a new `Fleet` column — every cell wrapped down to a few characters, shredding each value vertically:

```
  ID   Process   State   Region   Execution     Fleet   Instance   IP   Port   AZ   Release   Command   Route   Size
                                  Plane
 ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  00   web.1     up      us       ex01          exam    0000000    10   0000   us   1         example   0000a   Stan
  00             0000/                          ple-1              .0   0      -e             -comman   000-0   dard
  ...
```

The existing `--no-wrap` flag only truncated instead of wrapping, and it was opt-in — so the default experience stayed unreadable.

## Fix

Render one **vertical detail block per dyno** using `hux.styledObject` under a styled header — the same pattern as `releases:info` and other detail views:

```
=== web.1 (Standard-1X)
ID:              00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000
State:           up 0000/00/00 00:00 (~00m ago)
Release:         1
Command:         example-command as t-0000
Region:          us
Execution Plane: example-plane
Fleet:           standard-1x
Instance:        0000000.0.0.00
IP:              10.0.0.0
Port:            00000
AZ:              us-example-0a
Route:           00000000-0000-...
```

Benefits:
- **Never wraps** at any terminal width.
- **Full command** shown rather than truncated to 35 chars.

author: fercho-93
body:
## Resumen

Tres mejoras para sacarle más partido a lo que el juego ya tiene, siguiendo la propuesta de análisis discutida en el chat:

- **Repaso al terminar** (`app.js`): cada carta fallada —en partida local, solitario o competición— se registra aparte del descarte (`game.failed` / `solo.failed`), y al terminar la partida un botón "Ver lo que se falló" abre una pantalla con esas cartas: año/dato, época y su explicación completa, en vez de perderse en el descarte sin más.
- **Mapa a escala real** (`mapa.js`): las paradas ya no se reparten a partes iguales, se sitúan proporcionalmente a su valor real (año, superficie o población) dentro del rango de lo colocado, así que de un vistazo se ve la forma de verdad de la línea —racimos y huecos— y no solo un índice. Cuando dos paradas quedan demasiado cerca para pulsarlas por separado, se empujan lo justo para seguir siendo un botón de 44px.
- **Modo Competición** (`app.js`, entrada nueva en el inicio): una ronda de 5 cartas por cada uno de los seis juegos, en un orden al azar distinto cada vez y sin repetir ninguno, reutilizando el motor de solitario (`solo`, `kind: "comp"`). Al terminar la última ronda se ve el marcador agregado de toda la competición, con su propio botón de repaso cruzando fallos de varios temas. No se guarda entre sesiones: cada ronda cambia la modalidad seleccionada, y esa modalidad es la que decide dónde se guardan las partidas normales de solitario.

Sobre la carátula de competición: no tengo acceso a una herramienta de generación de imágenes fotográficas como las que ya existen en `assets/`. Construí una ilustración vectorial propia (SVG renderizado a webp con Playwright) en la misma paleta cálida de la app —medalla con laurel sobre fondo degradado, con los iconos de los tres bloques de fondo—, coherente pero no una réplica del estilo pictórico de las otras tres. Si se genera una más parecida, se sustituye sin tocar el resto del cambio.

`service-worker.js`: `CACHE` sube a `continuum-v13` (nuevos assets + cambios de contenido).

## Pruebas

- Las 7 suites de `tests/`: 0 fallos.
- Verificación manual con Playwright:
  - Repaso: partida libre en solitario y partida local terminadas con fallos a propósito, comprobando que el botón aparece y que cada carta mostrada trae su descripción.
  - Mapa: con 8 cartas colocadas, todas las paradas mantienen ≥44px de separación y las separaciones no son uniformes (confirma escala real, no reparto a partes iguales).
  - Competición: recorrido completo por los 6 temas sin repetirse, pantalla final con marcador agregado y una fila por tema, y la modalidad guardada en `localStorage` no cambia por haber jugado.

body:
Adds `.claude/skills/ngjfi-platform/` — a project skill both of us, and any agent working for either of us, picks up automatically when the repo is connected to a session. No account sharing needed; it travels with the repo.

## Why

Ulrich's palette work was finished on 6 August and did not reach GitHub until 27 August, because the session holding it had no push credential. Cloning a *public* repo needs none, so an unwired session looks completely healthy — it clones, reads, edits, commits and runs tests without a single warning — and the failure only surfaces at `git push`, by which point the work exists inside a container that gets reclaimed.

That is the second incident of the same shape. The remedy both times was a document explaining the correct setup, which is a remedy that depends on someone remembering to read it.

## What it does

**Step 0 is an empty push.** Before any code, on every session: branch, push nothing, confirm it lands, delete it. Thirty seconds. It converts a silent, late, expensive failure into a loud, early, free one — and it works regardless of which setup path the session is on.

Beyond that it carries the things we currently restate by hand:

- never push to `main`; branch, PR, CI green, Netlify preview, squash-merge
- claim the migration number in chat first — parallel work will otherwise collide on `0015`
- colour is semantic: vermillion means "down", the tier ramp encodes depth by lightness, all colour lives in one `:root` block
- respondents stay anonymous, orgs see aggregates only, never overclaim
- the repo is public — only `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` values, ever

`references/setup.md` covers both setup paths and how to rescue work from a session that cannot push. `references/architecture.md` maps the codebase. `references/guardrails.md` gives the reasoning behind each rule, because a rule you understand survives a situation its author did not foresee.

## Checks

Documentation only — no application code, no dependencies, no CI changes. Every file path, npm script and factual claim in it was verified against this repo before commit.

author: davidpit1565
body:
## Why

Follow-up from a 10-agent audit of the live app (security findings went out separately in #11, already merged). This PR is the highest-priority items that are already affecting production today, not hypothetical:

- **`ink-faint` fails WCAG AA contrast almost everywhere it's used** (~3.3–3.5:1 against `surface`/`ground`, need 4.5:1) — footer copy, form hints, every agent's metadata line, 30+ call sites. Lightened `#5f6b64` → `#8a978f` (6:1+ against both surfaces, still reads as muted).
- **Several animations never respected `prefers-reduced-motion`** (only the hero glow and `<Reveal>` did) — including the shake on a sign-in error and fade-up on hero/form elements, exactly the pages someone with a vestibular disorder is most likely to hit first.
- **Missing indexes** on columns filtered on every hot page load: `agents.creator_id`, `purchases(agent_id, buyer_id, status)`, `reviews.agent_id`.
- **Stripe webhook never checked its own DB write errors** — a charge could succeed while the purchase/membership/subscription/connect write silently never landed, with Stripe told `{received: true}` and no retry. Now logs with event context and returns 5xx on a real failure (treating a duplicate-event unique-constraint hit as the idempotent no-op it actually is).
- **`platform_fee_cents` had a second hard-coded `0.15`** instead of using `PLATFORM_FEE_PERCENT` — would've silently drifted from the real fee the moment it's ever changed. Same fix applied to the payouts page's copy.
- **No `charge.refunded` handler** — a refunded buyer kept `status: 'paid'` forever (still shown as owning it, still eligible to review it).

Also included, small and low-risk: accessible names on the search input and admin status `<select>`, `aria-pressed` on category filter chips, the notification dropdown overflowing off-screen on narrow phones, a duplicated `Notice` component, and a creator page missing the `<Reveal>` treatment every other agent grid has.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean
- [x] `npm run build` — clean
- [ ] After merge, run the updated `supabase/schema.sql` once (new indexes) — safe to re-run
- [ ] Manual: confirm `/dashboard/payouts`'s fee copy and a test refund both reflect correctly

author: dazewell
body:
Replaces #206, abandoned because a commit body in that branch carried an unharvestable-by-design example tag (`#foo`) that permanently poisoned the `BASE_SHA..HEAD_SHA` scan range with no way to remove it short of an amend/force-push. Same fix, replayed as a single clean commit on a fresh branch cut from `dev` — nothing on the old branch was rewritten.

Fixes two defects in the `#<slug>` change-tag enforcement (`.githooks/commit-msg` and `.github/workflows/commit-tag.yml`), plus a follow-up dedup fix and a CLAUDE.md wording correction, all from round-1/round-2 review on #206:

**Defect 1 (originally reported):** a bare numeric hashtag like a PR reference (`#202`) was harvested as a feature slug by the CI job's FEATURES.md check, demanding a catalogue entry for a slug that was never a real change tag. Hit live during the 12.10.1 sync.

**Defect 2 (found while scoping #206):** the same numeric hashtag also satisfied the tag-*presence* check in both the hook and CI, so a commit whose only hashtag was a PR reference silently passed as "tagged" while carrying no real change tag.

**Fix:** the presence regex and the slug-harvest regex in both files now require at least one letter somewhere in the hashtag token. Purely numeric tokens no longer count as a tag and are never harvested as a slug. Tags that start with a digit but contain a letter (`#2fa`) keep working.

**Review round 2 findings (from #206), also included here:**
- The CI slug harvester lacked the same leading-boundary guard the presence checks already had, so a hashtag glued to a preceding word (e.g. a URL anchor) could still be harvested as a slug. Fixed by reusing the boundary-aware regex and stripping the boundary character back off.
- Deduplication of harvested slugs happened on the raw match (which can carry different boundary characters for the same slug), which could print duplicate `::error::` lines for one missing catalogue entry. Fixed by stripping the boundary before `sort -u` instead of after.
- `CLAUDE.md`'s description of the numeric-hashtag rule read as if a bare PR reference were compliant on its own. Reworded so both halves are explicit: safe alongside a real tag, never a substitute for one.

No Java/Kotlin touched by the doc/CI files, but `.githooks/commit-msg` is part of the diff so the staging build will run.

**Verification (carried over from #206, all still valid against the identical final file state):**
- Regression-scanned `origin/dev` history: the only letter-free hashtags found are upstream PR/issue references from merge commits and `(#nnn)`-style commit titles — none is a genuine fork change tag.
- Exercised `.githooks/commit-msg` directly: a message whose only hashtag is a numeric PR reference is rejected; `#ci` and `#2fa` are accepted.
- Verified the boundary-aware harvest regex excludes a URL-anchor example and numeric refs, while still harvesting genuine tags, with no duplicate output after the dedup-ordering fix.

A known, separate, out-of-scope follow-up was identified during #206's review and is **not** addressed here: the harvester can still pick up a letter-bearing hashtag written as a plain example in commit prose (not meant as a change tag). Fixing that changes what every future commit's prose needs to avoid, so it needs its own recon and round-1 review rather than being folded into this diff.

body: Tracker: #421. Parent: #424. ```ts executeAuthorizedRequest(input, execute) ``` One Effectful request constructor. JWT identity is deployment-global. The trusted request path selects the database. The deployed unit must name that same database. Acquisition is `currentDb(routeDatabase)`. That database's deployed policy decides access. ## Contract ``` JWT establishes principal identity and global claims trusted request path selects the database deployed unit must name that same database database acquisition must use that same database that database's deployed policy decides access ``` There is no required `ramose.db` claim and no `verified.principal.db === pathDb` check. author: isaacammonbarlow-max
body:
## Summary

Wave A: the AI helper gets hands — crew scheduling. Per `a1-ai-scheduler-spec.md`'s settled decisions (cited throughout, never re-decided): **drafts-then-publish**, **permission mirror**, and a V1 toolset that is scheduling-only.

- **A1** — Saved crews: named teams (2-6 people) a supervisor builds on the Roster.
- **A2** — Tool-calling in the `ask` edge function: a bounded (≤6 round-trip) tool loop, and the three-tool scheduling toolset.
- **A3** — The "AI proposed" badge on the crew board.
- **A4** — The doors: Scheduling's "Plan with AI" button, and progress lines on Ask.
- **A5** — Tests: unit coverage alongside A1/A2, plus one e2e spec.

## A1 — Saved crews

- `supabase/migrations/20260955000000_saved_crews.sql`: table `saved_crews` (`name` 1-40 chars, `member_ids uuid[]` 2-6, `note`, `created_by`). RPC-only writes — `save_crew`/`delete_crew`, both supervisor+ (`my_role_rank() >= 2`), validating name length, member count, and that every member is an **active** profile. RLS select is foreman+ (crew visibility norm).
- Roster (`Crew.tsx`) gets a **Saved crews** section (`SavedCrewsSection.tsx`): read-only for foreman, full CRUD for supervisor+, a `sched-chip` member picker matching `AssignmentEditor`'s own.
- CONTEXT.md: new "Crew scheduling and the AI assistant" section, **Saved crew** term.
- `scripts/supabase_merge_lib.py` / `test_supabase_merge.py`: `saved_crews` → `DEDUP_KEYS = None` (a supervisor-chosen name isn't a natural key, same reasoning as `studio_projects`), table count 107 → 108.

## A2 — Tool-calling in `ask`

- `supabase/functions/_shared/anthropicTools.ts` (pure, unit-tested): `runToolLoop` — the tool_use/tool_result orchestrator, bounded to `MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS = 6`, with `send`/`executeTool` injected so it's fully mockable.
- `supabase/functions/_shared/anthropic.ts`: `anthropicToolChat` — the impure wrapper turning the loop into real Messages API requests carrying `tools`.
- `supabase/functions/_shared/schedulingTools.ts` (pure, unit-tested): the three tool definitions, the supervisor-rank gate (`schedulingRefusal`), pure entry/date-range validation, and the system-prompt addendum restating the settled team rules verbatim.
- `supabase/functions/_shared/auth.ts`: new `callerSupabaseClient(req)` — a client scoped to the **caller's own JWT**, mirroring `verifyCaller`'s internal construction. This is the actual permission gate: `schedule_assignments`' RLS is "authenticated full access" (wide open), so `my_role_rank()` run against the real caller is the only thing standing between a foreman's chat message and a draft write.
- `supabase/functions/_shared/estimate.ts`: `lib/estimate.ts`'s pure math (`estimateJob`/`recommendCrew`) moved here, same move `knowledge.ts` made — `app/src/lib/estimate.ts` now re-exports it, zero changes to its two existing importers (`ProjectDetail.tsx`, `Analytics.tsx`). `get_scheduling_picture` calls this SAME math server-side rather than letting the model re-derive job-duration numbers.
- `supabase/functions/ask/index.ts`: wires it all in. Tools are offered on **every** ask call to every real caller (never conditionally hidden by role) — a below-rank caller gets the tool's own clean refusal to relay, exactly like a human hitting a permission wall. Tool calls map to plain progress lines (`toolActivity`) for A4.

### The tool JSON shapes

**`get_scheduling_picture(from, to)`** — required `from`, `to` (`YYYY-MM-DD`). Returns:
```json
{
  "range": { "from": "...", "to": "..." },
  "active_jobs": [{
    "id": "...", "code": "BLACK22", "name": "...", "address": "...",
    "remaining": { "window": 4, "door": 1 },
    "estimate": {
      "remaining_openings": 5, "expected_minutes": 220, "p90_minutes": 310,
      "unknown_types": 0, "recommended_crew": 1, "crew_hours": 3.7, "hours_to_finish": 3.7
    }
  }],
  "crew": [{
    "id": "...", "name": "Chris", "skill_level": 4, "role": "installer", "active": true,
    "capabilities": ["wet_glazing"],
    "booked": [{ "job": "PECAN14", "start_date": "...", "end_date": "...", "status": "published" }]
  }],
  "saved_crews": [{ "id": "...", "name": "Sand Hollow Crew", "member_ids": ["..."], "note": "..." }],
  "existing_ai_drafts": [{ "id": "...", "job": "BLACK22", "start_date": "...", "end_date": "...", "profile_ids": ["..."] }]
}
```

**`draft_assignments({ entries })`** — `entries`: 1-200 × `{ project_id, profile_id, date }`. Writes one `schedule_assignments` row per entry (the board's own single-day/single-member draft unit — matches `Scheduling.tsx`'s `createDayDraft`), `status: 'draft'`, `created_via: 'ai'`. **Never** touches `status: 'published'`. Returns:
```json
{
  "results": [
    { "project_id": "...", "profile_id": "...", "date": "2026-09-01", "ok": true },
    { "project_id": "...", "profile_id": "...", "date": "2026-09-02", "ok": false, "reason": "double_booked" },
    { "index": 2, "ok": false, "reason": "invalid_entry", "detail": "date must be YYYY-MM-DD" }
  ],
  "drafted": 4, "refused": 1
}
```
Refusal reasons: `double_booked`, `unknown_project`, `unknown_profile`, `invalid_entry`, `write_failed`. Re-drafting the exact same (profile, project, date) is idempotent (`ok: true`, no duplicate row); the same profile/date under a **different** project is `double_booked` — checked against both the database and earlier entries in the same call.

**`clear_ai_drafts({ from, to, project_id? })`** — deletes only `status = 'draft' AND created_via = 'ai'` rows in range (published rows and a human's own drafts are never even selected). Returns `{ "removed": 3 }`.

All three: below supervisor rank, the tool returns the plain sentence *"Scheduling is a supervisor call. I can't read or change the crew board for you — ask a supervisor or owner to plan this, or ask me something else."* — not `is_error`, since the model is meant to relay it as prose, not retry.

## A3 — The AI badge on the board

- `supabase/migrations/20260955010000_schedule_assignments_ai_marker.sql`: `schedule_assignments.created_via` (`null` | `'ai'`). **Permanent** — publish never clears it, so the audit trail outlives the draft; only the chip's *visibility* is draft-scoped.
- `AiProposedChip.tsx` + CSS: its own component/class (same technique `DayFlowChip` uses to reuse `InstallChip`'s pill shape without extending its `InstallState` union — provenance isn't an install state). Accent tone per the spec ("InstallChip tones, accent"), rendered as a **corner badge** rather than inline text: `.cb-chip`'s label already runs single-line with an ellipsis at 11.5px, and a second inline pill would just get clipped on longer job codes.

author: pouzor
body:
Embeds a Homelable canvas in any Lovelace dashboard, read-only, as a native
custom card. HA auth applies, no new HTTP endpoint and no new WS command.

```yaml
type: custom:homelable-canvas-card
design_id: <uuid>        # optional — first design when omitted
title: Network           # optional card header
height: 500              # px, default 400
fit_view: true           # default
interactive: pan         # pan | none
open_on_click: false     # click a node to open http://<ip>, default off
```

## What's in it

- **Second Vite entry.** The ha build now emits `homelable-card-[hash].js`
  beside the panel bundle. HA loads it on *every* frontend page through
  `add_extra_js_url`, so the entry is a bare custom element — React, Tailwind
  and the canvas sit behind a dynamic import that only runs once a card is on
  screen. Eager cost: ~4 kB gzipped. Statically imported it was 440 kB.
- **The card element.** `setConfig` with validation, `getCardSize`,
  `getStubConfig`, card-picker entry.
- **The canvas.** Panel node and edge types, live status through the existing
  `useStatusPolling` subscription. Drag, connect, select, reconnect and the
  delete/selection keys are all off.
- **Registration.** `async_register_card` / `async_unregister_card` in
  `panel.py`, wired into setup and last-entry unload.
- **Dead code.** The stale standalone `LiveView.tsx` port and its test are gone
  — nothing imported them and `liveviewApi.load` only ever threw.

## Choices worth reviewing

- **The wheel doesn't zoom** (Ctrl+wheel and the zoom buttons do). A card that
  swallows the wheel traps a scrolling dashboard.
- **No demo-data fallback.** An empty or failed load shows a message. The panel
  falls back to `demoNodes`; doing that on a dashboard would put invented
  devices in front of a user as if they were real.
- **One card per dashboard view.** Node components read the global
  `canvasStore` singleton, so a second canvas would overwrite the first. Extra
  cards show a notice. Tracking is a module-level list, not a DOM query —
  Lovelace mounts cards inside its own shadow roots. Lifting the limit means a
  store factory behind React context (~8 files); it's on the README roadmap.
- **Static path fix.** It was registered inside `async_register_panel`, after
  that function's early return on a missing panel bundle, so a build with only
  a card bundle would have served it from a route that never existed. Now its
  own guarded helper, called by both registrations.

## Known issues

- `fit_view` doesn't cadre correctly in a Sections view: `fitView` fires on a
  50 ms timer and the card often hasn't reached its final width by then, so
  nodes are clipped on the right. The fix is to refit on React Flow's `onInit`
  rather than a timer — not in this PR.
- YAML-only, no visual config editor (`getConfigElement`) yet.

## Testing

Python 396 passed, frontend 1288 passed, ruff and tsc clean. 25 new tests
across `tests/test_panel.py`, `tests/test_init.py`, `cardConfig`, `haCard`,
`ReadOnlyCanvas` and `canvasPayload`.

Not yet exercised in a real HA container — `docker-compose.dev.yml` +
`scripts/dev-ha.sh` is the remaining check before merge.

author: gsdali
body:
## What & why

The 2D affine transform `scale * p + translate` was hand-rolled four times across
`DrawingComposition.swift`/`DrawingDispatch.swift`, with the canonical implementation never
actually called:

- `TransformedDrawing.apply(_:)` (`DrawingComposition.swift`) is documented as "the" implementation
  in the file's own header comment, but had **zero callers** anywhere in `Sources/OCCTSwift`
  (confirmed by grep before touching anything): even `DXFExporter.swift`/`PDFExporter.swift`/
  `SVGExporter.swift`'s `collectFromDrawing(_ transformed: TransformedDrawing)` overloads bypass it,
  destructuring `.translate`/`.scale` and forwarding into the free-function pipeline instead.
- `DrawingDimension.transformed(translate:scale:)`'s local `func t` re-derived the identical formula.
- `DrawingAnnotation.transformed(translate:scale:)`'s local `func t` re-derived it a third time.
- `collectProjectedEdges` (`DrawingDispatch.swift`, the edge-tessellation path every 2D exporter
  shares) re-derived it a fourth time.

**Ground-truthed against current `origin/main` before touching anything, per instructions.** All
four sites the issue cites matched exactly (same files, same shape, formula byte-identical at each,
`TransformedDrawing.apply(_:)` still uncalled) -- none of today's sibling Pass-4b PRs had already
touched this code. The issue's own "fifth, related site", `SheetLayout.swift:113`'s `place(_:at:)`,
computes the *inverse* of the formula inline and is explicitly flagged by the issue as "not a
literal copy, worth flagging to whoever unifies this" rather than one of the four to fix -- left
untouched here, both because the issue doesn't ask for it and because `SheetLayout.swift` is one of
the files several other in-flight Pass-4b fixes touch today.

**Fix**: `TransformedDrawing` gains an `internal static func apply(_:translate:scale:)` holding the
one formula. The instance method (`apply(_:)`, still `public`, same signature, same behavior) now
delegates to it, and all three local `t` closures (`DrawingDimension.transformed`,
`DrawingAnnotation.transformed`, `collectProjectedEdges`) now call
`TransformedDrawing.apply(p, translate:, scale:)` instead of re-deriving the arithmetic. After this
PR there is exactly one implementation of `scale * p + translate` in the module, and it is
genuinely exercised by every site that needs it (the "canonical, but dead" problem the issue
flagged is also fixed: `TransformedDrawing.apply(_:)`'s own body is now load-bearing).

No output values change anywhere: same formula, same order of operations, confirmed by the golden
byte-exact exporter tests (`ExporterDrawingCollectionGoldenTests`) and every existing
`.transformed(translate:scale:)` value-assertion test (`OrdinateDimensionTests.transformedCase`,
`BalloonTests.balloonTransformed`) passing unmodified.

Part of the Pass 4b duplication audit (#386).

Closes #1183

## CHANGELOG entry

### Four independent `scale * p + translate` transform sites unified, `TransformedDrawing.apply(_:)` is no longer dead code (#1183)

`DrawingDimension.transformed`, `DrawingAnnotation.transformed` (both `DrawingComposition.swift`)
and `collectProjectedEdges` (`DrawingDispatch.swift`) each independently re-derived the 2D affine
transform `scale * p + translate` in a local closure, while `TransformedDrawing.apply(_:)` --
documented as the canonical implementation -- had no callers at all. All four now share a new
`TransformedDrawing.apply(_:translate:scale:)` (internal static). No output values changed. Public
API unchanged (`TransformedDrawing.apply(_:)` keeps its existing signature and behavior).

## SemVer impact

NONE. Pure internal refactor. The only new symbol, `TransformedDrawing.apply(_:translate:scale:)`,
is `internal`. Every touched site's public behavior (transformed coordinates, byte-exact
DXF/SVG/PDF output) is unchanged, verified via existing golden-output tests plus new coverage
asserting exact coordinates at each of the four sites.

## Checklist

- [x] New or changed behavior is covered by a unit test in the same PR
- [x] Every new test and every new `--self-test` case was run once with its subject broken, and the failure is reported here
- [x] The CHANGELOG entry above is complete, and `docs/CHANGELOG.md` is **not** in this diff.
- [x] The SemVer impact above is stated, and `docs/SEMVER.md` is **not** in this diff.

## Notes for the reviewer

- New test suite: `Tests/OCCTDrawingTests/OCCTDrawingTests.swift`,
  `DrawingTransformUnificationTests` (5 tests), plus a small `RecordingSink: DrawingPrimitiveSink`
  test helper that records raw points so `collectProjectedEdges` can be checked directly (via the
  `internal collectDrawing(...)` entry point, reachable through `@testable import`) without parsing
  a writer's serialization format:
  - `applyDirect`: `TransformedDrawing.apply(_:)` computes an exact expected coordinate -- this
    site had **no existing test coverage at all** per the issue's own audit.
  - `linearDimensionTransform` / `radialDimensionTransform`: `DrawingDimension.transformed` for
    `.linear`/`.radial`, cases the issue found had no value-assertion coverage (only `.ordinate` did).
  - `centrelineAnnotationTransform`: `DrawingAnnotation.transformed` for `.centreline`, a case the
    issue found had no value-assertion coverage (only `.balloon` did).
  - `edgeCollectionTransform`: calls `collectDrawing(...)` on a real projected `Drawing` with a
    non-identity transform, and checks the recorded points' min/max exactly match
    `scale * drawing.bounds() + translate` computed independently in the test -- proving
    `collectProjectedEdges` applies the same transform as the other three sites, not merely *a*
    transform.
- **Prove-the-test-fails** (`okf/policies/prove-the-test-fails.md`): temporarily changed the new
  shared `TransformedDrawing.apply(_:translate:scale:)` from `scale * p + translate` to
  `scale * p - translate`, rebuilt, and reran `swift test --filter DrawingTransformUnificationTests`.
  All 5 new tests failed, 10 issues total, spanning all four transform sites (`apply`, `.linear`,
  `.radial`, `.centreline`, and the edge-collection path) -- this is itself evidence the
  consolidation happened: before this PR, breaking `TransformedDrawing.apply`'s formula would not
  have broken the other three sites' independent copies. Restored the correct formula, reran: all 5
  pass, 0 issues.
- Verified locally: `swift build`; `swift test --filter DrawingTransformUnificationTests` (new
  suite), `--filter DrawingCompositionTests` (existing `TransformedDrawing` coverage in
  `OCCTMathTests`), `--filter OrdinateDimensionTests`, `--filter BalloonTests`,
  `--filter ExporterDrawingCollectionGoldenTests` (byte-exact golden output),
  `--filter SheetStandardLayoutTests`, `--filter PDFWriterTests` (covers the untouched
  `SheetLayout.swift` consumer path) -- all green; full `swift test`, 5974 tests / 1517 suites, 0
  failures; all 8 gate scripts + their `--self-test`s, all 3 censuses' `--self-test`s, and
  `check-changelog-transcription.py --self-test`, all clean; `count-operations.py` unchanged at
  4366 across README/API_REFERENCE/index.md (no public API surface added); `swift-format lint
  --strict` and `swiftlint lint --strict` clean on both touched `Sources/` files and on the new test
  code (one pre-existing, unrelated `swift-format` violation at
  `OCCTDrawingTests.swift:1730` -- `let L` needing lowerCamelCase -- predates this PR, confirmed
  against `origin/main`, and is outside this PR's scope per the hotspot-file instruction).
- No `Sources/OCCTBridge/**` changes -- all four sites are pure Swift/`simd` 2D arithmetic with zero
  OCCT bridge crossings (confirmed by the issue's own investigation and re-confirmed here).

author: jakechampion
body:
The last open cell of the [#7259 matrix](https://github.com/JakeChampion/lang/issues/7259#issuecomment-5444032850): `mk()[i].k`, where `mk()` returns a fresh struct array — the shape #7659 deliberately left, with the mechanism recorded [here](https://github.com/JakeChampion/lang/issues/7259#issuecomment-5446248567). The index site's own reclaim cannot fire on the struct-element classes: releasing the container there frees the element box the downstream field read is about to enter.

## The fix

The release moves to the **field-access node**, which sees the whole shape: park the container in a scratch slot, index into it, read the field, *then* release with the exit sweep's class split (`__struct_drop_<T>` per element for a field-routing or rc-array-field element; `__fern_arrarr_free` for a scalar-field one). Gated to **scalar non-i64 field reads**: an rc-field result would alias a box the release frees, so `mkp()[0].s` keeps the arm off and the container's leak stays the recorded safe floor — pinned by an answer-stability row rather than a byte rate.

Measured (100 rounds, native + interp oracles agreeing on exits throughout):

| shape | before | after | native |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mk()[0].k`, `Inner { k, ys: i32[] }[]` | `500/0` live 20800 | **`500/500` 0** | `500/500` 0 |
| `mkp()[1].n`, `P { s: string, n }[]` | `700/0` live 20000 | **`700/700` 0** | `300/300` 0 |
| `mkp()[0].s.len()` — rc-field read (control) | answer stable, arm off | unchanged | 0 |

With this, every in-place consumer of a fresh producer in the #7259 matrix releases at every element kind — the matrix is closed column by column.

## Tests and gates (green locally)

- Three rows join `arrOwnedRetReleaseCases`; the two byte-rate rows fail on the parent commit at exactly **208** and **200 B/round**
- `TestSelfHostArrOwnedRetRelease{IRX86_64,IRArm64,WasmIR}`
- **`TestSelfHostStage2FixpointArm64`** (120 s) — the reclaim-change gate
- `TestSelfHostStructarrProducer`, `TestSelfHostArrReturnTransfer`, `TestSelfHostFeatureCensus`, `TestRepoComplexityRatchet`

Refs #7259.

author: amandaseibel-dev
body:
> "na real são todos alunos com a matrícula confirmada em 2026/2"

É o indicador certo — a operação existe para o aluno **voltar a estudar**, não para fechar acordo.

(A minha primeira ideia era medir "fechou acordo". Seria enganoso: **593 dos 694 acordos do mês vieram da importação do Prime**, não da mão do operador. Contar aquilo daria crédito ao arquivo.)

## O que já dá para ver — e por que ainda não vale

| Grupo | Alunos | Mensuráveis | Matricularam | Taxa |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Quitados na ficha | 708 | 202 | 188 | **93,1%** |
| Com baixa de parcela | 535 | 120 | 111 | **92,5%** |
| *Coorte geral 2026/1* | 5.423 | 4.515 | 3.551 | *78,6%* |

93% contra 78,6% é uma diferença grande e na direção esperada. Mas está apoiada em **28% do grupo**, e a amostra **não é aleatória**: a coleta só busca quem tem dívida em aberto, e quem foi quitado deixou de ter. Os mensuráveis são justamente os coletados **antes** de serem quitados.

Extrapolar daí seria inventar número — e ela levaria isso para a diretoria.

## Agora

Quem foi recuperado entra na fila **mesmo sem dívida**: **1.118 CPFs, dos quais 836 nunca foram consultados**. A coleta roda a cada 2 minutos com 60 por vez — fecha em algumas horas, uma vez só.

Prioridade deliberada: **cadastro repetido** e **sem telefone** continuam na frente. Trabalho parado vem antes de relatório.

author: that-guy-40
body:
Settles §14 item 3: `smoke-openbios.sh` stays the **single implementation**, and `tests/` carries one five-line `exec` wrapper per track — 22 of them — so the verdict, the SKIP and the exit code are all the driver's, and there is still one place to type a track by hand.

## The old runner header's objection was right, and had to be answered

It read *"all five are headless by construction"* and kept the tracks out because every one guards on a built artifact and SKIPs without it — so a suite that merely **included** them printed a green tick on a machine that cannot build. §14 had measured exactly that.

Including them is only safe once an all-SKIP sweep stops reading as a pass. So `run-all.sh` now:

- reports the two groups **separately** — `of which boot tracks: n/22`
- prints an explicit **UNKNOWN** when none executed, **PARTIAL** when some did not
- `OPENBIOS_REQUIRE_TRACKS=1` turns **any** skip into a failure

## Strict mode fails on ANY skip, and that was earned by measurement

Driven against an empty `OPENBIOS_WORKDIR`, the sweep came back **21 skipped, 1 passed** — because the `coreboot` track reads its ROM from the *linuxboot* lab (`COREBOOT_DIR`) and is independent of the tree under test. **A guard that only fires when every track skips is silenced by exactly that**: one unrelated pass hiding twenty-one unknowns.

### Which surfaces a finding, recorded rather than fixed here

`test-smoke-coreboot.sh` can **PASS while the firmware under test was never built** — it boots a ROM built earlier from a sibling lab's tree. Whether that ROM's embedded payload is re-derived or is a record outliving its subject is **not yet established**. Filed as an open question in TODO §14, not claimed as a bug or a non-bug.

## The coverage guard

`tests/test-every-track-has-a-wrapper.sh` holds driver and suite together in **both** directions — a track with no wrapper is a track nobody runs; a wrapper naming a dead track is drift — and also asserts each wrapper **`exec`s** the driver rather than reimplementing it, and that every one is **listed in `run-all.sh`** so the ratio is measured against the full 22. It borrows `arms_of()` out of `check-track-list.sh` rather than growing a second parser for the same dispatch.

**It caught a naming collision on its first run:** the wrappers were `test-track-<name>.sh`, which the existing headless `test-track-list.sh` matches — so "list" was read as a track. Hence the `test-smoke-` prefix. The runner's own disk-vs-list guard then caught the rename `sed` clipping `test-track-list.sh` out of the headless array.

Green: ratio checker (14 runners), `check-harness-net`, `check-track-list` (34 dispatch names), `link_check.py`, `paths.py --check`, shellcheck gate.

author: rubicon
body:
Closes #284

## What changed

`transportHint()` walks a transport error's cause chain for an untrusted-certificate
code (`DEPTH_ZERO_SELF_SIGNED_CERT`, `SELF_SIGNED_CERT_IN_CHAIN`,
`UNABLE_TO_VERIFY_LEAF_SIGNATURE`) and returns remediation naming
`NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`.

```
message: Connection failed: fetch failed (cause: DEPTH_ZERO_SELF_SIGNED_CERT)
hint:    The site's TLS certificate is not signed by anything this process trusts —
         normal for a local development site. Point NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS at the site's
         certificate in this MCP server's env and restart it … curl trusts it via the
         system keychain, which is why curl succeeds where this fails.
```

That last clause is deliberate. The `curl`-succeeds-Node-fails asymmetry is what made
three separate sessions rule TLS out; naming it in the hint is the difference between
an errno and a diagnosis.

## Two boundaries the tests pin

**It never suggests `NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED`.** That disables verification for
every host the process later contacts, including production ones. A convenience hint
that teaches the insecure fix is worse than no hint, so a test asserts the string never
appears for any of the three codes.

**It stays silent on causes it did not observe.** `ECONNREFUSED` gets the errno and no
hint. Guessing at an unobserved cause is exactly how the original investigation went
wrong, and a confidently wrong hint would industrialise that mistake.

## Scope beyond the issue, and why

Two things #284 did not ask for, both from the same reasoning — fix it where all callers
route through, not only on the path the ticket names:

1. **The hint and the cause chain are applied in `parseThrownError`**, the single funnel
   every tool's transport error passes through — not only at the connection check. This
   closes a gap #281 left: `describeError` reached `testConnection` and the boot
   handshake, so an ordinary page/preset/module tool still reported a bare `fetch failed`
   with no cause at all. There is a regression test for that path specifically.
2. **The boot handshake warning carries the hint.** That log line is where this actually
   hid — the desktop host emitted it 43 times across ten days while the server kept
   running with the gate disabled, and no envelope was ever consulted. A hint reaching
   only `meta_ping` would leave the exact scenario that motivated #284 silent.

`describeError` moves from `wp-client.ts` to `envelope.ts` so both can use it without an
import cycle — `wp-client` already imports `envelope`, not the reverse.

## Tests

Written first, each failure observed (6 red before implementing). New file
`transport-tls-hint.test.ts`: hint present for all three codes, absent for
`ECONNREFUSED`, never names the insecure variable, cause chain reaches non-meta tools,
and `testConnection` threads the hint. The handshake guard gains a case for the warning.

Full suites green: **651 server tests, 2009 PHP assertions across 51 files.**

author: estebanzimanyi
body:
The runner image ships Microsoft's azure-cli and prod repositories. Every
package this project installs comes from the Ubuntu archives, so those two
answer for nothing here, and from the Azure runners they answer 403
Forbidden: apt-get update then exits 100 and fails a step that asked only
for Ubuntu packages.

The retry count and transfer timeout the action already sets cannot reach
that failure, because a 403 is an immediate and unchanging answer and every
retry repeats it. The action removes the sources instead, which removes the
dependency rather than the symptom: apt reports on exactly the repositories
the build reads, and a genuine Ubuntu archive failure still fails the step.
The sources are matched by the host they name, so both the .list and the
deb822 .sources form are covered.

The doc reference check is the one workflow running apt-get update without
the action, so it gains the action and the trigger path that reruns it when
the action changes, as its nine siblings already carry.
