author: monodera
body:
Closes #479.

`validate_input()` seeds each check with `{"status": None}` and returns early at the first failure, so everything below that failure keeps the `None` — and has none of the other fields `show_results()` reads. Four sections went straight for those fields without testing `status` first:

| Section | Reads without checking `status` |
|---|---|
| `flux_columns` | `["filters"]`, `["success"]` |
| `flux_values` | `["frac_suspicious_flux_all"]`, `["min_flux"]`, `["max_flux"]` |
| `visibility` | `["success"]` |
| `unique` | `["flags"]` |

The issue named the first, third and fourth. `flux_values` is a fourth instance of the same shape — it reaches the unguarded access through a compound condition (`flux_columns and flux_values`) rather than a bare one, which is why it reads as safe at a glance.

## Nothing is broken today

Each of those sections sits above all four of `validate_input()`'s early returns, so by the time `show_results()` reaches one, the check has always actually run. The fixture-driven test added here passes both before and after the fix, which is the evidence.

What makes it worth defending anyway is the failure mode. `cb_validate()` in `pn_app.py` calls `show_results()` with no `try`/`except`, so a `KeyError` escapes the callback, `panel_timer.timer(on=False)` never runs, and the user is left on a spinner that never stops — a silent hang, not an error anyone can report usefully.

And the trigger is one line of unrelated work: a fifth early return, or a new check inserted in the wrong place.

## The change

Adds the `is None: pass` guard that the `str`, `values` and `internal_duplication` sections already use, plus a docstring on `show_results()` recording the invariant so the next check added follows it.

`flux_range` is converted to the same shape in a follow-up commit. It was already None-safe, through a compound `... is not None` condition, so that fixes no bug — but the point of the change is a single convention to copy, and an outlier in the middle of it is what the next contributor reads instead. Its `"flux_range" in validation_status` sub-clause went with it: `checker.py` seeds the key at line 1376 and assigns it again on both sides of the `min_mag`/`max_mag` branch, so it is never absent.

Three sections stay outside the convention, and the docstring now says why rather than glossing it: `required_keys` and `optional_keys` run before any early return and so are never `None`, and `empty` tests `is False` positively. (An earlier commit message in this branch claims "all nine now read the same way" — that was wrong on both the count and the uniformity; this is the accurate version.)

The `return`s stay as they are. They do a different job — stopping the render at a failure instead of reporting checks below it — and folding them into the same idiom would change what gets rendered. Out of scope per the issue, and unnecessary now that the sections defend themselves.

Worth noting for whoever touches this next: those returns use `not status`, which is `True` for `None` as well as `False`. That is not incidental — it is how an input rejected at the `empty` check stops before the `str` section. The docstring says so now.

**No behaviour change.** The new branches are unreachable for any input `validate_input()` can currently produce.

## Tests

`tests/test_show_results.py` fixes the contract rather than today's accident:

- **`test_renders_when_a_check_never_ran`** walks an early return through *every* position it could occupy in `validate_input()` — not just the four that exist — and renders the result. The guards then hold whether or not that control flow moves later.
- **`test_renders_every_fixture_outcome`** renders each real outcome from the `tests/data/` fixtures added in #494, reaching those states through `validate_input()` itself rather than by hand, so a status dict the first test assembles wrongly cannot hide a break.

Verified the `flux_columns`, `flux_values`, `flux_range`, `visibility` and `unique` cases fail without the fix:

```
FAILED tests/test_show_results.py::test_renders_when_a_check_never_ran[flux_columns]
FAILED tests/test_show_results.py::test_renders_when_a_check_never_ran[flux_values]
FAILED tests/test_show_results.py::test_renders_when_a_check_never_ran[flux_range]
FAILED tests/test_show_results.py::test_renders_when_a_check_never_ran[visibility]
FAILED tests/test_show_results.py::test_renders_when_a_check_never_ran[unique]
5 failed, 17 passed
```

`uv run pytest tests/` — 95 passed in ~39 s.

## Shared test setup

Both fixture-driven modules were validating the same 13 files with the same arguments — 13 duplicate runs of a check whose visibility pass dominates the suite, and two hand-kept copies of the check-name list that had already drifted apart (ten entries in one, nine in the other; the difference was deliberate, but nothing said so).

`tests/conftest.py` now owns the pinned dates, the canonical check list and the per-fixture arguments, and validates each file once per session, handing out deep copies so a test that edits a status dict cannot reach another. `test_show_results.py` derives its subset from the canonical list rather than retyping it. Suite runtime 57 s → 39 s.

author: arshadansari27
body:
Implements PR1 of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-28-coding-session-inventory-design.md`.

AEGIS launched coding runs blind: nothing checked whether someone was already working in the same repo on the coding host. This reads the session registry Claude Code already publishes and defers when a human is busy there.

## What it does

- Runs `claude agents --json` per configured account over the existing SSH identity — no new credential, and it is the documented TTY-free listing.
- Normalises both worktree conventions (`<repo>-aegis-wt/<id>` and `<repo>/.claude/worktrees/<name>`) so a worktree compares equal to its repo.
- Tags AEGIS's own runs `owner=aegis` so runs never block each other. Its headless runs register in the same registry, so this is load-bearing, not cosmetic.
- `launch_agent_run` and `run_task_investigation` return `skipped` instead of launching. Only busy, human-owned sessions in the same repo count.
- New read-only `list_coding_sessions` chat tool.

## Safety

- **Defaults OFF** (`coding.inventory.enabled`), so a fork sees no behaviour change and not one extra SSH round trip.
- **Fails open everywhere.** Unconfigured, disabled, unreachable, or unparseable all yield "no collision known" and the run proceeds — today's behaviour, so the worst case is no worse than the status quo.
- **Output fields are an explicit allow-list.** `messagingSocketPath`, `pid` and the sibling `.key` files are never read or surfaced: they are an undocumented private interface and auth material. A test asserts they cannot appear.
- **Nothing user-specific is hardcoded.** Every value comes from the `infra.coding` block; `validate_coding` rejects an account label that is not a `config_dirs` key, since that would enumerate nothing and silently disable the check.
- **A skip never parks the task.** Parking stamps `@waiting` and removes it from the eligible pool, so a transient collision would otherwise retire the task permanently. Covered by a flow test.

## Known trade-off

A skipped Todoist task is retried after the sweep's `cooldown_hours` (six by default) rather than on the next fifteen-minute tick, because its child workflow completes. The sweep cannot filter earlier: it does not know a task's repo until `resolve_task_repo` runs inside the flow. `cooldown_hours` is already configurable.

## Note for reviewers

`admin-panel/frontend/src/pages/Infra.tsx` had to change. `validate_coding` replaces the whole `coding` object, so a field the form does not carry is erased by any unrelated save on that page — the new block would have been wiped on the next edit.

## Verification

- core 1696, worker 1876, comms 207 — all pass; `ruff check` clean per package.
- Every new test was checked by breaking the implementation and confirming it fails. That found a real defect in my own tests: the SSH-failure cases originally passed for the wrong reason (a failed `_exec` yields empty stdout, so the *parse* branch reported the error). They now assert the specific stderr.
- Frontend `npm run build` typechecks clean.

Follow-ups: #345 (PROJECT_REPO_MAP hardcoding, found here and deliberately excluded). PR2 is #288 (per-agent short-TTL mount tokens), which is a prerequisite for the operator-mount work in PR3.

The java file scan is memoized across instances, so a later batch would otherwise inherit an earlier one's tree. It is also called between the two permutations of one test method, which `tearDown` does not run between. author: hf7y
body:
NO-DECISION: a reproducible counting bug in markdown-cost.sh, found while chasing a false CI failure on hf7y/scheduler#319, fixed and witnessed here for this repo's own self-dev to validate and merge.

`census()` (the live tree, via `git ls-files -z` -> `census_stream`, which does `[ -f "$f" ]` before counting) reaches through a tracked symlink to its target's content. `census_ref()` (any other ref, via `git archive | tar -x` into a scratch dir, then `find . -type f`) does not: `find`'s `-type f` reports a symlink's own type as `l`, never `f`, so the path never reaches `count_prose`.

Any repo with a tracked symlink to a prose-heavy file has that file's lines counted on the live side and silently dropped on the ref side. Every `--census` comparison against a merge base then bills the branch for the target's full line count, as if the branch had just added it -- whether or not the branch touched that file at all.

## How it was found and confirmed

`hf7y/scheduler`'s `prose` CI check flagged a trivial 5-line comment fix (hf7y/scheduler#319) as "+87 prose lines." Checking out the PR's own merge-base commit as its own branch (so HEAD == origin/main, zero real diff) still reported "+82" against itself -- proof the discrepancy was in the guard, not the diff. Extracting `git archive` for that commit into a scratch dir and diffing a per-file census (`git ls-files` vs `find -type f` over the extraction) against the live tree found exactly one missing path: `schedule/scheduler.conf -> ../.scheduler/schedule.conf`, a tracked symlink carrying 82 prose lines that `find -type f` skips over. 82 (the symlink tax) + 5 (the PR's real, deliberate net change) = 87, the exact number CI reported.

Since scheduler's `.prose-ratchet` is a stale unit (unit 1) and MEASURE_UNIT 2 (2026-08-26) made a stale-unit census always fall back to a live merge-base recompute via `census_ref()`, this means **every PR to hf7y/scheduler has been paying an 82-line phantom tax on the prose check since 2026-08-26**, regardless of what it actually changes.

## Fix

`find . -type f` -> `find -L . -type f` in `census_ref()`, so a tracked symlink is resolved before the type test the same way `[ -f ]` already resolves it on the live side.

## Test

New case G7 in `bin/tests/markdown-cost.test.sh`: a repo where HEAD is its own merge base (self-comparison, zero real diff) containing one tracked symlink to a 30-comment-line file. Asserts the census reports "adds nothing over the merge base" and raises no FLAG.

Verified by reverting only the script (keeping the new test) and confirming it fails first: exit 1, `FLAG [prose-ratchet]`, `adds 30 prose line(s)`. With the fix restored: `bin/markdown-cost.sh` census test suite is 81 passed / 0 failed (was 78; +3 for G7). Sibling suites `exit-codes.test.sh`, `mechanism-budget.test.sh`, `state-prose-lint.test.sh` are unaffected and still green.

Left as draft per this account's standing rule: cross-repo fixes land as a draft PR for that repo's own self-dev to validate, ready and merge -- not merged here. A companion issue is filed on this repo asking for that.

## Test plan
- [x] `bash bin/tests/markdown-cost.test.sh` -- 81 passed, 0 failed
- [x] `bash bin/tests/exit-codes.test.sh` -- 24 passed, 0 failed
- [x] `bash bin/tests/mechanism-budget.test.sh` -- 19 passed, 0 failed
- [x] `bash bin/tests/state-prose-lint.test.sh` -- 23 passed, 0 failed

<!-- DEFERRED -->
- none
<!-- /DEFERRED -->

<!-- DELIVERS -->

author: dergut
body:
## Which issue does this PR close?

While working on the `OAuth2Manager::contextual_session` implementation, following https://github.com/apache/iceberg-rust/pull/3081, I noticed that some auth manager state that gets set during `AuthManager::catalog_session` (at catalog initialization) could get overwritten by later repeated calls to the same function.
Because later sessions are derived from that state (e.g. contextual sessions depend on the shared catalog session), calling `AuthManager::catalog_session` again, would reset that state (and should likely reset any cached contextual sessions). Well-behaved catalog implementations would not call that method multiple times, but an auth manager shared between multiple catalogs would result in the same behavior.

The expected contract is that auth manager is only used per catalog. This PR tries to make the API a little bit harder to misuse.

## What changes are included in this PR?

This PR makes REST catalog builders take ownership of custom `AuthManager` implementations instead of accepting a shared `Arc`. This emphasizes that each manager is scoped to one catalog and prevents accidental reuse across catalogs from resetting authentication state that later sessions may rely on.

The manager remains shared internally across the catalog's authentication sessions and requests. The public API snapshot and `AuthManager` documentation are updated accordingly.

## Are these changes tested?

No new tests are included because this only touches the ownership API. My coming PR to implement the `OAuth2Manager::contextual_session` shows how it changes a `Mutex<ContextualAuthState>` to a `OnceCell<ContextualAuthState>` by forcing the contract of a single `catalog_session` call per manager, repeated calls may error in that case.

## AI Disclosure

AI was used during implementation and documentation.

author: jdolan
body:
Step 4 of the race module (#963): two more triggers and the first two barriers.

**Splits and stages.** `trigger_race_split` (`split` 1..N, `label`) times the run
without judging it: one reached out of order is simply not a split of this run.
`trigger_race_stage` (`stage` 2..N, `restart_target`, `label`) is timed the same
way, and is also where a practicing client returns to: reaching one stores its
`info_notnull` anchor as `store` would, so `kill` goes back to the stage rather
than the spawn. Both sequences validate on their own terms and spoil only
themselves; the course stays valid. Anchors are resolved in `ConfigureLevel`,
once every entity has spawned.

**Gates.** `func_race_checkpoint_gate` (`cp`, `mode` atleast|exact, `invert`) is
a brush that is solid to a racer until the run's checkpoints satisfy it, and
solid to everything else always. It binds only an *active* run, so a practicing
client with no run under way passes freely rather than being locked out of the
later sections.

**One-way walls.** `func_race_oneway_wall` (`angle`) passes a racer one way and
not the other, and needs no per-client latch: `G_Race_ClipEntity` stays pure by
asking `gi.Clip` whether the mover is already inside this one brush. That nested
call comes back through the hook with no mover, where a wall is a wall, so the
recursion ends there.

**Not carried from the fork:** the 1024-unit gate clearance rule, the 64-barrier
cap and the model-index uniqueness check all existed only for its client-side
latch bitmask; the FNV split-layout hash belongs with records (step 5).

Verified: autotools and Xcode build the race module, `verify_projects.py` agrees
across all three systems (no new files), and a headless
`quetoo-dedicated +game race +map racetest` on a test map extended with a gate,
split, stage + anchor and one-way wall spawns all seven classes with no
warnings (10 baseline entities, up from 6). Prediction of barriers on the client
is step 7; until then a client walking into a closed gate will be corrected by
the server.

Refs #963.

author: jeroensoeters
body:
Two commits: the fix, and the test weakness that let it exist.

## 1. `fix(provx/gcp)`: trust the issuer the caller names

`provx/gcp` resolved its issuer from the `provx.Endpoint` constant, so every workload identity provider it created trusted `https://oidc.cloud.formae.ai` regardless of the issuer the caller had been given. `gcp.New` now takes the issuer and validates it with `provx.ParseIssuer` — the same canonical-origin rule the AWS provisioner has always held it to.

**Why it matters.** The caller was already carrying an issuer and had nowhere to put it. formae's `internal/cli/connect/gcpprovision.go` takes an `issuer` argument, `openSession` validates it against what the control plane reports, and then the call to `gcp.New` drops it.

Production hides this because both values are the same string there. Anywhere else — a staging installation, an acceptance test with its own issuer — provisioning reports success and establishes trust that can never accept a token, and the failure surfaces later as an opaque exchange rejection rather than as the wrong issuer it is.

This is the AWS path's existing contract: `provxaws.New` takes the issuer, and the issuer travels verbatim from the control plane into the artifacts. This makes GCP match.

**Testing.** The gap that let this stand was that no test asserted the created provider's `issuerUri`. The fake-backed tests now trust a deliberately non-production issuer, so a value compiled in rather than passed through fails them:

- `TestProviderTrustsTheIssuerItWasGiven` — the created provider carries the caller's issuer.
- `TestRefusesAnIssuerThatIsNotACanonicalOrigin` — empty, http, trailing slash and ported issuers are refused at construction, not at provisioning.

## 2. `test(provx/aws)`: stop testing the issuer against the value it would be hardcoded to

The same weakness, on the side that happens to be correct.

`provx/aws` does take its issuer as a parameter and does thread it into the provider URL and the trust policy, and the tests pin both — the `Url` check in `connect_provider_test.go` and the whole trust-policy document in `role_test.go`, condition keys included. But `testIssuer` was the production issuer, so all of it would pass equally against an issuer resolved from `provx.Endpoint`. Those assertions pinned the issuer's shape and never its provenance, which is precisely how the GCP bug above went unnoticed.

`testIssuer` now points at a non-production origin. No production code changes and the suite still passes — which is the useful outcome: it confirms the parameter really is what reaches the artifacts, instead of leaving that true by luck and unproven.

## Scope

`go test ./...` passes across `provx`, `provx/aws` and `provx/gcp`. `cmd/oox` builds; its two GCP call sites now pass `provx.Endpoint` explicitly, so its behaviour is unchanged.

## Follow-up

formae must re-pin `oox/provx` and pass its issuer through `newGCPProvisioner` for the fix to reach `formae connect gcp`. That unblocks the GCP half of platform-engineering-labs/formae#696, whose test currently skips for exactly this reason.

author: alexander-turner
body:
### Motivation
- A single missed line can fail a PR under the repository's per-file coverage checks, which is too brittle for day-to-day work.  The goal is a small, bounded tolerance so runs do not fail for a single missed unit. 
- When a PR does reduce measurable per-file coverage, establish a daily, visible repair path that files a single marker-owned issue for maintainers to address.

### Description
- Relax per-file coverage gates to accept either a 99% percentage floor or at most eight uncovered units, preserving any stricter recorded baseline entries; this adds `FLOOR = 99` and `UNCOVERED_TOLERANCE = 8` and updates the ratchet logic for Python, kcov (Bash), and JS (`py-coverage-ratchet.py`, `kcov` gate, `c8-changed-ratchet.mjs`).
- Scope/rise semantics are preserved: ledgered baseline entries still control a file's floor and rises in recorded numbers remain reported (and block in changed-file scope) rather than silently weakening the ledger.
- Add staggered daily schedules for the three coverage workflows so the whole-tree check runs on main regularly (`.github/workflows/{kcov-checks,pytest-checks,js}.yaml`).
- Add a tiny trusted handler that runs on the default branch to create/update one marker-owned repair issue when a scheduled coverage run fails (`.github/scripts/coverage-failure-issue.py` + `.github/workflows/coverage-failure-issue.yaml`) so failures with no PR surface are visible and actionable.
- Update tests and harnesses to cover the two acceptance criteria (percent floor and uncovered-unit tolerance) and adjust docs/comments and workflow job names to reflect the per-file floor wording.

### Testing
- Ran the modified Python unit tests for the ratchet and issue helper: `uv run pytest tests/test_py_coverage_ratchet.py tests/test_coverage_failure_issue.py` and the targeted suites passed locally (tests for the ratchet logic passed).
- Ran the JS c8 ratchet test suite: `node --test .github/scripts/c8-changed-ratchet.test.mjs` and the c8 shortfalls/branch-detail tests passed.
- Ran the kcov-related unit tests and gate harness (`tests/test_kcov_harness.py`, `tests/kcov_gate.py`) exercised the new tolerance logic and the added unit tests for 8 vs 9 uncovered lines; the targeted assertions passed after fixes. 
- Ran lint/checks (`ruff` / `pre-commit` invocation via the session tooling) and fixed issues the linters raised; the checks completed in the session environment.
- Notes: one earlier run failed in this execution environment for an unrelated missing system package (`coverage`) used by a fake-GitHub transport; that is an environment dependency and not a logic regression in these changes.

author: molinajonyy-hub
body:
## DIALOG-TOUCH-1 — acciones de diálogo responsive con área táctil >= 44px

Baseline: `39f87a8c4d028db1f4085c58f2acbc3c1c059542` (origin/main).

### Causa raíz

Las acciones del footer de `ResponsiveDialog` medían **39px** (37,8px en 320px).

`.btn` en talla `md` **no declara `min-height`** y hereda el `line-height: 1.5`
de bootstrap (el CDN que carga `index.html`; el `.btn` de la app nunca fija
line-height):

```
21px (line-height) + 8+8 (padding) + 1+1 (borde) = 39px
```

`UI-CONSISTENCY-4` había cerrado `.icon-btn` y `.btn-lg`/`.btn-xl`, pero el CTA
del footer usa talla `md`, que quedó sin contrato. Resultado: dentro del **mismo
diálogo** convivían un cierre de 44px en el header y un CTA de 39px.

Extra medido: en 320px el botón se **comprime a ~37,8px** cuando el header ocupa
dos líneas y el footer cede alto — peor que lo reportado.

### Capa elegida

El arreglo vive en **el footer**, no en `AppButton`:

`footer` es un `ReactNode` arbitrario — cada consumidor arma sus propios botones —
así que el contrato no puede viajar en una prop ni en un size variant. El footer
es el único punto compartido por todos los consumidores.

```css
@media (max-width: 1023px) {
  .modal-content-responsive .modal-footer button,
  .modal-content-responsive .modal-footer .btn {
    min-height: var(--mobile-touch-target);
  }
}
```

- Reusa el token existente `--mobile-touch-target` (44px).
- Mismo breakpoint que `.icon-btn` y `.seg-field-option` (UI-CONSISTENCY-4).
- Sin `!important`, sin override feature-local, sin `minHeight` inline, sin
  quinto patrón de diálogo, sin tocar `.btn` global.
- Desktop (>=1024px) conserva la densidad compacta **a propósito**.

### Consumidores alcanzados

| Consumidor | Presentación | Estado |
|---|---|---|
| `NewOrder.tsx` · QuickCustomerDialog | fullscreen | corregido |
| `BarcodeScannerDialog.tsx` | fullscreen | corregido |
| `AppConfirmDialog.tsx` (`useConfirm`) | centered | corregido — sin consumidores vivos hoy |

Las tres presentaciones (`centered` / `sheet` / `fullscreen`) verificadas.

### Medición (geometría computada real)

| Viewport | Antes | Después |
|---|---|---|
| 320 | 37,83px | **44,01px** |
| 390 | 39px | **44px** |
| 430 | 39px | **44px** |
| 768 | 39px | **44px** |
| 1440 | 39px | 39px (densidad desktop preservada) |

Estados cubiertos: normal, deshabilitado, loading y `fullWidth`. Light y dark
verificados en los 5 anchos: los colores computados no cambian (el diff sólo
toca `min-height`).

### Gate

`tests/e2e/m7/dialog-touch-actions.spec.ts` — mide **geometría computada real**
(`boundingBox` + `elementFromPoint`), no la existencia de una variable CSS:

- 320 / 390 / 430, CTA primario y secundario;
- deshabilitado, habilitado y loading (con el alta demorada por `page.route`);
- hit-test en el borde superior, el centro y el borde inferior (que no lo tape nada);
- sin overflow horizontal;
- segundo consumidor real (BarcodeScannerDialog).

**Verificado que falla con el CSS anterior**: 4/4 en rojo, `Received: 39`.
Corre en CI (el job E2E usa `--project=m7-local` completo).

### Gates

| Gate | Resultado |
|---|---|
| `tsc --noEmit` | 0 errores |
| `lint:errors` | 0 |
| `build` | OK |
| `test:components` | 47 archivos / 653 tests |
| `test:unit` | 1038 pass / 0 fail |
| `test:mobile2a` | 4 / 11 + guards |
| `test:customer-core` | 3 / 48 + guard |
| `guards` | OK |
| `git diff --check` | limpio |
| E2E `@dialogtouch` + `@mobile2a` | 7/7 |
| E2E `customer-core-parity` | 12/12 |
| E2E `m7-local` completo | 117 passed / 2 failed |

Los 2 fallos son `finance-caja-visual` (`@visual-caja P1-A`), **preexistentes y
dependientes del día del mes** (el fixture siembra d0-1..d0-16). Verificado:
con el CSS de baseline fallan igual (4/9). No los introduce este lote.

### Fuera de alcance (declarado)

`Comprobantes.tsx` tiene 3 modales hechos a mano con `.modal-content` +
`.modal-footer` que **no** pasan por `ResponsiveDialog`, con el mismo 39px.
No se tocan: es otro patrón (legacy) y cae en superficie POS/comprobantes,
excluida por la lista de no-regresión de este lote.

### No tocado

Customer Core, POS, finanzas, Caja, CC, ARCA, Vault, DB, RLS, lógica de
MOBILE-2A, First Steps. Sin migraciones. Sin dependencias nuevas.
Ningún `data-testid` removido ni renombrado.

**NO MERGEAR AUTOMÁTICAMENTE.**

## Type of Change

- [ ] **Feature skill** - adds a channel or integration (source code changes + SKILL.md)
- [ ] **Utility skill** - adds a standalone tool (code files in `.claude/skills/<name>/`, no source changes)

- [ ] **Documentation** - docs, README, or CONTRIBUTING changes only

## Description

Middle layer of the provider-contract stack: the host seam.

Routes the host's provider spawn and group-init surfaces through a declared contract — project document, state volumes, skill backings and views, prepared files, and ordered group-init/spawn operations, all realized by core in the declared order. File reconciliation carries its transformer function directly on the contract, and every declared surface is cross-checked at registration: a required legacy adapter that is not registered, an operation referencing an undeclared surface, or an allowlisted mount without an explicit spawn position is rejected.

author: mmkal
body:
The day's voicelab overhaul, proven live on prd by two passing evals (`evals/voicelab-roundtrip`, `evals/voicelab-first-cause`). Net effect for a voice stream's user: the assistant keeps its memory across the reconnects the 60s idle deadline manufactures, its backend's replies actually reach the call (solicited or not), it knows and honestly relays what stage the backend work is at, and every conversation leaves a readable record.

- **Colleague per stream** (12.0.0): `note_to_self`'s agent lives at `/agents/voice-notes/<stream>` — one desk per stream, memory across calls — instead of an amnesiac per conversationId.
- **Durable transcripts + reconnect recap** (13.0.0): `utterance-transcript`/`answer-transcript` events per finished turn; the fold's bounded recap briefs every fresh provider session. `pnpm cli voicelab transcript` prints the record.
- **Status forwarding** (14–15.0.0): a copy-to-stream subscription transforms the colleague's `summary-updated` + model/script lifecycle into `colleague-status` events ("writing code", "running code", failed scripts WITH their error); whispered to the live session as quiet context, folded into the reconnect brief. Frontend briefed for open transparency about its backend — relay statuses, admit failures, never invent.
- **The reply lane is the subscription, not ask()** (16.0.0): every backend chat message forwards as a durable `colleague-note` — no 180s deadline, no order-matched correlation, no unsolicited-message loss (all three observed live); late notes brief the next session.
- **Ops/diagnostics**: `buildCacheKey` (ITERATE_WORKER_VERSION) surfaced via `health()` + the facet runtime bag, added while hunting a real prod window where stateful facet builds served a 3-commit-old bundle while the stateless entrypoint was fresh; report.json now written in attended mode too; `talk --auto`.

## Risk map

- Riskiest: the `#noteToColleague` mint block (subscription install revision-keying — an unchanged key keeps an old subscription forever) and the fold arms for the three new event lanes; both unit-tested (`voice-agent.test.ts`, 84 tests) and exercised by the prd evals.
- On merge: contract 16.0.0 re-reduces existing voice streams' folds; per-conversation colleagues are abandoned in place; boards need no changes (their event surface is untouched).
- Review order: `configs/voice-agent/voice-agent.ts` (contract comments narrate each version), `apps/os/scripts/voicelab/voice-agent.test.ts`, `talk.ts`/`transcript.ts`, evals, README, the one-line C fix in `apps/kit/.../main.c`.

author: asinglesprinkle
body:
Closes WAR-42: Gate Esc and q behind a centred quit confirmation in the TUI

## Problem

In `crates/warlock-tui`, Esc and `q` leave warlock immediately (`input::action_for` maps both to `Action::Quit`, and `main::run` returns on it). The dangerous case is the reflex second Esc: the first Esc cancels a pact, the run is still tidying up, and the next press — a press meant for the run — drops the reader back into a shell they did not mean to be in. Nothing stands between a twitch and the end of the session. A small confirmation over the view removes that whole class of accident without changing anything about how warlock is driven.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With no pact or refresh in flight, a press of Esc or `q` opens a confirmation instead of leaving: a small window drawn over everything else, centred on the terminal, with the area behind it cleared so no tree row, panel line or footer text shows through.
- [ ] The confirmation asks whether to leave and offers exactly two answers, Yes and No, with No highlighted when it opens.
- [ ] Left and Right move the highlight between the two answers; Enter takes the highlighted one; `y` answers Yes outright and `n` answers No outright, whichever is highlighted; Esc answers No.
- [ ] Every other key does nothing at all: the confirmation stays open and the highlight does not move. Asserted over a list that includes the tree's own bindings (`j`, `k`, `g`, `G`, space, `o`, `f`, `p`, `m`, Tab, PgUp/PgDn) so no keystroke leaks through to the app underneath.
- [ ] Answering Yes leaves warlock by the path a quit already takes, so the terminal is restored through the existing guard.
- [ ] Answering No closes the confirmation and leaves the app exactly as it was: an `App` compared before opening and after closing is equal — same selection, scroll offset, panel offset, focus, filters, collapsed set, message and counts.
- [ ] Ctrl-C still leaves immediately, both with the confirmation closed and with it open, and still takes a running `claude` with it as it does today.
- [ ] While a pact or refresh is in flight the confirmation never appears: Esc still cancels the run and `q` still leaves immediately. Pinned by tests at both settings of the in-flight flag `action_for` already takes.
- [ ] Mouse events arriving while the confirmation is open change nothing: selection, scroll offsets and focus are unmoved, and no row is selected or collapsed behind the dialog.
- [ ] The confirmation's contents and its behaviour are asserted against an in-memory buffer and plain values, with no tty attached, in the style of the existing `ui.rs` and `input.rs` tests.
- [ ] On a terminal too small to hold the window whole, drawing is clamped to the screen and does not panic; the confirmation is never a mode that is active with nothing on screen.
- [ ] The footer keeps its three lines and its existing wording — `q/Esc/Ctrl-C: quit` and `PACTING_KEYS` are unchanged — and no fourth footer line is added.
- [ ] `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --workspace` are clean.

## Context / pointers

Files: `crates/warlock-tui/src/input.rs` (`action_for(key, in_flight)` — the `KeyCode::Char('q') | KeyCode::Esc => Some(Action::Quit)` arm and the `Esc if in_flight => CancelPact` arm above it, plus `mouse_action`), `crates/warlock-tui/src/main.rs` (the event loop: `Some(Action::Quit) => return Ok(())`, `Action::CancelPact`, and the `Event::Mouse` arm), `crates/warlock-tui/src/ui.rs` (`draw(frame, &app, now)` at line 365, `areas`, `FOOTER_HEIGHT`, `KEYS`/`QUIT_KEY`/`PACTING_KEYS`, and `mark_area`, whose draw-it-whole-or-not rule is the nearest precedent for centring something over a pane), `crates/warlock-tui/src/app.rs` (`App`, `Focus`, `is_pacting`), `crates/warlock-tui/src/colour.rs` (`FOCUS_COLOUR`), `crates/warlock-tui/src/lib.rs` (re-exports). Design: `docs/red-brief-08-back-to-green.md` section 5, "A gate on the way out" (`depends_on: []`), and design doc section 3 on nothing new being fatal. Whether the mode lives as a field on `App` or as a small type of its own is the executor's call, but it must live in the `warlock_tui` library rather than in the binary's loop, so both the drawing and the key handling are testable with no terminal. Ctrl-C is a key event and not a signal in raw mode: it must not be routed through the confirmation. Sibling tickets of the same brief: WAR-39 (refresh), WAR-40 (`.warlockignore`), WAR-41 (WARLOCK.md rows) — none of them is a prerequisite here; the in-flight flag `action_for` already takes is what covers "never during a run", whether the run is a pact or a later refresh.

## Out of scope

Do not touch `crates/warlock-engine` at all. No refresh key `r` and no changes to the keys line's contents or width (WAR-39 owns that), no `.warlockignore` (WAR-40), no WARLOCK.md row insertion (WAR-41), no `warlock init` or `AGENTS.md`. No confirmation on anything other than quitting: the pact key stays unconfirmed and remains its own undo. No change to what Ctrl-C does, to cancel semantics, or to what happens to a worker thread on the way out. No clickable Yes/No: the pointer gets no new bindings, and mouse events during the dialog are read and dropped. No new dependency of any kind, no fourth colour, no new tree state, no fourth footer line, and no general dialog or widget framework — one confirmation, one mode.

## Sub-tasks completed

### WAR-42.01 Add the quit-confirmation mode as a pure type in the warlock_tui library, with its key handling and tests
Added crates/warlock-tui/src/confirm.rs: QuitConfirm (Closed | Open(Answer), Default = Closed, opens with No lit), Answer { Yes, No }, Answered { Open(Answer), Close, Leave } and the pure key handler answer_for(key, highlighted) — no terminal, no App, no new dependency. Left lights Yes / Right lights No positionally (Yes drawn left, No right — recorded in the module doc for the drawing sibling), Enter takes the lit answer, y/Y leaves, n/N and Esc close, every other key leaves the mode unchanged, and only KeyEventKind::Press counts. The mode is a value of its own rather than a field on App, so App is untouched and the sibling's before/after equality holds trivially; the module doc also records that Ctrl-C is deliberately not answered here and must be taken by the event loop first. All five items re-exported from lib.rs with house-style doc lines plus a crate-doc paragraph; 11 new unit tests. fmt/clippy/test --workspace clean.

### WAR-42.02 Draw the confirmation centred over the frame, cleared behind, in ui.rs
draw() in crates/warlock-tui/src/ui.rs now takes a QuitConfirm parameter and, when open, renders a small bordered window centred on the terminal with ratatui's Clear behind it: the question 'Leave warlock?', a blank line, then Yes and No, the lit one in FOCUS_COLOUR reversed+bold and the other DIM (no fourth colour, no new dependency). confirm_size measures the window off its own constants via display_width; confirm_area centres and clamps with min/saturating arithmetic rather than skipping the draw. main.rs passes QuitConfirm::Closed for now (WAR-42.03 owns opening it). Eight new TestBackend buffer tests cover: small/centred/bordered, question plus exactly two answers with Yes left of No, nothing from a busy frame showing through at 60x8 (window straddling panel, tree and footer, with the closed render checked non-blank first), cell-for-cell identity outside the window, no trace when closed, highlight opening on No and moving to Yes in the same columns, clamping without panic at 20x5, 4x2, 1x1, 2x20, 30x1, and the footer keeping its three lines and KEYS/QUIT_KEY wording. KEYS, QUIT_KEY, PACTING_KEYS and FOOTER_HEIGHT untouched. fmt/clippy/test --workspace clean (364 lib tests). Committed as f36ea81.

### WAR-42.03 Gate Esc and q behind the confirmation in the event loop and input layer
Gated Esc and q behind the quit confirmation. `input.rs` gained `Pressed` and `press_for(key, confirm, in_flight)` — Ctrl-C an

author: copilot
body:
## Summary

The CI job was failing at Nix **evaluation time** (before any building) with:

```
error: path '/nix/store/yp2dzf1vzm6i47in1rsl49pxkpzdw169-001-poetry-disable-embedded-wheel-tests.patch' is not valid
```

### Why this fails at evaluation, not build time

`devenv-nixpkgs` applies patches to nixpkgs via a `runCommand` derivation (`devenv-nixpkgs-patched`). The patch file is referenced as a **fixed-output source path** — its Nix store hash is content-addressed and baked into the lock file. When Nix evaluates the derivation graph (via `derivationStrict`), it validates that all input paths exist in the store or are fetchable from a binary cache. Because this is a **source path** (a plain file, not a `.drv` output), Nix has no recipe to rebuild it — the only way to obtain it is to fetch the exact store object from a binary cache. The old cache entry had expired/been purged, so evaluation fails immediately.

This is why the error appears before any builds run and cannot be recovered by triggering a rebuild.

### Fix

Updated `devenv.lock` to pin `cachix/devenv-nixpkgs` (`nixpkgs_2`) from `ee3d58d` → `256551e` (2026-08-26) and the corresponding `NixOS/nixpkgs-unstable` source (`nixpkgs-src`) from `54ba4bc` → `c8f9065`. These are the same revisions the devenv team bumped to in their own "deps: bump nixpkgs" commit, which no longer references the stale patch path.

## Changes

- `devenv.lock`: bump `nixpkgs_2` (cachix/devenv-nixpkgs) and `nixpkgs-src` (NixOS/nixpkgs-unstable)

author: fe-ax
body:
The headway rule had two gates:

- **lateral** — refuse any sample where the other vehicle is more than half a lane
  off your line
- **temporal** — measure only from `manoeuvreCompletedAt`, because before the merge
  *"the gap is not a following distance, it is just two vehicles on different bits
  of road"*

Both are true statements about the oprit — and being on the oprit is *exactly* what
"more than half a lane off your line" means. The second gate agreed with the first
everywhere anyone had looked, which made it invisible, which made it look free.

**It wasn't free.** On an open motorway there is no manoeuvre to wait for: the rider
is behind the lorry from the first frame, and sitting on its bumper while waiting
for a gap is a real fault the exam watches for. It was measured nowhere.

## The fix is a deletion

I had this written down as needing a scenario-controlled gate and its own
before-and-after. It needed neither — just the deletion. The before-and-after was
still worth doing, and it's what showed the deletion was safe:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `invoegen` clean | goed / goed | goed / goed |
| `invoegen` tailgate | **ongewenst** / goed | **ongewenst** / goed |
| `inhalen` clean | goed / goed | goed / goed |
| `inhalen` tailgate | goed / goed | **ongewenst** / goed |

Every merge row identical — the proof it had never done anything there. The
overtake's tailgater now gets caught, which is the point.

(My first attempt set the gate to `null` and got *no rows at all* — `null` means
"no manoeuvre happened, don't measure". Worth knowing before anyone touches it
again.)

## Pinned in three places

- The merge test that already builds a rider who **never merges** now also asserts
  it collects no headway row. That's the claim the whole change rests on: the
  lateral test alone does that work.
- The overtake gets the tailgater (`ongewenst`) and the clean rider (`goed`).
- And the rider who never overtakes at all — staying in lane 1 is its own fault and
  shouldn't collect a second one.

## Verification

- **275 tests**, `npm run build` clean, `rm -rf dist`.
- Discrimination coverage unchanged at 13/13, 2/2, 8/8, 11/11.
- The three `invoegen.test.ts` tests that pin held-state headway stayed green
  throughout — they're the ones that would catch this going wrong.

**`BUILDER-GAPS.md` is empty.** It now says what that does and doesn't mean: the
way these were found has stopped finding things, not that there's nothing left. The
list refills by building something with it — a roundabout, a pedestrian crossing,
something at night — not by reading the code.

body: ## What Removes the roadmap from `docs/scope-and-stance.md` and replaces "Scope of the first pass (v0.2)" with "How the modelling proceeds". Four references elsewhere pointed at one or the other — in `README.md`'s status, `docs/pinned-revision.md`'s in-flight-PR note, this repo's `CLAUDE.md` header, and the "Open, deliberately" list — and each is rewritten to match. ## Why The roadmap committed the first pass to a fixed set of sections — §2 identity, §3/§3.1, §4/§4.1, §5.1, §6, §10, §11, §12 — and to a fixed order of Lean modules: `Basic`, `Bundle`, `Policy`, `Gaps`, `Fixtures`. Both were decided on 2026-07-31, before any spec section had been read closely, and the section list was inherited from what `okf-graph` already commits to rather than from the spec's own shape. The replacement is to work down `SPEC.md` in the spec's own order, revising earlier sections as later ones constrain them. §2 is the case that motivates it. Its fourteen terms are a glossary, and nine of them defer their content elsewhere: `Actor` to §7, `Trust tier` to §5.3, `Attested Computation` / `Executor` / `Receipt` / `Attester` to §10, `Source` and `Credibility signal` to §5.1, `Link` to §6. A model of §2 written before those sections is *meant* to be reopened, so the new text says that explicitly rather than leaving revision looking like a slip. ## What is untouched The stance, the trust boundary, the `Policy` mechanism and the two theorem shapes, the non-goals, and the pinned SHA. This changes the order the work is done in, not what the repo claims. One exclusion is worth flagging rather than changing here: §5.3 trust-tier ownership is still listed out of scope on [okf-tools#62](https://github.com/ojhermann-org/okf-tools/issues/62). Under a section-by-section pass we now reach §5.3 as a matter of course, so that exclusion is due a decision when we get there. --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. Autofix is disabled.

body:
Fixes #4892.

Supersedes #4897 (closed unmerged). This PR is a reconciliation, not a continuation of that branch's 205-commit range: it transplants exactly one commit — the original seed `8a7fb6580f` "fix(session): recover metadata-only managed append drift (#4892)" — onto current `dev` (`f22f6c8428`), preserving the original commit and authorship. The rest of the superseded range (natives rewrite, SDK lifecycle, TUI, release tooling) was out of scope for this issue and is not included.

Reporter attribution: @jaepil-choi supplied the original Windows crash evidence and root-cause analysis in #4892.

## What changed

1. **Digest-bound append receipts.** The native `append_managed` return identity now carries the `sha256` it already computes; `ManagedFileIdentity`/`ManagedBoundedAppendExpectation` gained the optional `sha256` and `nlink` fields, and `#captureManagedPersistIdentity` stores a descriptor-bound digest with the persist expectation.
2. **Metadata-only drift is authenticated, not fatal.** When `appendExpectedIdentitySync` sees a descriptor mismatch, it re-authenticates instead of throwing: identical `dev`/`ino`/`nlink`/`size` plus a byte-exact digest proves benign metadata drift (AV scan, indexer, backup sync) and the append proceeds. A changed inode, length, link count, or digest still fails closed so a concurrent successor is never overwritten.

The recovery gate for a *deleted* predecessor (full rewrite from resident entries) and the fail-closed successor guarantee are unchanged, exactly as the issue requested.

## Evidence

- Reproduced independently on Linux before/after the fix: bumping only `mtimeNs`/`ctimeNs` between two appends previously rethrew `managed_append_identity_mismatch` (which surfaces as an unhandled rejection and `process.exit(1)` via the postmortem handler); with the fix the drift is accepted and the entry is durable in the transcript.
- Genuine-successor probe: overwriting the transcript with foreign bytes still throws `managed_append_identity_mismatch` and the successor file is left untouched.
- `bun test packages/coding-agent/test/session-manager/managed-rewrite-enoent-regression.test.ts packages/coding-agent/test/main-interactive-input.test.ts` — 16 pass.
- `bun --cwd=packages/coding-agent run check:types` clean; `bun run check:ts` and `bun run check:rs` clean; `cargo clippy` clean in `crates/pi-natives`.

## Risk classification
- [ ] `regression-risk`
- [x] `low-risk`
- [ ] `high-risk`

author: hoffbrandm
body:
Ten things from using it on a phone.

## Calculation

- **Cash in reserve is allowed a day at a time.** It is the month's spending money — "roughly £30 a day" — so it now pro-rates into the allowance by day-of-month, the way the sheet's column L does, instead of sitting out of it entirely. On the 27th of August, £810 of a £930 reserve is allowed, and the note under the check says so.
- **Out splits into its two halves**: **Cash out** (standing cash monthlies + annual reserve + cash in reserve) and **On to the card** (card monthlies + this month's planned + all weekly slots), with the live **Card balance now** beside them.
- **"First working day of the month" was duplicative** — you were right. It was only ever day 1 rolled to the next working day, which is the other option with `dueDay: 1`. It is gone, and an older record is stored as the rule it always meant.

## Entry

- **A pending row can be negative.** A refund or a credit on the statement is a real thing to record, and it now comes off the card side rather than being rejected.
- **Month and day inputs size to their content** instead of stretching the width of the sheet, so they read the same everywhere — no longer too wide on payslips or adrift in the exception form.

## Home

- **Accordions start closed**, so the statement reads first.
- **Each accordion sits in a box**, so it looks like something that opens.
- **The Weeklies room no longer duplicates Home.** It listed the same tickable slots. It is now the rules that make the slots, with a ticked count and total for the month on screen; ticking lives on Home only — the same shape Monthlies already had.

## Planned

- **A Planned per month table**: this month and every month ahead that has something in it, with a bar for relative size and a tap to open that month. A month quietly filling up is visible before it arrives rather than when it lands in Out.

## Verification

`npm test` — 140 pass. Driven in Chromium at phone width: all eleven screens and the add modals render with no console or page errors; accordions come up closed; the reserve pro-rate reads correctly through the month; a −£40 pending row flows through to the card side; the Planned table groups and totals the months ahead.

---

> **Medium Risk**
> Changes core month cashflow and card-allowance math (reserve pro-rating and Out split), plus signed pending amounts and due-roll normalization—well-tested but affects how overspend/underspend is computed.
> 
> **Overview**
> This PR tightens **Home’s month statement** and several flows that feed the card check.
> 
> **Cashflow logic** now treats **cash in reserve** as allowed **day-by-day** (pro-rated by day-of-month into the card allowance, matching the sheet’s column L), while still counting the full reserve in **Out**. **Out** is broken out on the statement as **Cash out** vs **On to the card**, with **Card balance now** beside them; the under-check note can show reserve progress through the month. **Pending** rows accept **negative amounts** (refunds/credits) so they reduce what counts on the cards. **Monthly due** drops the separate “first working day” option—legacy `firstWorking` is normalized to day 1 + next working day on read/save.

body:
## Tax status — now stated

The IRS determination letter is in hand and the foundation is listed in IRS Publication 78, confirmed by Zachary Lipson on 27 August 2026. The site says so for the first time:

> Lipson Foundation Inc. is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization. EIN 39-4624045. Contributions are tax-deductible to the extent allowed by law.

It appears in the footer on every page, and on `/donate` where it matters to someone mid-decision. One value in `lib/site.ts` (`taxNotice`), so the two can never disagree.

**CLAUDE.md previously forbade this outright** as an unconfirmed binder target. That prohibition is replaced by the confirmation, its date, and its source, so the rule now reflects reality rather than being reversed silently.

Two things stay forbidden and are called out as such:
- **FDACS registration** — a separate Florida filing from the IRS determination. Nothing here confirms it.
- **"Public charity"** as a phrase — the letter's classification has not been read here, so the site does not characterise the status beyond 501(c)(3).

## Footer blurb, foundation-wide

**Before**

> …builds cost-free community programs for underserved communities. **Fitness, wellness, and mentoring are where the work starts.** Every program is completely cost-free — no memberships, no fees, ever.

**After**

> …builds cost-free community programs for underserved communities across South Florida, Palm Beach County and surrounding counties. Whatever a neighborhood needs and cost has kept out of reach. No memberships, no fees, ever.

Every other place that names the three categories pairs them with an explicit limit-breaker in the same breath — "not where it ends", "the mandate is any cost-free program a community needs", "the mission is bigger than any category". The footer named them and stopped, and because it is the footer, that was the last thing a visitor read on every page.

No em dashes in the paragraph. `site.location` keeps its dash where it is set as a data field rather than prose.

- `npx eslint app components lib --max-warnings 0`
- `npx tsc --noEmit`

body:
## Summary

Implements MVP-P2B: the EAT-owned deterministic local Git acquisition mechanism required by the Engineering OS internal MVP.

The implementation resolves an explicitly supplied local Git repository and immutable revision into mechanical Git evidence for later EI consumption.

It does not establish source authority and does not implement EI Source Binding semantics.

## Commits

1. `19e70eb800614af00be631325c6386108668823d`
   `feat(eat): add deterministic local Git acquisition`

2. `21b66e9b3c717427c5bb5f2ac3826e7a9a54186f`
   `fix(eat): harden local Git acquisition integrity`

The remediation commit remains separate intentionally to preserve the independently reviewed implementation lineage.

## Implemented capability

MVP-P2B provides:

- exact local repository-root validation;
- immutable EXACT_COMMIT and one-time HEAD pinning;
- Git-tree-only tracked inventory;
- deterministic path/mode/type/OID/size output;
- no dirty/untracked worktree influence;
- symlink metadata without dereference;
- gitlink metadata without recursion;
- bounded subprocess execution with `shell=False`;
- hostile Git-environment isolation;
- Git replacement objects disabled;
- deterministic JSON stdin/stdout CLI;
- closed success diagnostic contract.

## Integrity guarantees

The implementation enforces:

- no parent repository discovery;
- no mutable branch/tag as final revision;
- no `git replace` commit/tree drift;
- no remote Git operations;
- no worktree mutation;
- no symlink target filesystem access;
- no submodule initialization/fetch/update;
- no untracked-file reads;
- no regular blob materialization for inventory;
- bounded failure diagnostics without raw Git stderr;
- deterministic repeated acquisition.

## Independent review findings

Initial independent review found:

- `MVP-P2B-R1-001`
  Git replacement objects could cause the reported commit and acquired tree to diverge.

- `MVP-P2B-R1-002`
  The result diagnostics schema accepted arbitrary payloads.

Both were remediated and independently re-reviewed.

Final state:

`MVP-P2B-R1-001 = CLOSED_CONFIRMED`

`MVP-P2B-R1-002 = CLOSED_CONFIRMED`

`OPEN_MUST_FIX_FINDINGS = 0`

`INDEPENDENT_IMPLEMENTATION_REREVIEW = PASS`

## Dogfood

Validated against:

`engineering-os-architecture-technology`

Commit:

`d781584c988040f0f8ff43b57a1f1336780a9e28`

Tree:

`a13fa8647183690df57b65d9429310cb9efb6b71`

Tracked files:

`158`

Submodules:

`0`

Symlinks:

`0`

Repeatability:

`PASS`

## Validation

Final candidate passed:

- 20 P2-B test methods;
- 7 positive cases;
- 28 adversarial classes;
- EAT contract validation;
- EAT semantic/governance validation;
- manifest validation;
- combined diff integrity;
- final fresh independent adversarial review.

## Scope

No changes to EAT authority.

No Core changes.

No EI changes.

No SPC changes.

No Source Binding semantics.

No remote acquisition.

## MVP consequence

After merge, EAT provides the reusable local Git acquisition mechanism required by MVP-P2C.

Next gate:

`MVP-P2C — EI Source Binding builder + Core admission adapter`

## Pre-merge checklist

- [ ] Base is `main`
- [ ] Head is `codex/eat-mvp-p2b-local-git-acquisition`
- [ ] Exactly 2 commits
- [ ] Head is `21b66e9b3c717427c5bb5f2ac3826e7a9a54186f`
- [ ] No unexpected files
- [ ] No authority files changed
- [ ] Open MUST_FIX findings = 0
- [ ] P2-B full regression = PASS
- [ ] Dogfood exact/repeatable = PASS
- [ ] Independent re-review = PASS
